articles.title: Exciplex-Facilitated Charge Extraction and Defect Chelation to Improve Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Rational molecular engineering of the perovskite/hole transport layer interface offers a promising route to simultaneously address inefficient charge extraction, defect-mediated recombination, and lead leakage in CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite solar cells. Herein, we introduce 2,2′-dinitro-9,9′-spirobifluorene (DN-SBF) as an interfacial molecular bridge to tackle these challenges. DN-SBF optimizes energy level alignment, establishes π–π interactions, and forms exciplexes with Spiro-OMeTAD, thereby facilitating interfacial charge transport. Meanwhile, DN-SBF passivates undercoordinated Pb2+ through multiple coordination modes, including robust bidentate chelation formed by adjacent nitro groups, effectively passivating defects and suppressing non-radiative recombination. Importantly, multipoint coordination immobilizes leachable Pb2+, substantially mitigating lead leakage and improving film biocompatibility. As a result, DN-SBF-engineered CsPbI3–xBrx devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.40% along with significantly enhanced operational and environmental stability. This work highlights the potential of versatile molecular bridges to concurrently enhance performance, stability, and eco-friendliness, which may contribute to the development of more sustainable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Data-Driven Flipping Engineering for High Thermal Anisotropy in Janus Two-Dimensional Materials
articles.abstract: The vertical integration of heterogeneous dies in three-dimensional integrated circuits demands materials with extreme thermal anisotropy to dissipate heat in-plane while suppressing cross-plane leakage. Randomly twisted van der Waals stacks can enhance anisotropy, but their stochastic nature lacks precise control. Here, we report flipping engineering in Janus MoSSe stacks, exploiting the intrinsic asymmetry between the S–Mo–Se and Se–Mo–S terminations as a programmable structural degree of freedom orthogonal to twisting. By integrating machine-learned potential molecular dynamics with Bayesian optimization for a 14-layer MoSSe stack, we identify a structure with strongly suppressed effective cross-plane thermal conductivity of 0.082 ± 0.002 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K while maintaining robust in-plane conduction, yielding an anisotropy ratio of about 760 and 35% higher than the crystalline reference. This effect arises from flipping-induced breaking of stacking periodicity, which perturbs midfrequency phonons (2–8 THz) and leads to band splitting and nearly flat, layer-localized modes. These changes reduce the cross-plane propagating channels and thus weaken their contribution to thermal transport, while their impact on in-plane transport dominated by low-frequency acoustic phonons is negligible. Flipping engineering thus provides programmable stacking-sequence strategy and a versatile route for designing anisotropic properties in layered materials.

articles.title: Experimental Design Signatures Emerge from Topic Modeling of Graphene Oxide Literature
articles.abstract: The literature on graphene oxide (GO) comprises hundreds of thousands of publications spanning synthesis, characterization, and applications in diverse domains. Advancing GO materials requires a structured knowledge map derived from systematic mining of this extensive corpus. However, extracting meaningful insights from this vast, heterogeneous, sparse, and unstructured data remains a challenge. To address this challenge, Natural Language Processing techniques, including topic modeling, community discovery, and parameter extraction, are here employed to establish a framework. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was applied to the full text of more than 120,000 articles, enabling the identification of eight macro-domains within the GO literature, and neural topic modeling was subsequently employed to characterize the granularity and heterogeneity of these domains. Parameter extraction was performed using Large Language Models (LLMs) on a subset of 8000 full-text articles, with a proto-ontology incorporated into the extraction prompt. Even with a broad prompt, an F1 score of 94% was achieved against manual validation. The extracted parameters were then clustered through community modeling and compared with the LDA-derived topics. At this intermediate resolution of the literature, we demonstrate the application of a recommendation system for relevant parameters according to the material family and application domain. The applicability of the framework at higher resolutions was further demonstrated through the construction of a data set of CO2 adsorption for graphene- and GO-based materials. This data set was subsequently employed in a downstream predictive case study using an Extremely Randomized Trees Regressor, with different training-test splitting strategies evaluated to assess in-domain and out-of-domain generalization at article-level resolution.

articles.title: Nanopore Signatures of High-Molecular-Weight Polysaccharides with Recurring Structural Motifs
articles.abstract: Polysaccharides in nature possess profound biological significance, and their structural complexity renders them of great research value. However, the structural heterogeneity of complex polysaccharides has long posed a great challenge for analysis. Here, a nanopore profiling strategy was developed for polysaccharide characterization. Experimentally, polysaccharides are hydrolyzed into informative fragments, and the distribution of their resulting nanopore events forms a unique profile that serves as a reliable molecular signature. Seven distinct polysaccharides, including xanthan gum, gum arabic, agarose, sodium alginate, gellan gum, heparin, and chondroitin sulfate A, were successfully identified and discriminated. A profile-based machine learning classifier was also developed, which utilizes the overall distribution profile of fragment events as training input, yielding 100% validation accuracy. Further application of the fully constrained least-squares (FCLS) algorithm enabled accurate quantification of polysaccharide mixture composition, allowing for unambiguous analysis of mixtures of polysaccharides in the same assay. Collectively, this work establishes a universal, label-free, and high-resolution framework for decoding the structural complexity of polysaccharides.

articles.title: Reversible Ferroelastic Strain Engineering Enables Stabilization of a Hidden Ga2O3 Polymorph
articles.abstract: Understanding the formation, transformation, and stabilization of metastable polymorphs in functional compounds is a central challenge in materials science and has a profound impact on phase engineering and property control. Ga2O3 is an ultrawide bandgap semiconductor whose rich polymorphism underpins diverse electronic and optoelectronic functionalities, motivating continued exploration of its metastable phases. Among the known Ga2O3 polymorphs, the P1̅-phase has been predicted to have the closest energy to the thermodynamically stable β-phase; however, its existence has not been definitively identified experimentally, and feasible preparation routes remain unclear up to now. Here, combining large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a high-accuracy machine learning potential, we reveal a reversible strain-induced ferroelastic β–P1̅ phase transition in Ga2O3 and further investigate the origin of instability of P1̅-Ga2O3. Our work not only explains the absence of experimental observations of P1̅-Ga2O3 from the perspectives of mechanical stability and crystallization kinetics but also extends the application of strain engineering in phase transitions of wide-bandgap semiconductor single-crystal materials.

Mechanistic Insights into the Colloidal Synthesis of Monodisperse CoF2 Nanorods
articles.abstract: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.

articles.title: A Histidine-Mediated, Pendulum-Like Proton Transport Mechanism Is Required for the High Catalytic Activity of [FeFe]-Hydrogenases
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: [FeFe]-hydrogenases are molecular hydrogen (H2) converting enzymes that employ a hexanuclear iron complex, the H-cluster, as the catalytic cofactor, and a proton transfer pathway (PTP) that enables efficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Recent phylogenetic analyses have revealed different groups of [FeFe]-hydrogenases. Although only very few members of other groups have been characterized, current knowledge suggests that high catalytic activity is predominantly associated with group A members. Here, we show that metal ions inhibit group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases by binding to three specific residues at the entrance of the PTP. Exchanging residue H565 of Clostridium pasteurianum CpI results in a metal-insensitive protein variant with wild-type-like activity. In contrast, exchanging S320 and H569 in CpI, and their counterparts in additional group A [FeFe]-hydrogenases results in enzymes with markedly decreased activities and large overpotential requirements. These features are consistent with important roles of both residues in catalytic proton transfer. CpI structures reveal that H569, locally anchored by E278, can be present in two conformations, such that we propose a histidine-dependent pendulum mechanism for exchanging protons between the bulk solvent and the PTP, which is well supported by theoretical calculations. In doing so, our study broadens understanding of how histidine mobility, governed by neighboring residues in the vicinity, contributes to the fundamental concept of PCET.

articles.title: Accessing Diverse C(sp3)-Rich Cyclophane Linkers in Macrocyclic Peptides via Nickel-Mediated Deaminative Macrocyclic Arylation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Within macrocyclic peptides of both natural products and pharmaceutical targets, aryl rings play a crucial role in linker structure, and C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers can imbue beneficial physicochemical properties. Yet, methods to deliver C(sp3)-rich cyclophane linkers remain limited, restricting the types of carbon-rich linkers that can be efficiently investigated in medicinal chemistry campaigns. Herein, we describe the development of a nickel-mediated deaminative macrocyclic arylation that uses amino acid monomers compatible with solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows, accommodates a wide range of peptide functionalities, and can access broad macrocycle architectures including those of a natural alkaloid derivative and polycyclic peptides.

articles.title: Aliphatic Diazonium Chemistry through Hydroquinone-Based Nitrate Reduction for Deaminative Halogenation and Nitrate Ester Formation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Alcohols are readily converted to electrophiles on a large scale, while deaminative functionalization of aliphatic amines is less developed. Aromatic amines are readily used as versatile synthetic intermediates through diazonium chemistry, but analogous aliphatic diazonium chemistry is currently not as useful because of the instability and explosiveness of aliphatic diazonium intermediates. Here, we develop aliphatic diazonium chemistry through nitrate reduction-based diazotization with substoichiometric hydroquinone as a chemically competent reductant. As a consequence, the deamination allows Sandmeyer-type reactivity to convert aliphatic amines into alkyl (pseudo)halides. Because all of the reagents are inexpensive, aliphatic diazonium chemistry provides potential access to alkyl halides and alkyl nitrate esters on scale.

articles.title: Topology-Engineered Dual-Functional COFs with Spatially Cooperated Hydrophilic and Photocatalytic Sites for Harvesting Safe Water from Polluted Atmosphere
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) has emerged as a promising decentralized solution for freshwater supply in off-grid regions by extracting ubiquitous moisture from the air. However, the atmosphere also carries airborne pathogens and, under extreme scenarios, toxic chemicals, which can be coharvested to contaminate the collected water. Despite extensive efforts to maximize water uptake, the safety of the harvested water has been largely neglected in the pursuit of higher water production yields. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) provide crystalline, molecularly programmable platforms for integrating water adsorption with photocatalytic detoxification. However, achieving such functional synergy depends on framework topology, which governs site accessibility and mass transport. Here, we report topology-engineered dual-functional COFs that regulate spatial cooperation among hydrophilic sites, photoactive sites, and pore structures in a series of 1D and 2D hydrazone COFs constructed from identical molecular building blocks. Compared to the compact 1D chain packing, the open and continuous channels of the 2D framework increase functional-site accessibility, support hydrogen-bonded water network formation, and facilitate charge-carrier separation and O2 activation. The optimized Por-TAH (2D) exhibits a saturated water uptake of 629 mg g–1, releases 94% of adsorbed water under mild heating, inactivates 99.99% of S. aureus within 1 h, and completely converts chemical agents with high selectivity within 10 min. As a proof-of-concept application, continuous-flow operation demonstrates integrated water harvesting and photocatalytic detoxification, yielding safe water free of detectable mustard gas simulants. This study establishes topology-directed spatial cooperation as a design principle for multifunctional porous materials, enabling safe water production from real contaminated air.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Dynamics of Strain-Driven Sn Segregation in GeSn Alloys
Plasmonic Coupling within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
articles.abstract: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N bond remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation under ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation. Systematic variation of the intercluster separation shows that a 6 Å nanogap maximizes near-field enhancement and hot-electron transfer to the adsorbed N2, accompanied by N–N activation. Consequently, N2 dissociation is achieved at incident field strengths as low as 0.5 V Å–1, whereas larger-gap dimers exhibit substantially lower activity. Similarly, isolated N2 remains intact under comparable conditions. These findings establish nanogap engineering as an effective strategy for optimizing plasmon-driven N2 activation and provide design principles for developing efficient plasmonic catalysts.

articles.title: Ultralow-Threshold NIR AgAuSe Colloidal Quantum Dot Laser
articles.abstract: Solution-processable quantum dot (QD) lasers are essential for next-generation integrated photonic circuits, ranging, and optical sensing. However, their practical deployment remains hampered by high lasing thresholds. Here, we report AgAuSe QD lasing with a record-low threshold of 0.01 μJ cm–2 at 900 nm, representing a reduction of more than 4 orders of magnitude compared to those of previous near-infrared (NIR) QD lasing reports. This achievement is enabled by a well-designed twisted-lattice photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity delivering extreme light confinement with an ultrahigh quality (Q) factor. The extended photon lifetime reduces the required gain volume, enabling lasing from a single-layer self-assembled QD superlattice (SL), which minimizes scattering losses. Crucially, the robust system allows us to push the operational regime to quasi-continuous-wave (q-CW) lasing at room temperature. These results establish a new benchmark for solution-processed NIR QD sources and provide a technologically viable pathway for sustained CW operation.

articles.title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
articles.abstract: Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells.

articles.title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
articles.abstract: Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes.

articles.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
articles.abstract: Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines. Water structures govern the behaviour of solutes across aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Here the authors use weakly hydrated anions to reshape hydration in the bulk and at interfaces, thereby regulating amine monomer partitioning and interfacial transport while suppressing acyl chloride hydrolysis during polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization.

articles.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
articles.abstract: Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

articles.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
articles.abstract: Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries.

articles.title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.

articles.title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
articles.abstract: Turning waste plastic into valuable chemicals requires precise control of competing reactions. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine.

articles.title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
articles.abstract: Structural isomers can be difficult to distinguish and map by mass alone. This study shows that Orbitrap-SIMS can separate and image isomeric sugars directly on surfaces, offering a new route to study complex biomolecules.

articles.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
articles.abstract: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

articles.title: Deep-Learning-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives
articles.abstract: The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with > 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.

articles.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
articles.abstract: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

articles.title: High-Density Iridium Single Atoms on Vanadium-Doped TiO2 for Electrochemical Water Oxidation Catalysis
articles.abstract: Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.

articles.title: Reductive Dispersion of In2O3 into H-CHA and Reversible Formation of Isolated In(I)/In(III) Species under H2/O2 Redox Cycling
articles.abstract: The reductive dispersion of metal oxides into isolated cationic species in zeolites is an important strategy for generating well-defined catalytic sites, yet its kinetics and molecular mechanism remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the H2-induced redispersion of In2O3 physically mixed with H-CHA using in situ/operando UV–vis spectroscopy, In K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), SEM-EDS mapping, modulation-excitation spectroscopy, H2-TPR, XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-resolved UV–vis spectroscopy quantitatively tracks the consumption of bulk-like In2O3 under H2 and reveals that the redispersion rate depends on temperature, H2 concentration, In2O3 precursor properties, and zeolite framework. Higher temperatures and H2 concentrations accelerate the process, with the highest reliable initial rate observed at 600 °C under 10% H2. In K-edge XANES indicates selective formation of reduced In species assigned to framework-stabilized In+ rather than metallic In0, demonstrating a partial-reduction pathway in CHA. H2-TPR provides quantitative redox evidence consistent with reductive solid-state ion exchange and reversible reduction of isolated oxygen-containing In species. SEM–EDS mapping shows the disappearance of surface In-rich domains after H2 treatment, consistent with indium redistribution, while XANES provides bulk-sensitive evidence for formation of reduced In species. Operando redox-cycling experiments reveal reversible interconversion between In(I) and oxygen-containing In(III) species under H2/O2 switching. DFT calculations using representative 1Al and 2Al CHA models suggest that local Al environments can influence the relative stability of framework-bound reduced In(I) and oxygen/hydroxyl-containing In(III)-type species. Together, these results support a two-step mechanism in which bulk In2O3 is first reduced to mobile In+ species and then anchored at acid sites within the zeolite framework. This work provides mechanistic insight into reductive redispersion and offers design principles for regenerable indium-based zeolite catalysts.

articles.title: Synergy of Ni Nanoparticles and MoO x Species for Selective Hydrodeoxygenation of Lignin into Cycloalkanes
articles.abstract: The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.

articles.title: Grain Boundary Character Governs Lithium Deposition Uniformity on Polycrystalline Copper
articles.abstract: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.

articles.title: Overcoming Indium-Tin-Oxide Optical Losses in InAs Colloidal Quantum-Dot Light-Emitting Diodes at 1550 nm
articles.abstract: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.

articles.title: Pressure-Driven Topological Reconfiguration toward Fast-Charging Hard Carbon with Plateau-Capacity Retention
articles.abstract: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.

articles.title: Vacuum-Evaporated Molecules with Giant Spontaneous Orientation Polarization for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

articles.title: Beyond Static Architectures: Responsive Tetrahedral Framework Nucleic Acids for Precise Theranostics
articles.abstract: Precise theranostics requires spatiotemporal control and high specificity to adapt to complex physiological microenvironments. Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNA), classic 3D DNA nanostructures, offer distinct advantages such as atomic-level structural precision, intrinsic programmability, and excellent biocompatibility. While traditional static tFNA lack dynamic responsiveness to external stimuli─severely limiting their clinical translation potential─the emergence of dynamically responsive tFNA has garnered increasing attention. These smart systems offer substantial advantages, including stimulus-triggered structural reconfiguration, targeted payload release, and real-time signal transduction. Despite rapid design innovations, a systematic summary of dynamic tFNA strategies remains lacking. Accordingly, we synthesize the design principles of responsive tFNA by categorizing their mechanisms into conformational rearrangement, chemical bond cleavage, and toehold-mediated strand displacement logic. We highlight their applications in precision diagnosis, smart therapeutics, and theranostics integration and discuss critical challenges in biological stability, scalable manufacturing, and biosecurity. By mapping current advancements and unresolved hurdles, this work provides a comprehensive reference for the rational design of responsive DNA nanodevices and discusses the challenges associated with the clinical translation of dynamic tFNA.

articles.title: Dynamic Ti–Cl Bonding Enables Corrosion-Resistant and Robust Seawater Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Seawater electrolysis is essential for sustainable green hydrogen production but remains hindered by chloride ions (Cl–)-induced corrosion of electrode catalysts. Herein, we report an “adsorption-guided protection” strategy to achieve the trade-off between corrosion resistance and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity for NiFe layered double hydroxide (NiFe-LDH). Unlike conventional strategies that aim solely to repel Cl–, this strategy incorporates Ti dopants as preferential Cl–-trapping centers. The Cl– dynamically adsorbed on Ti sites shields the OER-active Ni/Fe centers from corrosive attack and concurrently creates a localized electrostatic repulsion that inhibits further Cl– accumulation on the catalyst surface. NiFeTi-LDH exhibits high OER performance in alkaline seawater, achieving ampere-level current density with outstanding stability exceeding 3000 h. In situ spectroscopic analysis combined with theoretical calculations reveals that the Ti–Cl bonding not only lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining step for OER intermediates but also induces an electrostatic repulsion effect that further excludes additional Cl– from approaching the active surface. This study offers insights into the reasonable design of high-performance and corrosion-resistant non-noble-metal catalysts for practical seawater electrolysis.

articles.title: Gold Nanourchins Potentiate Intravesical Chemotherapy by Accelerating Drug Internalization within a Short Instillation Window
articles.abstract: Intravesical chemotherapy is a standard adjuvant treatment for nonmuscle-invasive bladder cancer after transurethral resection, but its efficacy is limited by drug exposure resulting from urinary dilution and physiological voiding. Most current delivery strategies aim to prolong the intravesical residence through mucoadhesion, depot formation, or sustained release. Although these approaches increase local drug availability, they do not directly address insufficient intracellular drug accumulation during the short instillation window. Here, we report a poly-l-glutamic acid-modified gold nanourchin platform, PGU3@DOX, designed to enhance intravesical chemotherapy by accelerating drug internalization by bladder cancer cells. By optimizing the nanoparticle morphology, we identified long-spiked gold nanourchins as the most effective architecture for rapid cellular uptake. The PLG coating enabled doxorubicin loading and supported pH-facilitated DOX release, while the internalized nanourchins induced lysosomal swelling and lysosomal membrane permeabilization in bladder cancer cells. Under a 1 h pulse exposure that mimics the short intravesical dwell-time window, PGU3@DOX showed greater cytotoxicity against bladder cancer cells after extracellular drug removal while showing lower toxicity toward normal urothelial cells. Furthermore, PGU3@DOX achieved a broader distribution and stronger damage in tumor spheroids than free DOX. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, a single short-duration intravesical administration of PGU3@DOX significantly suppressed tumor progression without detectable acute hematological, hepatic, renal, or cardiac toxicity under the tested conditions. These findings support rapid cellular internalization as a complementary strategy to improve intravesical chemotherapy and provide a morphology-guided nanocarrier platform for enhancing drug delivery within short therapeutic exposure windows.

articles.title: Low-Dimensional Nanostructured Molecular Architectures for Advanced CO2 Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Molecular catalysts have been found to be selective for the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), with Faradaic efficiencies approaching 100% for two-electron products such as CO and formic acid. However, translating the intrinsic activity of well-defined molecular active sites into practical high-current-density electrolysis remains challenging due to molecular aggregation, poor electronic coupling with electrodes, and limited stability. In addition, multielectron molecular CO2RR is hampered by complex reaction pathways and insufficient adsorption of intermediates. This perspective discusses how nanostructured molecular architectures, from controlled aggregation and support interactions to reticular frameworks, fundamentally alter catalytic performance beyond what is achievable through conventional coordination chemistry alone. We highlight recent advances demonstrating that molecular dispersion, curvature-induced strain, nanoconfinement, and layered confinement can redirect reaction pathways, enabling multielectron reduction products such as methanol and ethanol. We further discuss emerging opportunities in computation-accelerated molecular discovery, strategies to address high overpotentials, and the integration of CO2 capture with electrochemical conversion. By engineering the microenvironment surrounding molecular active sites, we argue that the next generation of molecular electrocatalysts can achieve the activity, selectivity, and stability required for practical deployment.

articles.title: High thermoelectric performance in n-type–cubic (SnSe)0.55(PbTe)0.45 polycrystals via suppressed ionized impurity scattering
Suppression of Structural Transitions in Iron: Magnetic Stabilization of the bcc-phase via Defect Control
Coupling Interfacial Defect Regulation With Lattice Relaxation in FACsPbI3 Perovskite
articles.abstract: FACsPbI3 perovskites, free of volatile methylammonium and mixed halides, are among promising absorbers for efficient optoelectronics owing to their favourable bandgap and intrinsic stability. However, the structurally soft lattice makes their surfaces prone to distortion and defect generation, creating a heterogeneous interfacial energy landscape that promotes non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Here, we report an interfacial regulation strategy that stabilizes the surface/interface configuration of FACsPbI3 through a defect‐lattice coupling mechanism. Introducing morpholinium chloride at the FACsPbI3 interface/surface enables coordination with undercoordinated lattice sites, thereby relieving local lattice strain, stabilizing surface Pb‐I octahedral network, and reducing the density of defect states. This coupling between interfacial chemistry and lattice energetics increases vacancy formation energies, homogenizes the interfacial electronic environment, and suppresses defect‐assisted recombination and ion migration. The resulting perovskite solar cells yield an efficiency of 26.67% with a 16.1 cm2‐aperture mini‐module reaching an efficiency of 22.79%. Moreover, the devices exhibit enhanced stability, retaining 95.8% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous operation. This work reveals a defect‐lattice coupling paradigm that links interfacial chemistry, lattice energetics, and ion migration kinetics, offering a general route toward stable and high‐efficiency soft ionic semiconductors.

articles.title: Disrupting Solvent Self‐Association via Dipole–Dipole Interactions for Improved Performance of Perovskite Solar Cell
articles.abstract: High‐quality perovskite films demand strongly coordinating solvents (SCS, e.g., DMSO, NMP) for crystal growth regulation, yet such solvents often leave residue and induce notorious voids. Prior work elucidated the voids distribution along the vertical direction but cannot explain their lateral dimensions and spatial patterning. Here, we find that the hundreds‐of‐nanometer lateral dimension and clustered morphology of buried voids originate from the self‐association of SCS. The tailored‐made 1‐bromo‐4‐dimethylphosphoryl‐benzene (BPPO) with inherently weak intermolecular interaction is introduced, which mainly exists in a monomeric form and can efficiently modify the buried interface by constructing dipole‐dipole interactions with SCS. The self‐association is disrupted, enabling uniform SCS distribution rather than forming big cluster, which accelerates the escape and ultimately eliminates voids at the buried interface. Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on BPPO show an efficiency increase from 25.2% to 27.2% (certified efficiency of 27.0%, aperture area of 0.0712 cm2), with improved stability under ISOS‐D‐2 and ISOS‐L‐2 protocols. Furthermore, the BPPO‐modified perovskite solar module (PSMs, aperture area of 17.4 cm2) achieved an efficiency of 24.2%, demonstrating its excellent scalability.

articles.title: Electrochemical and Mechanical Understanding of Extruded and Solvent‐Cast Solid Polymer Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on Poly(ethylene oxide)‐Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PEO–LiTFSI) are promising materials for solid‐state batteries. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted on their electrochemical and mechanical properties, with SPEs prepared via two processing methods: extrusion and solvent casting. The effects of Al2O3 addition and membrane thickness on SPE performance and cyclability were investigated. Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al2O3 improved membrane stability. Thicker membranes exhibited larger polarization gradients, slower ion diffusion, and lower Sand times, leading to reduced electrochemical performance. Mechanical properties, including yield stress, storage modulus, and fracture toughness, were assessed using rheology and dynamic mechanical analysis. Extruded SPEs displayed higher stiffness and greater resistance to dendrite formation than solvent‐cast membranes. Monotonic crack growth tests indicated that the presence of Al2O3 increased fracture toughness, enhancing crack resistance and potentially extending cycle life. Overall, membranes produced via extrusion, containing Al2O3, and optimized for reduced thickness, combined superior electrochemical properties, making them strong candidates for solid‐state battery applications, as demonstrated by their incorporation in multilayer cells.

articles.title: Selective Interfacial Coupling in Polymer Electrolytes Stabilizes High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes for > 500 Wh Kg−1 Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The interfacial chemistry of high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is strongly governed by electronic coupling between electrolyte components and cathode surfaces. However, current strategies generally regulate coupling as an overall interaction‐strength issue, overlooking the distinct contributions of individual electrolyte species and thereby limiting precise interfacial control. Here, we propose a selective interfacial coupling strategy by constructing an interfacial architecture comprising a coupling center and a weak‐coupling environment. Specifically, 2‐cyanoethyl acrylate (CA) acts as the coupling center, while a highly fluorinated acrylate (DFA) creates the weak‐coupling environment. Their synergy reconstructs the interfacial molecular organization, suppresses undesirable coupling from non‐target species, and preserves favorable CA‐cathode interactions. Multiscale calculations and operando spectroscopy reveal the reconstructed interfacial structure and its dynamic evolution. The resulting enlarged Ni 3d‐O 2p band‐center separation stabilizes the TM‐O electronic structure, suppressing lattice oxygen release, cation mixing, and transition‐metal dissolution. Consequently, Li||Ni90 cells retain 78% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.7 V, while a 5 Ah pouch cell delivers 529.4 Wh kg−1 at 4.6 V. This work establishes selective interfacial coupling as an effective strategy for regulating high‐voltage interfaces.

articles.title: A Starfish‐Inspired Hierarchical Multimodal Flexible Sensor for Decoupled Thumb Motion Perception and Virtual Human–Machine Interaction
articles.abstract: Wearable human–machine interfaces (HMIs) require sensing systems that combine high accuracy, mechanical compliance, and low system complexity. Here, we present a starfish‐inspired, hierarchically decoupled multimodal flexible sensor for high‐fidelity thumb motion perception and virtual human–machine interaction. Inspired by the distributed sensing mechanism of starfish tube feet, the architecture integrates radially distributed strain channels with spatially isolated pressure nodes. This design enables simultaneous sensing of global deformation and localized tactile stimuli while minimizing mechanical coupling. Finite element simulations and experimental characterization demonstrate effective strain amplification, low interchannel coupling, stable electromechanical performance, and long‐term durability. Combined with a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier, the system achieves validation and test accuracies of 99.82% and 99.27%, respectively, for six thumb motions, with strong cross‐subject generalization. The decoded motions enable intuitive, real‐time control in a virtual environment without bulky sensor gloves or external tracking systems. This work establishes a bioinspired strategy for structurally decoupled multimodal flexible sensing and provides a promising platform for wearable HMIs and intelligent robotics.

articles.title: Bistable Isochoric Chiral Metamaterials with Reprogrammable Multiaxial Responses
articles.abstract: Reprogrammable materials enable post‐fabrication tuning of mechanical properties, yet existing concepts are largely confined to uniaxial responses. Engineering materials, on the other hand, are routinely subjected to loading in multiple directions, yet their mechanical responses along these directions cannot be tuned in situ. Here, we introduce a class of chiral metamaterials built from isochoric rotationally bistable units that unlock reprogrammable behavior across multiaxial loading states. Integrating theory, simulations, and experiments, we demonstrate that the bistable units can reversibly switch between open and closed states under clockwise or counterclockwise torque, enabling isochoric switching between soft and stiff responses without geometric reconfiguration of the surrounding architecture. Upon selective activation of given bistable cores, the metamaterial exhibits reprogrammable snap‐through instabilities that alter in situ global buckling modes and energy dissipation pathways. Under multiaxial loading, a set of volume‐dominated properties, including effective bulk modulus and volumetric instability, can be reprogrammed, enabling erasable and rewritable two‐dimensional snapping sequences that encode complex mechanical memory within the material. Beyond property tuning, the work suggests a scalable, reprogrammable framework that can be extended to Cosserat media to achieve multiaxial multifunctionality in soft robotics, fluidic devices, and mechanically intelligent systems.

articles.title: Core‐Periphery Fullerene Architectures Engineer Catalytic Interfaces for Efficient Neutral Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Neutral hydrogen evolution is governed by coupled active‐site and solvent processes, posing a great challenge for catalyst design. Here, ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters are anchored on a sulfonated fullerene scaffold (Ru/C60‐S), exploiting its core‐periphery architecture to couple active‐site energetics with interfacial hydration. Electronic interaction with the fullerene cage polarizes Ru sites, facilitating water activation and moderating H/OH binding, while the sulfonated periphery establishes a less ordered and more field‐responsive interfacial hydrogen‐bond network. Ru/C60‐S requires only 10 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2, sustains 100 mA cm−2 for over 1000 h in phosphate‐buffered solution, and exhibits minimal activity loss from alkaline to neutral media. Molecular dynamics simulations, operando Raman, in situ FTIR and local pH measurements corroborate this interfacial restructuring under neutral HER conditions. Targeted perturbation of the fullerene periphery rigidifies the hydrogen‐bond network and is accompanied by increased isotope sensitivity, slower interfacial kinetics, and diminished HER activity. These results identify interfacial hydration as a kinetically important component of neutral HER and demonstrate a core‐periphery molecular strategy for cooperatively regulating active‐site energetics and solvent organization.

articles.title: Deciphering Anomalous Luminescence in Highly Doped Transition‐Metal Phosphors: Spin‐Exchange, Unusual Site Occupancy, and Trace Impurities
articles.abstract: Anomalous luminescence in phosphors highly doped with transition‐metal ions (e.g., Mn2+${\rm Mn}^{2+}$, Cr3+${\rm Cr}^{3+}$) has attracted significant interest for multifunctional optical materials and devices. However, rational optimization and materials design have been hindered by controversial mechanisms. Here, we establish a unified analytical framework for deciphering such complex emissions across a diverse range of host systems. Our framework categorizes the possible origins into distinct classes— transition‐metal dimers or clusters, configuration‐associated isolated transition‐metal centers, and impurities. We demonstrate that the various anomalous luminescence phenomena observed in highly doped transition‐metal phosphors cannot be explained by exchange‐coupled dimers alone, but instead arise from a variety of configuration‐dependent effects that arise at high doping levels (e.g., unusual site occupancy, defect‐dopant complexes, or alternative valence states), or trace impurities. In particular, the intervalence charge transfer transition in transition‐metal dimers is expected to be predominantly non‐radiative due to the large structural relaxation energy involved. This study provides a generalizable framework for deciphering complex luminescence in highly doped systems, reconciling long‐standing controversies and offering a mechanistic foundation for interpreting broadband near‐infrared emissions in highly doped phosphors for multifunctional optical applications.

articles.title: Dirac Semimetallicity Enabled by Stripe Antiferromagnetism in Monolayer FeSe
articles.abstract: Monolayer FeSe is a central platform for iron‐based superconductivity, yet the electronic phases emerging from its competing magnetic orders remain elusive. Here we identify a Dirac semimetal state in monolayer FeSe induced by stripe antiferromagnetism, which hosts symmetry‐protected Dirac nodes near the Fermi level. We show that breaking a single mirror symmetry enables an odd inter‐orbital coupling between opposite‐parity Fe 3d$3d$ states, enforcing robust Dirac crossings with a nontrivial Wilson‐loop topology and boundary‐dependent edge modes. We further predict a strong orbital diamagnetic susceptibility as a direct experimental fingerprint of this Dirac phase. Our work establishes FeSe as a magnetically tunable route to topological quasiparticles in iron‐based two‐dimensional quantum materials.

articles.title: Endosomal Escape of siRNA Polyplexes: A Molecular Dynamics Perspective on Underlying Mechanisms
articles.abstract: To achieve a therapeutic effect, nanoparticles delivering nucleic acids must facilitate endosomal escape (EE) of their cargo. Despite extensive research, the mechanisms that lead to an effective EE are not sufficiently understood. Herein, we compare the EE behavior of four polymeric formulations (polyplexes) and one lipid nanoparticle (LNP) in vitro. Simultaneously, we utilized molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in all atom (AA) and coarse grained (CG) resolutions to differentiate the interaction of those formulations with endosomal membranes. The identified interaction patterns were discussed in perspective with the in vitro performance of the formulations: On the one hand, the results emphasize the benefit of hydrophobic residues in the nanoparticles. On the other hand, the role of anionic lipids in the biological membranes is demonstrated by MD. Different interaction modes of polyplex formulations with endosomal membranes are visualized in simulation with the aim to distinguish potential EE mechanisms from one another. This work highlights the power of MD simulations for taking a big step toward explaining differences observed in vitro on a molecular level and toward better understanding EE efficiency.

articles.title: Framework Excavation of UiO‐66 for In Situ Confined Cu3 Cluster Assembly Toward Nitrite Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Heterogenizing molecular catalysts requires the simultaneous preservation of structural precision, active‐site accessibility, and long‐term stability. To address the limited capacity of robust small‐pore frameworks for molecular clusters and the susceptibility of large‐pore hosts to guest leaching and structural degradation, we propose a “Framework Excavation” strategy. This strategy selectively creates local enlargements within the microporous framework to generate sufficient space for the in situ formation of metal clusters, while the retained narrow channels kinetically confine the as‐formed clusters and allow substrates to pass through the pores to fully access the highly exposed cluster sites. As a demonstration, chemically stable UiO‐66 was engineered with missing‐Zr6‐node defects and employed as a host for the ship‐in‐a‐bottle assembly of Cu3 molecular clusters, yielding Cu3@UiO‐66‐Exc. In electrocatalytic nitrite reduction, Cu3@UiO‐66‐Exc achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 98.7% and a yield rate of 19.21 mg cm−2 h−1, with stable performance over 300 h of cumulative electrolysis. Mechanistic studies, including DMPO‐H spin‐trapping, in situ infrared spectroscopy and theoretical computations, reveal that the confined Cu3 architecture promotes active‐hydrogen generation and successive hydrogenation of nitrogen‐containing intermediates. This work establishes a catalyst support design principle that enables the in situ generation, long‐term retention, and high site accessibility of molecular clusters within a robust microporous framework.

articles.title: Hydrocarbothermal Reduction Co‐Upcycling of Spent Lithium‐Ion Batteries via Waste Plastics for Enabling Efficient Water Purification and Lithium Resource Recovery
articles.abstract: The upcycling of spent lithium‐ion batteries and waste plastics is critical for resource security and sustainable development. However, current recycling paradigms treat these waste streams separately, leading to energy‐intensive battery recovery and low‐value plastic downcycling. Here, we present a waste polyethylene‐driven hydrocarbothermal reduction strategy for upcycling spent LiNi0.6Co0.2Mn0.2O2 (NCM622) cathodes by exploiting the dual functions of plastics as in situ carbon sources and reducing agents, making a breakthrough on their co‐processing and joint upcycling, and constructing a closed‐loop system integrating mixed‐waste upcycling, water purification, and lithium recycling. Hydrocarbothermal reduction via polyethylene pyrolysis induces pronounced interlayer expansion and octahedral distortion within NCM622, triggering structural collapse and driving the formation of a stable NiCoMn alloy nanorod deposited on a carbon nanosheet (NiCoMn/C) catalyst. Kinetic analysis shows that Co sites act as the primary catalytic centers, while Ni and Mn mediate charge transfer. NiCoMn/C enables efficient peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation for bisphenol A degradation with a rate constant of 0.411 min−1, demonstrating competitive catalytic performance among reported alloy–carbon catalysts. Meanwhile, this system achieves 87% lithium recovery, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and strong economic viability. This work establishes a generalizable paradigm for integrated waste‐to‐resource conversion and environmental remediation.

articles.title: Interfacial Band Homogenization and Controlled Nucleation Synergistically Enable Vertical Monolithic Perovskite Films for High‐Efficiency Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Buried‐interface inhomogeneity remains a key limitation in inverted perovskite solar cells, where aggregated Al2O3 nanoparticles can generate nonuniform interfacial potentials, local band inhomogeneity, charge accumulation, and nonradiative recombination losses. Here, we report a small‐molecule‐mediated Al2O3 nanoparticle strategy that integrates interfacial band homogenization, gradient‐permeation defect passivation, and crystallization regulation. 1,3‐diamino‐2‐propanol (1,3‐DAP) anchors onto Al2O3 nanoparticles, suppressing nanoparticle aggregation through surface electrostatic repulsion and homogenizing the buried interfacial potential distribution. Meanwhile, unanchored 1,3‐DAP molecules permeate from the buried interface into the shallow perovskite bulk, where they passivate defects and act as nucleation‐regulating sites. This dual regulation promotes vertically oriented grain growth along the (100) direction and forms vertically interconnected large‐grain perovskite films. Consequently, the modified devices achieve champion power conversion efficiencies of 26.00% under N2 fabrication and 25.09% under ambient‐air fabrication, together with reduced voltage loss and enhanced stability. The unencapsulated modified devices further retain 90% of their initial maximum power output after 700 h of maximum power point tracking under continuous one‐sun illumination in N2. Comparative molecular studies further show that effective crystallization regulation requires cooperative amino‐hydroxyl functionalities and appropriate precursor compatibility, highlighting the broader applicability of the nanoparticle‐interface molecular regulation strategy represented by 1,3‐DAP.

articles.title: Low Hydrogen Crossover Poly(Arylene Quinuclidinium) Anion Exchange Membranes for Renewables‐Compatible Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) represents a transformative approach to green hydrogen generation, combining the kinetic advantages of alkaline systems with zero‐gap configurations and platinum‐group‐metal‐free catalyst compatibility. Current implementations, however, face major challenges, including device durability, adaptability to fluctuating renewable energy sources, and safety concerns due to hydrogen crossover. In this work, we demonstrate that poly(arylene quinuclidinium) membranes address these challenges through an engineered polymer backbone featuring extended arene units, which effectively enhance dimensional integrity and inhibit gas crossover. Therefore, the hydrogen permeation suppression achieves a remarkably low H2‐in‐O2 crossover of only 0.53 vol% @0.1 A cm−2, and delivers a high current density of 8.5 A cm−2 @2.0 V with stable operation over 1250 h. The optimized PQTPQui‐15 membrane demonstrates practical potential in a kilowatt‐level, three‐cell electrolyzer stack. Furthermore, photovoltaic‐integrated systems maintain safe operation (H2‐in‐O2 < 0.13 vol%) across 0–190% load fluctuations, and respond to sub‐second power transients while sustaining current densities of 0.04−1.91 A cm−2. These advancements underscore the critical need to enhance the gas barrier properties of anion exchange membranes and establish a new paradigm for durable, rapidly responsive electrolyzers compatible with intermittent renewables.

articles.title: Microfluidic ER‐Targeted Photodynamic Vesicles Overcome Radioresistance and Boost Antitumor Immunity via Organelle Stress Amplification
articles.abstract: Radioresistance remains a significant obstacle in oncology, underpinned by adaptive cellular stress responses that attenuate radiation efficacy. We present microfluidically engineered, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)‐targeted photodynamic vesicles designed to surmount radioresistance through a spatiotemporally controlled, phototriggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) cascade. Upon 660 nm irradiation, these vesicles elicit an organelle‐confined oxidative burst, initiating a self‐amplifying cycle of calcium efflux and acute proteotoxic stress. This photodynamic priming achieves a superior sensitization enhancement ratio (SER = 1.35 ± 0.16) versus non‐targeted vesicles (SER = 1.01 ± 0.03), drastically reducing clonogenic survival to 1.3 ± 0.6% at 6.0 Gy X‐ray. Mechanistically, this synergy disrupts multiple resistance pathways by exacerbating genomic instability, depleting glutathione defenses, and inducing concurrent apoptosis and pyroptosis. Transcriptomic analysis reveals the regulation of radiosensitivity‐associated genes, confirming comprehensive reprogramming of cellular stress responses. Crucially, this cascade induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), elevating dendritic cell maturation to 39.5 ± 5.5% in tumor‐draining lymph nodes. Combined with localized radiotherapy, this approach profoundly amplifies systemic antitumor immunity, increasing intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and robustly suppressing distant metastasis. This work establishes organelle‐targeted ROS cascade amplification as a paradigm‐shifting radiosensitization strategy that extends beyond conventional DNA‐centric approaches, thereby unveiling novel therapeutic avenues for intractable malignancies.

articles.title: Phase‐Selective NiCo Oxide Electrodes Enable Paired Electrochemical Conversion and Valorization of Nitrogen‐Containing Wastewaters
articles.abstract: Conventional wastewater treatment generally focuses on pollutant removal while consuming energy and recovering little chemical value. Here, we report a phase‐selective Ni‐Co oxide platform for paired electrochemical conversion of nitrogen‐containing contaminants, coupling cathodic acetonitrile (AN) hydrogenation to ethylamine (EA) with anodic hydrazine oxidation to N2. Annealing NiCo layered double hydroxide precursor under Ar and in air produces cubic NiCoO2 and spinel NiCo2O4, respectively, which exhibit complementary catalytic preferences. NiCoO2 achieves 90.4%–91.2% Faradaic efficiency toward EA over 50–200 mA cm−2 in 8 wt.% AN, whereas NiCo2O4 approaches 100% Faradaic efficiency toward N2 over the same current‐density range. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that this catalytic complementarity arises from phase‐dependent reaction energetics: NiCoO2 favors H‐assisted AN hydrogenation while enabling facile EA release, whereas NiCo2O4 promotes hydrazine dehydrogenation and, critically, N2 desorption and active‐site regeneration. A 100 cm2 membrane‐electrode assembly maintains 88–93% EA Faradaic efficiency and stable paired operation for 120 h. The paired system was further demonstrated using separately collected industrial wastewaters, together with downstream EA recovery and a preliminary process‐level assessment. These results establish crystal‐phase regulation of reaction and product‐release energetics as a strategy for matching distinct electrode reactions within paired wastewater valorization.

articles.title: Polarity‐Reconfigurable In1.5Mn0.5Se3 Photodetectors Enabled by Asymmetric Schottky Barriers Toward Optical‐Electrical Logic Gates and Encryption Communication Application
articles.abstract: Ensuring information security at the device level is a critical demand in the era of ubiquitous sensing and communication. In this work, we design an asymmetric two‐terminal Schottky photodetector based on Mn‐doped In2Se3. The regulation mechanism of Mn doping on electronic structure, interfacial charge distribution, and carrier transport is systematically investigated, and high‐performance optoelectronic logic operations and optical information encryption, decryption are realized. First‐principles calculations reveal that Mn doping can effectively narrow the bandgap of In2Se3 from 1.0878 to 0.8986 eV and introduce donor impurity levels, significantly improving carrier concentration and optical absorption. Benefiting from the polarity‐tunable photoresponse enabled by asymmetric Schottky barriers, the device successfully implements multifunctional optoelectronic logic gates including XNOR, NAND, NOR etc. Furthermore, a complete optical information encryption and decryption system is constructed based on the XNOR logic, realizing secure encoding and accurate recovery of plaintext information. This work not only provides an effective strategy for doping modification and interface engineering of two‐dimensional semiconductors, but also offers new concepts and experimental support for high‐performance devices toward next‐generation optoelectronic computing and optical communication security.

articles.title: Ratiometric Copper Iodide Scintillators for Temperature‐Resolved X‐Ray Imaging
articles.abstract: Multifunctional X‐ray imaging that simultaneously resolves structural and thermal information is highly desirable under thermally dynamic and extreme conditions. Yet conventional systems require separate temperature sensors, which increases complexity and limits direct spatial correlation between the two. Here, we report a structurally engineered copper iodide (Cu–I) cluster scintillator that integrates high‐resolution x‐ray imaging with ratiometric thermometry in a single material. Regulating the Cu–I cluster and ligand coordination environment yields dual‐emissive Cu4I4(3F‐py)4, which exhibits two well‐resolved excited‐state emissions and a high light yield of 40 000 photons MeV−1. The two channels respond differently to temperature, producing a pronounced intensity‐ratio change and continuous radioluminescence color evolution from orange to blue as the temperature decreases from 300 to 100 K. Excited‐state analysis reveals that the electron‐withdrawing substituent stabilizes ligand‐centered frontier orbitals and lowers the barrier for interconversion from the cluster‐centered state to the metal/halide‐to‐ligand charge‐transfer state, enabling broad‐range thermochromism. The resulting scintillation screen achieves a spatial resolution exceeding 13 lp mm−1, while the Boltzmann‐type temperature dependence of the emission ratio allows quantitative thermal information to be encoded directly into the spectral ratio and color of x‐ray images. This work establishes excited‐state engineering of cluster scintillators as a strategy for temperature‐resolved x‐ray imaging.

articles.title: Stacking‐Tuned Phonon Renormalization and Effective Heat Transport in Moiré Semiconductor Superlattices
articles.abstract: Optically driven moiré semiconductor bilayers involve coupled phonon anharmonicity, interlayer interactions, and local heat dissipation, but experimental benchmarks across supported homo- and heterobilayers remain limited. Here, we combine temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy, excitation-power-dependent Raman thermometry, and photoluminescence to study twisted MoS2/MoS2, WS2/WS2, and MoS2/WS2 bilayers. From 90 to 300 K, both homobilayers show conventional softening of Raman-active phonons with negative effective anharmonic coefficients. In contrast, the WS2-derived out-of-plane A-mode in the MoS2/WS2 heterobilayer hardens with increasing temperature, exhibiting a positive linear temperature coefficient of +0.00700 ± 0.00029 cm− 1 K− 1 and a positive effective Balkanski coefficient of +1.28 ± 0.19 cm− 1, while other modes remain softening-dominant. Photoluminescence reveals an interlayer excitonic channel only in the heterobilayer, indicating an interface-specific phonon renormalization pathway beyond equilibrium anharmonic decay. Using two excitation objectives with distinct laser-heating radii, the supported Raman thermometry resolves mode-dependent effective thermal-transport parameters and reduces covariance in extracting in-plane heat-transport and heat-sinking coefficients. We further develop a physics-guided monolayer-to-stacked neural-network framework to reconstruct Raman spectra across temperature and power conditions and identify optimal optothermal regimes. These results establish heterointerface-controlled phonon renormalization as a key factor in phonon dynamics controlling heat dissipation and provide a scalable platform for thermal design in moiré quantum devices.

articles.title: Sustainable Cellulose Chiral Photonic Films Enable Simultaneous Ultralong Room‐temperature Phosphorescence and High Luminescence Dissymmetry With Multicolor Tunability
articles.abstract: Simultaneously achieving high luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum ) and ultralong lifetimes in circularly polarized room-temperature phosphorescence (CP–RTP) materials remains a fundamental challenge, as it requires reconciling well-defined chiral ordering, efficient triplet-state stabilization, and matched energy-level alignment within a single material system. Here, we report a versatile bio-based strategy to overcome this trade-off by incorporating phosphorescent chromophores and polymer matrices into chiral cellulose nanocrystal films via one-step co-assembly. The resulting bio-based materials exhibit an ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence lifetime of up to 4.242 s. Through targeted optical path engineering using a chiral photonic crystal filter, these long-lived films achieve a large glum value of −0.7093, without compromising phosphorescence performance. To expand the emission scope, guest fluorophore doping enables broad spectral tuning of the chiral emission via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), yielding multicolor CP–RTP and controllable white-light emission. Benefiting from their switchable, multimodal optical properties, these films show strong potential for advanced dynamic optical anti-counterfeiting. This work addresses the core trade-off between ultralong lifetime and high glum in CP–RTP systems, and establishes a sustainable, general platform for the design of next-generation chiral luminescent materials.

articles.title: A Fully Integrated Wearable Sensor for Real Time Monitoring of Multiple Sweat Liver Disease Biomarkers
articles.abstract: Early diagnosis and personalized management of chronic liver disease are critical for preventing disease progression and reducing mortality. However, existing diagnostic methods primarily depend on invasive blood sampling and laboratory‐based analyses, which limit their suitability for continuous, real‐world monitoring. In this study, we developed a skin‐conformal, wearable electrochemical biosensing platform capable of real time monitoring of liver health by continuously analyzing liver‐related metabolic biomarkers (creatine and lactate) in sweat. To improve sensor reliability, we introduced a universal enzyme immobilization strategy based on covalent organic frameworks, which enhances enzymatic stability and maintains catlytic activity under dynamic conditions. The fully integrated system supports efficient passive sweat collection, real time multi‐analyte detection, on‐board signal processing, and digital display. The platform was applied in preliminary human studies to track dynamic changes in sweat creatine and lactate in healthy individuals and participants with chronic liver disease. Overall, this work demonstrates a versatile wearable platform for noninvasive, continuous assisted evaluation of liver metabolic functions, contributing to the advancement of next‐generation personalized healthcare technologies.

articles.title: A Mucosa‐Inspired Dynamic Biointerface Engineering a Biofilm‐Preventive Niche Against Pathogenic Microbiome Dysbiosis
articles.abstract: A stable symbiosis within the microbiome‐host axis is essential for human health. However, preventing microbiome dysbiosis using biomaterials remains challenging due to their unpredictable influence on microbiome evolution. Inspired by the defensive niche of symbiotic mucosa, we have developed a biointerface that forms an engineered mucosa‐inspired dynamic niche to prevent pathogenic dysbiosis. This biointerface features a dynamic zwitterionic network that emulates the mucosa's biophysical defensive functions. Notably, by leveraging its dynamic niche, the biointerface restricts microbial attachment and aggregation, thereby preventing biofilm formation. Comprehensive metagenomic analyses reveal that microbial communities adapt to this biofilm‐preventive dynamic biointerface compositionally and functionally. In particular, Gram‐negative bacteria were relatively reduced, along with decreased abundance of pathways associated with virulence and biofilm formation. Consequently, the mucosa‐inspired biointerface intrinsically prevents the development of pathogenic dysbiosis. This study demonstrates the groundbreaking potential of material‐based niche engineering to guide the ecological shifts of microbial communities from the material scale.

articles.title: A Synergistic Triphase Electrolyte Design Enables 4.6 V LiCoO2 Quasi‐Solid‐State Batteries with Ultra‐Long Cycling
articles.abstract: Pushing LiCoO2 to ≥4.5 V causes coupled degradation: electrolyte oxidation and cathode structural collapse, especially at high rates. Here, we propose a triphase synergistic gel‐electrolyte to tackle both failure modes. The system, constructed by in situ thermal polymerization, integrates an ether‐rich crosslinked polymer network, surface‐activated AlN fillers with Lewis acid–base sites, and a fluorinated electrolyte. This design regulates Li+ transport, confines free solvent molecules, and reconstructs the solvation sheath. More importantly, it induces a uniform, inorganic‐rich cathode–electrolyte interphase at an early stage. Consequently, LiCoO2‐based quasi‐solid‐state cells deliver exceptional stability: over 1000 cycles at 4.6 V and 5 C with an average decay of only ∼0.03% per cycle, and 85.98% capacity retention after 500 cycles in practical Si–C||LiCoO2 pouch cells.
