articles.title: Impact of anemia on length of hospital stay among patients hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo
articles.abstract: Background: Severe malaria remains a major cause of hospitalization in malaria-endemic sub-Saharan Africa, and anemia is among its most frequent severity criteria. Data on the impact of anemia on hospital length of stay (LOS) among adults with severe malaria remain limited in Central Africa. We assessed the impact of anemia on LOS among adults hospitalized for severe malaria in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional, descriptive, and analytic study of medical records from adult patients ([≥]18 years) diagnosed with severe malaria (WHO criteria) and admitted to four hospitals in Brazzaville between January 2020 and December 2024. We dichotomized LOS as short (<5 days) or prolonged ([≥]5 days). Multivariable logistic regression, using a backward stepwise procedure, identified factors independently associated with prolonged LOS; isolated hemoglobinuria served as the reference severity category. Results: Among 523 patients hospitalized for severe malaria, 296 met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 25.5 years (IQR 20-40); 51.7% were female, and 82.1% had a low socioeconomic status. Median hemoglobin was 10.55 g/dL, and median LOS was 4 days (IQR 3-5). In multivariable analysis, prolonged LOS was independently associated with delay to consultation (aOR 1.25/day, 95% CI 1.09-1.44), isolated anemia (aOR 7.07, 1.23-40.55), convulsions (aOR 5.86, 1.81-18.97), prostration (aOR 4.42, 1.21-16.2), and impaired consciousness (aOR 4.29, 1.17-15.7). The strongest associations involved combined severity criteria: anemia with prostration (aOR 8.58), anemia with jaundice or hemoglobinuria (aOR 16.21), and impaired consciousness with anemia (aOR 33.31). Conclusions: Anemia is a major, potentially modifiable determinant of prolonged hospitalization in adults with severe malaria, with a markedly amplified effect when combined with neurologic impairment. Early anemia screening, improved access to safe blood transfusion, and reduced delays to care could shorten hospital stays and ease the burden on health systems in this setting.

articles.title: LUCID: Lipid-featured Urine Cytology with Intelligent Detection for Non-Invasive Early Diagnosis of Bladder Cancer
articles.abstract: Leveraging its non-invasive and convenient nature, urinary cytology offers a way for the early diagnosis and surveillance of bladder cancer (BCa). However, its sensitivity remains substantially inferior to the histopathological gold standard, rendering it inadequate to support precise clinical diagnosis. Here, we developed Lipid-featured Urine Cytology with Intelligent Detection (LUCID), an automated platform integrating single-cell stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) imaging and explainable AI model for accurate BCa detection. Following a newly developed standardized urine-preprocessing protocol, 19,678 urinary exfoliated cells from 26 BCa patients and 54 non-BCa participants were imaged using two-color SRS microscopy to simultaneously visualize lipid and protein distributions. For cell-level analysis, a customized deep-supervised Cellpose segmentation algorithm and a YOLO-based detection model were developed to enable precise single-cell segmentation and intracellular lipid droplet (LD) identification, respectively. Totally 20 quantitative morphological and compositional features per cell were extracted and 10 related principal components were obtained via principal component analysis. These features were subsequently integrated into a multiple-instance learning (MIL)-XGBoosting model, which achieved robust diagnostic performance, with 92.31% sensitivity, 87.04% specificity, and an AUC of 0.940. We found that morphological and compositional features provided complementary diagnostic information, while LD-associated features provided primary discriminative information, supporting intracellular LD phenotypes as potential urinary cellular markers of BCa. More importantly, LUCID demonstrated exceptional accuracy in detecting early-stage and small tumors, and showed higher concordance than FISH in a preliminary paired subset (5/6 vs. 2/6). Together, LUCID establishes a chemical imaging-AI paradigm that transforms molecular urine cytology.

articles.title: Mapping county-level tick-borne disease risk in Illinois by integrating vector abundance, pathogen prevalence, and phenology
articles.abstract: Tick-borne disease risk reflects the combined influence of vector abundance, pathogen prevalence, human exposure, and seasonal activity, yet these components are rarely integrated at the county level. We developed species-specific ecological risk scores for three medically important tick species (Acari: Ixodidae): Amblyomma americanum (L.), Dermacentor variabilis (Say), and Ixodes scapularis Say, across all 102 Illinois counties using data from 2019 to 2022. County-level predicted tick abundance and pathogen prevalence were scaled and combined using equal weights to generate primary vector-level risk scores. Robustness to the equal-weight assumption was evaluated by systematically varying the relative weights assigned to abundance and pathogen prevalence, while a separate sensitivity analysis incorporated reported tick-bite incidence where available. Associations with human disease were evaluated using negative binomial regression of tick-borne disease case counts on the corresponding risk scores, with county population included as an offset. Monthly phenology indicators were constructed by integrating human disease cases, reported tick bites, and sampled tick abundance and were evaluated in relation to temperature and precipitation. Seasonal risk was estimated by combining county-level vector risk with species-specific monthly phenology, generating monthly risk surfaces that were deployed through an interactive R Shiny application. Higher risk scores were significantly associated with greater disease case rates for each tick species. County rankings were highly stable under moderate changes in abundance and prevalence weighting. Seasonal activity differed among species, with A. americanum and D. variabilis showing concentrated warm-season risk and I. scapularis exhibiting a broader seasonal profile. These county-level seasonal risk maps identify where and when relative tick-borne disease risk is elevated in Illinois, supporting targeted prevention, surveillance, and clinical awareness.

articles.title: Maternal body mass index in early pregnancy and offspring risk of multiple sclerosis: A population-based cohort study
articles.abstract: Objective To examine whether prospectively recorded maternal BMI in early pregnancy is associated with offspring multiple sclerosis (MS) risk, including childhood-onset and adult-onset MS. Design Nationwide population-based cohort study. Setting Swedish national health and demographic registers. Participants 1,524,863 singleton children born in Sweden from 1992 to 2007 and followed through 2025. Exposures Maternal BMI recorded at the first antenatal visit, categorised as underweight (<18.5), normal weight (18.5-24.9), overweight (25.0-29.9), and obesity ([≥]30.0), and also modelled continuously. Main outcome measures MS in offspring, identified as at least three ICD-10 G35 codes recorded on separate dates. Cox models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) adjusting for confounders. Results During follow-up, 1539 offspring (0.1%) were diagnosed with MS at a median age of 24 years (interquartile range, 20-27 years). MS incidence rates by maternal BMI category were 0.37 per 10,000 person-years for both underweight, and normal weight, 0.42 for overweight, and 0.45 for obesity. Compared with normal weight women, maternal overweight and obesity were associated with higher hazards of offspring MS, with adjusted HRs of 1.20 (95% CI, 1.05 to 1.37) and 1.35 (95% CI, 1.11 to 1.64), respectively. Onset-specific analyses showed similar findings for adult-onset MS and less precise but directionally consistent estimates for paediatric-onset MS. Each 1-unit increase in maternal BMI was associated with a 3%, 4%, and 3% higher hazard of overall, paediatric-onset, and adult-onset offspring MS, respectively. Conclusions In this population-based cohort study, higher maternal BMI were associated with an increased rate of MS in offspring. The findings provide large-scale prospective evidence that maternal adiposity may be related to offspring MS risk and support further investigation of the prenatal metabolic environment in the early-life origins of MS.

articles.title: Mechanisms of action of a community-led HIV prevention and treatment programme for female sex workers in Zimbabwe: a mixed-method analysis
articles.abstract: Background Community-led interventions for female sex workers (FSW) can improve HIV prevention and treatment outcomes by lowering self-stigma and strengthening social cohesion to improve service uptake. In Zimbabwe, the AMETHIST intervention trial integrated peer-led microplanning with self-help groups for FSW and demonstrated improved HIV treatment outcomes. We investigated the role of social cohesion and self-stigma in explaining these findings. Method We conducted a mixed-method analysis of data collected during AMETHIST. We re-analysed qualitative data from interviews and group discussions to identify narratives linking self-stigma, engagement with microplanners and/or self-help groups and HIV service use. We analysed quantitative data from endline respondent-driven sampling surveys for differences in self-reported measures of social cohesion and self-stigma between trial arms, and between those who did and did not participate in intervention activities or access services. Results In both arms, FSW self-reported engaging with peer supporters, participating in self-help groups and accessing HIV services. Qualitative narratives suggested peer support and group participation could reduce self-stigma and support service uptake. Lower levels of self-stigma were seen in the intervention arm (58.6% vs 63.2%; aOR 0.77; 95% CI 0.61-0.86). Social cohesion exceeded 50% across the whole sample, but was not associated with study arm, nor with engagement in intervention-related activities. Discussion Although qualitative data suggested some FSW felt their uptake of services was influenced by intervention components, quantitative analyses did not suggest either variable was on the causal pathway to the outcomes of the intervention. A limitation may have been the measurement of these complex constructs and the high levels of social cohesion across both study arms.

articles.title: Microbiological characteristics of ventilator-associated pneumonia in patients with neurological injuries: a multicentric cohort
articles.abstract: Incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is increased in patients admitted for brain injury. Staphylococcus aureus appears to be a particularly common pathogen in these respiratory infections. Our aim was to confirm the extent of S. aureus involvement in VAP among patients with neurological injuries. We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including patients with and without neurological injuries who developed VAP during their ICU stay. Among 15 702 patients admitted in the participant centers during the study period. 407 were finally included in the study. S. aureus was involved in 122 (61.6%) VAP in brain-injured patients and 63 (30.1%) of non-brain-injured patients. In brain-injured patients, multivariate analysis identified age (0.97 [0.95; 0.98]), antibioprophylaxis (0.31 [0.18; 0.53]; p < 0.0001), subarachnoid hemorrhage (2.18 [1.01; 4.68]; p=0.0461), lower Glasgow coma score (0.92 [0.87; 0.97]; p= 0.004) and SAPS II (0.98 [0.97; 1]; p=0.0174) as critical factors associated with the risk of S. aureus in VAP. In the non-brain-injured population, multivariate analysis identified antibioprophylaxis (0.38 [0.22; 0.65]; p=0.0006), age (0.96 [0.95; 0.98]; p<0.0001), SAPS II (0.98 [0.97; 1]; p=0.0265), thoracic surgery (0.21 [0.09; 0.48]; p=0.0002) and peripheral neurosurgery (1.95 [1.2; 3.19]; p=0.0076) as critical factors. A total of 172 patients (42.3%) died during their ICU stay and 90-days mortality was 194 (47.7%). No difference of mortality was noticed function of VAP-associated pathogen.

articles.title: Microstructural phenotyping and clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis lesions using quantitative susceptibility source separation
articles.abstract: Background: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) exhibits phase cancellation between paramagnetic (e.g. iron) and diamagnetic (e.g. myelin/protein) sources, obscuring microstructural lesion heterogeneity in multiple sclerosis (MS). We evaluated whether biophysical {chi}-separation identifies clinically meaningful lesion phenotypes and whether reduced echo sampling preserves microstructural sensitivity. Methods: In this cross-sectional study of 183 people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), we analyzed 3327 quality-controlled white matter lesions using 3T MRI with a five-echo gradient-recalled echo sequence (GRE5) and a subsampled two-echo dataset (GRE2). A hybrid framework combining unsupervised clustering on whole-lesion paramagnetic ({chi}para) and diamagnetic ({chi}dia) features with rule-based compartmental edge-core gradient assignment resolved MS lesion phenotypes. Intralesional microstructural properties were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. Multivariable linear regressions assessed associations with physical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS; n = 158), cognitive processing speed (Symbol Digit Modalities Test, SDMT; n = 79), and disease duration (DD; n = 161), with sensitivity models adjusting for total lesion volume, count, or DD. Results: The framework identified four reproducible lesion phenotypes (Adjusted Rand Index = 0.924): Type 1 (22.7%; preserved {chi}dia), Type 2 (32.9%; high {chi}para without positive edge-core gradient), Type 3 (35.8%; attenuated {chi}dia), and Type 4 (8.6%; high {chi}para with a positive edge-core paramagnetic gradient). Higher EDSS was selectively associated with more negative signed {chi}dia within Type 4 lesions (whole: {beta} = -0.37, q = 0.020; core: {beta} = -0.37, q = 0.006; edge: {beta} = -0.34, q = 0.030) and Type 2 edge ({beta} = -0.33, q = 0.044). Type 4 core associations remained robust across sensitivity models adjusting for total lesion volume ({beta} = -0.35, q = 0.004), total lesion count ({beta} = -0.37, q = 0.008), and DD ({beta} = -0.32, q = 0.033). Abbreviated GRE2 attenuated Type 4 compartmental associations to non-significance (all q greater than 0.05; core: {beta} = -0.20, q = 0.215). Conclusions: Quantitative {chi}-separation identified four internally stable susceptibility-defined MS lesion phenotypes, revealing disability-associated tissue heterogeneity beyond total lesion burden. Higher EDSS was associated with more negative diamagnetic measures within Type 4 cores after adjustment for lesion burden, pointing toward complex intralesional non-myelin tissue remodeling or reactive astrogliosis. Two-echo subsampling may influence compartment-specific clinical associations. By uncoupling susceptibility sources, {chi}-separation provides a quantitative framework for characterizing disability-associated lesion heterogeneity.

articles.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Cause-of-Death Assignment From Verbal Autopsy Records: A National Benchmark Study in South Africa
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Timely cause-of-death (COD) information guides health policy, yet many deaths in low- and middle-income countries are not medically certified. In Africa, fewer than 10% of deaths are. Verbal autopsy (VA) yields a structured symptom questionnaire and a free-text narrative. Mortality surveillance increasingly records the narrative alongside the questionnaire, but the algorithms used to produce VA-based statistics were designed for structured responses only, so narratives inform physician COD assignment but do not contribute to algorithmic COD assignment. We evaluated whether supervised models could use both modalities to improve COD assignment. METHODS We analyzed 4,999 VA records for deaths at ages 12 years or older from a national sample of registered deaths in South Africa (RSA), using physician-assigned CODs as the reference standard. We trained unimodal and multimodal pipelines on the labelled records: pretrained language models (PLMs) fine-tuned on narratives alone, machine learning (ML) models on structured responses alone, and the two combined at the data, feature, and decision levels. We also prompted a locally deployed generative large language model (LLM) on the same unimodal and multimodal inputs, without parameter updates. All were compared with InSilicoVA, the operational comparator representing current automated practice. We evaluated individual-level assignment, population-level agreement, calibration, and generalization across provinces in RSA, reporting these metrics rather than ranking pipelines on any one of them. RESULTS Every supervised pipeline improved on InSilicoVA by 8.5-15.9 percentage points in top-1 accuracy and 3.5-7.1 points in cause-specific mortality fraction (CSMF) accuracy. The narrative and structured pipelines performed similarly in aggregate but differed by cause: 63.9% of deaths received identical predictions, 11.6% were correct only from the narrative pipeline, and 13.6% only from the questionnaire pipeline, with the narrative pipeline more accurate for noncommunicable causes and the questionnaire pipeline for communicable causes. Against the unimodal approaches, the decision-fusion pipelines added 4.2-5.4 percentage points in top-1 accuracy, concentrated in the most common causes, whereas feature fusion with cross-modal attention improved the less common causes, adding 6.6 points (95% CI, 1.7-11.5) in balanced accuracy and 5.5 points (95% CI, 0.6-10.3) in macro F1. Feature fusion reached the highest CSMF accuracy (95.7%). Paired differences from the better unimodal representative ranged from -0.2 to +3.4 points, with all intervals including zero. The LLM exceeded InSilicoVA on individual-level metrics and reached the highest balanced accuracy of any pipeline (60.6%), while the supervised pipelines retained higher CSMF accuracy. Supervised pipelines had lower expected calibration error than InSilicoVA. Supervised gains held across all nine held-out provinces, including every top-1 comparison and nearly every macro F1 and CSMF comparison. CONCLUSIONS PLMs using narratives alone substantially improved on current best practice and matched ML pipelines using structured responses, while multiple multimodal strategies produced further gains in individual COD assignment. The zero-shot LLM showed particular strength on rare causes, whereas supervised pipelines better recovered the population cause distribution. These findings support incorporating narratives as a core input to automated VA systems and evaluating representative fusion strategies for the intended output. External validation across settings and age groups will support broader implementation.

articles.title: Municipality-level ecological analysis of COVID-19 mortality and infections in Austria, 2020 to 2023
articles.abstract: Background: Previous studies indicated that regional fluctuations in COVID-19 impact were associated with socioeconomic, demographic and environmental factors early in the pandemic. It is unclear whether factors associated with regional COVID-19 mortality and SARS-CoV-2 infections changed over the course of the pandemic. Methods: We evaluated the association of ecological factors with municipality-specific COVID-19 mortality in the national population of Austria between January 2020 and June 2023. Analyses were conducted separately per calendar year and pooled across years via random-effects meta-analysis. Outcomes were analysed using univariable and multivariable zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, including annually averaged environmental exposome exposure (including air pollution and UV radiation), socioeconomic, demographic and infection dissemination predictors with significance threshold set to p<0.005. Secondary analysis modelled SARS-CoV-2 infections using of negative-binomial model (NB). Two additional approaches for smaller predictor set selection were applied as sensitivity analyses. Results: Within the entire observation period 18,430 COVID-19 deaths were reported. In univariable analyses (pooled RR (99.5% CI)), COVID-19 mortality was significantly associated with the proportion of commuters (0.79 (0.73-0.86)), residents aged 75-84 (1.18 (1.01-1.37)) and [≥]85 years (1.29 (1.04-1.60)), residents with at most compulsory education (1.15 (1.02-1.29)), employed residents aged 15-64 (0.89 (0.85-0.93)), and homeowners (0.91 (0.83-0.99)), as well as with precipitation (0.94 (0.89-0.99)) and the average time with a mean temperature of 5-15 C (0.95 (0.90-0.99)). In multivariable analyses the share of population aged 85 or older (1.30 (1.09-1.54)) and home ownership (0.92 (0.87-0.98)) were independently significant. Mortality predictor estimates were relatively stable across pandemic years. Across 5,963,882 documented SARS-CoV-2 infections share of employed in 15- to 64-year-olds (1.01 (1.01-1.02)), part-time employment rate (1.01 (1.00-1.02)) and district level nursing care allowance recipiency (0.97 (0.95-0.98)) were associated with detected infections. Overnight stays, population 85 or older, income, compulsory education or less and air pollution all had multiple significant estimates with opposite directionality, leading to non-significant overall associations. Sensitivity analyses outcomes mirrored main analyses outcomes. Conclusions: Throughout the pandemic in Austria, demographic and socioeconomic factors were associated with COVID-19 mortality and infections, but many associations, especially for infections, were unstable over time. These findings underscore the importance of structural vulnerabilities in epidemic impact.

articles.title: National incidence of coccidioidomycosis in the United States estimated through machine learning integration of epidemiological, veterinary, and socioecological data
articles.abstract: Importance : Coccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley fever, is a serious fungal disease caused by inhaling Coccidioides spores aerosolized from the soil. Despite rising public health concern, the distribution and incidence of coccidioidomycosis in the US remain poorly characterized as not all states are required to report cases, and case under-ascertainment is presumed to be high, particularly outside of the endemic region. Objective : To estimate monthly, county-level coccidioidomycosis incidence across the US while accounting for widespread under-ascertainment. Design, Setting, and Participants : We integrated multisource data, including human cases diagnosed in electronic health records, serological testing of dogs, and ecological and sociodemographic predictors, in a machine learning model estimating monthly, county-level coccidioidomycosis incidence. The model was trained on surveillance data from Arizona and California from 2013 to 2023, then applied to predict incidence in states across the contiguous US over the same time period. Main Outcomes and Measures : Incidence of coccidioidomycosis at the monthly county level. Results : The model predicted coccidioidomycosis incidence from 2013 to 2023 for 3,108 counties from all states in the contiguous US. The model identified 60 counties in non-reporting states where predicted incidence was ≥2 cases per 100,000 population (considered moderate to high incidence). In states with mandatory reporting outside of Arizona and California, the model predicted county-level incidence rates that were 28% higher (95% bootstrap interval, 0.1%–69.8%) than those captured in national surveillance, equating to a total of 608 potentially missed cases per year (95% bootstrap interval, 340–964). Conclusions and Relevance : In this cross-sectional study, the model quantified case under-ascertainment for coccidioidomycosis relative to Arizona and California, and highlighted the potential for alternative data sources to fill in gaps in mandatory reporting. Estimating incidence while accounting for under-ascertainment and non-reporting may help efforts to improve public and physician awareness and to detect emergence in new regions.

articles.title: Physical Frailty Accelerates Multimorbidity Accumulation Across Distinct Disease Patterns
articles.abstract: Background Emerging evidence has linked frailty to individual chronic diseases, but whether it predicts a broad disease spectrum and accelerates multimorbidity accumulation over time remains unknown. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the associations of physical frailty with the burden of incident disease across a wide range of chronic conditions, and with the long-term rates of multimorbidity accumulation. Methods In this prospective cohort study of 466,864 UK Biobank participants , frailty status was assessed using the Fried frailty phenotype and categorized as robust, pre-frailty, or frailty. Chronic diseases were defined based on International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes, and disease patterns were identified using network analysis. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations of frailty status with incident chronic diseases, and linear mixed models were used to assess the annual rate of chronic disease accumulation. Results During a median follow-up of 13.8 years (IQR: 13.1-14.5), 536 incident chronic diseases across multiple systems were recorded. Physical frailty was associated with a significantly increased risk of 458 incident diseases (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.05/536). In the overall cohort, compared with robust participants, those with pre-frailty ({beta} = 0.266, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.264-0.267) and frailty ({beta} = 0.941, 95% CI: 0.936-0.946) exhibited significantly faster rates of multimorbidity accumulation. This accelerated multimorbidity accumulation was consistently observed across strata of baseline disease burden, including participant with 0 ({beta} = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.635-0.653), 1 ({beta} =0.748, 95% CI: 0.727-0.768), [≥] 2 ({beta} =0.940, 95% CI: 0.933-0.947) chronic conditions at baseline. Similar associations were also found across distinct disease patterns, including neurodegenerative, metabolic, and psychiatric patterns. Conclusions Physical frailty predicts a broad range of incident diseases and is associated with accelerated multimorbidity accumulation. Incorporating frailty assessment into prevention strategies may help mitigate the growing burden of multimorbidity.

articles.title: Pickleball injuries, search interest, and participation in the United States, 2014-2023: an ecological time series study
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe (1) US emergency department-treated pickleball injury burden and the injury-to-participation measure among total players, with burden among adults aged 60 to 79 years as a descriptive subgroup, and (2) determine whether general internet search interest for 'pickleball' is also associated with total pickleball-related injuries. DESIGN: Ecological time series study, United States, 2014 to 2023. DATA SOURCES: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) emergency department microdata yielded 1,738 adjudicated pickleball cases, 921 of them orthopedic, weighted to an estimated 101,450 injuries nationally. Google Trends, English Wikipedia pageviews, and GDELT news volume served as general pickleball attention signals, with the Trends index for 'sourdough' as a negative control. Sports and Fitness Industry Association (SFIA) participation estimates supplied a total player denominator. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Annual national injury estimates with design-based 95 percent confidence intervals; injury-to-participation measures; and correlations between total pickleball-related injuries and general pickleball attention signals before and after removing trend and seasonality. RESULTS: Estimated emergency department-treated pickleball injuries rose 17.5-fold, from 1,391 in 2014 (highly unstable) to 24,294 in 2023. 70 percent of adjudicated cases involved adults aged 60 to 79. During 2017-2023, injury estimates rose 4.0-fold and participation rose about 4.4-fold. No temporal trend was detected in the injury-to-participation measure (P=0.59). Search interest looked like an excellent proxy: in annual levels it correlated with total pickleball-related injuries at R=0.96, and Pickleball Wikipedia pageviews at R=0.98. However, so did searches for "sourdough", at R=0.76. Removing trend and seasonality left little (monthly residual R=0.084; year-on-year R=0.28 over 96 months, 2015-2023), and the seasons ran opposite, with injuries peaking in February and searches in July, such that, on 12-month mean profiles, the sourdough negative control fitted the injury season (R=0.96) while pickleball ran against it (R=-0.40). General pickleball search interest and pickleball news coverage remained correlated in year-on-year changes in 2017-2023 (R=0.64), whereas their corresponding correlations with total pickleball-related injuries in 2017-2023 were 0.25 and 0.20. CONCLUSIONS: The absolute burden of emergency department-treated pickleball injury has grown substantially, but the available surveillance data cannot resolve whether the sport has become more hazardous per participant. The observed rise is consistent with growth in exposure alone. The strong correlation between search interest and injury counts was not specific, the association was substantially attenuated after detrending, and the seasonal patterns were opposed. These descriptive results do not establish that search interest can substitute for injury surveillance, and series that rise together should not be assumed to be related.

articles.title: Pre-Deployment Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Outcomes among United States Antarctic Program Participants: Insights from Contemporary Risk Models
articles.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular (CV) screening is critical for personnel deploying to Antarctica, where geographic isolation and limited medical care make the management of acute cardiovascular events challenging. The utility of contemporary risk prediction tools such as the AHA PREVENT equations in this unique population remains uncertain. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 154 individuals referred for enhanced CV evaluation before deployment to the U.S. Antarctic Program (USAP). Participants were evaluated across three temporal cohorts (2018-2020, 2021-2023, and 2024-2026). Demographics, CV risk factors, cardiac testing, and deployment clearance outcomes were collected. Risk was estimated using the Framingham Risk Score (FRS), AHA/ACC Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE), and AHA PREVENT risk models. Results: The cohort was predominantly male (79.9%; mean age 44.6 {+/-} 14.6 years), and abnormal ECG was the most common referral trigger (70.8%). Median 10-year risk was low by PREVENT and FRS and borderline elevated by PCE (PREVENT 2.7% [IQR 1.1-6.6], FRS 2.3% [IQR 0.5-7.1], and PCE 6.1% [IQR 2.4-9.2]). Among 72 participants with all scores, 51% were classified discordantly; PREVENT ASCVD agreed closely with FRS (=0.77) but poorly with PCE (=0.24-0.35), which consistently estimated higher risk. PCE was calculable in 52.6% versus 70.8% for PREVENT. Overall, 132 participants (85.7%) were cleared for deployment, while 8 (5.2%) were not physically qualified (NPQ); 6 of these NPQs were due to cardiovascular causes. Of 22 cardiac medical evacuations during the study period, 21 involved individuals without prior advanced cardiovascular screening. One screened individual was evacuated for symptoms subsequently found to have no cardiac cause. Conclusions: Risk calculators disagree substantially in the fitness-selected population. We recommend PREVENT as the primary risk-stratification tool as it is the most contemporary derivation, incorporates renal function, is race-agnostic, extends to heart failure, applies from age 30, and agrees closely with FRS, easing transition. Targeted imaging, including coronary artery calcium scoring, may supplement intermediate-risk candidates.

articles.title: Professional Identity and Its Influencing Factors Among Nursing Interns: The Mediating Role of Career Adaptability Between Social Support and Professional Identity
articles.abstract: Purpose: The internship period is a critical stage for nursing students to develop professional values. This study aimed to investigate the current status of professional identity among nursing interns, analyze the effects of social support, perceived stress, psychological resilience, and career adaptability on professional identity, and explore the mediating role of career adaptability between social support and professional identity, so as to provide empirical evidence for enhancing professional identity and optimizing nursing talent training systems. Methods: Using convenience sampling, 407 nursing interns from a tertiary hospital in Quanzhou were selected as participants from May to July 2025. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Social Support Scale, the Perceived Stress Scale, the Psychological Resilience Scale, the Professional Identity Questionnaire for Nursing Students, the Career Adaptability Scale, and the Questionnaire for Nurse Intention to Retention Employed. SPSS 26.0 was used for reliability analysis, descriptive analysis, independent samples t-test, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression analysis. The PROCESS macro was employed to test the mediating effect. Results: The total score of professional identity among nursing interns was (61.74{+/-}11.08), with 73.5% showing moderate professional identity. Parents' attitude toward nursing, reasons for choosing the profession, personal attitude toward the major, and employment intention showed statistically significant differences in professional identity scores (p<0.05). Pearson correlation analysis revealed that professional identity was significantly positively correlated with social support (r=0.474), psychological resilience (r=0.389), and career adaptability (r=0.609) (p<0.01), and significantly negatively correlated with perceived stress (r=-0.378) (p<0.01). Multiple linear regression analysis indicated that career adaptability ({beta}=0.309, p<0.001) and social support ({beta}=0.383, p<0.001) were significant positive predictors of professional identity, whereas reasons for choosing the profession ({beta}=-3.603, p=0.001) and employment intention ({beta}=-7.116, p<0.001) were significant negative predictors. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in professional identity. Mediation effect analysis showed that career adaptability played a partial mediating role between social support and professional identity, with a mediation effect value of 0.288 (95% CI: 0.221-0.363), accounting for 40.2% of the total effect. Conclusions: Nursing interns' professional identity is at a moderately high level. Social support and career adaptability are positive influencing factors. Career adaptability plays a partial mediating role between social support and professional identity; social support indirectly enhances professional identity by strengthening career adaptability.

articles.title: Prognosis after a new episode of musculoskeletal pain in children and young people, 2005-21: population-based study
articles.abstract: Objective: to estimate reconsultation risk and trajectories after a new episode of musculoskeletal pain in children and young people (CYP), and to determine routinely recorded prognostic factors associated with reconsultation. Design: Population based retrospective cohort study. Setting: Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum, 2005-2021. Participants: CYP aged 8-18 years consulting primary care for a new musculoskeletal pain episode (no musculoskeletal consultation in prior 12-months). Main Outcome Measures: Musculoskeletal pain reconsultation within 12-months, and 3-year musculoskeletal reconsultation trajectories derived using latent class growth analysis. Prognostic factors selected from a literature search and two-year symptom histories (sample prevalence >1%) were examined using regression models (conditional logistic; multinomial). Results: Among 313,830 CYP with >12 months' follow-up, 32% reconsulted for musculoskeletal pain within 12 months. Among 240,384 CYP with >3 years' follow-up, three trajectories were observed: single episode (62%), early reconsultation (18%), and persistent reconsultation (20%). Older age; female gender; hip, knee, multisite and back pain on index; previous headache; previous abdominal pain; and analgesic prescribing were associated with higher reconsultation risk. Asian or Black ethnicity, and residing in more deprived areas, were associated with lower recorded reconsultation. Conclusion: Most CYP had no further recorded consultation, but 38% followed early or persistent reconsultation trajectories. Routinely recorded prognostic factors, particularly index pain side and prior pain/symptom history, may differentiate groups who could benefit from proactive follow-up. Lower recorded reconsultation among Asian and Black individuals, and living in more deprived areas, should not imply lower need and warrants equity-sensitive monitoring of access, health-seeking, and coding.

articles.title: Reconstructing Dengue Exposure Dynamics and Assessing the Public Health Impact of Vaccination Scenarios Using Mathematical Models in Brazil
articles.abstract: Brazil experienced its worst dengue epidemic in 2024, with an increase in severe outcomes among elderly individuals, highlighting the need for vaccination strategies informed by population immunity. We reconstructed state- and age-specific immune profiles by fitting an age-structured catalytic model to dengue surveillance data from 2000-2025. This inferred immune profile was incorporated into an SIR-type transmission model to project disease burden and to evaluate the public health impact of vaccine allocation strategies. We observed substantial spatial heterogeneity in accumulated immunity, which was closely associated with projected burden and optimal allocation. Strategies prioritizing states with lower historical incidence and larger susceptible populations yielded greater benefits. Under limited vaccine supply, targeting children resulted in the greatest reductions in DALYs, whereas targeting elderly populations achieved smaller DALY reductions but larger reductions in mortality. We further showed that accelerated vaccine supply markedly increased impact, while allocation choices remained critical when availability was constrained.

articles.title: Recurrence patterns and adjuvant therapy in endometrioid early-stage endometrial cancer with a p53-abnormal pattern
articles.abstract: Objective: Current guidelines recommend different adjuvant treatment strategies for women with endometrioid early stage endometrial cancer exhibiting a p53 abnormal pattern. We aimed to evaluate recurrence patterns and explore the clinical implications for adjuvant therapy in this population. Materials and methods: This multicenter retrospective study included 86 patients with endometrioid, p53 abnormal, FIGO stage I, II endometrial cancer treated between 2013 and 2023 at six hospitals in the Republic of Korea. Clinicopathologic data were collected through medical record review. Progression free survival (PFS) was estimated using the Kaplan Meier method, and prognostic factors were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression models. Results: The 12, 24, and 36 month PFS rates were 91%, 78%, and 76%, respectively. Among the 16 patients who experienced recurrence, 12 (75%) had distant metastases. Adjuvant chemotherapy showed a trend toward improved PFS compared with adjuvant radiation therapy with or without chemotherapy (p=0.10). In multivariable analysis, the p53 overexpression pattern was independently associated with worse PFS compared with the p53 null pattern (HR 8.59, 95% CI 1.61 to 45.79, p=0.01). Conclusion: Given the poor PFS, the predominance of distant recurrence and the observed trend toward improved PFS with chemotherapy, adjuvant chemotherapy may be considered in women with endometrioid early stage endometrial cancer exhibiting a p53 abnormal pattern. Further studies are warranted to clarify the prognostic impact of p53 abnormality subtypes.

articles.title: Remission of Type 2 Diabetes in Linked Health Records: Uncommon, Short-Lived, and More Often Ended by Treatment Restart Than by Rising HbA1c
articles.abstract: Objective: To estimate how often remission of type 2 diabetes is recorded in routine care, how long it lasts, and what ends it, separating a return of hyperglycemia from a restart of treatment. Research design and methods: We studied 136,781 adults aged 18 years or older with laboratory confirmed type 2 diabetes in the Protege linked electronic health record (EHR) and claims database. The 96,817 adults with glucose-lowering treatment recorded at or before cohort entry formed the primary (previously treated) cohort; 39,964 adults with no treatment recorded at entry were analyzed in parallel. Remission required two HbA1c values <6.5%, 90 to 365 days apart, the first at least 3 months after all glucose-lowering drugs were discontinued, with no therapy recorded between them. After remission we followed glycemic relapse (HbA1c over 6.5%) and treatment restart (a new outpatient prescription or dispensed fill) separately, with death as a competing event (Aalen Johansen). Results: Remission was documented in 4.33% of previously treated adults cohort and 15.57% in the cohort of untreated adults at entry. Five-year cumulative incidence (Aalen Johansen) was 3.82% (95% CI 3.69 ;3.93) and 13.27% (12.90;13.59) in each cohort, respectively. Remission was less common with greater baseline treatment burden: exploratory adjusted 5-year incidence was 4.65% in adults with 1 glucose-lowering class with a treatment episode recorded at or before entry, 3.62% with two, 2.69% with three, and 2.02% with four or more such drugs.. The Median Kaplan Meier duration of first remission was 226 days (IQR 93 to 855) in previously treated adults and 371 days (166 to 1,027) in adults untreated at entry; 37.9% (treated cohort) and 23.1% (untreated cohort) of episodes had ended by 152 days. Among remission episodes that had ended, median duration was 159 days (71 to 362) and 265 days (129 to 565) for the treated and untreated at entry cohort, respectively. Within 5 years of remission in previously treated adults, the first event ending remission was glycemic relapse in 31.94%, treatment restart in 47.83%, and death in 4.65%.Treatment restart was about 1.5 times as common as glycemic relapse as the first event ending remission. A second remission followed within 5 years in 19.53% of previously treated and 24.10% of untreated remitters. Conclusions: Recorded remission was uncommon and short-lived, and it ended more often with a treatment restart than with a rise in HbA1c. Studies of remission in real-world data should report relapse and restart separately and state how they confirm remission and establish that treatment stopped.

articles.title: Restoring Physical Resilience: Consistent Functional and Sarcopenia Gains Across Two Vivifrail Cohorts
articles.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate change in physical function and probable sarcopenia following a 36-week community multicomponent exercise programme (Vivifrail model) across two consecutive cycles, and to assess the consistency of this change between cohorts. Study design: Quasi-experimental, single-arm, repeated-measures service evaluation. Ninety-two older adults (2025-2026 cohort; mean age 75.9 years, 88.0% women) completed baseline and post-intervention assessments; an independent 2024-2025 cohort (n = 86) was analysed jointly for replication (n = 178). Main outcome measures: Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score (primary); Timed Up and Go (TUG), handgrip strength, 6-metre walk time and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) (secondary); probable sarcopenia (EWGSOP2), SPPB-based frailty category, and a fall-risk indicator computed identically in both cohorts. Results: SPPB improved by a mean of 1.33 points (Cohen's d = 0.96; p < .001), with concordant improvement in all four secondary outcomes (all q < .005). 72.8% reached the substantial minimal clinically important difference. Probable sarcopenia fell from 17.4% to 5.4% (p = .006), and frailty category shifted toward higher functional levels (p < .001). Effect sizes were consistent between cohorts for SPPB, handgrip and 6-metre walk; the Time x Cohort interaction was significant for TUG only. In the pooled sample, elevated fall risk fell from 19.7% to 11.2% (p = .002). Conclusions: A 36-week multicomponent exercise programme was associated with clinically meaningful, reproducible improvement in physical function and a reduction in probable sarcopenia across two independent cohorts. The single-arm design precludes causal inference.

articles.title: Social Needs Z Codes and Subsequent Acute Care Across 21 U.S. Health Systems
articles.abstract: Health systems increasingly record ICD-10 Z59 social-needs codes for housing, food, transportation, and related hardship to trigger referrals, report quality, and adjust risk. However code documentation occurs at varying rates and no study has separated what the code says about a patient's hardship from what it says about being documented at all. Using a linked electronic health record and claims corpus covering 4.95 million patients in 21 identifiable health systems, we matched 26,153 adults with a first outpatient Z59 code to similar uncoded patients and, as a negative control, repeated the entire design around an administrative code. Coding ranged from 1 percent to 24 percent of patients across systems and remained highly variable after adjustment for patient mix. A hardship code was associated with 67% (95% CI=1.61, 1.74) more emergency department (ED) visits and 43% ( 95% CI=1.38, 1.49) more hospital admissions in the next year (62 versus 49 of every 100 patients with any acute event). The administrative-code reproduced 46 percent of the Z59 association for ED visits and 70 percent for admissions. In the five systems with the most complete stay dates, no hardship-specific admission excess was detectable. Homelessness codes forecast two and a half times the ED visit rate. At national planning prices, excess emergency and preventable hospital care totaled roughly $2,000 to $2,500 per coded patient-year ($2,516 base scenario; about $1,100 under an exploratory assumed-discount scenario (not an estimate of hardship-attributable spending)), with the largest emergency burden among Medicaid patients. The Z code added no increment to clinical and utilization-based risk prediction models in any system.

articles.title: T-cell dysregulation is implicated in the encephalopathy of prematurity
articles.abstract: Preterm birth is strongly linked to systemic inflammation and encephalopathy of prematurity, which underlies subsequent cognitive impairment. T-cell immunity contributes to brain-immune crosstalk across the life course but its role in the pathogenesis of encephalopathy of prematurity is unknown. Protein epigenetic scores are DNA methylation (DNAm)-based proxies of circulating proteins. We tested the hypothesis that T-cell dysregulation has a specific role in child neurodevelopment following preterm birth. Multimodal data were collected from 144 preterm infants (median gestational age at birth 29+5 weeks [range 23+3 to 32+6]) recruited to a prospective cohort study: saliva DNAm for protein epigenetic score derivation and brain MRI, both at term-equivalent age, and the Mullen Scales of Early Learning Composite score at 5 years from a subset. We investigated associations of the epigenetic scores for cytotoxic and regulatory T cell-associated molecule (DNAm CRTAM) and C-reactive protein (DNAm CRP; a non-specific marker of inflammation) with MRI metrics of encephalopathy of prematurity: global and regional brain volumes, and general factors of diffusion tensor imaging and neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging metrics averaged across 42 white matter tracts. We tested whether DNAm CRTAM explains more variance than DNAm CRP in MRI metrics of the encephalopathy of prematurity and cognitive scores in childhood. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower general factor of fractional anisotropy ({beta} = -0.252, q = 0.011) and higher general factors of radial diffusivity ({beta} = 0.215, q = 0.039), mean diffusivity ({beta} = 0.198, q = 0.047) and orientation dispersion index ({beta} = 0.201, q = 0.048), independent of inflammatory morbidities and other biological covariates after false discovery rate correction. DNAm CRTAM explained more variance than DNAm CRP (maximum incremental R2 = 4.2% vs 1.5%) in diffusion MRI metrics. Higher neonatal DNAm CRTAM was associated with lower cognitive scores at 5 years, independent of DNAm CRP and other covariates ({beta} = -0.332, P = 0.008), and explained more variance in cognitive scores than DNAm CRP (incremental R2 = 9.4% vs 1.2%). An epigenetic proxy of CRTAM in preterm infants is associated with both encephalopathy of prematurity in the neonatal period and lower cognitive performance at 5 years, explaining greater incremental variance than a non-specific marker of inflammation. The data implicate T-cell dysregulation in the pathophysiology of atypical neurodevelopment following preterm birth.

articles.title: Trends and Disparities in Respiratory Failure Mortality with Co-Listed Atrial Fibrillation and Flutter Among U.S. Adults Aged >= 65 Years, 1999 to 2024, with AAMR Forecasts Through 2035: A CDC Wonder Analysis
articles.abstract: Background: Respiratory failure (RF) and atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL) often occur together in older adults, but long-term national mortality trends for the two conditions combined have not been described. We examined trends and disparities in deaths with co-listed RF and AF/AFL among U.S. adults aged 65 years and older from 1999 to 2024, and projected rates through 2035. Methodology: We used the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to identify deaths with ICD 10 codes J96 (RF) and I48 (AF/AFL) listed together. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 were standardized to the 2000 U.S. population and stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, urbanization, state, and place of death. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Forecasts for 2025 to 2035 were generated with an exponential smoothing (ETS) model. Results: A total of 433,598 deaths were recorded. The overall AAMR rose from 12.8 in 1999 to 66.7 in 2024 (AAPC 8.11%; 95% CI, 7.35 to 8.87; P < 0.0001). Three segments were identified: an increase from 1999 to 2018 (APC 7.73%), a sharp rise from 2018 to 2021 (APC 18.10%), and a decline from 2021 to 2024 (APC -5.25%). Males had a higher AAMR and a steeper increase than females (AAPC 8.44% vs 7.81%). Non-Hispanic White adults had the highest mean AAMR, Hispanic adults had the largest relative increase (AAPC 8.72%), and Non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander adults had the smallest (AAPC 6.23%). The Midwest had the fastest regional growth (AAPC 9.35%). From 1999 to 2020, non-metropolitan areas increased faster than metropolitan areas (AAPC 10.09% vs 8.21%). State AAMRs ranged from 24.7 in Ohio to 85.1 in Louisiana. Most deaths occurred in hospital inpatient settings (64.1%), followed by nursing homes (14.1%) and the home (11.9%). The model projects an AAMR of 122.96 per 100,000 by 2035 (95% prediction interval, 85.42 to 160.50). Conclusions: Mortality involving RF with AF/AFL among older U.S. adults increased more than fivefold over 25 years, with a marked surge during the COVID 19 period and only a partial decline afterward. Differences by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization point to groups that may benefit from earlier detection and coordinated cardiopulmonary care.

articles.title: Vaccination and Non-School NPIs Shaped Ontario's Pre-Omicron COVID-19 Hospital Burden
articles.abstract: We develop an age- and immunity-structured COVID-19 model with setting-specific contacts, calibrated to Ontario incidence and hospital admissions before Omicron. We simulate counterfactual vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in schools, workplaces, and other community settings, evaluating projected severe-case demand against an illustrative healthcare-capacity benchmark. Vaccination combined with workplace and community contact restrictions keeps simulated demand within capacity. In contrast, relaxing restrictions in either setting produces large surges and repeated capacity threats, even when school restrictions remain. School-only changes produce smaller effects on severe disease. These findings highlight the value of vaccination and setting-specific contact restrictions that prioritize workplace and community settings for pathogens with adult-concentrated severe outcomes.

articles.title: Validation and culture adaptation of the Arabic version of the Rapid Eating Assessment for Participants - Shortened Version (REAP-S): A Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Rasch Analysis Study
articles.abstract: Aim: To translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate the Arabic version of the REAP-S among Arabic speaking young adults using Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) and Rasch Measurement Theory (RMT). Design: A cross-sectional methodological psychometric validation study. Methods: The study included 500 undergraduate and postgraduate nursing students recruited from Saudi universities during the 2025–2026 academic year. The REAP-S was translated into Arabic using standardized forward backward translation procedures and cross-cultural adaptation guidelines. Participants completed the Arabic REAP-S through an online self-administered questionnaire. Construct validity was evaluated using CFA with robust estimators, assessing the Comparative Fit Index (CFI), Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI), Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA), and Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR). Rasch Measurement Theory was applied to examine item fit, response category functioning, person item targeting, and person reliability. We assessed internal consistency using Cronbach's alpha and the Rasch Person Separation Index (PSI). Results: Psychometric analyses included 490 participants with a median age of 20 years (IQR = 19–22), of whom 54.1% were female. CFA supported the hypothesized one-factor structure and showed good model fit (CFI = 0.984, TLI = 0.978, RMSEA = 0.076, SRMR = 0.061). Standardized factor loadings ranged from 0.429 to 0.768, and internal consistency was good (Cronbach's α = 0.863). Rasch analysis confirmed the scale's unidimensionality, with satisfactory person reliability (Expected A Posteriori [EAP] = 0.872; Weighted Likelihood Estimate [WLE] = 0.848). All items demonstrated acceptable infit and outfit mean square statistics (0.826–1.311 and 0.866–1.283, respectively), with ordered response thresholds and adequate person-item targeting. Overall, the Arabic REAP-S effectively discriminated between different levels of dietary behavior among Arabic-speaking young adults. Conclusion: The Arabic REAP-S demonstrated strong validity and reliability, supporting its unidimensional structure and appropriate psychometric performance. Evidence from both CFA and Rasch analysis confirmed acceptable model fit, good internal consistency, and adequate item functioning. The instrument provides a brief and practical tool for assessing dietary behaviors among Arabic-speaking young adults in clinical and research settings. Implications for the Profession and/or Patient Care: The Arabic REAP-S provides nurses and other healthcare professionals with a brief, standardized tool for rapidly assessing dietary behaviors and identifying individuals at nutritional risk. Its integration into routine clinical and community practice may support early dietary screening, guide nutrition education, and strengthen evidence based preventive care for diet related chronic diseases. Keywords: Arabic REAP-S; Dietary Screening; Confirmatory Factor Analysis; Rasch Measurement Theory; Construct Validity; Young Adults.

articles.title: Why Have Drug Names Become So Weird? A Retrospective Analysis of the Orthographic Distinctiveness of Proprietary and Generic Names Across Four Decades of FDA Approvals
articles.abstract: Background. Regulatory pressure to avoid confusingly similar drug names appears to have pushed manufacturers to coin more distinctive proprietary names, but no one has quantitatively analyzed this trend. Objective. To determine whether proprietary drug names became more orthographically distinctive (unusual in spelling) over time. Methods. We examined 1,321 US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) new molecular entity (NME) names (1985-2024), 2,769 FDA Orange Book trade names (1982-2026), 177,337 US pharmaceutical trademarks (1980-2026), and 1,273 generic names (1982-2025). Compared to prior names (including those already marketed) and ordinary English, we scored each name's character trigram (three-letter sequence) surprisal (statistical unexpectedness) and its edit-distance similarity to the closest existing names. Linear regression tested time trends, controlling for name length. Results. Mean NME trigram surprisal rose in every decade between the 1980s and 2020s, from 7.21 to 8.50 nats (natural-logarithm units, higher meaning less predictable), an 18% increase (b = 0.038, p < .001, R2 = 0.34). Half of 2020s names (7% in the 1980s) contained a letter sequence found in no common English word (e.g., Jesduvroq, Omvoh). Nearest-neighbor similarity fell after the early 1990s. Trademark data showed the same trend (b = 0.016, p < .001). Generic names showed a weaker trend (b = 0.011, R2 = 0.063). Conclusions. Over four decades, drug names became more orthographically distinctive, consistent with namespace crowding, deliberate efforts to avoid confusing names, and branding strategy. Because unfamiliar letter sequences can introduce other error pathways, increased distinctiveness does not necessarily imply improved safety.

articles.title: Why are girls more distressed than boys? A multi-domain framework applied to longitudinal data across four countries
articles.abstract: Background: Girls are more likely than boys to experience psychological distress during adolescence. Drivers of this gender gap remain under-studied, despite its large impact on later life and outcomes, especially for women. Explanatory factors can be gendered in their prevalence (differential exposure) and/or in their impact (differential susceptibility). We developed a multi-domain framework of explanatory factors for distress and applied it in four low- and middle-income countries. Methods: We first proposed a framework of explanatory factors for psychological distress grouped into seven domains (biological, cognitive, psychological, behavioural, social, environmental and broader societal). We applied this framework to identify explanatory variables assessed in childhood and adolescence in the Young Lives longitudinal cohort studies in Ethiopia (N=908), India (N=952), Peru (N=634) and Vietnam (N=887). Distress symptoms at 18-19 years were measured with the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire Emotional Symptoms scale. Gendered prevalence of each explanatory factor was tested with Mann-Whitney tests, and gendered impact with country-specific linear regressions including a gender-by-factor interaction term. Exploratory boosted-tree machine-learning models, interpreted with SHAP values and permutation feature importance, examined the contribution of these factors to the gender gap in each country. Results: Distress was higher in girls than boys in every country, the gap ranging from 0.62 points in Ethiopia and Vietnam to 1.76 in India and 2.45 in Peru. Some explanatory factors were consistently gendered in prevalence (e.g. girls experienced greater role overload in each country), while others were gendered only in some countries (e.g. study amount was higher for girls in Peru and Vietnam, but not Ethiopia or India). Gendered impacts on distress displayed more variability across countries. For example, higher self-esteem was more protective for boys than girls in India, Peru and Vietnam, but more protective for girls in Ethiopia. The machine-learning models identified important predictors across all framework domains, though their salience varied by country. Conclusions: Our findings underscore the importance of considering multi-domain explanations for mental-health outcomes and observed inequalities in mental health. Large cross-country differences in the gender gap and in the prevalence and influence of explanatory factors caution against generalising drivers of mental-health outcomes and inequalities across contexts.

articles.title: Wildfire smoke leaves a large five-year imprint on mortality in the United States
articles.abstract: Wildfire smoke poses a growing health risk worldwide, yet the magnitude and temporal evolution of mortality after episodic exposure remain poorly resolved, limiting burden assessment. Using monthly county-level wildfire PM2.5 and mortality data from the United State, we exploit episodic exposure contrasts to deconvolve overlapping mortality responses and recover the impulse-response function. The excess mortality response peaks approximately three years after an exposure pulse and subsides by five years. We estimate 1.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.1-2.3) million smoke-associated deaths during 2011-2023, approximately ten times estimates using long-term ambient PM2.5 mortality relative risks. Circulatory and respiratory diseases contribute comparably and dominate this burden. Responses are markedly greater among adults [≥]65 years; during the COVID-19 pandemic, population-wide cumulative responses are significantly higher over at least the first seven months after exposure. Reducing wildfire smoke exposure can thus yield substantial health benefits over multiple years, particularly when population vulnerability is heightened.

articles.title: Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Dearomatization of Tryptamines with Alkoxyallenes
articles.abstract: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes. This protocol features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, delivering chiral pyrroloindolines in good yields (up to 93% yield) with stereoselectivity (up to >19:1 E/Z, 99% ee). Mechanistic studies suggest that a covalent adduct forms between the alkoxyallene and the chiral phosphoric acid. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.

articles.title: Metal-Dependent Control of Methoxy Retention versus Cleavage in Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Lignin-Derived Aromatics
articles.abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation of lignin-derived aromatics offers a route to biomass upgrading, but controlling methoxy retention versus cleavage remains challenging. Here, we compare carbon-supported Rh, Pt, Ru, and Pd catalysts for guaiacol conversion under identical conditions. Rh/C and Pt/C are the most active catalysts but favor sharply different pathways: Rh/C promotes methoxy-retaining ring hydrogenation, whereas Pt/C preferentially forms demethoxylated products. Time-resolved profiles, intermediate-feeding experiments, and initial-rate analysis indicate that this selectivity difference emerges predominantly during early reaction branching. The apparent activation free energies of methoxy retention and demethoxylation are closely matched on Rh/C (91.1 and 91.8 kJ mol–1, respectively), but favor demethoxylation on Pt/C (91.1 and 89.2 kJ mol–1, respectively). Calculations on model surfaces suggest that metal-dependent interactions with adsorbed guaiacol facilitate access to different bond-activation pathways, providing a possible molecular basis for the observed kinetic preference. The Rh/Pt selectivity contrast persists across the investigated potentials and temperatures and extends to four additional lignin-derived aromatics as a broader difference in functional-group retention and cleavage. These results link metal-dependent early pathway partitioning to control over oxygen retention in electrochemical biomass upgrading.

articles.title: Tailoring Dynamic Cu Redox Responsiveness via Pr-Modified Ceria for Enhanced Reverse Water–Gas Shift
articles.abstract: The reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a key technology for converting CO2 into CO as a versatile intermediate for chemical production. Among various catalysts, Cu/CeO2 has attracted considerable attention owing to its high CO selectivity, yet its activity is affected by the oxidation and reduction behavior of Cu under reaction conditions. Although rare-earth modification has been widely employed to improve the redox properties of ceria, the relationship between support modification and the dynamic Cu redox behavior during RWGS remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that Pr modification effectively tailors the Cu redox response of Cu/CeO2, leading to enhanced RWGS performance. Systematic comparison of lanthanide modified ceria supports revealed that Pr-modified CeO2 exhibited the highest catalytic activity while maintaining approximately 99% CO selectivity. Comprehensive structural characterization combined with in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy showed no major difference in the surface species detected after Pr modification. Instead, the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst exhibited a faster oxidation response under CO2 together with reversible reduction under an H2 atmosphere. The enhanced Cu redox dynamics are associated with the modified redox characteristics of the Pr-modified CeO2 support. These results identify dynamic Cu redox responsiveness as an important characteristic associated with the enhanced RWGS activity of the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst and provide a practical strategy for engineering reducible oxide-supported Cu catalysts for efficient CO2 conversion.

articles.title: Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry for Characterization of Ir-Based Catalysts for PEM Water Electrolyzers
articles.abstract: Iridium-based catalysts remain essential for enabling durable oxygen evolution in proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), yet their surface and subsurface chemistries remain insufficiently resolved by conventional characterization methods. Here, we establish time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), combined with multivariate analysis, as a framework for deconvoluting chemical-, structural-, and depth-dependent features across commercial IrOx powders spanning amorphous and rutile phases. Static and Ar cluster-sputtered ToF-SIMS spectra reveal distinct surface hydroxylation, oxide fragment distributions, and subsurface chemical signatures that differentiate amorphous and rutile IrOx and expose synthesis-dependent residues. Across all powders, surface regions are enriched in hydroxylated IrOx fragments, while subsurface regions show increased reduced Ir species and carbon-based ions. ToF-SIMS fragments are correlated with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) extracted parameters, providing complementary surface chemical information that supports species identification. Finally, integrating ToF-SIMS and XPS descriptors with electrochemical and structural metrics yields a chemically resolved picture linking hydration depth, oxidation state distribution, and structural order to catalytic behavior. This multi-technique, multivariate framework provides insight into the chemical features governing Ir-based OER performance and supports the rational design of robust, efficient catalysts.

articles.title: Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS2/WS2-Nb2CTx Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
articles.abstract: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

articles.title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
articles.abstract: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

articles.title: 14C-Enabled Quantitative Fate Mapping of Orally Administered Polystyrene Nanoplastics in Laying Hens
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging pollutants of global concern, yet their quantitative in vivo fate in terrestrial vertebrates remains poorly resolved owing to analytical limitations. Here, we constructed a quantitative whole-body fate map in laying hens orally exposed to backbone 14C-labeled polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) at 0.4 mg kg–1 day–1, a dose selected to represent an environmentally plausible upper-bound exposure scenario. The 14C-PS-NPs had an approximately 80 nm dry-state primary particle diameter, while the vacuum-dried dosing material showed micrometer-scale agglomeration upon standardized redispersion. Excreta represented the dominant compartment in the mass balance, accounting for 88.55 ± 0.54% and 90.06 ± 1.02% of the cumulative administered dose after 3- and 7-day exposures, respectively. Gastrointestinal contents constituted the largest residual nonexcreted compartment, whereas kidney, liver, and lung showed the most prominent 14C signals among internal organs. Trace brain-associated 14C was below the matrix-specific LOD at day 3 but quantifiable at day 7, and the overall egg-associated signal remained below 0.1% of the cumulative administered dose. In a complementary 21-day dietary study, laying hens were exposed to PS-NPs at 0.4 and 2 mg kg–1 day–1 to assess intestinal responses together with circulating and selected-organ readouts. The 21-day study showed intestinal histopathological changes, elevated permeability markers, and pro-inflammatory and oxidative-stress readouts, while cecal microbiota compositional shifts were most evident in the 2 mg kg–1 day–1 group. This study provides a quantitative whole-body fate map of PS-derived 14C together with an assessment of biological responses to repeated dietary PS-NP exposure in laying hens.

articles.title: Accelerated Screening of Dimension-Controlled Cu3– y A y VS4– x Se x (A = K, Rb, Cs) via Soft Chemistry
articles.abstract: Dimension-driven design offers a powerful strategy for tuning the electronic structure of multinary chalcogenides, yet its application to solar absorbers remains limited. Previously explored systems lack candidates with optimal band gaps, while the time-consuming nature of solid-state synthesis impedes rapid synthesis and characterization of high-purity materials. Here, we report a colloidal soft-chemistry approach to systematically explore the Cu3–yAyVS4–xSex (A = K, Rb, Cs; y = 0, 1, 2; 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.5) compositional space, enabling simultaneous control over structural dimensionality (y), alkali-metal composition (A+), and chalcogen ratio (x) within a unified synthetic framework. By varying only precursor ratios, we access a broad family of phases spanning three-dimensional (3D), two-dimensional (2D), and one-dimensional (1D) [Cu–V–S] frameworks, as well as highly complex septenary solid solutions such as Cu(K, Rb, Cs)2VS2Se2. The resulting materials exhibit x-, y-, and A+-dependent optoelectronic properties, with band gaps tunable within the solar-relevant range of 1.40–1.67 eV, favorable band-edge alignment with CdS buffer layers, and intrinsic photocurrent responses. Theoretical calculations further elucidate the energy landscape and band structures of the understudied 1D series. Temperature- and time-resolved aliquot studies reveal pathway-dependent formation mechanisms, including direct nucleation of sulvanite Cu3VS4 and a two-step alkali-metal incorporation process governing the formation of alkali-metal-containing structures, providing key insights for related multinary chalcogenide systems. Overall, this work establishes a versatile platform for efficiently screening composition–structure–property relationships in complex chalcogenides for optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Flexible Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Film with Ultrahigh Absolute Electromagnetic Shielding Performance
articles.abstract: The rapid development of wearable electronic devices and fifth-generation (5G) communications have stimulated an urgent demand for flexible electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials. Conventional metal-based EMI shielding materials typically fail to concurrently achieve good flexibility and effective EMI shielding performance. In this study, we prepared single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films comprising high-purity, high-crystallinity and high-aspect-ratio SWCNTs by floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition (FCCVD) followed by gas-phase purification. The obtained SWCNT film showed good flexibility, low density, and high electrical conductivity. A record-high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SSE/t) of 5.42 × 105 dB·cm2/g and an exceptional normalized EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE/t) of 2.93 × 105 dB/cm, about twice as high as the highest reported EMI SSE/t value, were achieved for our SWCNT films. These results demonstrate that SWCNT films can be an ideal flexible EMI shielding material for use in next-generation wearable electronics and 5G communication systems.

articles.title: Fluorescence Encoding-Enabled Multiplexed Droplet Digital Recombinase Polymerase Amplification-CRISPR/Cas12a Assay for Rapid Screening of Lower Respiratory Tract Infection-Associated Bacterial Pathogens
articles.abstract: Digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a assays enable accurate nucleic acid quantification; however, their multiplexing capacity is inherently limited by signal confounding arising from the promiscuous trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a effectors. To overcome this limitation, we developed a fluorescence encoding-enabled multiplexed droplet digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a (FLEMD-CRISPR) assay that integrates combinatorial fluorescence encoding, deterministic droplet pairing within a calabash-shaped microwell array, and a machine learning-assisted decoding pipeline. In FLEMD-CRISPR, small-volume fluorescence-encoded CRISPR/Cas12a droplets, each assigned a unique spectral signature corresponding to a specific crRNA, are one-to-one paired with large-volume RPA droplets. Following RPA amplification and droplet merging, Cas12a-mediated reporter cleavage occurs only in droplets containing target amplicons. The decoding pipeline then localizes droplets, classifies their colors to assign crRNA identities, and finally detects positive signals, enabling high-throughput, hands-off analysis of the entire droplet array. FLEMD-CRISPR enabled simultaneous quantification of nucleic acid targets from eight major lower respiratory tract infection-associated bacterial pathogens, showing strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.9987–0.9998) and consistent detection efficiency (slopes = 0.9849–1.0198) relative to single-plex digital PCR. The complete workflow, from sample preparation to final readout, can be completed within 2 h. Clinical validation using 30 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples showed that the bacterial detection outcomes of FLEMD-CRISPR were highly concordant with standard-of-care culture, achieving 100% (20/20) positive percent agreement and 99.1% (218/220) negative percent agreement. By enabling panel reconfiguration through simple modifications of the droplet encoding library, FLEMD-CRISPR provides a flexible platform for the development of highly multiplexed digital CRISPR assays.

articles.title: In Vivo Blood Kinetics and Transcript Integrity of Three mRNA–Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines in Humans
articles.abstract: mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines are detectable in human blood after vaccination, but platform-specific differences in systemic persistence and transcript integrity remain poorly defined. We analyzed serial blood samples from 73 participants receiving Moderna mRNA-1273 (three formulations), Pfizer/BioNTech BNT162b2, or an investigational receptor-binding domain (RBD) mRNA vaccine (three different doses). Using droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) assays, we quantified total and long-range linked (“intact”) vaccine mRNA, and we measured vaccine-specific ionizable lipids by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS).
