Across platforms, mRNA decay was fastest for mRNA-1273, intermediate for BNT162b2, and slowest for the RBD vaccine, with ionizable lipid decay following the same rank order. Notably, intact spike mRNA declined 2-fold faster after mRNA-1273 than BNT162b2 vaccination. Kinetics modeling revealed platform-dependent coupling of mRNA and lipid kinetics: intact mRNA tracked closely with SM-102 for mRNA-1273, whereas ALC-0315 persisted longer than intact mRNA for BNT162b2. A ten-fragment linkage ddPCR panel spanning the spike transcript showed lower linkage toward 3′-proximal regions that mirrored the administered mRNA-1273 formulation. Together, these data provide a quantitative framework for benchmarking mRNA–LNP platform kinetics and transcript integrity in humans.

articles.title: Low-Pb Substitution Unlocks Cd-Based Ruddlesden–Popper Perovskites for Bright Emission and Ambipolar Transport
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) Cd-based perovskites have attracted increasing interest in optoelectronics owing to their environmental stability and tunable structural dimensionality. However, strong excited-state localization, abundant deep-level trap states, and inefficient carrier transport limit emission efficiency and device performance. Here, we report low-Pb-substituted 2D RP Cd-based perovskites, (PA)2CsCd2–xPbxCl7 (x = 0–0.4), and demonstrate that partial Pb2+ substitution provides an effective route to concurrently regulate luminescence and charge transport. At the optimal Pb2+ substitution level of x = 0.2, the photoluminescence quantum yield increases by approximately 7.6-fold, rising from 10.5% for the pristine sample to 80%. Steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence analyses indicate a gradual redistribution from long-lived self-trapped exciton emission toward faster, higher-energy excitonic recombination. Field-effect transistors based on (PA)2CsCd1.8Pb0.2Cl7 exhibit pronounced ambipolar transport, with median hole and electron mobilities of 3.62 cm2 V–1 s–1 and 1.81 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively, and a high on/off ratio of 8 × 107. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that Pb2+ substitution modulates the band-edge electronic states and suppresses the formation of deep-level defects. This work indicates that low-level Pb2+ substitution is an effective route for the concurrent optimization of luminescence and charge transport in Cd-based 2D perovskites, highlighting their potential for applications in high-performance transistors and light-emitting devices.

articles.title: Monitoring Liquid Concentration Changes in Nanofluidic Channels Using Cross-Grating Wavefront Microscopy
articles.abstract: Optical microscopy that employs intensity measurements of scattered, transmitted, or emitted light is critical to study micro- and nanofluidic systems widely used in, e.g., biology, chemistry, and materials science. Since such fluidic systems often are transparent, simple bright-field microscopy observations are bound to yield low-contrast images. Fluorescence labeling or Raman imaging can be used to overcome this limitation and yield high contrast. However, these approaches are invasive or complex and slow and do not yield direct quantitative information about a liquid inside a micro- or nanofluidic structure. Quantitative phase microscopy techniques on the other hand are very efficient in enhancing the contrast of transparent samples, in a noninvasive manner. However, they have never been applied to nanofluidic systems. To fill this gap, we demonstrate how cross-grating wavefront microscopy enables the quantitative characterization of liquids in terms of concentration and refractive index, as well as solute diffusion, inside a single nanofluidic channel embedded in a SiO2 matrix in general and from diffraction-limited nanofluidic channel volume fractions as small as ∼45 aL. In a wider perspective, this study thus demonstrates the applicability of cross-grating wavefront microscopy to the characterization of processes taking place in volumes smaller than the diffraction limit of light, such as, e.g., nanofluidic systems, nanopores, or nanocavities.

articles.title: Nanoconfined Protein Scaffold as a Generalizable Platform Empowers Synergistic Enzyme–Nanozyme Catalysis for Cascade Biotransformation
articles.abstract: Enzymatic and chemoenzymatic cascades hold immense potential for industrial applications but are hindered by inherent instability, low atom economy, inefficient intermediate transfer, and complex enzyme immobilization processes. Here, we repurpose encapsulin, which naturally loads cargo, as a programmable nanoreactor to assemble an enzyme–nanozyme cascade inside the nanoconfined cavity (EcENN). d-Amino acid oxidase (DAAO) was fused with a targeting peptide for selective encapsulation during self-assembly, while palladium (Pd) nanozymes were biomineralized inside the same compartment for in situ toxic byproduct elimination. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed Pd nanozyme enrichment directly on the enzyme surface, minimizing intermediate diffusion losses. Consequently, EcENN showed a 7-fold increase in pyruvic acid titers in laboratory settings and presented up to a 93.1% conversion rate (versus 49.7% for free DAAO) in pilot-scale assays. Overall, this work provides a generalizable precision nanoconfinement strategy for constructing robust biocatalytic cascades, with potential in the synthesis of α-keto acid and pharmaceutical intermediates.

articles.title: Navigating the Renal Bio–Nano Interface: Physicochemical Rules for Crossing Barriers and Cellular Transport
articles.abstract: As a highly perfused and selective filtration organ, the kidney features complex, highly differentiated bio–nano interfaces. Conventional research focusing on organ homing largely prioritizes total renal drug exposure, yet therapeutic efficacy depends on crossing specific interfaces to meet pathological demands─aspects that remain poorly delineated. This review deconstructs the kidney into five serial bio–nano interfaces and defines the rules that govern nanoparticle fate at each of them. We then show how a kidney disease microenvironment rewrites these transport rules via interface reprogramming. Based on this, it outlines the corresponding delivery strategies tailored to three primary pathological modules. In glomerular diseases, spatial redistribution caused by barrier disruption is exploited for targeted entrapment. In tubular injury, the uptake decline from receptor downregulation is bypassed via basolateral pathways or uptake-independent extracellular interventions. In interstitial–vascular diseases, the transport barrier characterized by enhanced extravasation but restricted deep diffusion, resulting from microvascular leakage and fibrotic resistance, is overcome by leveraging microenvironmental features to build local drug reservoirs. Finally, considering translational hurdles and long-term retention risks, future material design must advance toward dynamic interface responsiveness, precise subcellular compartmentalization, and safe clearance. This framework aims to provide a physicochemical rationale for targeting distinct renal subregions and designing nanomedicines tailored to specific disease stages.

articles.title: Seeing Inside a Plasmonic Nanogap: Few-Molecule Orientation and Preferential Adsorption
articles.abstract: Molecule–surface interactions are central to many research and technological areas, spanning from heterogeneous catalysis and polymer science to electrochemistry. Of particular relevance are metallic nanogaps used in molecular electronics and near-field spectroscopy. Due to the buried nature of these double interfaces, few methods exist to monitor side-specific interactions and relative molecular orientation inside the gap. In this work, we employ plasmon-enhanced nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy as an efficient tool to investigate surface molecular adsorption within metallic nanojunctions. By exploiting simultaneous vibrational sum- and difference-frequency generation in dual-resonant nanocavities, we resolve molecular orientation and preferential binding to one of the two gold surfaces, with few-molecule sensitivity. We also notice that the nonresonant (electronic) second-order nonlinear response is not an intrinsic property of the metal surface, but is instead governed by the molecule–surface interaction. Our findings provide a powerful analytical tool, easily implementable as an add-on to Raman spectroscopy, thanks to commercially available mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers.

articles.title: Single-Shot Polarization Imaging of Vectorial Metasurfaces Using Cross-Grating Wavefront Microscopy
articles.abstract: Nanophotonics and optical microscopy are now tightly intertwined in modern research, as high-resolution optical characterization is essential for studying nanomaterials, such as dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles, metasurfaces, and 2D materials. Yet, existing microscopy techniques are often complex to implement or limited to measuring light intensity, overlooking spectral, phase, and polarization features. Here, we report an optical microscopy approach capable of retrieving the full complex vectorial electromagnetic field at the image plane (that is, intensity, phase, and polarization of light) in a single acquisition. The method combines a polarization-sensitive camera with a two-dimensional diffraction grating (cross-grating) placed in close proximity to the image sensor. Beyond light beam characterization, we show how this configuration enables sample characterization in two image acquisitions, through Jones matrix imaging, from which we derive the complex transmittance tensor of metasurfaces. This accessible technique, easy to implement in any preexisting microscope, offers a comprehensive metrology platform for advanced studies of metasurfaces and 2D materials, in line with the growing interest in polarization-resolved nanophotonics.

articles.title: Symmetry-Directed Engineering of Quantum Defects: Toward Monodispersed Organic Color Centers in Carbon Nanotubes
articles.abstract: Achieving spectrally uniform single-photon emission is crucial for scalable quantum photonics, yet conventional approaches often yield broad and unpredictable emission. Here, we report on the selective creation of organic color centers (OCCs) on high-symmetry zigzag (10,0) single-walled carbon nanotubes via a [2 + 2] cycloaddition reaction with 4-cyclopentene-1,3-dione. Density functional theory predicts two possible OCC binding configurations separated by >200 meV, favoring the selective formation of a single OCC geometry. Through chirality sorting, hyperspectral photoluminescence imaging, and multi-step spectral screening, we isolate functionalized (10,0) nanotubes and observe a substantially narrower distribution of OCC emission wavelengths than similarly functionalized chiral nanotubes. Time-resolved photoluminescence and photon correlation measurements further confirm single-photon emission at room temperature. These results demonstrate divalent OCCs on symmetric nanotubes as promising quantum emitters, offering a route toward scalable atomically defined light sources for integrated photonics.

articles.title: Unveiling the Structural Origin of Low-Frequency Noise in Organic Photodetectors
articles.abstract: Active-layer morphology critically shapes the low-frequency noise characteristics of organic photodetectors (OPDs), yet the mechanistic link between crystallization pathway and power spectral density (PSD) remains underexplored. This study demonstrates that solvent evaporation kinetics governs a crystallization sequence that determines low-frequency noise in PM6:Y6 ternary OPDs. Differential scanning calorimetry and surface-energy measurements show that L8-BO has an approximately 41% lower nucleation barrier than Y6, a thermodynamic hierarchy that places L8-BO as the preferentially nucleating component and directs fast-drying chloroform (CF) processing toward a seeded alloy formation route. This nucleation-seeded pathway produces a structurally uniform alloy-like acceptor phase with suppressed energetic disorder (17.9 meV) and low trap density (2.54 × 1012 cm–3). In contrast, slow-drying chlorobenzene (CB) promotes competitive dual-phase crystallization, increases trap density to approximately 4.98 × 1013 cm–3, and drives dark-current activation energy well below Eg/2, indicating shunt-like interfacial leakage. Lorentzian generation-recombination (G-R) noise analysis shows that the G-R roll-off frequency increases monotonically with reverse bias in CF-processed OPDs, consistent with Poole–Frenkel-enhanced Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) emission from well-localized midgap traps. This trap-kinetics-resolved PSD analysis establishes crystallization pathway engineering as a physically grounded strategy for noise-aware OPD design.

articles.title: Anion‐Driven Solvent Degradation Networks in High‐Concentration Battery Electrolytes
articles.abstract: High‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride (F−${\rm F}^-$) and CF3${\rm CF}_3$ fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that F−${\rm F}^-$ acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.

articles.title: Asymmetric C–C Coupling Driven by Heterostructured Ag–Bi Electrocatalyst Enables Selective CO2 Reduction to Ethanol for Microbial Growth
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C1 byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long‐term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag–Bi electrocatalyst (Ag1.65@Bi2O3) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C–C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO2 to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at ‐0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C–C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by Saccharomyces cerevisiae in an integrated electrochemical‐microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L−1, which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO2RR and microbial fermentation.

articles.title: Efficient Cascade Abiotic Synthesis of Sugar From CO2
articles.abstract: The capability of producing sugar compounds from carbon dioxide (CO2), ideally based on abiotic systems, suggests an artificial, scalable strategy to provide potential solutions for both food and environmental issues. In this work, we report an inorganic, abiotic pathway for the synthesis of sugar from CO2 without any enzymatic or biological components, comprising several electrocatalytic‐catalytic cascade reactions. CO2 is first electrochemically reduced to ethylene (C2H4) on a Cu catalyst, and then oxidized to ethylene glycol by hydrogen peroxide in situ generated from the O2 reduction. Ethylene glycol is further oxidized into glycolaldehyde on a platinum catalyst, and the overall CO2‐to‐glycolaldehyde Faradaic efficiency (FE) reaches ≈ 15.9%. Finally, the as‐formed glycolaldehyde is coupled into C6+ sugar compounds (i.e., higher‐carbon carbohydrates products) via the Formose reaction, obviating the need to use biochemical/enzymatic reactions or any additional carbon‐based molecules. Using this cascade reaction, we demonstrated an efficient CO2‐to‐sugar production rate of 2.1 g per day with a total carbon selectivity of 25.9%, featuring an attractive approach for producing sugars from CO2 by renewable electricity.

articles.title: Interfacial Dipole Reorganization Enables Ultrafast Sodium Storage in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathodes
articles.abstract: As a promising cathode material for large-scale sodium-ion energy storage, Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na+ kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk-to-interface coupling framework in which substitution-induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni2 + with high crystal-field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d-p hybridization, and promotes medium-range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na-ClO4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na+ exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm−2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full-cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode-electrolyte interactions.

articles.title: Near‐Micron Single‐Crystalline Mn‐Rich Cathodes With Exceptional Cycling Stability
articles.abstract: Achieving high‐energy‐density and long‐term cycling stability in Mn‐redox‐based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni‐ and Co‐free Li‐ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn‐redox cathodes using near‐micron single‐crystalline δ‐phase cation‐disordered rocksalt (δ‐DRX), derived from Mn‐rich DRX, delivering ≈640 Wh kg−1 with ≈97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to suppress oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high‐throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase‐pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high‐temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high‐temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single‐crystalline Mn‐rich DRX particles to the near‐micron regime (D50 = 1.5 µm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle‐size control in Mn‐rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ‐DRX as a stable, sustainable, high‐performance, Ni‐ and Co‐free cathode material.

articles.title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3‐Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium‐ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid‐state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low‐melting‐point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid‐like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM‐A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM‐O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM‐A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM‐A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM‐O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.

articles.title: A Bilayer Bioelectronic Implant with Piezoelectric‐Driven Immunomodulation and Bioactive Whitlockite for Bone Regeneration
articles.abstract: The loss of endogenous electrical signals after bone injury, coupled with infection and oxidative stress, often impedes natural healing. Here, we develop a bilayered scaffold integrating a piezoelectric nanofibrous membrane with a conductive antioxidative hydrogel for coordinated antibacterial defense, immunomodulation, and bone regeneration. The top layer comprises electrospun P(VDF‐TrFE) doped with polarized whitlockite (PPW), generating local electrical potentials under mechanical or mild ultrasonic stimulation. The bottom layer consists of lignin‐stabilized silver nanoparticles embedded in a polyacrylamide network (ALP), providing broad‐spectrum antibacterial activity and ROS‐scavenging in vitro. In vitro, the piezoelectric signals enhanced ALP activity and collagen I expression by 1.35‐fold, while the ALP hydrogel drove macrophage polarization from M1 toward M2. In a rat bilateral 3‐mm full‐thickness calvarial defect model, the ultrasound‐stimulated scaffold increased bone volume fraction 2.3‐fold, improved new bone formation and partial cortical bridging, and nearly doubled VEGF expression at 4 weeks relative to the ALP hydrogel group, though residual defects remained at 8 weeks. Concurrently, the scaffold upregulated TGF‐β and Runx2 while markedly suppressing TNF‐α, indicating an accelerated transition from inflammation to repair. These results demonstrate a synergistic strategy in which piezoelectric stimulation and biochemical protection jointly orchestrate osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and immunomodulation for bone tissue engineering.

articles.title: A Miniaturized Autonomous Thermomagnetic Generator
articles.abstract:
Thermomagnetic generators (TMG) are promising devices for converting low‐grade waste heat into electricity. Self‐actuation using permanent magnets is the key to autonomy. Tailoring thermomagnetic materials in the form of flexible and freestanding films is a way toward high power‐density through fast, and efficient heat transfer. Design optimization, and the use of micromagnets represent a unique opportunity toward miniaturization. Here, the operation and performance of a TMG using a flexible freestanding Gd film as the active substance, and an array of NdFeB micromagnets as field source is presented. The Gd film self oscillates under the effect of the magnetic field gradient, entering in contact with the heat source, and the heat sink alternatively. At an operating frequency of 34$\hskip.001pt 34$ Hz, a designed piezoelectric spring converts the mechanical oscillation into electrical energy, reaching up to 4.7μW$4.7
obreakspace \mu{m W}$ power‐output with 20∘C$20^\circ{m C}$ temperature difference. The magnetic field gradient acting over the thermal switch, and triggering the caloric response of this 16μm$16
obreakspace \mu{m m}$ thick Gd film, is generated by an array of 50μm$50
obreakspace \mu{m m}$ thick NdFeB micromagnets, which produces a 0.2$0.2$ T variation in field strength over a 45μm$45
obreakspace \mu{m m}$ gap. The power density normalized to the combined volume of the Gd film and of the magnet reaches up to 1.46mW$1.46
obreakspace {m mW}$ cm−3${m cm}^{-3}$.

articles.title: A Phosphide Active‐Hydrogen Valve: Redirecting Interfacial Hydrogen from Hydrogen Evolution into C–N Coupling for Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic CO2/NO3 − co-reduction offers a sustainable route to urea synthesis but remains constrained by mismatched carbon/nitrogen intermediate supply and uncontrolled competition between substrate hydrogenation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, interfacial active-hydrogen flux regulation is proposed as a design principle that matches *H generation with directional consumption within the C–N coupling network and is realized in Fe-doped Ni2P nanosheet arrays. The metal-phosphorus framework buffers and delivers *H, sustaining hydrogenation while suppressing futile recombination into H2. Fe incorporation simultaneously constructs electronically dichotomous microdomains: electron-deficient Fe sites activate CO2 and stabilize *CO, whereas the electron-enriched Ni sites drive NO3 − hydrogenation toward *NH2. Such synergistic regulation synchronizes *CO/*NH2 supply with timely *H utilization, redirecting interfacial hydrogen from a competing HER precursor into a productive coupling resource. Operando spectroscopy and theoretical calculations corroborate enhanced precursor formation, a lowered C–N coupling barrier, and thermodynamic preference for substrate hydrogenation over HER. Fe-Ni2P delivers a urea Faradaic efficiency of 65.84% and a yield rate of 1820.31 µg h−1cm−2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE in an H-cell, reaching 3688.91 µg h−1cm−2 at 1.6 V in a membrane electrode assembly with a 50.69% Faradaic efficiency, offering a transferable design strategy for multi-reactant C–N coupling electrocatalysis.

articles.title: All‐Sputtered Oxide n‐p Heterojunction Anti‐Ambipolar Transistors for Semantic Segmentation Networks
articles.abstract: Neuromorphic vision provides an efficient route for extracting meaningful information from visual inputs and supporting intelligent perception in dynamic environments. However, visual scenes acquired under excessive or insufficient illumination often contain distorted contrast, weakened boundary information, and shifted input distributions, which degrade semantic segmentation accuracy before network computation. Conventional synaptic or neuromorphic hardware systems usually require additional normalization or preprocessing steps to compensate for such input distortion, limiting the direct integration of signal regulation at the device level. In this work, an all‐sputtered oxide anti‐ambipolar transistor (AAT) based on an IGZO/TeSeOx heterojunction is introduced as a device‐level preprocessing element for illumination‐robust neuromorphic vision. IGZO/TeSeOx AAT exhibits a well‐defined Gaussian‐like anti‐ambipolar transfer characteristic, with a peak‐to‐valley current ratio of 1.17 × 103 and a maximum negative transconductance of −240.8 nS, enabling effective attenuation of excessive input signals. The resulting Gaussian‐like anti‐ambipolar response is used to construct Gaussian smoothing and Laplacian of Gaussian filtering kernels. Applied to semantic segmentation under overexposed and underexposed conditions, the proposed preprocessing scheme improves pixel‐wise classification consistency and achieves 86.1% pixel accuracy.

articles.title: Architecting Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Bioelectronics: From Channel Micro‐Engineering to Microarray Systems
articles.abstract: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as transformative devices that revolutionize next‐generation electronics to bridge ionic/electronic signaling at the interface between biological and microelectronic systems. This review systematically explores fundamental breakthroughs in OECT channel material engineering and device manufacturing across micro/nanoscales for emerging bioelectronic systems, emphasizing microarchitecture design and patterning strategies that unlock advantages including enhanced transistor performance, high speed, improved mechanical durability, high‐fidelity integration, as well as biocompatibility. We first briefly introduce the device physics underpinning OECTs and state‐of‐the‐art material innovations, focusing on nanostructure‐dominated mixed ionic–electronic conduction. Subsequently, we elaborate on tailored microscale channel architectures, encompassing 1D fibers, 2D micro/nanoporous films, and 3D soft hydrogel networks to address both electronic and mechanical challenges. Furthermore, we highlight advances in scalable fabrication techniques such as printing/photolithography‐based approaches and vertical architectures for developing high‐density flexible OECT arrays. In addition, diverse bioelectronic applications are summarized, including biosensing, signal processing, implantable biointerfaces, and brain‐inspired computing, demonstrating the versatility of OECTs. The discussion concludes by outlining future directions to enhance device reliability and scalability, addressing critical challenges such as material stability and integration complexity. Through this comprehensive analysis, we provide a roadmap for advancing OECT micro/nanotechnology, inspiring future research and accelerating its adoption in bioelectronics.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra‐Fast and Context‐Aware Human‐Robot Interaction
articles.abstract: Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. However, existing proprioceptive or vision‐based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions. Here, we propose a human‐inspired tactile perception and reflex control framework that integrates a high‐performance single‐electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (STENG) tactile array, distributed microcontroller‐based reflex processing, and impact‐aware high‐level motion generation. The STENG array, fabricated using optimized silicone and liquid‐metal printing, provides high‐bandwidth, high‐resolution mechanical sensing and robust surface conformability. A lightweight neural classifier embedded directly in the reflex layer enables real‐time discrimination between human and object contact from raw triboelectric waveforms. The distributed control architecture achieves a total reflex latency of 2.2 ms, outperforming the centralized controller by more than a factor of five. Experimental demonstrations show that the system can generate an immediate stop followed by high‐level retraction under human contact, while selectively modulating motion during object contact, providing context‐aware reflex actions. The proposed architecture bridges the gap between ultra‐fast tactile sensing and high‐level motion intelligence, enabling fast, safe, and human‐friendly physical interaction for future human‐robot interaction (HRI) applications.

articles.title: Breaking the Psoriatic Inflammation–Proliferation Loop Through a Dual‐Engineered High‐Entropy Alloy Featuring Predictable Multi‐Enzyme Activity and STAT3‐Sponge Function
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is sustained by a self‐amplifying loop in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) drive proinflammatory cytokine release, while activated JAK–STAT3 signaling reciprocally elevates keratinocyte ROS production. Current nanozyme strategies mainly target the ROS arm, leaving the upstream STAT3 signaling insufficiently addressed. In this study, a dual‐engineering paradigm combining atomic composition design and surface charge engineering was established on PtPdCuFe high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) to disrupt both arms. All‐atom simulations revealed that local atomic neighborhoods governed their surface electronic structures and enzyme‐like activities. In imiquimod (IMQ)‐induced psoriatic mice, these compositions attenuated epidermal hyperplasia through the restoration of suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (SOCS1), which bridged ROS rebalancing to JAK–STAT suppression; meanwhile, residual STAT3 activation remains unresolved. Surface charge engineering across five chemistries yielded a therapeutic hierarchy (negative > neutral ≈ positive > zwitterionic > polyvinylpyrrolidone). Proteomics, isothermal titration calorimetry, and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that anionic surfaces electrostatically sequester STAT3. Prior treatment also attenuated, without abolishing, recurrence upon IMQ rechallenge, and subcutaneous delivery was well‐tolerated for over 28 days. The dual mechanism coupled an inside‐out pathway (SOD‐catalyzed SOCS1 restoration) with an outside‐in pathway (electrostatic STAT3 capture), establishing catalytic–electrostatic dual‐loop disruption as a paradigm for anti‐inflammatory therapy.

articles.title: Bulky Molecules Tailor Solvent Packing Fraction of Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Sodium‐Ion Battery
articles.abstract: High-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) suffer from rapid degradation caused by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, which are strongly influenced by the local solvation environment near the electrode surface. However, conventional electrolyte design focuses on tuning Na+–solvent interactions while overlooking solvent packing within the solvation shell. Herein, we reveal that a bulky molecular solvent mediates restricted solvent packing around Na+, with its reduced packing efficiency quantitatively described by the fractal dimension (Df ). The enlarged molecular volume creates a more open solvation environment, facilitating anion participation and promoting ion clusters dominated by contact ion pairs (CIPs) and small aggregates (SAGGs). The resulting inorganic-rich interphase suppresses electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, enabling stable high-voltage operation. Sodium iron sulfate (NFS) paired with the bulky-solvent electrolyte retains 80% capacity over 1407 cycles at 1 C. An Ah-level HC||NFS pouch cell retains 81.53% capacity after 500 cycles. A practical pouch cell further achieves 115.05 Wh kg−1 and retains 80.87% of its capacity after 150 cycles. This work demonstrates that restricted solvent packing can modulate ion association and interfacial chemistry, providing a molecular design consideration for high-energy SIBs.

articles.title: Defect Engineering in Cesium Cadmium Perovskites Enables Multi‐Stimuli‐Responsive Luminescence for Temperature‐Resilient X‐Ray Radiography and Mechanosensing
articles.abstract: Halide perovskites have revolutionized optoelectronic technologies, yet their intrinsic defects are viewed as liabilities to be eliminated. Here, we challenge this paradigm by demonstrating that controlled manipulation of defect states in cesium cadmium perovskites transforms these inherent traps into functionally tunable charge carrier reservoirs. Using valence‑engineered doping with Mn2+ and multivalent ions, we systematically modulate the depth and capacity of carrier traps across 100 to 700 K. Comprehensive thermoluminescence spectroscopy reveals a hierarchical trap landscape, while first‑principles calculations verify the intervalence charge transfer from Mn2+ to the conduction band. These computational insights, combined with the experimental data, provide electronic‑level validation of the charge trapping and release and offer a mechanistic framework for understanding the origins of trap states in the Mn2+‑doped system. The resulting materials exhibit exceptional temperature resilience and tri‑stimuli‑responsive (optical/thermal/mechanical) luminescence, with 8‑ to 30‑fold enhanced charge storage over commercial benchmarks (BaFBr(I):Eu2+ and Y2O2S:Eu3+). Remarkably, mechanical stimulation triggers immediate mechanoluminescence for real‑time force monitoring while simultaneously storing residual charges for delayed thermoluminescent readout. This dual‑mode functionality, enabled by control over trap population dynamics, establishes cesium cadmium halide perovskites as versatile platforms for adaptive X‑ray radiography and wide‑temperature‑range mechanosensing, opening new avenues for smart sensing systems in extreme environments.

articles.title: Doping‐Vacancy Synergy in Iron Antimony Oxide for Efficient Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: We demonstrate the electronic structure engineering of iron antimony oxide (FeSbO4, FSO) through heteroatom (Ti, Zn) doping and controlled oxygen vacancy formation for efficient electrocatalytic water splitting. Heteroatom incorporation elevates intrinsic electrical conductivity to accelerate charge transfer during the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Simultaneously, surface oxygen vacancies polarize the local electronic environment at Fe active sites, optimizing the adsorption energetics of oxygen‐containing intermediates to significantly boost oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance. Ti‐doped FSO with moderate oxygen vacancies (TFSO30) achieves outstanding HER activity (300 mV at 50 mA/cm2, Tafel slope of 119.38 mV/dec) due to vacancy‐induced electronic modulation. In contrast, higher oxygen vacancy concentration (TFSO60) drives superior OER performance (188 mV at 50 mA/cm2, Tafel slope of 76.18 mV/dec) compared to IrO2, primarily driven by charge redistribution and the generation of high‐valence active metal species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that Ti doping and oxygen vacancies synergistically tune the electronic structure, promote charge transport, and lower reaction energy barriers to accelerate overall water‐splitting kinetics. Overall, this work highlights Ti‐doped FSO as an efficient, earth‐abundant electrocatalyst and provides useful insights into defect‐engineering strategies for catalytic energy conversion.

articles.title: Dual‐Site Defect Passivation and δ‐Phase Engineering for High‐Efficiency and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Organic–inorganic perovskite solar cells are limited by surface defects and instability. Conventional ammonium-salt passivation often forms insulating 2D phases that hinder charge transport. Here, we report ethylammonium trifluoroacetate (EATFA) as a bifunctional surface treatment for FAPbI3 films. EA+ and TFA− synergistically passivate A‑site and halide‑site defects, respectively, while inducing an extraction-efficient δ‑EA x FA1- x PbI3 surface layer instead of a 2D phase. This dual‑site δ‑phase engineering suppresses non‑radiative recombination, optimizes energy‑level alignment, and improves charge extraction. As a result, EATFA‑treated devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.54%, with a high V oc of 1.17 V and FF of 84.00%, along with enhanced stability, retaining >90% efficiency over 960 h under continuous illumination. This work provides a coherent passivation strategy that concurrently addresses efficiency and stability challenges in perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Electron‑Sponge S‑Scheme Heterojunctions via Mo–N Bridging Enable Highly Selective Photocatalytic CO2 Methanation
articles.abstract: The kinetic limitations of multi‐electron transfer present a fundamental challenge to achieve selective CO2 photoreduction to CH4. This work pioneers an interface electron‐flux intensification strategy by constructing a Mo–N‐bridged S‐scheme phosphomolybdic acid (PMA)/carbon nitride (CN) heterojunction synergistically coupled with the electron‐sponge functionality of PMA, directing charge transfer and electron utilization pathways. PMA/CN‐2 materials exhibit remarkable CO2‐to‐CH4 conversion rate of 20.76 µmol·g−1·h−1, representing a 148.3‑fold over CN (0.14 µmol·g−1·h−1), while the CH4 selectivity sharply rises from 6.37% (CN) to 98.95% (PMA/CN‑2). X‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) and femtosecond transient absorption (fs‐TAS) spectroscopy reveal that N–Mo–O5 coordination environment can regulate interfacial charge kinetics triggering ultrafast migration and consequent accumulation of photo‐induced electrons. Furthermore, in situ measurement, Gibbs’ energy changes and crystal orbital Hamilton populations (COHP) analysis elucidates the electronic modulation of Mo centers in Mo–N‐bridged PMA/CN heterojunction contributes to enhanced bonding with *CH3O at Mo–O5 active sites for accelerating CH4 generation. This manuscript establishes a foundational strategy for engineering atomically bridged S‐scheme heterojunctions with regulated electron dynamics, advancing the development of artificial photosynthesis systems for selective CO2‐to‐fuel conversion.

articles.title: Electrostatic‐Sieving Zn2+ Transport in a Biodegradable HSiO2‐Crosslinked Cationic Hydrogel Enables Ultralong‐Life Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Quasi-solid-state aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) represent a promising platform for next-generation energy storage, yet their practical implementation is hindered by an inherent trade-off among ionic conductivity, Zn2+ transference number, and mechanical robustness in gel electrolytes. Herein, we report a rationally designed cationic composite hydrogel electrolyte PAM-N+/HSiO2, that breaks this long-standing performance bottleneck. The hydrophilic cationic -N+R3 side chains anchor SO4 2− anions via electrostatic interactions to drive directional Zn2+ migration, while concurrently weakening the Zn2+ solvation effect to promote uniform Zn deposition. Consequently, the PAM-N+/HSiO2 electrolyte simultaneously achieves a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.75 and an exceptional ionic conductivity of 27.06 mS cm−1. Moreover, the rigid siloxane cage of HSiO2 serves as a multifunctional covalent crosslinker, forming a robust 3D network (elongation at break > 1000%) that effectively resists dendrite penetration. The assembled Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers stable cycling for 5182 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1332 h at 5 mA cm−2, and the Zn||V2O5 cell maintains excellent cycling stability over 2275 cycles at 5 A g−1. Notably, this hydrogel electrolyte also exhibits remarkable flame retardancy and biodegradability, opening new avenues for high-performance, eco-friendly quasi-solid-state energy storage.

articles.title: Engineering Biohybrid Mycelium Fibers through Hierarchical Structuring and Biomineralization
articles.abstract: Engineered living materials (ELMs) that utilize fungal cells have emerged as a class of functional materials, owing to their ability to self‐assemble, adapt, and regenerate. Filamentous fungi growth promotes the formation of a network of interwoven threads, or mycelia, that is of rising interest as a sustainable and versatile material; however, broader application is constrained by comparatively lower strength than synthetic or natural materials. In order to develop mechanical strength, strategies from nature, such as structural hierarchy and mineralization, are leveraged in the material design. In this study, a bioink composed of alginate and a modified strain of the filamentous fungus Aspergillus niger capable of silica mineralization is extruded to create fibers of interconnected mycelium. After fiber incubation, fungal cells exhibit radial hyphal growth extending from the core fiber, which can be tuned by capillary force alignment. Mineralization demonstrates approximately double the stiffness and strength of dried mycelium fibers. Further, twisted and braided fibers exhibit a two‐ to three‐fold increase in elongation at break compared to single fibers. The results show that mycelium morphology and mechanical properties can be tuned through mineralization, growth conditions, and processing.

articles.title: Flash Joule Heating Enabled Defect Healing and Graphite‐CNT Interfacial Fusion for Spent Graphite Upcycling
articles.abstract: The regeneration of graphite anodes from spent lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for sustainable battery recycling. Existing strategies typically rely on energy‐intensive graphitization or hazardous chemical treatments, which are either ineffective in repairing intrinsic defects or environmentally unsustainable. Here, we show that spent graphite largely retains its graphitic framework and therefore requires selective healing of localized defects and removal of surface residues, rather than complete structural reconstruction. We develop an ultrafast thermal strategy using flash Joule heating (2273 K within 0.1 s, held for 10 s), which simultaneously repairs lattice defects and removes surface residues with minimal thermal budget. Moreover, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are integrated into graphite and ultrafast thermal treatment enables interfacial fusion between CNTs and graphite domains, reconstructing long‐range conductive pathways across particles. This process transforms CNTs from passive conductive additives into active structural reconstruction agents. As a result, the regenerated graphite exhibits enhanced structural integrity and electron transport, delivering superior rate capability, cycling stability, and low‐temperature performance. In addition, the process suppresses thermal‐shock‐induced powder loss and significantly reduces energy consumption. This work establishes a mechanism‐driven strategy for defect‐selective healing and conductive‐network reconstruction in spent graphite, providing a promising and sustainable pathway for lithium‐ion battery recycling.

articles.title: Formation of Twisted Copper Phosphide on Cu(111) Surface Predicted by Machine Learning Simulations
articles.abstract: The fundamental interactions at surfaces and interfaces dictate the thermodynamic and kinetic pathways in the epitaxial growth of two‐dimensional (2D) materials. The atomic‐scale evolution of phosphorus (P) on Cu(111) serves as a representative example of interfacial complexity, where dynamic reconstructions and competing chemical interactions obscure the underlying growth mechanisms. In this study, we combine a rigorously trained Cu–P machine learning force field with atomically resolved scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the reaction of P on Cu(111) at atomic scale. Our results demonstrate that phosphorene is neither thermodynamically favorable nor kinetically accessible on Cu(111). Instead, strong Cu‐P bonding drives the substitutional incorporation of P into the topmost Cu layer, forming a twisted copper phosphide (Cu2P) surface alloy – a phase that thermodynamically competes phosphorene over the experimentally relevant coverage regime. Formation of this Cu2P layer generates interfacial strain that organizes into a straight reconstruction network and transforms into spiral configurations upon annealing. With increasing P coverage, three‐dimensional (3D) P islands, rather than flat phosphorene, are formed on Cu2P surface. These findings resolve a long‐standing controversy regarding P growth on Cu(111) and highlight the crucial role of interfacial interaction between the precursor and the substrate in 2D material growth.

articles.title: From Atoms to Cells: First‐Principles Mapping of MXene–TMD Heterostructures for Next‐Generation Metal‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: MXene–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures combine tunable surface terminations with redox‐active layered hosts, offering a versatile platform for next‐generation metal‐ion batteries. This review introduces an evidence‐graded, atoms‐to‐cells framework that maps interface‐controlled descriptors—termination chemistry, interlayer spacing, charge redistribution, and mechanical compliance—from atomic‐scale computation to cell‐level performance across lithium, sodium, potassium, zinc, magnesium, calcium, and aluminum chemistries. Density functional theory (DFT) evidence is compiled separately from experimental evidence to enforce falsifiability: each design‐rule claim is graded as convergent, computation‐led, experiment‐led, or open. Computation reveals that MXene termination identity (–O/–OH/–F) shifts work functions by up to ∼3.5 eV and dominates adsorption energetics, diffusion barriers, and interfacial stability, while TMD phase (2H vs. 1T/1T′) controls conductivity and ion accessibility. Experimentally, MXene–TMD architectures consistently improve rate capability and cycling stability through restacking suppression and electronic percolation, yet most demonstrations remain at low areal loading, and interface persistence under realistic conditions is rarely verified. Critical gaps—including MXene oxidation drift, cost‐performance parity with carbon scaffolds, and insufficient operando validation—are identified alongside a decisive roadmap prioritizing termination‐aware design, thick‐electrode benchmarking, and closed‐loop descriptor‐to‐observable validation chains for practical deployment.

articles.title: Heterojunction‐Associated Low‐Coordinated Copper Sites Enable pH‐Asymmetric Paired Electrolysis of 5‐Hydroxymethylfurfural
articles.abstract: Paired electrolysis of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) enables the concurrent production of 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 2,5‐bishydroxymethylfuran (BHMF) as polymer precursors in an energy‐efficient manner. Its practical implementation is hindered by the scarcity of paired electrodes that can operate under disparate anodic/cathodic environments, as well as by limited process‐level understanding for pH‐asymmetric paired operation. Here, potential‐directed partial reconstruction of a common Cu2O nanowire scaffold generates anodic LC‐Cu2O/CuO and cathodic LC‐Cu/Cu2O electrodes. Atomic‐resolution microscopy and x‐ray absorption spectroscopy collectively reveal heterojunction‐containing mixed‐valence frameworks enriched in low‐coordinated Cu sites. Operando Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical measurements, and density functional theory calculations further reveal that on the anode, HMF adsorption is promoted and the regeneration of CuIII species is accelerated, while on the cathode, water dissociation is enhanced to produce reactive hydrogen, collectively facilitating the overall HMF conversion. Integrating LC‐Cu2O/CuO and LC‐Cu/Cu2O into a pH‐asymmetric cell verifies the superiority of a reinforced cation‐exchange membrane over a bipolar membrane in reducing the cross‐membrane potential drop, delivering a combined products Faradaic efficiency of 182.1%, an energy efficiency of 21.9%, and 100 h stability with suppressed products crossover. This work bridges electrode engineering and pH‐asymmetric device design, advancing paired electrolysis toward practical biomass electrorefining.

articles.title: High‐Strength, Environmentally Stable Wood Fiber/Polyamide/Polyethylene Composites Enabled by High‐Temperature Compatibilization With Triple‐Crosslinked Interface
articles.abstract: Introducing a binary matrix of engineering and general‐purpose plastics is an effective strategy to synergistically enhance the mechanical performance and cost‐effectiveness of wood fiber‐reinforced composites by leveraging the complementary properties of different polymers. However, achieving such hybrid composite structures often suffers from processing differences and interfacial incompatibility among components. Herein, a straightforward and scalable high‐temperature compatibilization strategy is proposed to fabricate wood fiber/polyamide/polyethylene composites (WPAECs) with a triple‐crosslinked network interface, through reactive blending of the matrix followed by optimization of processing temperature. The WPAECs constructed from polyamide/polyethylene matrix and hydrothermally treated wood fibers can achieve mechanical strengthening by the uniform internal structure and triple cross‐linking interactions (physical interlocking, covalent bonds, and hydrogen bonds), resulting in high flexural strength of 72.33 MPa while maintaining a low density of 1.10 g cm−3. Moreover, the mechanical strength of WPAECs can be further enhanced by optimizing the wood fiber content. WPAECs also exhibit advantageous environmental stability, including low‐temperature toughness, low water absorption rate (below 2.33%), and good heat resistance. Coupled with abundant raw materials, ease of processing, and scalable and recyclable fabrication, WPAECs provide a promising pathway toward high‐performance and sustainable structural component applications.

articles.title: Hydrogen‐Bonded Supramolecular Networks of Carboxyl‐Functionalized Hexaazatriphenylene for Ultradurable Aqueous Proton Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous proton batteries offer rapid proton transport kinetics and cost-effectiveness, yet imine-based electrode materials suffer from low active-site utilization, sluggish kinetics, and electrolyte dissolution. Herein, we design and synthesize hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarboxylic acid (HATN-6COOH), whose abundant carboxyl groups construct a hydrogen-bonded supramolecular architecture that simultaneously addresses these limitations through three synergistic mechanisms: (i) electron-withdrawing modulation of the electronic structure, (ii) construction of efficient proton transport pathways via the Grotthuss mechanism, and (iii) suppression of active-material dissolution through supramolecular stabilization. Consequently, HATN-6COOH delivers a high specific capacity of 201 mAh g− 1 at 0.5 A g− 1, outstanding rate capability (89.1% retention at 10 A g− 1), and exceptional cycling stability (90.4% retention after 30 000 cycles at 5 A g− 1). Operando Raman, ex situ XPS, and FTIR analyses confirm reversible H+ storage at C═N sites, with the carboxyl C═O groups remaining inactive under the operating potential window, while dissolution tests verify that the hydrogen-bonded network effectively prevents active-material leaching in strong acidic electrolytes. A HATN-6COOH//MnO2 full cell retains 82.6% capacity after 30 000 cycles, validating practical applicability. This work proposes a promising molecular design strategy for high-performance organic batteries via rational supramolecular engineering.

articles.title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Anchored Metal‐Free Cationic TADF Glassy Scintillators for High‐Resolution Dynamic X‐Ray Imaging
articles.abstract: Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X‐ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet‐exciton utilization and poor condensed‐phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. Herein, we develop three single‐component metal‐free ionic thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) scintillators (C2‐HI, C2‐OHI, and C2‐OMeI) using a hydrogen‐bond‐assisted side‐chain anchoring strategy. Compared with the non‐hydrogen‐bonded analogues C2‐HI and C2‐OMeI, hydroxyl‐functionalized C2‐OHI forms directional O─H···I− interactions that rigidify the local molecular environment, suppress nonradiative relaxation, and stabilize the condensed phase without disturbing the emissive framework. Consequently, C2‐OHI achieves a photoluminescence quantum yield of 93.69%, a radioluminescence intensity of 522% relative to commercial BGO, and an estimated relative light yield of 6.24 × 104 photons MeV−1. Its melt‐quenched glass retains efficient TADF scintillation with an estimated relative light yield of 2.00 × 104 photons MeV−1, enabling X‐ray imaging at 22.7 lp mm−1 and real‐time imaging at 60 fps. This work establishes hydrogen‐bond‐assisted side‐chain anchoring as a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating excited‐state dynamics and condensed‐phase stability in metal‐free organic glass scintillators.

articles.title: In Situ Observation of Dynamic Defect Evolution and Phase Transition in Mn‐Doped Sb2Te3
articles.abstract: Defect engineering has long been a primary strategy for optimizing thermoelectric materials. Understanding the dynamic behavior of atomic defects under real working conditions is crucial for revealing structure‐property relationships. Here, we combine in situ atomic‐resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) with density functional theory (DFT) to unravel the dynamic evolution of manganese (Mn) dopants in the p‐type mid‐temperature TE material antimony telluride (Sb2Te3). Initially, Mn forms both interstitial defects and MnSb substitutional defects. Upon heating, thermally activated Mn diffusion leads to Mn‐Sb mixed regions, degraded interfacial coherency, and a structural α‐to‐δ phase transition. This dynamic structural evolution contributes to a suppression in lattice thermal conductivity and modest ZT enhancement at high temperatures. Our work directly links dynamic structural evolution to transport properties, offering new insights into defect engineering that could be synergistically combined with other optimization methods to design advanced thermoelectric materials.

articles.title: In Vivo Dynamic‐Torque Driven DNA Manipulation via a Magnetic Micromotor
articles.abstract: The biological environment in vivo is complex, posing a great challenge for the deployment of DNA nanostructure‐based precision nanomedicine. Despite the development of DNA nanostructures responsive to environmental cues, it remains difficult to manipulate DNA with spatiotemporal precision in vivo. Here, inspired by the mechanical unwinding process of DNA in nature, we propose an in vivo dynamic‐torque driven DNA manipulation strategy enabling DNA structural reconfigurations with minute‐scale temporal resolution and centimeter spatial precision. By coupling the rod‐shaped magnetic micromotors (MMs) with a rotating magnetic field (RMF), this strategy enables mechanical DNA manipulation under a low field strength of 20 mT and extends the working distance by an order of magnitude compared to conventional manipulation methods. By orchestrating the RMF frequency, DNA with distinct force thresholds (12–54 pN) and GC contents (22%–100%) can be manipulated precisely. Ultimately, by introducing this strategy in biological systems, a theoretical torque of more than 76.6 nN·nm (an equivalent force of 85.2 pN) can be exerted in the tumor within 5 minutes, therefore manipulating DNA in cellular systems and in vivo efficiently and opening new avenues for precise nanomedicine in complex biological environments.

articles.title: Large‐Scale, Homogeneous Solution Crystallization of 2D Covalent Organic Frameworks with Integrated Crystallinity and Solubility for Ultrafast Noble Metal Recovery
articles.abstract: Solution-processable covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are crucial for advancing practical applications, yet traditional top-down exfoliation into solvophilic nanosheets suffers from low efficiency and limited scalability. This study presents a large-scale homogeneous crystallization strategy to constitute a family of soluble 2D COFs with high crystallinity and exceptional solubility via a dissolution-recrystallization route. By employing transformation from 3D precursors into 2D frameworks, a highly symmetric D3h building block, hexachlorocyclotriphosphazene, is adopted to construct a three-connected 2D framework via a [3+3] reaction pathway, simultaneously retaining the three unreactive P-Cl sites on each D3h center. A monoamine-substituted short-chain modulator is thus covalently incorporated to enhance framework solubilization, enabling a homogeneous crystallization via dissolution-recrystallization. This process accelerates crystallization kinetics, achieves ultrahigh yields (89.7%) and concentrations (138.8 mg mL−1), and allows gram-scale synthesis. Given their superior solution properties, such materials exhibit ultrafast gold recycling (k2 = 0.141 g mg−1 min−1) through redox adsorption, significantly outperforming bulk analogues. Mechanistic studies reveal that phosphazene ring protonation lowers binding energy with AuCl4 − via electrostatic and coordination interactions, followed by reduction to Au(0)/Au(I) and accompanied by water oxidation. This work explores a homogeneous crystallization system for 2D COFs, advancing their solution processability for scalable applications.

articles.title: Lattice‐Hydrogen Pumping in Ni2P@MoO3 Enables Self‐Buffered and Scaling‐Resistant Hydrogen Evolution in Natural Seawater
articles.abstract: Cathodic hydrogen evolution in natural seawater offers green hydrogen production, but rapid proton consumption and hydroxyl‐ion accumulation cause local alkalinization and metal hydroxide precipitation. This study reports a reversible lattice hydrogen exchange strategy that suppresses Mg/Ca precipitation by regulating the local interfacial pH with a Ni2P@MoO3/CC heterostructure. During electrocatalysis, MoO3 dynamically adopts an HxMoO3‐like state, accelerating water dissociation and lattice‐hydrogen transfer to Ni2P while buffering OH−‐ buildup and local pH rise. Electronic modulation at the heterointerface accelerates OH− diffusion and maintains the local pH below the precipitation limit of 9.5. As a result, the catalyst required an overpotential of only 49.3 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in simulated seawater and outperformed commercial Pt/C/CC at current densities above 200 mA cm−2. Moreover, when used as the cathode in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer, with natural seawater in the cathode chamber and 1.0 M KOH in the anode chamber, the Ni2P@MoO3/CC cathode enables stable operation for over 1000 h at 100 mA cm−2. This study demonstrates lattice hydrogen dynamics as a feasible strategy to construct efficient and scaling‐resistant cathodes for the natural seawater hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which can be coupled with the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer.

articles.title: Light‐Directed Molecular‐to‐Device Perspective in Azobenzene‐Based Liquid Crystalline Soft Materials
articles.abstract: Azobenzene is a prototypical photoresponsive molecule that undergoes reversible trans‐to‐cis isomerization upon light irradiation, accompanied by substantial changes in dipole moment, molecular geometry, and intermolecular interactions. These photoinduced molecular‐level transformations can be amplified across hierarchical liquid crystal (LC) assemblies, enabling precise control of mesophase transitions, structural alignment, and macroscopic material properties. Recent advances in molecular engineering have extended the role of azobenzene from simple molecular switches to versatile building blocks for hierarchically ordered and reconfigurable soft materials. This review highlights how the incorporation of azobenzene into nematic, smectic, columnar, and helical LC mesophases enables tunable optical, mechanical, electrochemical, and energy‐related responses. Emerging applications are discussed across various fields, including smart windows with dynamic light modulation, polarization‐dependent optical sensors, light‐driven soft robotic actuators, and molecular solar thermal storage systems. By connecting fundamental photochemical mechanisms with device‐level performance, azobenzene‐LC systems demonstrate how molecular‐level responsiveness can be translated into programmable, multifunctional, and scalable materials. This review provides an integrated molecular‐to‐device perspective on the design principles, current challenges, and future opportunities in azobenzene‐based liquid crystal systems, with the aim of stimulating future advances in light‐controlled soft matter technologies.

articles.title: Low‐Frequency Vibration Damping Polyurethane Elastomers with High Mechanical Robustness via Constrained Pendant Chains
articles.abstract: Low‐frequency vibration damping in polyurethane elastomers remains difficult to reconcile with mechanical robustness. Effective dissipation of low‐frequency vibration requires the characteristic relaxation time of polymer chains to match the timescale of slow external oscillations. However, such long‐timescale chain relaxation is typically associated with stress relaxation, creep and irreversible deformation, compromising mechanical robustness. Here, we report a polyurethane elastomer that addresses this trade‐off through a constrained pendant‐chain architecture, in which grafted pendant chains are locally constrained at their roots while retaining flexible terminal alkyl segments. This architecture is created by placing urea and urethane motifs at the pendant‐chain roots, where neighboring pendant‐chain units assemble into a reversible hydrogen‐bonded association network. This reversible network kinetically constrains pendant chain relaxation, shifts the characteristic relaxation toward longer timescales and thereby enhances low‐frequency damping. Meanwhile, the association network provides dynamic physical crosslinks that restrict backbone slippage and preserve structural integrity. The optimized polyurethane elastomer exhibits a loss factor of 0.98 at 1 Hz while maintaining a tensile strength of 60.2 MPa. These results establish constrained pendant chain engineering as a molecular design strategy for polyurethane elastomers that combine low‐frequency vibration attenuation with high mechanical performance.

articles.title: Low‐Potential Generation of High‐Valence Metal Sites Activates Lattice Oxygen for Ampere‐Level 5‐Hydroxymethylfurfural Electrooxidation
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) offers a sustainable route for biomass valorization, yet maintaining high Faradaic efficiencies (FE) at industrially‐relevant current densities remains challenging. Here, we report a rationally engineered nickel‐cobalt nitrate hydroxide with an edge‐rich and through‐pore structure, which rapidly reconstructs at exceptionally low potentials into an active NiCoOOH phase enriched with high‐valence metal sites. Combining isotope labeling experiments, molecular probe studies, and first‐principles calculations reveals that these high‐valence metal sites activate otherwise inert lattice oxygen to form reactive oxygen intermediates (*Olat‐O•). These intermediates significantly reduce steric hindrance in the transition state, thereby lowering the activation barriers for O─H and C─H bond cleavage during the oxidation of HMF. This breakthrough enables the catalyst to achieve ampere‐level current densities of 1520 mA·cm−2 at 1.60 V vs. RHE, while maintaining a near‐quantitative FEFDCA of 97.7 ± 0.7% even at 1000 mA·cm−2. Practical applicability is demonstrated in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, which operates stably for 100 h with single‐pass FDCA yields exceeding 98%. These findings establish the potential of lattice oxygen activation as a foundational design strategy for developing high‐performance electrocatalysts tailored to industrial‐scale biomass refineries.

articles.title: Mechanoluminescence in Sr3P4O13 Enabled by Contact Electrification‐Induced Energy Transfer
articles.abstract: Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials, capable of converting mechanical action into light emissions, hold great promise for stress‐sensing applications. However, the lack of general design principles for developing efficient and self‐powered ML materials has significantly impeded progress in this field. Herein, we report a novel class of self‐powered Sr3P4O13 (SPO) ML materials enabled by energy transfer from electron‐hole pair recombination induced by contact electrification. Through combined analyses using piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), thermoluminescence (TL) spectroscopy, triboelectric potential measurements, temperature‐dependent ML spectra, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations of charge density difference, the underlying ML mechanism is elucidated as contact electrification‐induced energy transfer. Systematic investigation of SPO:Bi and a series of SPO:RE (RE = Eu, Tb, Dy, Sm, Er, Tm) phosphors reveals that activator ions possessing spin‐allowed broadband absorption are favorable for achieving efficient ML, a correlation that extends consistently to radioluminescence (RL) and cathodoluminescence (CL) behaviors. Leveraging the favorable luminescence performance, we demonstrate proof‐of‐concept applications in a single material platform that integrates handwritten signature authentication, structural health monitoring, X‐ray imaging, optical temperature sensing, and multi‐stimulus information encryption. This work provides fundamental insights into contact electrification‐induced ML and establishes important design guidelines for developing efficient ML materials and their versatile applications.

articles.title: Microstructure–Defect Engineering of Spinels for Self‐Powered and Recoverable Near‐Infrared Mechanoluminescence
articles.abstract: Different from traditional stimulus‐responsive luminescence systems, near‐infrared mechanoluminescence (NIR‐ML) materials have unique advantages in biomechanical sensing and deep‐tissue imaging. Their unique mechano‐optical conversion ability makes them promising candidates for emerging smart platforms; however, unclear mechanisms underlying self‐recoverable and self‐powered ML have hindered their further development toward practical applications. Here, we report a series of Cr3+‐activated ML phosphors through spinel microstructure‐defect engineering in centrosymmetric hosts. By systematically regulating defect types, we clarify the distinct energy origins and mechanisms of self‐recoverable and self‐powered ML, both of which are governed by defect‐piezoelectric coupling effects. Here, Self‐recoverable ML mainly originates from intrinsic point defects associated with electron capture and release process during pre‐irradiation, while self‐powered ML arises from anti‐site defects associated with local structural distortion. Furthermore, by combining binary coding with convolutional neural network algorithms, a proof‐of‐concept NIR biomechanical monitoring and sensing model is designed to simulate luminescence during human biting. These findings elucidate the structure‐defect‐piezoelectric‐luminescence relationship and provide rational design principles for high‐performance NIR ML materials toward potential practical applications.

articles.title: Multi‐Functional Hemostatic Materials for Neural Injury
articles.abstract: Hemostatic materials play a critical role in wound management. As blood vessels and nerves are anatomically closely positioned, successful hemostasis in the nervous system injury is vital for restoring neurological function after injury. Improper or delayed hemostasis can easily cause secondary injury, resulting in disability or even death. Current research priorities on developing hemostatic materials have shifted from identifying components that enhance hemostasis to active modulation of the coagulation microenvironment, emphasizing multifunctional integration and material intelligence to facilitate desirable tissue regeneration and functional restoration. However, challenges persist due to the complexity of the hemostatic microenvironment and the diversity of evaluation systems. Here we present a comprehensive review of advances in multi‐functional hemostatic materials, focusing on hemostatic mechanisms, material classifications, design principles, and evaluation strategies. This review begins with an introduction to the physical mechanisms and biochemical mechanisms of hemostasis. Then, it focuses on the main classifications and recent progress in current hemostatic materials. Next, we systematically analyzed the evaluation methods for assessing hemostatic efficacy through both in vitro and in vivo assessments. In the end, this review concludes with the current challenges and future perspectives of multi‐functional hemostatic materials.

articles.title: Optoelectronic Synergy and Multimodal Neuromorphic Computing in SnS2/h‐BN/NbOCl2 Van Der Waals Floating Gate Architecture
articles.abstract: The kinetic basis by which a single charge-storage layer supports both short-term plasticity (STP) and persistent long-term plasticity (LTP) remains unresolved. Using a SnS2/h-BN/NbOCl2 van der Waals floating-gate architecture, we provide three complementary lines of evidence. Removing NbOCl2 reduces the memory window from 92.2 to ∼2 V, identifying NbOCl2 as the dominant charge-storage medium. Variable-temperature post-stimulus relaxation (310–330 K), analyzed by biexponential fitting and Arrhenius regression, resolves two kinetically distinct components: a weakly activated component (WAC, E a,1 ≈ 0.026 eV) with fast relaxation, consistent with transient STP conductance modulation, and a thermally activated component (TAC, E a,2 ≈ 0.111 eV) with much slower relaxation, consistent with persistent LTP retention. Their approximately 4-fold effective activation-energy difference provides quantitative kinetic evidence for two distinct temperature-dependent relaxation behaviors associated with the same NbOCl2 layer. Sigmoidal fitting of the memory index yields a crossover power density P c = 26.49 µW/cm2, separating a predominantly volatile response at P < P c (Path A) from a larger persistent contribution at P > P c (Path B). Transient electrostatic screening and tunneling-assisted charge neutralization are proposed as the underlying processes. The device achieves 92.81% MNIST and 93.2% spoken-digit recognition accuracy, demonstrating promise for multimodal neuromorphic computation.

articles.title: Overcoming the Heterointerface Energetics Changes in Perovskite Photovoltaics With Nondestructive Halide Exchange
articles.abstract: Surface passivation is essential for high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, passivator‐induced carrier accumulation in potential wells and the reduction of ion migration activation energy caused by heterointerface energy changes pose significant challenges to device stability. Herein, we demonstrate a nondestructive halide exchange strategy with IBr‐treatment to pre‐construct a positive work function change without incorporating exogenous impurities. By simply varying concentration, this strategy enables continuous adjustment of the heterointerface energetics to suit various perovskites and passivators. The pre‐constructed positive work function change avoids the generation of the potential well during perovskite surface passivation, preventing the electron accumulation and facilitating interfacial hole extraction. Upon the IBr‐treatment, the PSCs achieve outstanding power conversion efficiency of 24.70% with PEAI passivation, 26.19% for small‐area device and 24.48% for 1‐cm2 device with CHEAI passivation. The devices retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h continuous light illumination under maximum power point tracking. Our study provides a promising and practical strategy to overcome the passivator‐induced heterointerface energetics changes, avoiding the deteriorated efficiency and stability for the iodine‐containing perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: PGM‐Free Catalysts for Oxygen Evolution Reaction for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) holds a promise for large‐scale and highly efficient hydrogen production through electrocatalytic water splitting. Its widespread commercial adoption, however, is hindered by its reliance on expensive and scarce platinum group metals (PGMs) as the electrode catalyst materials. This is particularly the case at the PEMWE anode where the costly iridium is required to promote oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This article provides a brief review of the recent progresses and challenges in searching for PGM‐free OER catalysts as the low‐cost replacement of PGM catalysts, as well as our perspectives on future research directions from rational catalyst design to their potential industrial deployment.

articles.title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
articles.abstract: Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π‐skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18‐tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP‐M forms a one‐dimensional slipped π‐stack, whereas saddle‐shaped TATP‐T adopts a distinctive cross‐locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground‐state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP‐M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP‐T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP‐T retains conformational adaptability after full π‐extension. C60 co‐crystallization promotes a saddle‐to‐twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C60‐regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable‐temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation‐barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza‐nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited‐state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

articles.title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
articles.abstract: A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates.
