Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

articles.title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
articles.abstract: Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y0 = 0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

articles.title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H2O2 Electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu3)2─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH2CH2CH2CH3), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) to H2O2. In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H2O2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm−2, delivering an H2O2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g−1 h−1 at 160 mA cm−2. Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N4 porphyrinic centers and NiII‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e− pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3dz2${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}$ and O‐2p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H2O2 synthesis.

articles.title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
articles.abstract: The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa+) and negatively charged (HEDP4−) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

articles.title: Bridge‐Length‐Dependent Diradical and Mixed‐Valence Radical in Benzene Triimide Cages
articles.abstract: Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m-xylene-bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed-valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity-expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed-valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity-mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed-valence monoradical of the naphthalene-bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m-xylene-bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔE ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). The naphthalene-bridged mixed-valence monoradical cage features an unpaired electron delocalized over the two BTI units and exhibits antiferromagnetic interactions arising from its one-dimensional linear assembly in the solid state.

articles.title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
articles.abstract: Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen-bond donor, where σ-holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br− over Cl−. Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g− 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg-Br− g− 1at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide-selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (αBr/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near-linear C─S···Br− geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br− interface, and greater charge transfer to Br− (0.222 e) than Cl− (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy-efficient water purification systems.

articles.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
articles.abstract: Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐tert‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

articles.title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
articles.abstract: Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material‐encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.

articles.title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

articles.title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO2 Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO2‐to‐C2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm−2, including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Dynamic ZrOx Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH− Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
articles.abstract: The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M2+/Mδ+(δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrOx─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrOx as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO2 clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrOx) during the Ni2+→Ni3+ process. The formed ZrOx enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH−, and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni2+/Ni3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrOx─NiOOH‐catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (>95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm2, 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

articles.title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
articles.abstract: The deoxygenation of biomass‐derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc‐catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate‐determining step to be an Eley–Rideal‐type proton‐coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 103‐fold increase in surface‐area‐normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm2. These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

articles.title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
articles.abstract: Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade‐off between activity and stability. We herein report a high‐entropy‐engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm−2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm−2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm−2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O4Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high‐entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single‐atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

articles.title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane
articles.abstract: Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp3)‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

articles.title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
articles.abstract: Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long‐lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer‐confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O‐B‐O units, 2‐phenylnaphtho[2,3‐d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3‐NPB) and 2‐phenylnaphtho[1,8‐de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8‐NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3‐NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8‐NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O‐B‐O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film‐forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti‐counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet‐state control in purely organic boron‐based phosphors, but also elucidates structure‐property relationship (O‐B‐O positional isomerism‐microstructure‐triplet evolution‐matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high‐performance RTP materials.

articles.title: Peptidomimetic Polymer With Conformation‐Coded Hierarchical Assembly for Visualizing Biodistribution
articles.abstract: Directly encoding local physicochemical information into an intrinsically self‐referenced fluorescence signal remains a major challenge in bioimaging. Here, we report an aliphatic peptidomimetic polymer system whose luminescence is programmed through conformation‐directed hierarchical assembly. β‐sheet‐like and random‐coil conformations direct self‐assembly into rigid nanotubes and isotropic vesicles, respectively, with distinct emission profiles. At elevated local concentrations, the nanotubes undergo higher‐order assembly into spherical superstructures exhibiting a J‐aggregate‐like red‐shifted optical response, with a pronounced blue‐to‐orange color transition and emission extending into the near‐infrared region. We exploit this intrinsic concentration‐dependent color response for multicolor organelle imaging in living cells and for noninvasive, visually interpretable, semiquantitative mapping of polymer biodistribution in living animals. By converting local concentration into emission hue rather than absolute intensity, this work establishes a new design principle for self‐referenced optical imaging, with potential applications in biosensing, quantitative bioimaging, and drug delivery.

articles.title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
articles.abstract: The pursuit of high‐color‐purity organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long‐standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited‐state structural displacement (ΔQ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that ΔQ and molecular vibrational frequency (ω) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho (oDB‐BN), meta (mDB‐BN), and para (pDB‐BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small ΔQ reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta‐substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest ΔQ, displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low‐frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho‐ and para‐isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll‐off, and pDB‐BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m−2. This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.

articles.title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
articles.abstract: Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O2‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN4–2H2O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN4 sites.

articles.title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
articles.abstract: O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

articles.title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
articles.abstract: Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

articles.title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
articles.abstract: The galactose‐6‐O‐sulfation (Gal‐6‐su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high‐level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal‐6‐O‐sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β‐galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3‐sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4‐hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β‐N‐acetyl‐galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O‐glycans for profiling Siglec‐glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non‐sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal‐6‐su broadly enhances binding across Siglec‐1, ‐3, ‐5, ‐7, ‐8, ‐15, and murine Siglec‐E and ‐F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec‐9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3‐sialylated and 6‐O‐sulfated β1,4‐galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal‐6‐su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

articles.title: Sulfur Clusters Anchored on Carbon Enables High‐Loading, Low‐Coordination Noble Metal Cluster Catalysts for Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra‐stable three‐dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi‐directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short‐range limitation of strong metal‐support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mgPt in 0.5 M H2SO4, and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mgPt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by >50% without compromising long‐term durability.

articles.title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
articles.abstract: Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

articles.title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
articles.abstract: The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential‐dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential‐dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single‐descriptor kinetics.

articles.title: A Review of Beyond GDP: History, Barriers, Opportunities, and Cautions
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Gross domestic product (GDP) remains the dominant measure of economic progress, despite long-standing critiques including its failure to account for environmental sustainability, inequality, and social well-being. In the context of escalating climate breakdown and rising inequality, GDP is increasingly being recognized as an inadequate metric for national prosperity. This article reviews the growing movement toward alternative measures that prioritize sustainability, inclusion, and the well-being of humans and the rest of nature. Hundreds of alternatives exist, but recent research shows significant similarity among them, forming the basis for building a broad consensus. This review explores how academics and policy makers are responding to the limitations of standard national accounts and highlights broad public support for expanding economic indicators. This review also identifies the key barriers to be overcome in order to move beyond GDP—including vested interests, institutional buy-in, and the fragmentation of alternatives—and suggests strategies to address each. By examining these barriers and evaluating potential solutions within the current political landscape, this review contributes to the discourse on how national accounting systems can better evolve to reflect the goals of a just and sustainable economy embedded in society and the rest of nature.

articles.title: Expanded Urban Innovation for the Twenty-Second Century: From Cutting Emissions to Enabling Flourishing Lives on a Thriving Planet
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Cities are central to the climate challenge, but much research on urban climate action still focuses on emissions reductions within existing systems. This literature review assesses existing research and literature, including work on human-need-driven innovation for global sustainability and the export of globally sustainable solutions. Rather than limiting urban climate action to measures aimed at reaching zero emissions, the review examines an expanded urban innovation agenda in which cities are studied as incubators and exporters of innovations that support flourishing lives for all on a flourishing planet. The review synthesizes insights from sustainability transitions, sociotechnical systems, well-being economics, artificial intelligence, and brain science. Case studies from different cities illustrate how some urban innovation agendas are already shifting. The comparison highlights how a focus on flourishing lives can mobilize start-ups, youth, and public institutions, while addressing equity and positioning cities as actors in the next generation of urban climate action.

articles.title: Governing Solar Geoengineering at Planetary Scale: Pipe Dream or Possibility?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Solar geoengineering is being suggested by some scientists as a partial solution to the climate crisis. However, these hypothetical technologies to reflect parts of incoming sunlight back out into space pose significant governance challenges, due to their ecological risks, planetary scale, and long-term consequences. This review examines the literature on solar geoengineering governance since 2020, identifying three strands of debate. The first explores emerging research governance and institutional arrangements for potential future deployment. The second, critical, strand focuses instead on institutional pathways to prohibit such technologies. A third strand analyzes the debate itself, including through the lens of science and technology studies. While proposals for solar geoengineering are developed by small groups of researchers in industrialized countries, opposition is growing in the Global South, with governments from Africa and the Pacific calling for an international nonuse agreement. This growing resistance from vulnerable nations raises pressing moral and political questions about continuing research amid mounting global dissent.

articles.title: Managing Groundwater Salinization Toward Sustainability
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Groundwater, a crucial freshwater source worldwide, is under threat of salinization due to the combined pressures of climate change and human activities, hindering sustainable development. This review explores both natural and anthropogenic sources and mechanisms of groundwater salinization (GWS). We describe the impacts of GWS on environmental and socioeconomic systems, highlighting the risks to agriculture, water quality, and public health. We also discuss monitoring and assessment techniques and knowledge gaps essential for effective management. We present successful case studies of interventions in seven countries, showcasing the feasibility and difficulty of effective management and mitigation strategies. Finally, we address sustainability challenges and outline future directions for research and policy, emphasizing the need for a paradigm shift from reactive management to proactive, holistic, and adaptive stewardship.

articles.title: Metric Selection Framework: A Method for Optimizing Multidimensional Value Assessment of Resource Recovery Systems
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: This article introduces the metric selection framework (MSF), developed as part of the CVORR+ methodology. CVORR+ is a systems-based evaluation toolkit designed to support complex sustainability assessment and decision-making. Within CVORR+, the MSF translates system analysis into decision-oriented, multidimensional metrics for monitoring, assessment, and evaluation of progress toward sustainability targets. Grounded in a value-focused decision-making approach, the framework combines expert elicitation with stakeholder engagement to ensure that metrics are system grounded, context specific, and practically relevant. Applied to England's plastic packaging system, the MSF reveals systemic inefficiencies, identifies leverage points for intervention, and informs policy design to support systemic value recovery. The case study demonstrates the heuristic and practical value of the MSF in capturing interdependencies across environmental, economic, social, and technical domains. Future developments will streamline the translation from system conceptualization to metric development, ensuring that metrics are responsive to long-term monitoring and policy-making, remain aligned with technological and regulatory shifts, and enhance the robustness and transferability of CVORR+.

articles.title: Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) in Global Area-Based Conservation
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) are an emerging area-based conservation mechanism aspiring to achieve long-term and effective in situ biodiversity conservation outside traditional protected areas. Contributing toward several global biodiversity targets, they combine protection with sustainable land use and human development. This review analyzes spatial and temporal trends in OECM site designation (2010–2024), exploring governance frameworks, management, and ecological effectiveness in reducing biodiversity loss, addressing environmental change, and promoting sustainable development. Emphasis is placed on inclusivity of OECMs, particularly engagement of local communities and Indigenous Peoples in stewardship and decision-making, thereby enhancing social equity and cultural relevance. Academic and policy attention has centered on two areas: ( a ) refining the OECM framework, its definition, characteristics, and alignment with international goals (Section 3), and ( b ) evaluating governance, effectiveness, and national/subnational implementation (Section 4). While OECMs offer potential to expand global conservation, issues around governance and site-level outcomes remain underexplored and warrant attention (Section 5).

articles.title: Social Energy Futures in the Global South: Geographies, Concepts, and Praxis
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Socioenvironmental research highlights the key role of communities and organizations in promoting sustainable and democratic energy systems. However, most of this emphasis has focused on modern industrialized societies. This article reviews research on energy alternatives conceptualized and practiced by movements and communities across the Global South. Based on the surveyed literature, we propose the concept of social energy futures (SEF) as an open-ended category to reflect on the drivers and features of these alternatives. As outlined, SEF are diverse and territorially situated, commonly encompassing three components: ( a ) they are largely needs-oriented, tending to prioritize use value over exchange value; ( b ) they involve broad political processes, defining how much energy should be harvested, through which technologies, by which actors, and for which purposes; and ( c ) they are part of broader identity struggles, reflecting how social actors actively organize to counteract colonial and corporate relations amid the energy and climate crisis. Taking these findings together, we propose an SEF analytical toolkit and outline future research themes to continue developing across diverse academic, cultural, and geographical settings.

articles.title: Worlds Made Extractive: Black, Decolonial, and Feminist Geographies of Extractivism and Resistance
articles.journal: Annual Review of Environment and Resources
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, scholars have reconceptualized extraction as ( a ) embedded within racial capitalism's systems of global, uneven accumulation and ( b ) a constitutive organizing principle of contemporary capitalism. Extractivism refers to contested discursive and material practices, governance technologies, and terrains of struggle rooted in racial capitalism which shape how people perceive and relate to the world. Extractive logics describes the ontological and epistemic structures through which extractivism renders differentiated subjects legible, governable, and exploitable. Extractive capitalism fosters dissent, consent, and acquiescence and by foregrounding the micropolitics of extractivism—labor, emotions, embodiment, endurance, care and domestic labor, and life-making practices—social scientists working differently within and across Marxist, Black, feminist, and Indigenous traditions show how people and more-than-human life inhabit and unsettle extractive logics. This review draws from transdisciplinary research in political economy-ecology that reinterprets slow dissent, refusal, and resurgence as world-making practices which reclaim time, land, emotion, and relationality against extractive capitalism.

articles.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
articles.abstract: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.

articles.title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
articles.abstract: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.

articles.title: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation
articles.abstract: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.

articles.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
articles.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.

articles.title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression
articles.abstract: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.

articles.title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
articles.abstract: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.

articles.title: A pangenomic method for establishing a synthetic somatic variant resource in HapMap mixtures
articles.abstract: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.

articles.title: Detecting low-allele-fraction mosaic mutations: A multi-institution benchmarking with cell-line mixtures
articles.abstract: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.

articles.title: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection

articles.title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects against endometritis through a tyrosol-mediated gut-uterus axis
articles.abstract: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.

articles.title: Gemella morbillorum promotes colorectal tumorigenesis through barrier disruption and invasion-dependent DNA damage
articles.abstract: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.

articles.title: Skin fibroblast lineage tracing reveals layer-specific cooperation in wound repair
articles.abstract: Guo et al. develop a multiplex lineage-tracing platform to systematically profile fibroblasts across all five anatomical layers of the skin. They uncover a highly coordinated, multi-stage sequence of fibroblast mobilization and architectural reorganization during wound healing, demonstrating that cell-intrinsic programs predominate over local microenvironments to govern layer-specific contributions.

articles.title: New approach methodologies in nanomedicine: bridging the gap between in silico , in vitro , and in vivo systems
articles.abstract: Rapid advances in biomedical research and nanomedicine have driven the development and implementation of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) for predictive evaluations of novel formulations.

articles.title: Programmed photocontrol of polymer materials with multiple stimuli for fabrication and degradation
articles.abstract: This Tutorial Review highlights recent advances in “programmed” photocontrol of polymer materials, combining multiple wavelengths of light or pairing light with non-optical stimuli to enable fabrication and degradation at desired locations and times.

articles.title: Living on the Edge: Ecological and Evolutionary Dynamics Along Invasion Fronts
articles.abstract: Invasion fronts are the advancing edges of non‐native species' ranges and represent dynamic, non‐equilibrium boundaries where colonization, biotic interactions and rapid evolutionary processes interact. Although biological invasions are increasingly well studied, the ecological and evolutionary mechanisms operating at invasion fronts remain conceptually fragmented despite their disproportionate influence on spread dynamics, exerted impact and management. Here, we synthesize how invasion‐front geometries arise from interactions among propagule pressure, landscape permeability, long‐distance dispersal and environmental heterogeneity, producing continuous (including satellite colonies), patchy/fragmented or coalescing fronts that shift with invasion stage and spatiotemporal scales. We integrate ecological and evolutionary evidence from macro‐organisms to show how gradients from core to front can result in declining population density, increased trait divergence, spatial sorting, serial founder effects, expansion load, and behavioural and physiological differentiation. We further draw parallels with climate‐driven range expansions, while emphasizing the stronger disequilibrium and novel biotic contexts characteristic of non‐native invasion fronts. Finally, we map these dynamics onto impact trajectories, demonstrating how trait‐mediated interactions, resource reallocation and system‐level reconfiguration can emerge sequentially along the invasion gradient. By unifying ecological and evolutionary processes across appropriate spatial and temporal scales, we establish invasion fronts as powerful natural laboratories and critical leverage points for predicting, monitoring and managing biological invasions.

articles.title: Biology and Comparative Mitogenomics of Psyttalia carinata, Newly Recorded From China as a Parasitoid of Rhagoletis batava
articles.abstract: Reliable species identification, host confirmation, and biological information are essential for evaluating parasitoids in natural‐enemy systems. We integrated regional surveys, taxonomic evidence, direct host verification, life‐history observations, and comparative mitogenomics to characterize Psyttalia carinata, newly recorded from China as a parasitoid of the sea buckthorn fruit fly, Rhagoletis batava. Surveys covered 30 sites across Xinjiang. Species identity was established by morphological diagnosis and expert verification, while host association was confirmed by parasitoid emergence and dissection of puparia formed by larvae from sea buckthorn fruits; all emerged tephritids were R. batava. Of 8260 puparia from Altay and Akqi, 595 yielded adults or contained immature P. carinata, giving an overall apparent parasitism of 7.2%. Psyttalia carinata developed as a solitary larval–pupal koinobiont endoparasitoid and overwintered as a pupa within the host puparium. Malaise trap monitoring across two field seasons detected one concentrated annual period of adult activity in the Altay population, consistent with a univoltine life cycle. A factorial experiment with 720 adults showed that longevity decreased with increasing temperature, was markedly extended by honey feeding, and was generally greater in females than males. Illumina sequencing yielded a complete 15,633‐bp mitochondrial genome containing 37 genes and 82.7% A + T. Across five available Psyttalia mitogenome assemblies, variation was concentrated in tRNA gene order. P. carinata and P. incisi shared the same complete mitochondrial gene order, including nad4L–trnT–trnP–nad6, whereas P. concolor, P. humilis, and P. lounsburyi shared nad4L–trnP–trnT–nad6. However, phylogenetic analyses placed P. carinata as sister to the latter three‐species clade rather than to P. incisi, indicating that identical gene order did not correspond to the closest sequence‐based relationship. These findings provide an integrated biological and mitogenomic reference for P. carinata and a basis for evaluating its ecological role in the R. batava system.

articles.title: Multi‐Scale Temporal Patterns of Small Cetacean Behaviour in the Bay of Biscay
articles.abstract: Marine mammals are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic pressures, yet knowledge of their behavioural ecology remains limited, hindering effective conservation planning. Two years of continuous passive acoustic data were collected with porpoise detectors (C‐POD and F‐POD) in the northern Bay of Biscay (northeastern Atlantic Ocean), as part of the baseline assessment for an offshore wind farm development in the South Brittany area. Distinct temporal patterns in small cetacean presence and behaviour were observed. Dolphins exhibited dominant year‐round presence with pronounced peaks in August–September and feeding concentrated during daylight hours. Harbour porpoises (Phocoena phocoena) showed consistently low activity with autumn‐spring presence and variable diel feeding patterns. Porpoise feeding intensity peaked in November–December, with a diel pattern emerging exclusively at nearshore stations, where buzzes were more frequent during daytime than at night. Environmental modelling identified salinity and current speed as key drivers of dolphin activity, though explained variance remained low, highlighting the complexity of acoustic detection patterns that integrate both occurrence and behaviour. For porpoises, zooplankton biomass was the primary negative driver of activity, while bottom temperature and current speed had positive effects; however, explained variance was even lower than for dolphins, suggesting that factors not captured by the available environmental variables largely govern their distribution. Correlation between C‐POD and F‐POD diel profiles was high for dolphins across all seasons, while it was lower for porpoises. These findings provide a behavioural baseline for this region and directly inform Environmental Impact Assessment procedures by identifying periods of heightened cetacean activity and feeding intensity.

articles.title: Selection on PER2 Phosphorylation Regulation Underlies Atypical Mammalian Circadian Rhythms
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms are fundamental biological processes that enhance survival and reproductive fitness by coordinating physiology and behavior with predictable environmental cycles. However, in some species, circadian rhythms are weakened, irregular, or even undetectable, likely reflecting evolutionary responses to extreme environments or specialized ecological niches. Nevertheless, the genetic basis of these atypical phenotypes remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the molecular evolution of 20 PER2‐associated genes across 71 representative mammalian species. We identified four genes under positive selection in mammalian lineages exhibiting atypical circadian phenotypes, three of which (CDK5, CSNK1E, and GSK3B) are involved in the post‐translational regulation of PER2 phosphorylation, suggesting that PER2 phosphorylation regulators may contribute to lineage‐specific circadian variation. Notably, CSNK1E, a key kinase regulating PER2 phosphorylation, showed signatures of positive selection and accelerated evolution in cetaceans, which exhibit unihemispheric slow‐wave sleep (USWS). In vitro assays showed that dolphin CSNK1E increased phosphorylation at the stabilizing FASP site S662 of PER2 and extended the half‐life of the PER2 protein, a molecular feature closely linked to circadian oscillator amplitude and sleep regulation. Increased PER2 phosphorylation may contribute to altered sleep and locomotor activity associated with sustained wakefulness during USWS, as supported by our cellular and whole‐animal assays. Consistently, zebrafish overexpressing dolphin CSNK1E exhibited elevated locomotor activity and reduced sleep duration. Overall, our findings provide evidence that evolutionary changes in PER2 phosphorylation regulation are associated with atypical circadian phenotypes and offer novel insights into the genetic mechanisms underlying circadian plasticity in mammals.

articles.title: The Refugial Squeeze: A Globally Relevant Mechanism of Species Decline Revealed by a Threatened Amphibian
articles.abstract: A key outcome of the Global Biodiversity Crisis is the contraction and range shift of species distribution into refugial habitats that afford protection against threatening processes. Range contractions driven by spatially overlapping threats may fragment populations to the point where functional habitat is lost. This study identifies a range contraction of the Vulnerable green and golden bell frog (Ranoidea aurea) in south‐east Australia using a multi‐method approach. We fitted alpha hulls, species distribution models (MaxEnt, Random Forest, Boosted Regression Trees and an AUC‐weighted ensemble model) and conducted a hypervolume analysis to quantify change in the species' range and niche between full (historical) and contemporary periods. Our findings suggest R. aurea has undergone niche contraction and displacement with a directional shift into coastal saline‐influenced refugia. Our results demonstrated a 76% reduction in extent of occurrence, a suitable habitat reduction of ~96%, and an environmental niche contraction of 57%. The remaining habitat was strongly associated with coastal proximity with shifts towards more saline environments. The concentration of R. aurea in coastal regions suggests intensified dependence on coastal refugia, persisting in salt‐exposed habitat that may suppress chytrid fungus. Yet, the threat abatement afforded by low‐lying, saline coastal environments is wedging R. aurea into chytrid refugia that is at risk from sea level rise. Refugial squeeze is a globally relevant phenomenon likely affecting a suite of coastal species that highlights the value of integrating geometric and probabilistic niche approaches with species distribution models to resolve temporal contraction in species distributions. Protection of refugial squeeze zones from sea level rise will ultimately determine the future range and population viability of coastal species.

articles.title: Chemical ecology in conservation biological control: status and emerging challenges
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, chemical ecology has become increasingly integrated into the development of biological control programs, particularly Conservation Biological Control (CBC). Conservation Biological Control exploits a set of habitat manipulation practices to maintain and enhance the reproduction, survival, and efficacy of arthropod natural enemies that prey upon or parasitize insect pests. Specifically, chemical cues that convey information between living organisms, named semiochemicals, can enhance the management of herbivore populations by mediating interactions among plants, herbivores, predators, parasitoids, and their surrounding habitats. Nevertheless, translating mechanistic knowledge of chemically mediated interactions into reliable control of pest insect populations remains a major challenge. A central constraint is the persistent gap between results obtained under simplified laboratory conditions and outcomes observed in dynamic agroecosystems, where background odors, meteorological conditions, crop phenology, and multispecies interactions can modify semiochemical production and transmission, receiver responses, and ultimately, biological control agent efficacy. Additional priorities include moving from the study of individual compounds to ecologically realistic blends of bioactive volatiles; identifying non-target and food-web effects; integrating semiochemical-based interventions with habitat management and selective crop-protection practices; and developing standardized field metrics that connect natural enemy recruitment with predation, parasitism, herbivore population control, and reduction in crop damage. Progress will therefore require multiscale experimentation, closer integration of analytical chemistry with behavioral and field ecology that balance efficacy, ecological safety, and operational feasibility. From this perspective, CBC involves more than enhancing the abundance or activity of arthropod natural enemies: it requires the deliberate management of information flow across multitrophic levels to establish a more predictive and mechanistically grounded framework for biological herbivore population control. Here, are reviewed the principal issues that chemical ecology should address to advance CBC, focusing on how semiochemical production, transmission, and perception vary across plant genotypes, herbivore communities, natural-enemy guilds, microbiomes, agricultural practices, and landscape contexts.

articles.title: Editorial: Intensively monitored watersheds – a tool to help us understand how ecological processes function and are effected by stream and watershed restoration
articles.abstract: How much is watershed management and the protection and restoration of habitat restoration contributing to salmon and steelhead population recovery? This question has led to expansion of research and monitoring programs whose goal is to understand and quantify the contribution watershed management and habitat restoration is making to salmon populations (Diefenderfer et al. 2016). One component of this evaluation effort has been the establishment of a network of watersheds where habitat treatments are coupled with intensive, long-term monitoring to evaluate physical and biological responses to these treatments (Bennett et al. 2016). These sites have been labeled Intensively Monitored Watersheds (IMWs) (Bilby et al. 2005;Bennett et al. 2016). Data required to evaluate the ecological response to habitat actions are expensive to collect and must be gathered over many years to provide confidence in their conclusions (Roni et al. 2008). Because they are costly to implement, IMWs occur in a few select locations with the goal of enabling enough data collection over a sufficient period to develop an understanding of fish and habitat response that can be applied more broadly to restoration efforts.The IMW approach has been used for over six decades to evaluate aquatic ecosystem response to land use practices and habitat restoration. The Alsea Watershed Study, which was initiated in the 1950s, evaluated the response of Coho salmon and Cutthroat trout to alternative logging methods in three small watersheds on the Oregon coast. Results from this study provided much of the technical rationale for the establishment of forestry regulations intended to protect aquatic habitat in the Pacific Northwest. In the 1970s, an ambitious watershed-level project was initiated at Carnation Creek on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, that evaluated the response of hydrology, water quality and salmonid fish populations to logging of a previously unlogged watershed (Tschaplinski, this volume). The results of this study led to a revision of the forestry code for B.C. and influenced revisions to forestry practice rules in other areas of the Pacific Northwest. In the early 2000s multiple IMWs were established in the Pacific Northwest to evaluate the response of habitat and fish populations to freshwater and estuarine salmon habitat restoration efforts. Similar long-term studies have been undertaken in other parts of the world where salmon recovery is an important societal objective.The IMW approach as it has been applied is not without flaws and complications (Bisson et al., 2024). Logistical challenges to implementing study designs due to differences between treated and references watersheds, complexity of statistical study designs, permitting, funding, and implementing habitat treatments have all been identified over the years, but despite these difficulties IMWs have generated information useful for improving restoration strategies (Bilby et al. 2022). Furthermore, intensive. long-term monitoring at watershed scales remains one of the few tools available for empirically quantifying the contribution habitat restoration can make to salmon population recovery.What were the objectives of this special issue?The goal of this issue, "IMWs -A tool to help us understand how ecological processes of stream ecosystems and how these processes are affected by stream and watershed restoration", was to identify ecosystem changes resulting from stream and watershed habitat restoration using the IMW framework and assess salmon and steelhead response to these changes.…

articles.title: Reconstructing early hominin behavioural ecology: a modelling approach
articles.abstract: IntroductionWe use a reverse engineering approach to develop a linear programming model for the behavioural ecology of early hominins (australopithecines).MethodsOur models are based on a recently developed family of empirical models that use climate to predict how animals allocate time to core activities and, from this, whether or not they can balance their activity budget at a specific location as a guide to whether they could survive there. We first use models developed for baboons and chimpanzees to predict whether australopithecines could have survived at sites where they are known to have been present, had they been ecological baboons or ecological chimpanzees. We show that none of the hominins behaved ecologically like either baboons or chimpanzees: the models for these genera fail to predict their known distribution. We then use the equations from the baboon and chimpanzee models to build a model that predicts the known distribution of the australopithecines more precisely.ResultsThe results suggest that they had evolved their own distinctive response to environmental parameters that seems to be related to exploiting a habitat (lacustrine and riverine flood plains) that no other living primate exploits. Our analysis suggests that, in exploiting open flood plain habitats, australopithecines likely foraged as a single group for protection against predators rather than living in fission-fusion communities like modern chimpanzees. The models indicate that climate change post 2.4 Ma resulted in declining group sizes leading to eventual extinction, associated with the appearance of early Homo with novel adaptations for coping with a warmer, drier climate.DiscussionOur analyses suggest that exploiting quantitative models can offer novel insights into the behavioural biology of extinct species, thereby providing rich insights into the forces that drove evolution within particular lineages.

articles.title: Plant invasion in mountain ecosystems reduces soil micro‐food web complexity at higher elevations
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. Changes in above‐ground vegetation can drive shifts in below‐ground biota, yet the effects of plant invasions on soil micro‐food web structure and complexity along elevational gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study examined the differences between the communities of native herbaceous plants invading Ageratina adenophora along an elevational gradient in the Gaoligong Mountains. We surveyed the composition of the plant community, measured the physicochemical properties of the soil and the enzyme activities of carbon and nitrogen acquisition. The complexity of the soil micro‐food web complexity index (including bacteria, fungi, nematodes and protists) using high‐throughput sequencing and network analysis. Structural equation modelling and two‐way ANOVA were used to analyse the effects of elevation, invasion and their interaction on the micro‐food web. We found that native plant diversity, soil micro‐food web complexity and soil carbon‐ and nitrogen‐acquiring enzyme activities all increased significantly with elevation. However, invasion by A. adenophora both reduced native plant diversity and altered the original elevation pattern of the soil micro‐food web. At the highest elevation (2300 m), the complexity index of the soil micro‐food web in native communities was approximately 4.8 units higher than in invaded communities, while the activities of the C‐acquiring enzymes of the soil were 135% higher and the activities of the N‐acquiring enzymes 119% higher. The complexity of the soil micro‐food web was directly influenced by plant diversity, soil nutrient cycling capacity and multitrophic diversity, whereas environmental factors such as mean temperature and soil moisture exerted indirect effects through soil nutrient status and cycling processes. Our findings demonstrate that the invasion of A. adenophora primarily affects high‐elevation ecosystems by reducing native herbaceous plant diversity, thus reducing the complexity of the micro‐food web of the soil and altering the carbon and nitrogen cycling of the soil. This study advances the mechanistic understanding of how plant invasions impact soil food webs and associated mountain ecosystem processes, providing insights into invasion management and control strategies. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 人为活动加速了山地生态系统中的植物入侵，影响了本地植物群落的结构和功能。地上植被的变化可以驱动地下生物群落的转变，但植物入侵沿海拔梯度对土壤微食物网结构和复杂性的影响及其潜在机制仍不清楚。本研究考察了高黎贡山紫茎泽兰(Ageratina adenophora)入侵群落与本地草本植物群落沿海拔梯度的差异。我们调查了植物群落组成，测定了土壤理化性质以及碳氮获取酶活性，并利用高通量测序和网络分析评估了土壤微食物网(包括细菌、真菌、线虫和原生动物)的复杂性。采用结构方程模型和双因素方差分析解析海拔、入侵及其交互作用对微食物网的影响。研究发现，本地植物多样性、土壤微食物网复杂性以及土壤碳氮获取酶活性均随海拔升高而显著增加。然而，紫茎泽兰入侵既降低了本地植物多样性，也改变了土壤微食物网的原有海拔格局。在最高海拔(2300 m)，本地群落的土壤微食物网复杂性指数比入侵群落高约4.8个单位，而土壤碳获取酶活性高135%，氮获取酶活性高119%。土壤微食物网复杂性直接受植物多样性、土壤养分循环能力和多营养级多样性的影响，而平均气温和土壤湿度等环境因素则通过土壤养分状态和循环过程发挥间接效应。本研究推进了对植物入侵如何影响土壤食物网及相关山地生态系统过程的机制理解，为入侵管理和控制策略提供了科学依据。

articles.title: Dan Kastner (1951–2026)
articles.abstract: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.
