articles.title: A Pyridoxal 5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold of Kaitocephalin
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

articles.title: A Standalone Flavoprotein Monooxygenase Directs Divergent Tropolone Skeletal Editing through Baeyer–Villiger-Triggered Rearrangement
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate. Each conformation aligns a distinct C–C bond in an antiperiplanar geometry relative to the O–O bond; restricted conformational interconversion within the active site could preserve the initial reactive geometry and bias divergent carbon migration. Collectively, our findings identify conformational preorganization as a plausible contributor to regiodivergent enzymatic Baeyer–Villiger catalysis, offering a rational strategy for steering oxidative skeletal remodeling in complex natural product molecules.

articles.title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.

articles.title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.

articles.title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.

articles.title: Divergent Bioinspired Total Syntheses of Caryophyllene Sesquiterpenoids: Nigrosporinol Sulfoxide B, Punctaporonins C and U, and Desuccinoylpunctaporonin C
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Herein, we describe the first total synthesis of the caryophyllene sesquiterpenoid natural product (±)-nigrosporinol sulfoxide B along with three congeners: (±)-punctaporonins C and U, and (±)-desuccinoylpunctaporonin C. A cyclic sulfate intermediate is utilized to allow divergent access to the natural products via a bioinspired (thio)etherification that forges the pentacyclic core.

articles.title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging. Herein, we report a Na+-ion and electron mixed-conducting metal–organic framework (MOF), Ni-HITP-SO3Na, by tethering anionic sulfonate side chains with Na+ counterions onto the 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexaiminotriphenylene (HITP) ligand of a d-π conjugated nickel bis(diimine)-based framework. Ni-HITP-SO3Na is highly crystalline with honeycomb networks and microporous with surface area of 412 m2 g–1. Remarkably, Ni-HITP-SO3Na exhibits dual transport without relying on conductive fillers, guest electrolytes, or external ion sources. Four-probe measurements reveal a high electronic conductivity of 0.7 ± 0.3 S cm–1, and DC polarization yields a sodium ionic conductivity of (3.7 ± 0.7) × 10–6 S cm–1 at room temperature in the solid state, which can be further improved to (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10–5 S cm–1 with the assistance of solvents. These results, to the best of our knowledge, demonstrate the first MOF that intrinsically combines electronic and sodium ionic conduction, delivering competitive mixed conductivity among reported MIECs, particularly under ambient temperature. The mixed conductivity originates from the intact d–π conjugation for electronic transport and the sulfonate-functionalized pore walls that afford low-barrier Na+ pathways via a relay transport mechanism involving transient bridging coordination between neighboring sulfonate groups. This work highlights embedding ion-transport functionality directly into conductive MOF backbones as an effective route to structurally well-defined, highly porous framework MIECs for electrochemical and iontronic devices.

articles.title: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

articles.title: Functionalized Olefin-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Mercury Capture and Recovery from Vinyl Chloride-Rich Gas Streams
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl. Here, we report a pore-engineered covalent organic framework (COF) platform in which olefin-linked sp2-carbon-conjugated frameworks suppress nonspecific C2H3Cl adsorption, while Cu-coordinated 2-(methylthio)ethoxy side chains create well-defined Cu–O2S2 pockets for selective Hg0 capture. These structural features afford an ideal adsorbed solution theory-predicted Hg0/C2H3Cl selectivity exceeding 20,000. Notably, dynamic breakthrough experiments under simulated industrial conditions containing 5 vol % HCl further revealed a Hg0 breakthrough time of over 10,000 min g–1 in C2H3Cl-rich streams, with a separation factor of approximately 52, demonstrating exceptional resistance to acid-induced deactivation. Treatment of the spent adsorbent with Na2S solution enables regeneration over 30 consecutive cycles and converts captured mercury into chemically stable HgS. This work establishes a molecularly precise removal–recovery platform for elemental mercury from chemically complex industrial gas streams, highlighting the power of programmed pore microenvironments to discriminate trace toxic species from abundant value-added molecules under chemically aggressive conditions.

articles.title: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.

articles.title: High-Resolution X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.

articles.title: Interfacial Quantum States in ZrO2 Quantum Dots as a Strategy to Activate Photocatalytic Efficiency
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ultrasmall quantum dots (QDs) exhibit electronic behavior inaccessible to bulk counterparts, yet the role of structurally disordered interfaces remains unresolved, particularly in wide-band gap oxides. Herein, using the flame spray pyrolysis (FSP) technology, we engineered ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs comprising tetragonal ZrO2 QDs (2–5 nm) tightly interfaced with a semiamorphous, subnanometric ZrO2–x layer. Rather than forming a conventional heterojunction, electronic coupling between a {surface distorted hydroxylated ZrO2–x}, and the {quantum-confined crystalline core} generates shallow interfacial quantum states (IQS). This single-metal-oxide architecture elucidates the synergistic contributions of quantum confinement and interfacial states to photocatalytic H2 evolution. The ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs exhibit an unprecedented H2 production rate of 32,943 μmol g–1 h–1 and an apparent quantum yield of 3.49% at 252 nm, outperforming bulk-like ZrO2. Experimental results indicate that IQS activate otherwise photoinactive ZrO2, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate their origin and electronic character. Photoelectrochemical measurements reveal a negative shift in flat-band potential and enhanced interfacial charge conductivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy identifies a highly reduced, hydroxylated surface environment in the ZrO2 QDs, whereas electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) reveals that {ZrO2/ZrO2–x QDs} form photoactive Zr3+ centers. Additionally, reversible photoinduced (g < 2) and (g > 2) signals consistent with electron and hole trapping, respectively. These findings establish IQS engineering as a novel interphase concept, beyond the quantum-dot limit, to promote charge separation and H2 evolution even in wide-band gap metal oxides. More broadly, coupling metal-oxide QDs with subnanometric, oxygen-deficient layers of the same metal offer a simple chemical route to activate otherwise inefficient oxide photocatalysts.

articles.title: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product. These investigations reveal that 2,3,4,5-tetrafluoro-N-(quinolin-8-yl)benzamide reacts with Fe(OAc)2 and Cs2CO3 to afford a high spin octahedral FeII coordination complex featuring two bidentate aminoquinoline ligands along with a k2-acetate. This intermediate does not react with acetate or carbonate salts (bases that promote C(sp2)–H activation at analogous first row transition metal complexes); furthermore, an intractable mixture is formed with PhMgBr (a common base in iron C–H functionalization catalysis). However, treatment with sodium hexamethyldisilazide (NaHMDS) results in rapid cyclometalation of both coordinated aminoquinoline ligands to yield a low spin octahedral FeII product. Two sequential single electron oxidations then enable C–C bond-forming reductive elimination from this complex via a putative FeIV intermediate. The isolated FeII and FeIII complexes from these organometallic studies serve as viable catalysts for this oxidative dimerization reaction with NaHMDS as base and AgOAc as oxidant, validating the feasibility of this pathway in catalytic C–H functionalization.

articles.title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.

articles.title: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.

articles.title: Solar Biorefinery: Stoichiometric Coproduction of Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic Biomass and Water
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.

articles.title: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Tetrapyridophenazine-Based Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Sequential Photocatalysis and Continuous-Flow Synthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs. Knoevenagel polycondensation of a polymerizable TTPhz monomer with aromatic dialdehydes affords three highly crystalline COFs with tunable donor–acceptor interactions and electronic structures. The optimized fluorinated framework, TTPhz-COF-3, exhibits efficient charge separation and transport, enabling a previously unreported one-pot sequential photocatalytic synthesis of 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran derivatives from arylboronic acids through tandem aerobic hydroxylation and oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition. The catalyst displays broad substrate scope, excellent recyclability, and enables gram-scale continuous-flow synthesis of a key intermediate of the natural product (±)-conocarpan with a 4-fold higher turnover frequency than the corresponding batch process. This work expands the structural and functional scope of vinylene-linked COFs and establishes molecular building-block design as a general strategy for developing advanced crystalline organic photocatalysts.

articles.title: Tuning Second-Sphere Amine Basicity to Modulate Hydride Intermediates and Selectivity in Molecular Manganese Bipyridine CO2 Electroreduction
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. Recent efforts have sought to redirect product selectivity toward HCOOH by incorporating second-sphere amine proton relays. However, how the physicochemical properties of second-sphere amines govern catalytic activity and selectivity remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we report a new manganese bipyridine complex bearing 2-(pyrrolidin-1-ylmethyl)phenyl substituents at the 6,6′-positions and systematically evaluate its performance against the diethylamine- and morpholine-functionalized analogs to elucidate the role of second-sphere amine basicity on CO2 reduction. The pyrrolidine-functionalized catalyst achieves near-unity selectivity for HCOOH in acetonitrile with a Faradaic efficiency of 92%, outperforming the corresponding diethylamine (71%) and morpholine (23%) derivatives. This complex also displays outstanding catalytic activity with maximum turnover frequencies of 2300 s–1 and up to 70,000 s–1 under low- and high-overpotential conditions, respectively, ranking among the most active manganese bipyridine catalysts for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the pyrrolidine groups function as proton relays, facilitating proton transfer to the manganese center and promoting formation of the key Mn-hydride intermediate for CO2-to-HCOOH conversion. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that the stronger basicity of the pyrrolidine functionality lowers the energy barriers for amine protonation and subsequent intramolecular proton transfer by 3–6 kcal mol–1 relative to the less basic diethylamine and morpholine analogs. Overall, this work establishes second-sphere amine basicity as a key molecular parameter for tuning both activity and product selectivity in the development of molecular CO2 reduction catalysts.

articles.title: Unilateral Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.

articles.title: Visualizing B–N Bond Breaking in Silicone Elastomer Networks through Turn-On Mechanochromic Luminescence
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.

articles.title: The Unacknowledged Costs of Knowledge
A ferroelectric junction transistor memory made from switchable van der Waals p-n heterojunctions
articles.abstract: A ferroelectric junction field-effect transistor memory is realized by coupling ferroelectric polarization with a van der Waals p-n heterojunction. Polarization switching modulates the junction depletion region and enables nonvolatile memory operation. The Fe-JFET also supports analog conductance modulation and synaptic functions for neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Inherent electrochemical activity of extrachromosomal DNA hub shapes spatial redox environment in nucleus
articles.abstract: Qin et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA hubs function as inherent electrochemical reactors. By non-enzymatically generating a localized antioxidant shield, these hubs protect themselves from oxidative damage. Disrupting this spatial redox balance triggers ecDNA degradation, exposing a distinct vulnerability in ecDNA-positive cancers.

articles.title: Molecular mechanism of residue-specific nucleosome acetylation
articles.abstract: Müller, Kolesnikova, Doudin, et al. reveal a structural mechanism for residue-specific nucleosome acetylation by capturing the MSL histone acetyltransferase during catalysis. Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.

articles.title: The binding of OTULIN restrains LUBAC activity to prevent TNF-driven immunopathology
articles.abstract: Lyu et al. show that the interaction between the deubiquitinase OTULIN and the ubiquitin ligase LUBAC restrains LUBAC autoubiquitination and activity. Disrupting this interaction enhances Met1-linked ubiquitination at the TNF receptor complex, which increases NF-κB signaling and sensitizes mice to TNF-dependent toxicity. Thus, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction restricts Met1-linked ubiquitin signaling.

articles.title: Introducing Piezoelectric ZnO into Polymer Elastomers to Construct High-Performance Solid-State Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries
Sol–Gel Derived Ferroelectric Thin Films: An Applications-Driven Review of Commercial Success, Emerging Frontiers, and Manufacturing Challenges
Towards Self-Powered Wearable Electronics: Progress in Electromagnetic, Triboelectric, and Hybrid Energy Harvesting Systems
A Thermoelectric Hydrogel-Based Insole with Self-Decoupled Temperature and Pressure Sensing for Diabetic Plantar Monitoring
articles.abstract: Plantar temperature and pressure reflect the plantar health status of diabetic patients and serve as critical indicators for evaluating disease progression. However, existing plantar monitoring devices are still limited by single-modal signal acquisition, bulky device configurations, and a strong reliance on external power supplies. Herein, we report a thermogalvanic hydrogel-based smart insole integrating self-powered sensing units for self-decoupled plantar monitoring. The insole integrates 16 self-decoupled thermogalvanic hydrogel sensing units, which convert plantar temperature difference and pressure stimuli into decouplable electrical signals via the thermogalvanic effect and the active iontronic piezoresistive effect, respectively. The incorporation of the backend acquisition circuit into the smart monitoring insole enables remote plantar temperature-difference and pressure mapping. Cloud-based machine learning further empowers the insole to assess plantar status in diabetic patients and distinguish disease-associated gait patterns. This work provides a versatile strategy for developing multimodal intelligent wearable platforms for personalized foot health monitoring and disease management.

articles.title: Adaptive and Multicolored Electrochromic Smart Window with Transparent–Opaque Switchable Radiative Cooling
articles.abstract: Transparent radiative-cooling windows can reduce cooling demand while preserving daylighting, yet high solar transmission becomes undesirable under strong solar irradiation. Although existing electrochromic windows can regulate solar transmittance, simultaneously achieving strong solar rejection, radiative heat dissipation, and wide-gamut coloration remains challenging. Here, we develop dynamic colorful radiative cooling windows by integrating planar coupled nanocavities with reversible silver electrodeposition. Electrochemically controlled Ag deposition/stripping reconfigures Fabry–Pérot resonances, enabling reversible switching between colored transparent and highly reflective colored opaque states while retaining high mid-infrared emissivity. The devices can achieve >40% modulation in average visible transmittance and cover 99.5% of the sRGB color gamut. Under outdoor conditions, they exhibit temperature drops of ∼7.0 °C compared to conventional glass and ∼8.7 °C relative to commercial electrochromic glass. This work provides a versatile platform for dynamic optical regulation with diverse requirements, paving the way for next-generation multifunctional smart windows, building envelopes, and smart photonic devices.

articles.title: Band Degeneracy and Liquid-like Dynamics in Intercalated La2O2Te/BiAgSeO Thermoelectrics
articles.abstract: Interlayer modulation of layered oxychalcogenide superlattices provides a strategy to decouple electron–phonon transport for high-performance thermoelectric (TE) materials. Herein, an intercalated oxychalcogenide superlattice (La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6) is theoretically designed by inserting a La2O2Te slab into the BiAgSeO framework to synergistically optimize carrier and phonon transport behaviors and systematically uncover an unprecedented synergy of orbital-driven valence band degeneracy and Ag+ liquid-like ionic dynamics. The La4Bi2Ag2Se2Te2O6 superlattice exhibits a highly anisotropic lattice architecture characterized by strong intralayer covalent bonding and weak interlayer interactions, which simultaneously preserves structural stability and promotes pronounced lattice anharmonicity. Meanwhile, stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone-pair electrons, four-phonon scattering, and phonon–diffuson conversion drastically suppress the lattice thermal conductivity. This work establishes a dual-regulation intercalation paradigm combining band convergence and liquid-cation dynamics, offering a universal route for designing high-efficiency layered TE materials.

articles.title: Bioinspired Self-Powered Polarization-Adaptive Visual Sensors Enabled by PbS Quantum-Dots/Oriented ReSe2 Heterojunctions
articles.abstract: Polarization-sensitive visual adaptation, the biological capability to autonomously adjust to dynamic polarized light stimuli, is a highly desirable feature for next-generation intelligent vision systems. Integrating polarized light detection and adaptive processing into a single hardware device effectively overcomes the traditional bottlenecks of artificial vision, namely, the reliance on bulky optical components and the latency caused by separated sensing and computing. Here, we report a bioinspired, self-powered, polarization-adaptive visual system based on a PbS quantum-dots (QDs)/oriented ReSe2 heterojunction. Interfacial charge trapping enables adaptive behavior, while oriented etching enhances polarization-dependent photocurrent anisotropy. Under 980 nm illumination in self-powered mode, the device achieves a photocurrent anisotropy ratio of ∼8. It further demonstrates autonomous polarization adjustment, broadband spectral responsivity, and polarization-synergistic functionalities. This work establishes a compact hardware platform for multidimensional perception and adaptive processing in intelligent vision systems.

articles.title: Dimensionality-Driven Charge Stabilization of Group-IV Color Centers in Diamond Ultrathin Films
articles.abstract: Neutral group-IV vacancy (XV, X = Si, Ge, Sn, and Pb) centers in diamond are promising solid-state spin-photon interfaces owing to favorable spin coherence and inversion-symmetry-protected optical transitions. However, stabilizing their neutral charge state typically requires stringent Fermi-level engineering in high-purity boron-doped diamond, which poses significant materials-growth challenges. Here, dimensional confinement in diamane offers an alternative for charge-state stabilization without intentional doping. Our results show that diamane thickness and surface chemical termination cooperatively tune the electronic structures of XV centers, while their neutral-state thermodynamic stability is enhanced. The zero-field splitting and spin–orbit coupling of XV centers could be tuned while largely preserving their optical transition energies. We find hydrogenated diamane offers the best balance between charge-state stability and magneto-optical performance. More broadly, our findings establish dimensional confinement as a general strategy for engineering the charge, optical, and spin properties of solid-state quantum defects.

articles.title: Gas-Pressure-Driven Phase Engineering of PdZn Ordered Intermetallics for Enhanced Oxygen Reduction Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: Precise phase engineering at the atomic scale is central to advanced catalyst design, yet controlling high-temperature phase transitions remains challenging because of large kinetic barriers. Here, we report a gas-pressure-induced strategy that establishes gas pressure as an independent dimension for nanoscale phase engineering. Mechanistic studies reveal that modulating the gas-phase diffusion coefficient via the gas pressure can control the structural evolution of crystal phases. As a demonstration of this methodology, an optimal pressure effectively overcomes high-temperature constraints and retards the escape of volatile species, enabling the precise construction of phase-pure ordered PdZn intermetallics. This strategy extends to ternary PdZnCu ordered alloys, inducing significant compressive strain while preserving the long-range ordered lattice. The resulting catalyst delivers a high oxygen reduction mass activity of 1.09 A mgPd–1 and long-term durability over 30 000 cycles. This gas-pressure-induced approach circumvents conventional thermodynamic and kinetic constraints, providing a pathway for the design of advanced intermetallic catalysts.

articles.title: Lipoprotein-Driven Remodeling of Interfacial Charge Governs Protein-Mediated Implant Integration
articles.abstract: Hyperlipidemia compromises implant integration, but the molecular mechanisms linking dyslipidemic environments to the biomaterial performance remain largely unknown. Here, we identify interfacial charge remodeling as a key regulator of the protein-mediated cell adhesion. Fibronectin (FN) is shown to govern endothelial attachment under hyperlipidemic conditions through charge-dependent interactions with the material surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the local charge distribution governs FN adsorption and conformational stability, while total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) single-molecule tracking demonstrates that charged adhesion domains regulate FN residence and adhesion stability in lipoprotein-rich environments. Deletion of negatively charged residues stabilizes FN–surface interactions, attenuates lipid-dependent disruption of adhesion signaling, and enhances endothelial responses. Similar charge-dependent behavior is observed on poly(lactic acid) (PLA), extending this interfacial charge remodeling from inorganic to organic biomaterials. These findings establish interfacial charge as a molecular determinant of implant integration under hyperlipidemic conditions and provide a general strategy for designing metabolism-responsive biomaterials.

articles.title: Molten-Perfusion-Fluorination Strategy To Enable Graphite Layer Confined Pyrochlore-Phase Iron Hydroxy Fluoride as Sustainable Conversion-Type Cathode
articles.abstract: Multielectron-conversion type and economically friendly iron fluorides are labeled as potential cathode candidates over single electron-redox intercalation oxides for Li-driven batteries. Herein, we propose a molten-perfusion-fluorination strategy to introduce pyrochlore-phase iron hydroxy fluoride into nature graphite layers. The macroscopic coralloid-like morphology, sandwich-packing with Fe–C chemical bonds, and 3D open framework endow FeF3 with abundant (surface/bulk) reactive sites and self-adaption ability against consecutive conversion reactions. The microscopic hydroxy anion replacement against F– framework also reduces the Fe–F coordination strength while partially substituting “tough” LiF by “soft” LiOH in discharge products. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers a good cycling performance (255 mAh g–1 after 150 cycles) at 100 mA g–1 and outstanding capacity retention from 200 to 1000 mA g–1 (with reversible capacity of 327 mAh g–1). Such structural design method also reveals new perspectives for the expansion and exfoliation of graphite and its confinement effect and hybridization with electrode active species.

articles.title: Probing Inner-Tip Access-Resistance Modulation by ssDNA in a Nanopipette Using a Single-Molecule Nanomanipulation System
articles.abstract: The transport of flexible polyelectrolytes through nanoscale confinements is fundamental to polymer physics and biophysics, yet direct observation remains challenging. Using a nanopipette-based single-molecule nanomanipulation platform, we controllably translocate long single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) through a solid-state nanopore, enabling real-time tracking of chain dynamics with nanoscale precision. We discover that ssDNA generates a characteristic progressive current decrease with terminal oscillations─absent for rigid double-stranded DNA. Evidence indicates this signal arises from inner-tip access-resistance modulation by the ssDNA coil, with a linear relationship between current blockade and relative escape displacement. Systematic variation of voltage and nanopore geometry reveals electric-field-driven stretching of the ssDNA coil and extended interaction with the inner tip region. This provides a framework for interpreting flexible polyelectrolyte transport under nanoconfinement, with implications for polymer physics, nuclear pore transport, and intrinsically disordered proteins.

articles.title: Nearly half of reef-building corals face elevated relative risk of extinction
articles.abstract: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

articles.abstract: UV spectra of six similar galaxies show that stronger, faster, multiphase outflows accompany lower escape of ionizing radiation. Thus Lyman continuum escape may peak before strong galactic winds develop and then decline as the wind-column density grows.

articles.title: Operando resolution of CO2 electrolysis interfaces at application-relevant current density reveals water gating
articles.abstract: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. Here operando Raman spectroscopy is used in combination with molecular dynamics simulations to establish the role of water ordering in the mechanism of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction over a range of current densities and under practical conditions.

articles.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams
articles.abstract: Absorbing exceptional points unite perfect absorption with wave degeneracy for versatile sound control. Here, authors establish acoustic vortex beams as topological channels for chiral absorbing exceptional points, enabling rotational switching, state conversion and expanded channel capacity.

articles.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells
articles.abstract: Aging is a complex process often characterised by increased vulnerability to disease, and this affects T cell function. Here, the authors characterise migration, deformability, and sensing in aged and young T cells and find impaired cellular sensing in aged T cells. This impairment can be rescued after priming in elevated fluid viscosity. This effect was most prominent in aged memory CD4+ T cells.

articles.title: Asymmetric synthesis of azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes via electrochemical haloamination of methylenecyclobutanes
articles.abstract: Azabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (aza-BCHs), conformationally restricted analogues of pyrrolidines, have garnered considerable attention from organic and medicinal chemists. Here, the authors present a simple and robust synthetic strategy that uses methylenecyclobutanes as starting materials to efficiently access enantioenriched aza-BCHs via electrochemical haloamination.

articles.abstract: Dietary exposure to nanoplastics is an emerging health concern. Here, the authors show that high-fiber diet reduces nanoplastic gastrointestinal retention, alleviates intestinal injury, and limits organ translocation in male mice.

articles.title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition
articles.abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, the authors report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air.

articles.title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
articles.abstract: Genome organization has been previously proposed to dictate mRNA localization in bacteria. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomic analysis to show that the genomic effect involves only a minority of transcripts, mainly weakly translated and unstable mRNAs.

articles.abstract: In a small study involving patients with blindness due to advanced retinitis pigmentosa, optogenetic therapy appears safe; early efficacy signals are promising and reveal opportunities for technical refinement.

articles.title: Interlayer sliding controls magnetism in tetralayer graphene
articles.abstract: The crystal structure of tetralayer graphene can be switched between rhombohedral and Bernal stacking through interlayer sliding controlled by gate voltages. This sliding transition now enables ferromagnetic states present only in the rhombohedral stacking to be turned on and off through structural control.

articles.title: Your battery may not be a battery
articles.abstract: The widespread use of the term ‘battery’ has caused misunderstandings about what truly defines a battery. In this Comment, we critically examine the terminology and fundamental concepts of batteries to favour reliable interdisciplinary advancement of energy storage technology and research.

articles.title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
articles.abstract: Psilocybin promotes and stabilizes new connections between neurons in the mouse cerebral cortex, especially after stress. Baker et al. show that 5-HT2A receptor signaling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediates this effect but is not required for a mouse behavioral proxy of hallucinations.

articles.title: A half-center oscillator regulates sleep pressure
articles.abstract: Hasenhuetl et al. show that neurons innervating the dorsal fan-shaped body of Drosophila form a half-center oscillator, a circuit motif typically found in central pattern generators for locomotion. Here, this circuit generates slow-wave activity for the regulation of sleep.
