Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the ‘critical’ scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2° of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.

articles.title: The cow udder as an influenza mixing ground
articles.abstract: Bovine mammary tissue can support infection and replication of diverse influenza A viruses and may provide an environment in which different viral strains can co-infect cells.

articles.title: The petal identity gene PhDEF has a major binding and regulatory action in the epidermis
articles.abstract: In flowering plants, floral organ identity is specified by the combinatorial action of homeotic genes. While the role of these genes in the early specification of organ identity is well established, their late function throughout floral organ development and in specific cell types is much less characterized. In particular, since plant organs are structured in clonally independent cell layers, whether and how homeotic identity interacts with cell layer identity is unknown. We have previously identified cell layer-specific mutants for the petal identity gene PhDEF in petunia flowers, resulting in drastically different petal phenotypes whether PhDEF is expressed in the petal epidermis or in the mesophyll. In this study, using a combination of single-cell RNA-Seq and chromatin immunoprecipitation on phdef cell layer-specific mutants, we find that PhDEF regulates a different set of target genes in the petal epidermis and mesophyll, with a major regulatory action in the epidermis. We uncover a high diversity of binding profiles in PhDEF target genes, with a complex combination of layer-specific or non-specific binding sites, and a much more prominent binding of PhDEF in the epidermis than in the mesophyll. Our study highlights that floral homeotic genes like PhDEF can have different regulatory actions in different cell contexts, here different cell layers, demonstrating that cell layer identity indeed influences the regulatory processes underlying homeotic identity.

articles.title: A data-driven system for insulin pump dosing in type 2 diabetes: development, prospective evaluation and clinical applicability
articles.abstract: Open-loop insulin pump therapy depends on clinical expertise for dose initiation and titration. We developed a long short-term memory-based system, using 1738 treatment courses from 1641 patients with type 2 diabetes for initial prescribing and daily basal and bolus titration. Patient-grouped five-fold validation showed closer agreement with recorded prescriptions for subsequent titration than for initiation. Prospective evaluation in 97 patients from the model-directed arm of a randomized trial yielded a median derived time in range (3.9-10.0mmol/L) of 84.5%, with low hypoglycemic exposure. Favorable control extended to previously treated patients. Higher mean glucose during the first 24 hours was associated with poorer glycemic control thereafter. The association between distance from development data and glycemic outcomes was stronger when early glucose responses were included alongside baseline characteristics. These findings support model-directed pump dosing and highlight early treatment response as a clinically relevant signal for assessing applicability and identifying patients who may require additional oversight. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07066891 .

articles.title: Accuracy and completeness of death recording in primary care electronic health records compared with national death registrations in England using OpenSAFELY-TPP
articles.abstract: Introduction: Primary care electronic health records (EHRs) are an important resource for health research, but death recording in primary care EHRs may be incomplete or differ from Office for National Statistics (ONS) death registrations. We used OpenSAFELY-TPP to assess the completeness and concordance of death recording and provide recommendations for using date-of-death information. Methods: Using linked primary care EHRs and ONS death registrations, we assessed whether ONS-registered deaths from 2020-2025 had a primary care date of death and, where present, calculated the difference between dates. Where a primary care date was absent, we assessed death-related SNOMED CT codes. Analyses were conducted overall and by year, population subgroup, and general practice. We also examined GP registration end dates and primary-care-recorded deaths without a corresponding ONS record, including monthly patterns near the data extraction date. Results: Among 1,409,275 ONS-registered deaths, 88% had the same date recorded in primary care and 8% had no corresponding primary care date. Among 1,324,995 deaths recorded in primary care, <2% had no corresponding ONS record. Deaths recorded in only one source were more frequent among people aged <45 years and those from Mixed, Asian or Asian British, Black or Black British, and Chinese or Other ethnic groups. ONS-only dates were also more frequent in London and the West Midlands. Primary-care-only deaths increased close to date of data extraction, reaching 7% in February 2026. Same-day GP deregistration increased from 9% in 2020 to 85% in 2025. Conclusions: Death recording in primary care EHRs showed high completeness and concordance with ONS registrations, but discrepancies remained for recent deaths and some population groups. Data recency and population-specific completeness should therefore be considered when using linked mortality data for research.

articles.title: Alzheimers disease blood-based biomarkers in the Boston Latino Aging Study (BLAST): Associations with cognition and depressive symptoms
articles.abstract: Background: Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) may facilitate early detection of Alzheimers disease (AD), yet data in Latino populations remain limited. We examined associations of plasma biomarkers with cognition and depressive symptoms in Spanish-speaking Latino older adults enrolled in the Boston Latino Aging Study (BLAST). Methods: Baseline data from 122 older adults without dementia were analyzed. Plasma AB42/40, brain-derived phosphorylated tau (p-tau) 217, neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) were measured using NULISA. Cognition was assessed with the Latin American Spanish version of the Preclinical Alzheimers Cognitive Composite (LAS-PACC5) and depressive symptoms with the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). Regression models were adjusted for age, sex, and education. Results: Cognitively impaired participants had higher p-tau217 and GFAP than cognitively normal participants. Higher p-tau217 and GFAP were associated with poorer LAS-PACC5 performance, while higher NfL was associated with greater depressive symptoms. AB42/40 showed no significant associations. Conclusions: Distinct biomarker associations with cognitive and emotional functioning support further longitudinal evaluation of BBMs for risk characterization in Latino older adults and potential disease monitoring applications.

articles.title: Attenuated GlycoRNA-microglial transcriptional coupling in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of patients with major depressive disorder: an exploratory interaction-based in-silico analysis
articles.abstract: Background: Glycosylated RNAs (GlycoRNAs) participate in immune recognition and intercellular communication, but their relationship with brain cell-type transcriptional signatures in major depressive disorder (MDD) remains unclear. We examined GlycoRNA-related transcriptional coupling with microglial and other cellular signatures in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Method: Postmortem DLPFC transcriptomic data from 22 controls and 26 MDD patients (GSE102556) were analyzed. GlycoRNA-related pathway enrichment was quantified using gene set variation analysis (GSVA), whereas microglial, neuronal, astrocytic, and oligodendrocytic signatures were derived using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Pearson correlations, linear regression, and generalized estimating equations (GEE) evaluated cell-type-specific associations and diagnostic interactions. Exploratory GEE results underwent false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Results: No differentially expressed genes survived FDR correction, and GlycoRNA-related and cell-type signatures did not differ significantly between groups. In controls, GlycoRNA enrichment was positively associated with the microglial signature (beta = 0.447, FDR-adjusted P = 0.006), with significantly weaker associations for neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). The two-way GlycoRNA x is_microglia interaction was nominally significant (beta = 0.210, P = 0.048), confirming that GlycoRNA transcriptional coupling is substantially stronger for microglia than for the other three cell types combined. The microglial association was numerically attenuated in MDD (beta difference = -0.273, P = 0.167), but diagnostic interactions were nonsignificant. Conclusions: GlycoRNA pathway transcriptional enrichment exhibits preferential microglial association in control DLPFC. Its possible attenuation in MDD remains to be validated. keyword: Major depressive disorder; GlycoRNA; microglia; dorsolateral prefrontal cortex; generalized estimating equation; ssGSEA; bioinformatics

articles.title: Auxiliary modalities add no detectable discrimination or calibration over structured EHR for 30-day COPD readmission: evidence from a leakage-audited MIMIC-IV cohort
articles.abstract: Background: Hospital readmission is a common and costly outcome in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Multimodal deep learning models combining structured electronic health record (EHR) data with physiological, imaging, and textual data have been proposed to improve its prediction, but whether such fusion outperforms EHR data alone, once temporal-leakage safeguards are applied, remains unclear. Methods: Using a stratified MIMIC-IV cohort of COPD patients enriched to about 50% readmission (natural prevalence 18.1%; n=1,279; 895/192/192 training/validation/test), we predicted 30-day, all-cause readmission from four frozen, pre-trained encoders (electrocardiogram, chest radiograph, clinical notes, structured EHR). We audited and corrected temporal leakage in the admission-linkage pipeline of each modality, then compared three fusion architectures (naive concatenation, scalar gated fusion, EHR-anchored residual fusion) against unimodal baselines and an EHR-alone reference, using bootstrap significance testing, a missingness stress test, and calibration analysis with and without post-hoc recalibration. Results: The audit corrected three previously undetected temporal-alignment issues, affecting 5-9% of patients for clinical notes, 29-43% for chest radiographs, and 53-58% for ECG. After correction, every modality except EHR showed near-chance discrimination alone (ROC-AUC 0.46-0.53), confirmed with a non-linear adapter probe. No fusion architecture significantly outperformed the EHR-alone baseline (ROC-AUC 0.63); removing auxiliary modalities improved rather than degraded fusion performance under stress testing. The raw Brier score was lower for all three fusion architectures than for EHR-alone (about 0.24 versus 0.32), but this reflected overconfidence of the EHR-alone probe (calibration slope 0.12); after logistic recalibration fitted on the validation set, Brier scores were indistinguishable (EHR-alone 0.239; fusion 0.240-0.244; all paired bootstrap 95% CIs included zero). Conclusions: Structured EHR data alone matched the discrimination and, after recalibration, the calibration of more complex multimodal fusion for 30-day COPD readmission prediction. These findings highlight the importance of rigorous temporal-leakage auditing in multimodal clinical prediction research and suggest that reformulating this task around temporal proximity to the outcome, rather than refining the fusion mechanism further, may be more productive for future work.

articles.title: BIRTH SPACING AND UNDER-FIVE CHILD SURVIVAL IN GHANA: EVIDENCE FROM THE 2022 DEMOGRAPHIC AND HEALTH SURVEY.
articles.abstract: Background: Short birth intervals are a well-documented, modifiable risk factor for child death in low- and middle-income countries, yet nationally representative evidence from Ghana's most recent Demographic and Health Survey has not been fully examined. This study assessed the association between the preceding birth interval and under-five mortality using the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey. Methods: The analysis used the complete birth history reported by women aged 15-49 years. The cohort comprised births occurring 60-119 completed months (5-10 years) before the survey, which allowed a complete five-year observation window for under-five survival (n = 8,418; 397 deaths). Spacing models were restricted to second-or-higher-order births with a defined preceding interval (n = 6,340; 282 deaths), categorised as under 18, 18-23, 24-35 (reference), 36-47, and 48 or more months. Crude and adjusted odds ratios were estimated using survey-weighted, Taylor-linearised logistic regression, adjusting for birth order, child sex, plurality, maternal age, residence, region, maternal education, wealth quintile, and marital status. Results: Weighted under-five mortality in the cohort was 45.4 per 1,000 live births (4.54%). Among second-or-higher-order births, weighted mortality fell from 9.3% after intervals of under 18 months and 8.0% after 18-23 months to 4.2%, 3.2%, and 3.5% after 24-35, 36-47, and 48 or more months, respectively. Relative to 24-35 months, the adjusted odds of death were higher after intervals of under 18 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.48-4.49, p < 0.001) and 18-23 months (AOR 2.09, 95% CI 1.33-3.29, p = 0.001); longer intervals did not differ from the reference. Multiple birth (AOR 2.48, 95% CI 1.33-4.63) and having a mother who was never in union (AOR 3.25, 95% CI 1.29-8.17) were also associated with higher odds of death, and marked regional variation persisted after adjustment. Conclusion: A short preceding birth interval, particularly one of under 18 months, was independently associated with an approximately two- to two-and-a-half-fold increase in the odds of under-five death in this nationally representative sample. The findings support continued investment in postpartum family planning to help women space births at least 24 months apart, alongside closer attention to multiple births, unmarried mothers, and the regions carrying the greatest burden.

articles.title: Baseline Response Criterion and Changes in Emotional Bias as Markers of Esketamine Response in Treatment-Resistant Depression
articles.abstract: Negative emotional bias, including reduced processing of positive information and negative interpretation of ambiguous stimuli, is a core feature of depression. Esketamine, an N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonist with rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), reduces depressive symptoms, but its effects on distinct components of emotional processing remain unclear. Fifty-three patients with TRD and 53 healthy controls performed an Emotional Facial Expression Morphing task. Patients were assessed at baseline, 24 hours after the first esketamine administration, and after 4 weeks of treatment. Statistical models examined detection thresholds for happy and sad faces, negative categorisation of neutral faces, and signal detection indices separating emotion-neutral discrimination sensitivity (d') from response criterion (c), indexing the evidence required to report the presence of an emotion. At baseline, patients required greater happy-face intensity for emotion detection and were more likely to categorise detected neutral faces as negative. They also showed a more conservative response criterion without group difference in discrimination sensitivity. Responders showed an early increase in d'; and, by week 4, less negative categorisation of neutral faces than non-responders. A lower baseline response criterion was associated with responder status and, in secondary continuous analyses, with greater subsequent MADRS improvement. These findings indicate that TRD involves abnormalities across detection-related, valence-related, and decisional aspects of facial-emotion processing that are differently associated with esketamine response: baseline response criterion emerged as a candidate prognostic marker, whereas negative categorisation of neutral faces tracked clinical response. Assessing these domains may inform clinical evaluation, pending independent replication.

articles.title: Beyond Usual Pace: Quick Walking Speed and Brain Health Outcomes in the Framingham Heart Study
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stroke, dementia, and late-life depression share overlapping vascular pathophysiology, yet simple markers of shared neurological vulnerability across these conditions remain limited. Most gait research has relied on usual walking speed (UWS) alone, leaving it unclear whether quick walking speed (QWS) and gait adaptability (QWS minus UWS), relate to these conditions in the same way. METHODS: We examined associations of UWS, QWS, and gait adaptability with executive function, verbal memory, depressive symptoms, and incident stroke and dementia in the Framingham Heart Study Offspring cohort. A larger sample (n=2,308; mean age 61.5 years [SD 9.2]; 54% women) was used for cross-sectional and stroke analyses, and a dementia-free sample of 1,148 participants aged 60 years or older (mean age 68.5 years [SD 5.8]; 53% women) was used for analyses of incident dementia. We estimated associations per SD slower walking or smaller adaptability using linear, logistic, and Cox regression (10-year follow-up), overall and in women and men. RESULTS: Slower QWS and UWS were each associated with worse executive function, higher odds of high depressive symptoms (QWS OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.07-1.45; UWS OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.09-1.46), and greater hazard of incident stroke (QWS HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.03-1.64; UWS HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.11-1.65). Executive function and stroke associations were observed primarily in men (stroke QWS HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.11-2.17). For incident dementia, slower QWS reached significance (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.10-1.63), while UWS did not (HR 1.20, 95% CI 0.98-1.46). Lower gait adaptability was associated with worse executive function overall and in women and men, and with incident dementia in women (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.04-1.76), but not with depressive symptoms or stroke. No gait measure was associated with delayed recall. CONCLUSION: Slower QWS was associated with incident dementia; UWS was not. Adding a brief quick walking trial to routine gait assessment may identify risk that habitual-pace screening overlooks.

articles.title: Computationally Guided Design of Facet-Defined Multielement Active Sites on Hexagonal Close-Packed High-Entropy-Alloy Nanosheets for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Nonconventional hexagonal close-packed (HCP) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) provide distinct catalytic surfaces, but their synthesis with well-defined facets remains challenging, leaving facet-dependent multielement ensemble effects largely unexplored. Here, we report the computationally guided realization of atomically thin RuRhIrPtPd HEA nanosheets with predominantly exposed HCP {001} facets for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify HCP {001} as the most favorable facet over {100} and {110}, where near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption, narrow energy distribution, and balanced hydrogen/hydroxyl binding create an optimized alkaline HER landscape. Guided by this prediction, RuRhIrPtPd HEA atomic layers are epitaxially grown on HCP Ru nanosheets to maximize {001} exposure, with atomic-resolution electron microscopy and synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirming atomically mixed HEA layers. Electrochemical measurements demonstrate that the {001}-faceted HEA nanosheets exhibit higher alkaline HER activity and durability than irregular-faceted nanocrystal counterparts and commercial Pt/C. Climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) calculations, operando XAS, and CO-stripping measurements identify Ru-centered ensembles as favorable Volmer sites, showing the lowest water-dissociation barrier of 1.04 eV compared with 1.13–1.47 eV for other metal sites, while neighboring multimetallic sites balance hydrogen and hydroxyl adsorption. This work provides a structural blueprint for harnessing facet-defined multielement ensembles to design high-entropy electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Coordination-Controlled Stability of Pd Single-Atom Catalysts under Electrochemical Conditions
articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) maximize atom utilization and site-specificity for diverse chemical and electrochemical transformations. While activity and selectivity have been optimized through advanced synthetic methods, the electrochemical stability of SACs remains insufficiently understood and limits practical application. Here, we employ operando inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to quantify the dissolution kinetics of palladium (Pd) SACs in acidic electrolyte across a wide potential window. Operando electrochemically coupled mass spectrometry (EC-MS) confirms concurrent carbon support corrosion. By systematically varying heteroatom dopants, applied potentials, electrolyte pH, and adsorbing anions, we decouple coordination-driven (intrinsic) and electrochemical (extrinsic) factors controlling metal leaching. Specifically, the external potential exhibits a more pronounced influence on the stability of Pd SACs, while the coordinating heteroatoms modulate stability through both direct interaction with the isolated Pd centers and influence on the carbon support. Complementary X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveal dynamic restructuring of the Pd coordination environment, linking local chemical structure to macroscopic stability. These results provide mechanistic insights into SAC degradation pathways and establish design principles for stable single-atom architectures in energy conversion applications.

articles.title: Deep-Red Photocatalysis via Charge-Transfer Excitation of a Dicationic Ru(II) Sensitizer Using 740 nm Light
articles.abstract: We report rare examples of deep-red Ru(II) photochemistry from a charge-transfer (CT) excited state using [Ru(bpy)2(p-biphe)](PF6)2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine; p-biphe = 6,6′,7,7′-biphenanthridine). The absorption of deep-red light (740 nm) generates a dark but reactive CT excited state that can be harnessed in proof-of-principle reductive and oxidative electron-transfer and energy-transfer photocatalysis.

articles.title: Insertion of Alkenes into Aryl Nitrile C–C Bonds Enabled by Thiophenolate Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Insertion of alkenes into chemical bonds represents a powerful strategy for carbon framework editing, yet direct insertion into C–C bonds remains a formidable challenge due to the nonpolarity, high-lying σ* orbital, steric shielding, and high thermodynamic stability of the C–C bond. Here, we present a visible-light-driven thiophenolate photocatalytic system that enables direct insertion of alkenes into the C–C bond of aryl nitriles. Mechanistic studies reveal a photoinduced single-electron transfer from the excited thiophenolate anion to the aryl nitrile, generating a radical pair that undergoes radical addition and radical–radical cross-coupling, followed by elimination and nucleophilic addition to afford the insertion product. This strategy not only provides an avenue for editing inert C–C bonds but also establishes thiophenolate photocatalysis as a platform for challenging bond constructions under transition-metal-free and redox-neutral conditions.

articles.title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Vinyl Transfer Using Vinylene Carbonate for Direct Synthesis of C2,C3-Unsubstituted Indoles
articles.abstract: C2,C3-unsubstituted indoles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet their direct assembly from simple C2 feedstocks remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report an example of Y(OTf)3-catalyzed C–H [3 + 2] annulation of anilines with vinylene carbonate, enabling direct access to structurally diverse parent indoles through a Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl-transfer process. Readily available vinylene carbonate serves dually as a C2 building block and an internal oxidant, allowing the reaction to proceed without directing groups, external oxidants, or preinstalled unsaturation while exhibiting broad functional-group compatibility. Mechanistic studies reveal a bifunctional catalytic role of Y(OTf)3 in sequential N-formylmethylation and electrophilic cyclization. This work establishes a distinct strategy for bulk chemical-based indole synthesis and provides opportunities for Lewis acid-catalyzed vinyl transfer chemistry.

articles.title: Photoenzymatic Enantioselective [2+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynes Enabled by Whole-Cell Directed Evolution
articles.abstract: Enantioselective excited-state photocycloadditions represent an attractive yet challenging strategy for accessing optically active strained molecules. Here, we report a whole-cell directed evolution platform for engineering artificial triplet photoenzymes that catalyze the enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition of alkynes. By employing calcium chloride-mediated membrane permeabilization, we overcome substrate accessibility limitations in whole-cell systems and enable high-throughput evolution without the need for cell lysates or purified enzymes. Through ten rounds of directed evolution, a primitive ancestor (APC1.0; 46% yield, 6% ee) was transformed into a highly efficient variant (APC10.0; 92% yield, 94% ee under whole-cell conditions; 99% yield, 97% ee as the purified enzyme). The enhanced activity of APC10.0 enabled a total turnover number of 1800. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the evolution of artificial photoenzymes and expands the scope of biocatalysis toward stereoselective excited-state transformations.

articles.title: Quantified Structure–Performance Relationships for Fe(III)K(I) Heterodinuclear Catalysts in Cyclohexene Oxide/CO2 Ring-Opening Copolymerization
articles.abstract: Catalyst design and understanding are improved by quantified structure–performance relationships, but these are underutilized in polymerization catalysis. In epoxide/carbon dioxide ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP), an important route to make polymers from bio- and waste-based feedstocks, significant success has been achieved in understanding cobalt catalysts, but understanding of other metal catalysts is much less developed. This work targets earth-abundant bimetallic catalysts featuring iron and potassium. A series of seven Fe(III)K(I) catalysts, coordinated by different ancillary ligands, are compared with analogues Co(III)K(I) catalysts; the iron catalysts demonstrate both high activity (TOF = 675 h–1) and polymer selectivity (98%) in cyclohexene oxide/carbon dioxide copolymerization (20 bar CO2 pressure, 100 °C). The Fe(III)K(I) catalysts also show a linear free energy relationship between the copolymerization rates and the catalyst ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) wavelength, with a volcano relationship identifying the best catalysts. The most active catalysts have an Fe(III) center with an intermediate LMCT wavelength, and these features are consistent with the proposed copolymerization mechanism. In this field of catalysis, quantified structure-performance relationships are very rare; thus, the findings are fundamentally interesting and should help to accelerate the design of better-performing iron-based polymerization catalysts.

articles.title: Spatial Separation of Metal–MOF Tuning Catalytic Selectivity in CO2 Hydrogenation and Methanol Partial Oxidation
articles.abstract: Tuning the interactions between metal nanoparticles (NPs) and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is pivotal for selective catalysis, yet systematic regulation of metal–MOF spatial separation remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that systematically regulating the metal–MOF separation enables controlled modulation of catalytic activity and reaction selectivity. A series of MOF-encapsulated Pt catalysts with adjusted Pt–MOF separations were designed and synthesized by varying the surface coverage of capping agents on Pt NPs. Both CO2 hydrogenation and methanol partial oxidation exhibit volcano-type dependencies of catalytic performance on Pt–MOF separation, revealing the existence of an optimal spatial window for catalytic cooperation between Pt NPs and MOF nodes. Theoretical calculations indicate that an appropriate Pt–MOF separation facilitates the formation of key reaction intermediates, thereby governing catalytic selectivity. This work establishes metal–MOF spatial separation as an important structural parameter for catalyst design and provides a practical strategy for developing proximity-engineered NP–MOF catalysts with tunable reaction selectivity.

articles.title: Structural and Mechanistic Insight into Oxidative Ring Opening Catalyzed by L-DOPA Extradiol Dioxygenase from Beta vulgaris
articles.abstract: Betalain pigments replace anthocyanins in the majority of plants from the order Caryophyllales, but they are also present in some fungi and bacteria. Their biosynthesis attracts considerable scientific interest due to their applications across various fields and also because plant pigmentation is used to study complex evolution within Caryophyllales. The key step in betalain biosynthesis is the oxidative ring opening of L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) catalyzed by L-DOPA extradiol dioxygenase (DODA, EC: 1.13.11.29), which yields 4,5-seco-DOPA; the latter cyclizes to betalamic acid, the chromophore of all betalains. Betalain-producing plants feature two to six homologues of DODA, yet only one of them is highly active and participates in the betalain biosynthesis. Here, we report the crystal structures of the highly active DODAα1 from Beta vulgaris (beetroot), the main commercial source of betalain pigments. High-resolution structures of the apo form and complexes with L-DOPA and three substrate analogues (4-nitrocatechol, 6-nitro-L-DOPA, mimosine) provide insights into the key interactions responsible for effective substrate recognition by the enzyme. Enzymatic reaction kinetics for WT BvDODAα1 show that the enzyme is three orders of magnitude more efficient than the previously studied homologue BvDODAα2, with a pH optimum of 6.5, and that the kinetics are affected by modest substrate inhibition. The residues selected based on X-ray structures for site-directed mutagenesis, except Asp81, are critical for efficient catalysis, whereas molecular dynamics simulations show that they form strong direct and through-water contacts with the L-DOPA amino acid side chain. Mössbauer spectroscopy, supported by DFT calculations, suggests that the catechol ring of L-DOPA binds to the enzyme with both hydroxyl groups unionized, yet upon coordination to Fe2+, one of its protons is transferred to a second-shell histidine. EPR spectroscopy of NO adducts suggests that both L-DOPA and NO can bind simultaneously to Fe2+ in the active site. Based on these experimental data, a cluster model of the Michaelis complex was constructed and used in DFT investigations of the key steps of the enzymatic reaction, which reproduce the observed reaction regiospecificity and provide clues on how this regiospecificity is achieved. Comparison of the BvDODAα1-L-DOPA complex to other experimental structures of ES complexes of extradiol dioxygenases highlights the catalytic role of the distal “proton-shuttle” histidine.

articles.title: Titanium-Catalyzed Divergent Deoxycyclization for Synthesizing Semisaturated Nitrogen Heterocycles
articles.abstract: Semisaturated nitrogen heterocycles, such as 3-pyrrolines and unsaturated azepanes, possess highly prized three-dimensional geometries for drug discovery. However, their divergent synthesis from simple, unactivated feedstocks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a highly selective, titanium-catalyzed divergent radical deoxycyclization coupling of nitrosoarenes and 1,3-dienes. Following an initial aza-Diels–Alder cycloaddition, an in situ generated low-valent titanium(III) species mediates single-electron homolytic cleavage of the robust oxazine N–O bond, yielding a transient nitrogen-centered aminyl radical. By rationally tuning the solvent coordination sphere and chlorosilane dissociation kinetics, this radical’s trajectory is selectively directed down two orthogonal pathways: a 5-exo-tet cyclization to afford 3-pyrrolines (formal [4 + 1]) and a highly strained vinylaziridine-mediated aza-Claisen rearrangement to yield unsaturated azepanes (formal [4 + 3]). This radical-polar crossover protocol features broad functional group tolerance and enables a streamlined, cyanide-free synthesis of the antiarrhythmic drug candidate SU-13197. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including EPR spin-trapping, support the crucial aminyl radical intermediacy and the important role of titanium coordination in orchestrating cascade divergence.

articles.title: Understanding the Role of Band Bending and Surface Coordination in Steering Piezocatalytic In Situ H2O2 Evolution Routes
articles.abstract: Piezocatalytic H2O2 production, employing water and oxygen as the raw materials, is emerging as a promising and viable alternative for in situ H2O2 evolution. However, the understanding of the structure–activity relationship of piezocatalysts still poses challenges, and the key factor steering the H2O2 evolution pathway also remains ambiguous. Herein, two bismuth ferrite-based materials with different crystal structures, perovskite-type BiFeO3 and mullite-type Bi2Fe4O9, were prepared for a systematic comparison of their piezocatalytic activity and an in-depth investigation into the routes of H2O2 in situ production. As a result, BiFeO3 achieved a higher H2O2 production rate (252.86 μmol·L–1) than Bi2Fe4O9 (140.32 μmol·L–1) over 60 min in ambient aqueous conditions without any sacrificial agent. Mechanism analysis reveals that a higher piezocatalytic H2O2 yield of BiFeO3 arises from its stronger piezoelectric response and surface coordination mode of bridging hydroxyl groups. The piezoelectric-induced band bending made water oxidation thermodynamically feasible, and the bridging hydroxyl groups offered hole-transfer channels, thereby collectively triggering the simultaneous occurrence of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and water oxidation reaction (WOR). This work provides fundamental insights into the crystal-structure-dependent piezocatalytic activity, offering a profound understanding of the mechanism underlying H2O2 evolution routes.

articles.title: Untangling the Molecular Mechanism of SpCas9 HNH Domain Checkpoint Activation: A Gear-and-Wedge Fitting Model
articles.abstract: The CRISPR-associated endonuclease Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (SpCas9) facilitates site-specific DNA cleavage, with structural transition from the checkpoint state to the catalytic conformation representing a critical activation step. This transition involves an approximately 38 Å displacement of the HNH domain catalytic residue H840 toward the target DNA. However, the molecular determinants governing this large-scale rearrangement of the HNH domain during checkpoint activation, and the conformational routes by which HNH repositioning may occur, remain incompletely understood. To address this knowledge gap, we combined nudged elastic band-guided sampling with unbiased molecular dynamics simulations, reaching a cumulative timescale of 160 μs, and constructed a kinetic model describing HNH domain dynamics during checkpoint activation with Markov state modeling. The mechanistic features suggested by these simulations were further evaluated through biochemical DNA cleavage assays and an intracellular fluorescence reporter system. Our results identify conformational plasticity of the L2 linker and coupled motion of the REC2 domain as key regulatory elements of the HNH domain relocation during SpCas9 checkpoint activation. The model suggests that L2 linker remodels toward a disassembled state to enable release and repositioning of the HNH domain, while the REC2 domain outward displacement guides HNH domain relocation through transient interactions that stabilize activation-associated intermediates. Site-directed mutagenesis of key residues in the L2 linker and REC2 domain significantly reduced DNA cleavage efficiency in both biochemical and cellular assays, supporting their functional importance in SpCas9 activation. Taken together, this study provides an experimentally grounded mechanistic framework for understanding how linker dynamics and REC2 domain coupling regulate HNH domain checkpoint activation, and offers insights for rational engineering of SpCas9 variants with altered activity and specificity.

articles.title: Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Enables Energy-Efficient Hydrogen Peroxide and Carbonate Coproduction from CO-Rich Flue Gas and Air
articles.abstract: The electrochemical carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) is an attractive anodic alternative to the oxygen evolution reaction, offering a route to lower the energy demand of electrosynthesis while utilizing abundant industrial waste gas. However, COOR has rarely been implemented in practical paired electrolysis systems because of modest device-level performance, reliance on purified CO feedstocks, and operational instability. Here, we establish a COOR∥two-electron oxygen reduction reaction paired electrolysis platform for H2O2 and CO32– coproduction using simulated CO-rich steelmaking flue gas. The system sustains bias-free operation for >140 h. Under high-current-density operation, in situ surface analysis revealed that interfacial carbonate accumulation causes anodic passivation and current decay. Pulsed electrolysis was introduced to alleviate such carbonate buildup and stabilized operation at 100 mA cm–2. Techno-economic analysis estimated an H2O2 minimum selling price of $0.71 kg–1. Together, these results establish COOR as a practical strategy for energy-efficient electrosynthesis using industrial waste gas.

articles.title: Tautomeric Metal-Polymer Coordination Enables Damage-Free Laminated Carbon Electrodes in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Integrating dry carbon electrodes (CEs) into inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) offers a solvent-free, scalable route to low-cost photovoltaics. However, mechanical stress during lamination and the large work-function mismatch between the CE and the electron transport layer (ETL) can compromise performance. Here, we report an interface engineering strategy utilizing a silver-2-mercaptobenzothiazole (Ag-MBT) metal-polymer buffer layer to enable high-efficiency inverted CE-based PSCs (C-PSCs). XPS reveals Ag-induced changes in the sulfur and nitrogen chemical environments of MBT, consistent with the formation of an Ag-MBT interfacial coordination layer involving Ag–S coordination. This coordination-derived interlayer serves a dual function: it acts as a structural buffer, enabling damage-free dry CE lamination, and it establishes an energetic band alignment that bridges the ETL/CE work-function gap. Consequently, our devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.12% and maintain their initial efficiency after 1000 h of dark N2 storage, establishing metal-polymer interfacial coordination as a viable pathway for robust inverted C-PSCs.

articles.title: Unlocking Quantum Confinement in Two-/Three-Dimensional Tin-Based Perovskites for High-Efficiency Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) mixed tin halide perovskites are promising lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, but uncontrolled crystallization produces excessive low-n phases that impede charge extraction due to a quantum confinement effect. Here, we employ 1,4-benzenediammonium iodide (1,4-BDI2) as a multifunctional additive to regulate crystallization, phase distribution, and defects. The additive modulates precursor colloid assembly and retards low-dimensional crystal growth, yielding dense films dominated by highly oriented three-dimensional perovskites with suppressed n = 1 and reduced n = 2 phases. Meanwhile, 1,4-BD2+ cations and unincorporated organic ligands accumulate at grain boundaries to form a passivating complex that passivates deep-trap states and forms favorable interfacial energy-level alignment to promote charge transfer. Consequently, inverted tin perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.94% and an open-circuit voltage of 0.91 V, together with improved operational and storage stability. This work establishes an integrated molecular strategy for phase regulation and defect passivation in efficient lead-free photovoltaics.

articles.title: Activity-Stability Balance Enabled by Orbital Splitting Energy in Ruthenium-Based Oxide Catalysts
articles.abstract: Ruthenium oxides have been the model catalyst for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction. It has been a challenge to achieve both stability and activity and establish a comprehensive descriptor for Ru-based catalysts. Herein, guided by the ligand field theory, we introduce the Ru orbital splitting energy (ΔRu) as a quantitative parameter to describe the interaction between Ru 4d and O 2p orbitals to govern the overall catalytic performance. A series of two-dimensional (2D) multielement metal oxides are synthesized via a self-assembly method to modulate ΔRu. The optimized RuCoFeNiO catalyst for water oxidation delivers a current density of 10 mA cm–2 at a low overpotential of 180 mV and shows high activity for more than 2500 h at 1 A cm–2 in acidic condition. In situ measurements and theoretical analysis reveal that the surface hydrogen-bond network balances the amount of surficial two-hydrogen-bonded water and free water, boosting the proton-transfer process. Moreover, the optimized ΔRu (2.405 eV) modifies the adsorption of *OOH on Ru sites, switching the dominant reaction pathway from the lattice oxygen mediated mechanism to absorbate evolution mechanism. This work highlights the pivotal role of ΔRu in tailoring both stability and activity and may offer insights into high-entropy 2D Ru-based oxides as high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Breaking the High-Voltage Limit of Na2CO3 Presodiation: An Interfacial Engineering Approach to Ampere-Hour Sodium-Ion Devices
articles.abstract: Na2CO3 is a promising sacrificial presodiation agent owing to its high capacity, excellent air stability, and low cost. However, its practical application is severely hampered by a high decomposition overpotential (>4.3 V vs Na/Na+), inducing detrimental electrolyte oxidation and cell degradation. To break this high-voltage limit, we propose an in situ interfacial dual-modification strategy, synergistically introducing interfacial oxygen vacancies and triggering electronic reconstruction, which thermodynamically lowers the reaction Gibbs free energy and kinetically diminishes the activation barriers, resulting in a dramatically reduced decomposition potential by 350 mV. Operando three-electrode diagnostics within a full sodium-ion capacitor reveal that this interface engineering not only facilitates efficient Na+ release (496.9 mAh g–1) at lower potential but also reduces the actual working potential of cathode, thereby fundamentally avoiding high-voltage parasitic reactions, according well with the DEMS and TOF-SIMS results. Consequently, the full cell achieves a considerable 117.4% enhancement in energy density. Most importantly, this strategy demonstrates compelling practicality in ampere-hour-level devices, delivering a substantial 22.4% boost in energy density with only 3 wt % additive in 1.5 Ah pouch cells. This work bridges microscopic interfacial chemistry and macroscopic device performance, providing a scalable and efficient blueprint for low-potential presodiation toward high-energy-density sodium-ion devices.

articles.title: Exclusive Detection of Dimethyl Sulfide by a Pd–WO3 Sensor with the CuO/Al2O3 Filtering Overlayer
articles.abstract: Selective detection of trace (weakly reducing) dimethyl sulfide (DMS) in highly humid exhaled breath using metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors, with the presence of strong reducing H2S interference gas, is essential for the early diagnosis of hepatic diseases. However, it remains a big challenge in principle. Herein, a bilayer MOS sensor with a Pd–WO3 sensing film and a CuO/Al2O3 filtering overlayer was proposed. The temperature-dependent H2S catalytic oxidation experiment suggests that CuO could effectively filter H2S even under room temperature. Dispersing the CuO particles into insulative Al2O3 carrier could not only selectively remove H2S without significant consumption of DMS but also isolate the underlying Pd–WO3 sensing layer’s response signal from interference caused by that of CuO. By adding the CuO/Al2O3 1:9 filtering overlayer, the response ratio of DMS to H2S was significantly enhanced from 3.3 to 50.4, furthermore, an ultrahigh response (701.3) to 10 ppm DMS, and a low limit of detection of 10 ppb under 90% RH were achieved, which promises the future breath disease diagnosis.

articles.title: Morphology and Ion Transport in Zwitterionic Polysiloxanes
articles.abstract: The recent discovery of superionic conductivity in doped polyzwitterions (PZIs) has opened a new direction for polymer electrolytes (PEs). Solid-state battery research is currently dominated by inorganic electrolytes due to their rigidity and high conductivity, but they suffer from poor electrode adhesion and processability issues. While PEs overcome these issues, they typically suffer from low ionic conductivity. Recently, salt-doped PZIs have emerged as promising candidates, where high concentrations of ionic species and local dipolar interactions can reduce energy barriers for ion transport and therefore increase room-temperature ionic conductivity. Here, we demonstrate that superionic conductivity is not a universal behavior of doped PZIs, but rather a strategic design of ion-transport pathways is required. Using a flexible polysiloxane-based PZI doped with LiTFSI salt, we observe that room-temperature conductivity remains limited (∼10–8 S/cm at 293 K) despite a relatively low glass transition temperature and high dielectric constant. X-ray scattering reveals the structural origin of this behavior; namely, zwitterionic groups aggregate into isolated nanodomains separated by the polymer matrix, which slows down ion mobility. Once these clusters start overlapping, doped PZI showed significant enhancement in conductivity. These results demonstrate the critical role of percolating ion channels for superionic conductivity in PZIs.

articles.title: Single-Molecule Studies Reveal That Water Starts to Protect Proteins Even at the ppm Level
articles.abstract: A consensus established by extensive thermodynamic and structural studies of proteins and DNA is that water acts as an indispensable structural cofactor rather than a passive solvent for biomolecules. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether trace water still exerts a stabilizing effect on proteins under ultradry conditions. Nonpolar organic solvents that spontaneously absorbed trace water provide an ideal platform to investigate this issue. Herein, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) was employed to investigate the mechanical behaviors of two model polyproteins, (GB1)8 and (I27)8, in nonpolar organic solvents with varying water contents. It was found that even at the ppm level, water protects protein stability and acts as a molecular switch: polyproteins fully denature at water contents ≤80 ppm (nonane and tetradecane), while metastable folded fragments can be retained at water contents ≥95 ppm (tetrachloroethane (TCE) and octane) with a characteristic unfolding force of approximately 100 pN. Force-free molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a smaller (I27)2 model in TCE further suggested that trace water accumulated preferentially around the protein, reorganizing the local solvation environment, thereby serving as a stabilizer. Based on the SMFS results, the water-content range of 80–95 ppm was identified as a critical threshold, across which polyproteins toggle between fully denatured and partially stabilized states. This work reveals the protective effect of trace water on proteins, quantifies its stabilizing capacity down to the ppm level, and offers insights for protein storage and astrobiology research.

articles.title: Unified Single-Transistor Cell for Multimode Reconfigurable Logic and Ternary In-Memory Search
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of data-intensive applications demands efficient data processing with reduced data movement. Logic-in-memory (LIM) and in-memory search, exemplified by ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM), offer promising solutions; however, their typical implementation in separate device modules leads to increased circuit complexity and limited cell-level functional density. Here, we demonstrate a split-gate van der Waals ferroelectric field-effect transistor (vdW FeFET) as a unified operational cell for multimode reconfigurable logic and ternary in-memory search. The architecture integrates two parallel split gates, employing MoS2 as the channel and ferroelectric CuInP2S6 as the gate dielectric. Polarity-dependent modulation by the split gates and the drain bias enables multimode reconfigurable logic operation, supporting six Boolean functions, including directional data transfer. The same device can be programmed for associative memory equivalent to a one-transistor-per-cell TCAM, where two spatially separated ferroelectric regions are programmed within one continuous MoS2 channel, allowing ternary states to be stored and match and mismatch responses to be encoded directly into the channel current. Device-calibrated statistical simulations confirm ranking-based row discrimination under realistic device variability. By linking reconfigurable logic, spatial ferroelectric programming, and current-domain associative search within a common split-gate device framework, this work presents a compact transistor platform for logic-search-coupled in-memory computing.

articles.title: Coordination Number-Bandgap Relationships at Grain Boundaries in Battery Electrolytes
Multiple phases growth dynamics of a recycled Al alloy under pulse magnetic fields – an operando study by the ESRF-EBS and multiphysics modelling
Anion‐Transferring Electrolyte Enables In Situ Construction of Uniform LiF‐Rich Interphases for Long‐Cycling Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Stabilizing electrode/electrolyte interphases is crucial for high-performance lithium–sulfur batteries; however, simultaneously fabricating robust interphases on both the lithium anode and sulfur cathode is challenging. Here, we report an anion-transferring functional electrolyte containing non-expendable tetramethylammonium (TMA) bromide that enables the in situ formation of LiF-rich interphases on both electrodes. The TMA+ cations act as ion carriers that electrostatically shuttle PF6− anions from the bulk electrolyte to the electrode/electrolyte interfaces in the form of ion pairs. This localized enrichment of PF6 − facilitates its electrochemical decomposition, leading to the formation of a uniform LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase on the anode and a cathode-electrolyte interphase on the sulfur cathode. The LiF-rich interphases show a high Young's modulus, which help suppress interfacial parasitic reactions and Li dendrite formation. The adsorbed TMA+ cations form an electrostatic shielding layer that mitigates local Li+ flux heterogeneity, further suppressing dendrite growth. When applied to Li-SPAN batteries, they maintain a 92% capacity retention after 350 cycles at 1 C and deliver a high reversible capacity of 1039 mAh g−1 after 300 cycles at 0.5 C. This work provides an innovative alternative to conventional interphase engineering for stabilizing lithium battery interphases.

articles.title: Antiferrodistortive Matrix Engineering Reprograms Polarization Pathways for Ultrahigh Energy Storage at Moderate Electric Fields
articles.abstract: Relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs) are promising dielectric materials for pulsed multilayer ceramic capacitors because of their rapid polarization response. However, under practical electric fields, polarization rapidly approaches saturation as polar nanoregions exhaust their nonlinear switching capability, fundamentally limiting energy-storage performance. Here we demonstrate that antiferrodistortive matrix engineering reprograms the polarization evolution pathway through a polarization dormancy–awakening process. Long-range antiferrodistortive modulation, introduced by the intrinsic lattice instability of CaZrO3 in a (Bi0.5Na0.4K0.1)TiO3 matrix, creates local strain fields that temporarily suppress PNR switching and progressively awaken dormant polarization under moderate electric fields. This substantially extends the nonlinear polarization-response regime without inducing ferroelectric or antiferroelectric ordering. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy, electron diffraction, and phase-field simulations collectively reveal the structural origin of the awakening behavior and its coupling to local polarization dynamics. Consequently, the engineered relaxor ceramic achieves an ultrahigh recoverable energy-storage density of 12.3 J cm– 3 with an energy-storage efficiency of 87.4% at 520 kV cm– 1, representing a benchmark performance for bulk RFE ceramics operating under moderate electric fields. This work establishes antiferrodistortive matrix engineering as a promising design strategy for reprogramming polarization evolution in RFEs toward high-performance dielectric energy storage.

articles.title: Asymmetric Interfacial Charge Gradients Enable Dual‐Pathway Proton Transfer for High‐Flux Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Accelerating water dissociation while maintaining efficient proton transfer remains a substantial challenge in high‐flux alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we introduce an interfacial engineering strategy to develop a high‐flux alkaline HER electrocatalyst with controllable spatially asymmetric interfacial charge gradients, by incorporating size‐tunable Ni nanoparticles at Mo2N/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfacial regions to create a Ni‐nanoparticle‐bridged dual‐interface heterogeneous structure with coordinated proton‐transfer pathways. The resultant electrocatalyst achieves an industrial current density of 1.0 A cm−2 at 1.74 V in an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer, outperforming commercial Pt/C by 10%, while sustaining 100 h intermittent operation under 10–1000 mA cm−2 current cycling, demonstrating robust operational stability under high‐flux conditions. Such high‐flux HER capability can be attributed to the formation of asymmetric charge gradients along the Ni/Mo2N and Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interfaces, which reorient interfacial water molecules into favorable configurations to promote dissociation at apical Ni nanoparticle sites and continuously supply protons. Simultaneously, the generated protons are directed through two coordinated pathways consisting of electrostatically guided surface migration at the negatively polarized Ni/Mo2N interface and hydrogen‐bond‐network‐mediated hopping at the positively polarized Ni/Ni0.2Mo0.8N interface, safeguarding against proton‐transfer bottlenecks and active‐site blockage under high‐flux conditions. This work establishes interfacial charge gradient regulation as a design principle for high‐flux alkaline HER.

articles.title: Breaking the Degradation Domino in Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathode Via Precise Electrostatic Pinning and Gradient Shielding
articles.abstract: Benefiting from the anionic redox activity, lithium‐rich layered oxide cathodes exhibit high specific capacity, but the migration of transition metal (TM) can exacerbate vacancy clustering, resulting in domino‐like structural degradation. To stabilize the structure, the electrostatic pinning effect is precisely incorporated into the Li layer to mitigate the TM migration via strong electrostatic repulsion. Concurrently, this configuration effectively modulates the electronic distribution around the oxygen ligands, thereby stabilizing the oxygen redox. Furthermore, robust electrostatic interactions endow the material with the capability to adaptively adjust its interlayer spacing, thereby buffering the structural evolution of the layered framework during (de)lithiation processes. The modified cathode achieves an 89.1% capacity retention over 400 cycles in half‐cells and an impressive 96.2% over 1000 cycles in full cells. To further decouple the capacity‐stability trade‐off while concurrently enhancing both bulk and interfacial stability, we engineered a gradient shielding architecture. This design not only attains 219.8 mAh g−1 at 0.5C and delivers capacity retention of 90.8% after 400 cycles but also promotes the formation of a compact CEI at the near‐surface region, markedly improving interfacial stability under harsh conditions. This progressive structural engineering paradigm offers fresh insights into overcoming the intrinsic structural challenges of lithium‐rich cathode materials.

articles.title: Chelation Compensation Strategy for High‐Performance Iron‐Based Redox Flow Batteries
articles.abstract: Iron‐based redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are compelling candidates for cost‐effective grid‐scale energy storage, benefiting from high safety, low cost, and the natural abundance of iron‐based active species. However, heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and kinetic deactivation lead to capacity decay and energy efficiency reduction, which limits the long‐term cycle stability of IRFBs. Chelation compensation is employed to regulate metal‐ion redox species through multidentate ligand design. Their coordination environment, solvation structure, and interfacial reactivity are thereby optimized, leading to improved energy efficiency and cycling stability. This review summarizes the major degradation mechanisms of IRFBs and highlights recent progress in chelation‐modified systems constructed with representative chelating functional groups. Particular attention is given to the influence of chelation on heterogeneous interface instability, side reactions, and reaction kinetics. Finally, current challenges and future directions in ligand design, electrolyte compatibility, mechanistic understanding, and practical implementation are discussed, offering guidance for the development of high‐performance chelation‐modified IRFBs for large‐scale energy storage.

articles.title: Clean Tin Oxide via Volatile Additive Engineering for High‐performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: SnO2 is a benchmark electron transport material for perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, SnO2 films from the conventional chemical bath deposition (CBD) are limited by impurities and defects that accelerate non‐radiative recombination and compromise device stability. Here, we present a volatile additive engineering strategy using pyruvic acid (PA) as a dual‐functional nucleation promoter and surface modulator during SnO2 deposition. Owing to its volatility (sublimation at 145°C), PA can be effectively removed during annealing, resulting in cleaner SnO2 surfaces with reduced residual groups. This is accompanied by a decrease in oxygen‐related defect densities in the SnO2 layer. This improvement leads to enhanced charge recombination and improved thermal stability at the buried interface. Consequently, PA‐engineered PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.17%, together with improved device stability, retaining >80% of their initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation, 1000 h at 65°C, and 30 days under 30% relative humidity. Furthermore, this approach is compatible with large‐area fabrication, yielding efficiencies of 24.83% for 1 cm2 lab‐scale cells and 20.21% for 30 cm × 30 cm industrial‐scale solar modules. These results suggest that controlling additive volatility improves CBD‐SnO2 quality and offers a promising route for stable, scalable perovskite solar cells.

articles.title: Deciphering Interfacial Water Configuration via Nucleophilic Doping: Highly Connected H‐Bond Networks for Efficient Neutral Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Neutral hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) faces sluggish kinetics due to strong cation hydration disrupting interfacial hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks, impeding mass transport. Herein, we propose a nucleophilic doping strategy to reconstruct the interfacial water structure and boost neutral HER performance. By engineering a nucleophilic oxygen‐doped molybdenum selenide/molybdenum phosphide hybrid on carbon cloth (Ox‐MoSe2‐x/MoP/CC), we successfully manipulate the local electronic environment to attenuate cation hydration effects. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations coupled with in situ Raman spectroscopy provide compelling evidence that the incorporated nucleophilic O species trigger a reconfiguration of interfacial water, fostering the formation of highly connected H‐bond networks. These optimized networks serve as efficient highways for intermediate transport, significantly lowering the mass transfer resistance. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal a synergistic mechanism where the MoP phase acts as a potent water dissociation promoter, facilitating the Volmer step. Consequently, the Ox‐MoSe2‐x/MoP/CC electrode delivers a remarkable overpotential of only 34 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M phosphate buffer solution, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and exhibits superior long‐term stability. This work not only presents a high‐performance electrocatalyst but also highlights the pivotal role of nucleophilic modulation in engineering interfacial H‐bond networks for efficient neutral electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Decoding Multiscale Degradation of Layered Cathodes in All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries: An Advanced Diagnostics‐Driven Framework
articles.abstract: All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) with layered oxide cathodes such as LiNi 1-x-y Mn x Co y O2 (NMC), LiNi 1-x-y Co x Al y O2 (NCA), LiNiO2 (LNO), and lithium-rich layered oxides (LLOs) offer superior energy density and safety, yet their performance is severely limited by complex, coupled degradation mechanisms at the cathode/inorganic solid-state electrolyte (SSE) interface and within the cathode bulk. This review establishes a Diagnosis-Mechanism-Mitigation (D-M-M) framework that decodes these multiscale degradation phenomena by cross-validating multimodal diagnostic evidence from electronic structure to the cell level. Two categories are dissected: interfacial degradation, encompassing chemical decomposition, space-charge layer formation, and resistive interphase growth; and bulk cathode degradation, including structural phase transitions, cation disorder, oxygen loss, and microstructural cracking. Drawing on advanced spectroscopy, microscopy, 3D imaging, and in situ/operando methods, each degradation cascade is traced from its diagnostic signature to its mechanism and to the validated mitigation it informed, from interfacial coatings to dopant engineering and microstructure optimization. Machine learning and artificial intelligence are assessed for interpreting complex diagnostic datasets and guiding predictive cathode design. The framework is further extended to practically relevant conditions (thick electrodes, low stack pressure, and large-format cells), and the field's unresolved controversies are delineated together with the experiments that would decide them.

articles.title: Dual‑Diol Synergized Electrolyte for Wide‑Temperature Hydrogel Zn‑Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) feature low cost, superior safety, and eco‐friendliness, promising extensive prospects for next‐generation electrochemical energy storage. Nevertheless, inferior interfacial stability, uncontrollable Zn dendrite formation, and poor temperature tolerance severely hinder their practical exploitation in flexible electronic devices. Herein, glycerol (Gly) and ethylene glycol (EG) are incorporated into a polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogel matrix via a facile one‐pot route to fabricate a wide‐temperature‐tolerant PAM‐based composite hydrogel electrolyte (PAM/Gly/EG). Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the two diols, the hydroxyl‐rich structure reconstructs the intrinsic hydrogen bond network of confined water, while coordination interactions modulate the solvation configuration of Zn2+, thereby fundamentally restraining Zn dendrite propagation and parasitic hydrogen evolution. The resultant Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers a long stable lifespan over 3000 h at 1 mA·cm−2, and sustains steady cycling for 500 h at −20°C and 300 h at 50°C. This synergistic diol modification strategy affords a feasible avenue for structural optimization and practical deployment of wide‐temperature flexible AZIBs.

articles.title: Electrochemically Driven Refrigeration Based on Dissolution–Crystallization Cycle of Redox‐Active Salts
articles.abstract: Developing energy‐efficient and environmentally sustainable refrigeration technologies is critically important for mitigating climate change. Here, we report an electrochemically driven dissolution–crystallization refrigeration cycle (EDCR), a liquid‐state electrochemical cooling concept in which cooling is generated by the endothermic dissolution of electrochemically regenerated redox‐active salts. Unlike conventional electrochemical refrigeration, where the cooling effect arises directly from endothermic redox reactions and is therefore partly offset by Joule heating, EDCR spatially separates electrochemical regeneration from dissolution‐based cooling. The EDCR achieves a maximum temperature drop of 5.65 K and a maximum coefficient of performance of up to 15.51 under ideal condition without heat loss, corresponding to a relative Carnot efficiency of 29.8% at room temperature. This proof‐of‐concept study establishes EDCR as a promising hydrofluorocarbon‐free refrigeration strategy and provides a new route for exploring liquid‐state electrochemical cooling cycle.

articles.title: Electrochemically Driven Refrigeration Based on Dissolution–Crystallization Cycle of Redox‐Active Salts (Adv. Energy Mater. 38/2026)
articles.abstract: Refrigeration Electrochemically driven dissolution–crystallization refrigeration couples the endothermic dissolution of redox‐active salts with electrochemical regeneration. As depicted on the cover, regenerated crystals dissolve in the foreground cooling reservoir to absorb heat, while the electrolyte circulates through the electrochemical cell for recrystallization and reuse. Spatially separating cooling from electrochemical regeneration minimizes direct interference from Joule heating. More in article number e71304, Pei Liu, Jia Li, Jiangjiang Duan, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Elucidating the Suppression of High‐Voltage Degradation in O3‐type NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2: A Voltage‐Switching Strategy for Na‐ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Elevating depth‐of‐charge (DoC) enhances the energy density of layered oxide cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries; however, such high‐DoC cycling inevitably triggers severe structural and interfacial degradation. In practice, battery management systems commonly adapt voltage‐derating strategies dynamically according to battery state of health, achieving a favorable trade‐off between energy density and cycle life. Nevertheless, a critical yet overlooked question remains: how high‐DoC‐induced damaged regions evolve when reverted to moderate‐DoC cycling. Here, using NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM111) as a prototype, a voltage‐switching strategy is employed to elucidate the dynamic and long‐term behavior of these damaged regions. During high‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.3 V), the rapid capacity fading is driven by pronounced formation of bulk defects and interfacial disordered spinel phases. However, upon switching these cells to moderate‐DoC cycling (charging to 4.0 V), these pre‐existing damaged regions become stabilized: their rapid propagation is suppressed, and they no longer accelerate degradation in surrounding intact regions. This enables degraded NFM111 to deliver capacity retention comparable to that of cells cycled solely under moderate‐DoC conditions. This work presents a dynamic and evolving picture of high‐DoC degradation and subsequent moderate‐DoC stabilization in NFM111 cathodes, providing mechanistic insights into voltage‐derating process and the lifetime prolongation of compromised cells.

articles.title: Enabling Low‐Temperature Fast‐Charging Anode‐Free Sodium Metal Batteries: A Synergistic Design of Electrolyte Solvation and Current Collector Interface
articles.abstract: Anode‐free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) promise ultrahigh energy density (>350 Wh kg−1) and low cost, yet their operation under low‐temperature and fast‐charging conditions is critically hindered by limited sodium inventory and sluggish interfacial kinetics. This conflict creates a “stability paradox”: the pursuit of high energy density amplifies interfacial instability, leading to inhomogeneous sodium deposition and rapid capacity decay. This review systematically analyzes AFSMB failure mechanisms under extreme conditions and demonstrates that overcoming these bottlenecks requires integrated co‐design across four synergistic domains: (1) engineering electrolyte solvation structures (weakly solvating, high‐concentration, and high‐entropy designs) to lower the desolvation barrier and stabilize the solid–electrolyte interphase; (2) tailoring current collector interfaces with sodiophilic coatings or three‐dimensional architectures to guide uniform sodium deposition; (3) incorporating rational pre‐sodiation strategies to compensate irreversible sodium loss; and (4) leveraging artificial intelligence and molecular simulations for data‐driven electrolyte screening. We critically assess the trade‐offs of each strategy and provide a forward‐looking perspective on reversible sodium compensation, multi‐scale AI platforms, and full‐cell integration. This review offers a roadmap for developing practical, wide‐temperature‐range, high‐energy‐density AFSMBs, with recent pouch cells already demonstrating >200 Wh kg−1 and stable cycling from −40°C to 60°C.

articles.title: Enhanced Figure‐of‐Merit Energy Harvesting in [001]‐Oriented PMN‐PZT Ceramics Via Synergistic Multi‐Scale Engineering
articles.abstract: Developing piezoelectric materials with a high figure-of-merit (FOM = d 33×g 33/tanδ) is crucial for advanced energy-harvesting technologies. Here, a high FOM is achieved in [001]-oriented Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbZrO3-PbTiO3 (PMN-PZT) textured ceramics by synergistically integrating grain orientation, defect engineering, and morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) design. The textured ceramic exhibits exceptional properties (piezoelectric charge coefficient d 33 = 1120 pC·N−1, piezoelectric voltage coefficient g 33 = 62 × 10−3 V·m·N−1, and an ultralow dielectric loss tanδ = 0.23%). Atomic-scale analysis reveals that the [001] intrinsic anisotropy and mixed rhombohedral-tetragonal domains facilitate polarization rotation to boost d 33 and g 33, while Mn doping-induced defect dipoles suppress dielectric loss. Consequently, an ultrahigh FOM of 30,180 × 10−12 m2·N−1 is realized. Furthermore, a cantilever energy harvester utilizing this textured ceramic delivers an outstanding power density of 0.72 µW·mm−3, which is 78 times higher than that of commercial soft PZT. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high-FOM piezoelectric materials for high performance energy harvesting applications.

articles.title: Experimentally Determined Spatiotemporal Charge Carrier Dynamics for the Development of Particulate Photocatalysts
articles.abstract: Particulate photocatalysts have generated interest for the low‐cost implementation of various photocatalytic processes, including the production of solar fuels as clean energy sources. With light absorption, charge generation, charge transport, and interfacial charge transfer all constrained in individual particles, complex photophysical and photochemical processes occur on a wide range of timescales within spatially defined volumes. The allure of deciphering the charge carrier dynamics to build a fundamental picture of photocatalysis in different materials has motivated the development of state‐of‐the‐art spatiotemporal measurement techniques. Monitoring charge carrier dynamics on relevant time and length scales is a challenging experimental task. Many experimental barriers have been overcome in recent years, providing some guidance for future directions for material development. This review delves into the underlying origins of spatial heterogeneity in charge carrier dynamics, introduces charge carrier transport phenomena, and details the recent examples of spatiotemporal investigation of charge carrier dynamics in particulate photocatalysts. These new experimental capabilities pave the way for a more comprehensive description of photocatalytic processes, guiding the optimization of photocatalytic materials.

articles.title: Functional Motif Directed Decoupling‐Recoupling Strategy for Constructing Multi‐Site Pt‐Based Catalyst Toward Efficient Hydrogen Oxidation in Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: Hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) in alkaline media suffers from multiple challenges of sluggish kinetics, CO poisoning, and active-site degradation. Multi-metallic catalysts with multiple active sites hold promise for addressing the issues; however, they are thwarted by structural heterogeneity at the atomic level and reliance on empirical trial-and-error screening. Herein, we introduce a novel functional motif directed decoupling-recoupling strategy for the design of multi-site catalysts capable of super-active and durable HOR electrocatalysis. Leveraging the well-defined atomic coordinates for each element and superlattice ordering structure of the PtM intermetallic compound (IMC), the development of a multi-functional Pt-based HOR catalyst is decoupled into the independent screening of discrete Pt–M functional motifs. These optimally selected Pt–M motifs were subsequently recoupled into an L10-PtFe framework, constructing the designed PtRuFeGaMo-I catalyst. PtRuFeGaMo-I integrates the multifunctionality of Pt–Ru/Ga/Mo motifs to simultaneously overcome the key limitations of alkaline HOR. Consequently, the engineered PtRuFeGaMo-I exhibits exceptional HOR performance. In an anion exchange membrane fuel cell (AEMFC), PtRuFeGaMo-I achieves a remarkable mass activity of 0.84 A mgtotal PGM −1, surpassing commercial Pt/C and most reported noble-metal-based catalysts. This work provides a new platform to design advanced catalysts tailored to diverse electrocatalytic demands.

articles.title: Holistic Top‐to‐Bottom Film Restructuring to Achieve Highly Stable Unencapsulated Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: While perovskites have emerged as frontrunners in optoelectronics due to their exceptional properties, their performance remains bottlenecked by film imperfections such as interfacial defects, non‐uniform crystallization, and band alignment mismatches. Conventional treatments often fail to simultaneously address issues at the top surface, the bulk, and the buried interface. In this work, we introduce a holistic top‐to‐bottom restructuring strategy using a facile vapor‐phase post‐treatment. This approach induces a gradient‐distributed 2D perovskite phase that extends from the surface into the bulk while uniquely healing structural voids and chemical inhomogeneities at the buried interface. This synergistic restructuring optimizes the energy band structure for accelerated carrier extraction and passivates defects throughout the entire film depth. As a result, our unencapsulated n‐i‐p solar cells demonstrate exceptional environmental resilience, maintaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 2,800 h of high‐humidity exposure. This study establishes a new benchmark for stability and provides a robust pathway for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Integrating Machine Learning and High‐Throughput Calculations for the Rational Design of Photocatalytic 2D‐COFs on Overall Water Splitting
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D-COFs) with tunable structures offer a promising platform for photocatalytic overall water splitting (OWS) under visible-light. However, it is challenging to quickly find photocatalytic OWS materials from the massive amounts of 2D-COFs and then achieve precise synthesis. In this work, we constructed 11 934 hcb-type 2D-COFs by assembling 28 building blocks and 9 linkages. The machine learning (ML) and high-throughput computation (HTC) were integrated to predict feasible photocatalytic OWS hcb-type 2D-COFs. Through training 10 initial algorithms and optimizing the hyperparameters of top 4 algorithms in terms of performance, the ETR model for predicting the band-edge levels with R2 of 0.97 and 0.99 was developed, and the KNR and RFR models were built for predicting ΔG *H and ΔG *OH with R2 of 0.99 and 0.83, respectively. 2581 2D‑COFs (21.63% of dataset) are screened to be potential structures for visible‑light‑driven water splitting. After applying the optimal ML models on all assembled 2D-COFs, a list of high-frequency building blocks and linkages is suggested as a set of suitable candidates for the first time. Then TBTZ_FBN0_Imine (TBTZ-FBN0-COF) was assembled and experimentally synthesized. Its OWS activity verified our ML-HTC paradigm, which provides the researchers recommendation to construct photocatalytic OWS 2D-COFs.

articles.title: Interface Engineering via Ceria Coating Reconciles Ion Transport and Lithium Compatibility in Composite Polymer Electrolytes
