articles.abstract: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) exhibit considerable potential for solid−state lithium−metal batteries (SLBs). However, incompatibilities between the various components in the electrolyte continue to hinder the full realization of its performance and practical applications. In this work, a multifunctional ceria interfacial layer is proposed to achieve uniform dispersion of ceramic fillers and facilitated interfacial transport of lithium ions in CPEs. At the same time, the physical barrier provided by this multifunctional interface layer prevents direct contact between the ceramic filler and the lithium metal, thereby avoiding potentially harmful side reactions that could further lead to a performance deterioration in battery cycling. Owing to the introduction of this multifunctional interface layer, the CPE exhibits high ionic conductivity (0.772 mS cm−1) and Li–ion transference number (0.626), with a wide electrochemical window (5.03 V). Furthermore, the Li|CPE|Li symmetric cell exhibits a lithium deposition/stripping capacity exceeding 1500 h at room temperature, indicating the CPE's excellent ability to suppress interfacial side reactions. Li|CPE|NCM811 cells retained a capacity of 77% after 350 cycles, whilst pouch cells retained 76% after 300 stable cycles at room temperature and 0.5 C. The method of optimizing ceramic fillers offers new insights into the design of novel composite solid–state electrolytes for SLBs.

articles.title: Internal Electric Field‐Guided, Low‐Adsorption Ferroelectric Anode Protective Layers for Sustainable Suppression of Polysulfide Side Reactions in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) offer energy densities beyond lithium-ion batteries, yet parasitic reactions between soluble polysulfides and lithium metal cause active-sulfur loss and porous Li, undermining cycle life. To address this problem, an anode protective layer is needed, but interactions between protective layers and polysulfides remain insufficiently understood. In this work, representative anionic and ceramic protective layers are employed as model systems to establish how strong polysulfide adsorption and persistent sulfur-species retention affect protective-layer functionality. Building on these findings, a positively polarized ferroelectric β-pvdf layer incorporating fluorinated boron nitride nanosheets (PPFBN) is introduced. Corona poling aligns polarization to establish an internal field, while insulating nanosheets suppress free-charge relaxation, thereby sustaining the field. The field promotes Li+ transport to the anode and impedes the approach of polysulfide anions, while intrinsically low polysulfide affinity limits long-term degradation of layer functionality. With PPFBN, Li/Li symmetric cells cycle stably for >1000 h in polysulfide-containing electrolytes at 2 mA cm− 2 and 2 mAh cm− 2. Full cells retain 80.4% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C; under lean-electrolyte conditions, cycle life extends by more than 150 cycles relative to bare Li. This study establishes a ferroelectric-field, low-polysulfide-affinity design principle for durable anode protection in LSBs.

articles.title: Ion‐Adaptive Molecular Structure Facilitates Mg‐Ion Dynamic for High‐Capacity Aqueous Magnesium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous magnesium‐ion batteries (AMIBs) have emerged as promising energy storage systems owing to their intrinsic safety, high energy density, and cost‐effectiveness. However, the intercalation of high‐charge‐density Mg2+ usually leads to irreversible structural degradation toward conventional electrodes with low practical capacity and inferior stability. To overcome the inherent lattice stress caused by Mg‐ion, we investigated a series of flexible organic molecules (FOMs), and for the first time proposed a novel ion‐adaptive strategy, achieving a high‐performance FOM with modulated molecular steric hindrance, high practical capacity, and robust stability in AMIBs. In contrast with ever‐increasing lattice stress with successive Mg‐ion intercalation in conventional electrode, the subsequent ion intercalation reduced the stress by facilitated ion‐storage in the optimized ion‐adaptive FOM, such as tribenzoquinoxaline‐5,10‐dione (3BQ), with ultimately improved practical capacity (332.1 mAh g−1 at 1.0 A g−1), ranking among the highest capacity in AMIBs to date. Furthermore, the expanded planar architecture confers enhanced cycling stability on the ion‐adaptive 3BQ, maintaining a high specific capacity of 196.7 mAh g−1 even after 7,000 cycles at 10.0 A g−1. The novel ion‐adaptive strategy provides a new pathway to design high‐capacity electrode materials in AMIBs and other multivalent‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Lewis Acid‐Enabled Functional SEI/CEI Design for Durable Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: The development of practical lithium metal batteries requires facile strategies that simultaneously stabilize anode and cathode interfaces while eliminating their native surface oxides. However, the reported research could rarely achieve this dual functionality. Herein, we have developed a dual‐side‐modification strategy using tributylphosphonium tetrafluoroborate (TBPFB) as a Lewis acid to synchronously eliminate the heterogeneous native oxide layers and reconstruct multifunctional inorganic interfaces on both the cathode and anode. The constructed artificial interface on the lithium anode contains LiF, LiBO2, Li3P, and Li3PO4, boosting the anode stability by reducing the Li+ desolvation barrier and enabling uniform Li+ transport. Meanwhile, the LiF‐rich LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathode interface suppresses side reactions and particle cracking, protecting the cathode from transition metal dissolution. Based on the benefits brought by the multifunctional interfaces, the Li||Li symmetric cells achieve a cycling lifespan of over 1700 h, while the Li||NCM811 full cells retain 77% capacity after 500 cycles. Additionally, a 2 Ah pouch cell with an energy density of 423.1 Wh kg−1 maintains over 90% capacity after 100 cycles. This work provides a simple but highly efficient surface modification strategy that stabilizes the most critical interfaces in lithium metal batteries.

articles.title: Light‐Induced Phase Segregation in Mixed‐Halide Perovskites: Reconciling Mechanistic and Thermodynamic Models
articles.abstract: Mixed‐halide perovskites often undergo reversible phase segregation under illumination, yet the origin and the material properties governing this process remain debated. Several driving forces for halide segregation have been proposed, including polaronic strain, bandgap effects, internal electric fields, and photoinduced redox reactions. These are often treated as competing frameworks for the interpretation of seemingly similar experimental observations. Here, we argue that progress in the field is limited due to an intertwining of kinetic and thermodynamic aspects of segregation and encourage the use of a generalized thermodynamic description in which different microscopic models correspond to different ways of modifying the free‐energy balance under illumination. We therefore analyze the assumptions, predictions, and experimental signatures of the most widely discussed mechanisms. We further identify key limitations in current experimental approaches, mostly associated with an overreliance on photoluminescence as a characterization tool, and how variations in experimental conditions further obscure comparison across studies. By outlining descriptors and experimental strategies, we provide a basis for systematically testing competing mechanisms. This work thus aims to move the field from parallel model interpretations toward a more unified and quantitative understanding of halide segregation in perovskites.

articles.title: Local Coordination Asymmetry Engineering Activates Oxide Path Mechanism in Dopant‐Free RuO2 for Ultra‐Durable Acidic Water Oxidation
articles.abstract: Developing ruthenium‐based anode electrocatalysts to replace commercial iridium is crucial for reducing the cost of proton exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolysis. However, conventional RuO2 suffers from limited long‐term stability and severe overoxidation drawbacks. Herein, we employ dynamic H2 bubble template (DHBT)‐assisted electrodeposition combined with calcination to fabricate disorderly connected regular/irregular Ru‐O6 octahedra. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that this local coordination asymmetry favors an oxide path mechanism (OPM) involving direct O‐O coupling while suppressing *OOH formation and substantial lattice‐oxygen participation. The optimized d‐RuO2‐x catalyst requires an overpotential of only 154 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for over 3200 h at this current density. Crucially, in a PEM water electrolyzer, the catalyst operates robustly for over 2100 h at 200 mA cm−2 under continuous and start‐shutdown conditions. These results demonstrate that local coordination asymmetry engineering can tune OER pathway selection in dopant‐free RuO2‐based catalysts and provide a promising route toward durable acidic OER anodes.

articles.title: Machine Learning for Rational Electrolyte Design in Lithium Batteries: Bridging Macroscopic Performance and Physically Interpretable Descriptors
articles.abstract: Rational design of high‐performance electrolytes is central to the development of next‐generation lithium batteries, but it remains hindered by vast molecular design space, intricate multiscale structure–property relationships, and multiple performance requirements. Although machine learning (ML) accelerates electrolyte discovery through data‐driven performance prediction, most existing studies rely on sparse performance data and provide limited physical interpretability, thereby falling short of true rational design. This review traces the evolution of ML‐enabled electrolyte research from macroscopic performance prediction to mesoscale mechanistic understanding, with particular emphasis on the limited coverage of electrolyte chemical space in existing performance datasets and the insufficient evaluation of model extrapolation. We then review the physically interpretable descriptors and examine their intercorrelations and domains of applicability using a common set of 26 representative solvents. The current maturity and remaining limitations of ML‐based descriptor prediction are further assessed to support the high‐throughput virtual screening of electrolyte candidates. Finally, we review recent advances in performance‐guided autonomous experimentation and discuss the key challenges associated with establishing descriptor‐guided closed‐loop discovery platforms. Although descriptor‐driven rational electrolyte design has yet to be fully realized, this review outlines an actionable roadmap for integrating physically interpretable descriptors, generalizable ML models, and autonomous experimentation toward interpretable, data‐driven electrolyte discovery.

articles.title: Magnetic Field‐Induced Mass Transfer Acceleration and Spin Polarization for Highly Efficient Photocatalytic Urea Synthesis
articles.abstract: Different from traditional industrial urea synthesis using NH3 and CO2, heterogeneous photocatalysis enables direct urea synthesis from N2 and CO2 in aqueous, where water acts as both solvent and hydrogen source. Its low yield is mainly restricted by poor reactant activation efficiency, mismatched reaction kinetics, slow C─N coupling and slow gas mass transfer via water hydrogen bond networks. Herein, an external magnetic field was adopted to boost photocatalytic urea synthesis. Upon magneto‐photocatalysis, water hydrogen bonds were disturbed to form gas diffusion channel and release sufficient hydrogen protons. Driven by the Lorentz force and magnetohydrodynamic convection, electron‐proton interactions were strengthened. Meanwhile, spin‐polarized electrons and regulated active sites activated N2 and CO2 and accelerated C─N coupling. Under ambient conditions and a 40‐mT magnetic field, ZIF‐67@MIL‐101(Fe) achieved a urea yield as high as 147.28 µmol g−1 h−1. Mechanism to the enhancement along with reaction pathways were clarified via experimental and simulation results. Practical applicability was confirmed using simulated flue gas, and the obtained urea solution could cultivate wheat seedlings. Overall, this work proposed a magnetic field‐enhanced photocatalytic urea production strategy, offering a universal approach for efficient N2 activation toward urea and other nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

articles.title: Molecular Design of Fluorinated Ester Electrolytes via Skeleton Regulation Enables Aggressive Cathode Chemistries in 5V‐Class Fast‐Charging Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium‐ion batteries can deliver higher energy densities when using high‐voltage cathodes such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO), yet their practical application is hindered by the catalytic nature of high‐voltage cathode materials which usually cause electrolytes decomposition. Although the utilization of fluorinated carbonates as electrolyte solvent considerably inhibited the parasitic reaction at cathode side, the irrational fluorination often leads to the sluggish Li+ transport which finally causes poor rate performance. Here, we design a family of trifluoromethyl‐substituted carboxylate esters as electrolyte solvents. We found that the spatial arrangement between the ‐CF3 and the carbonyl group in these fluorinated esters is critical for regulating the electrolyte solvation structures. A short distance (α‐substitution) severely weakens the solvating power of the solvent, resulting in a substantial decrease in ionic conductivity, whereas an extended separation (γ‐substitution) compromises the oxidation resistance against high‐voltage cathodes. Only the trifluoromethylation at the β‐position yields optimal solvent (methyl 3,3,3‐trifluoropropionate, MTFP) that can simultaneously meets high‐voltage and fast‐charging requirements of LNMO||Gr cells when pairing with fluoroethylene carbonate and 1 M LiPF6. In such electrolyte, the Ah‐level LNMO||Gr pouch cells deliver 78% capacity retention at 6C charge/discharge rate (13.2 mA cm−2), and stably operate over 300 cycles at the high rate of 3C.

articles.title: Nanoscale In2O3 Induced Fast Kinetics and Stable Interface for High‐Loading Solid‐State Cathode
articles.abstract: Sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) with high‐loading cathodes are currently hindered by sluggish Li+/electron kinetics and poor interfacial compatibility. Conventional carbon additives, despite their high conductivity, often trigger detrimental side reactions with sulfide electrolytes. To mitigate these issues, we introduce a multifunctional nanoscale In2O3 conductive agent, integrated via a facile one‐step ball milling process. This nano‐In2O3 effectively mediates interactions between large Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (LPSC) and LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) particles, enhancing mixing homogeneity and collision efficiency. The resulting composite cathode features a low‐tortuosity Li+ transport network and establishes rapid “NCM‐nano In2O3‐NCM” electronic pathways within particle gaps. Crucially, In2O3 improves interfacial compatibility between the LPSC and conductive additives, suppressing interfacial degradation. Consequently, a high‐loading cathode (18.34 mg cm−2) demonstrates a specific capacity of 131 mAh g−1 at 3C and exhibits excellent cyclability, retaining 97.6% capacity after 500 cycles in NCM811||Li cells. This strategy highlights the potential of nanoscale metal oxide additives for achieving high‐energy‐density ASSLBs through optimized interfacial and transport kinetics.

articles.title: Proton Flux Engineering for Selective CO2 Electroreduction
articles.abstract: The carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) is central to carbon valorization and renewable electricity storage, yet its selectivity, efficiency, and durability depend on coordinating proton availability with electron transfer at dynamic electrochemical interfaces. Despite advances in catalysts, electrolytes, hydrogen evolution suppression, and devices, proton effects are described by isolated descriptors, such as pH, water activity, buffer capacity, cation identity, hydrophobicity, ionomer chemistry, and local alkalinity. This fragmentation obscures how protons regulate initiation, *COOH formation, *CO/formate branching, *CO coverage, C─C coupling, hydrogen evolution, and high‐flux decay. A proton‐centered perspective is needed to link atomic proton‐transfer events with interfacial microenvironments and device operation. This review establishes proton regulation as a mechanistic framework for CO2RR by examining proton sources, transport pathways, interfacial accessibility, hydrogen‐bond‐network reorganization, local electric fields, and proton‐coupled electron‐transfer timing. By integrating molecular mechanisms, microenvironment modulation, in situ characterization, and gas‐diffusion or membrane‐electrode architectures, we organize dispersed observations into a source–transport–utilization framework. This framework shows how proton location, dose, and temporal availability define kinetic boundaries between hydrogen evolution, one‐carbon (C1) products, and multicarbon (C2+) pathways, while governing stability under practical fluxes. Proton regulation guides selective, scalable, and durable CO2 electroconversion.

articles.title: Redox‐Buffering PEAI‐CeOx Passivation Suppresses Thermo‐Mechanical Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells Under Rapid Thermal Cycling
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) show critical thermo-mechanical and defect mediated degradation at interfaces, limiting their deployment in terrestrial high-temperature and space-like environments. This study presents a dual-function interfacial passivation strategy that combines nanoparticle cerium oxide (CeO x ) with phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI) to form a hybrid surface treatment (PC) for poly[bis(4-phenyl)(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)amine (PTAA) based n-i-p PSC architecture, where defect passivation is complemented by redox coupling and enhanced thermal stress stabilization. Optimized PC-treated devices achieved a champion efficiency of 25.3% and exhibited enhanced operational stabilities under continuous 1 SUN light soaking and 85°C/85% RH damp heat respectively. To probe the engineered interface mechanistically, we employed an accelerated thermal shock (TS) cycling to mimic low Earth orbit (LEO) relevant thermal cycling condition. Under realistically simulated TS conditions of cycling temperature between 80°C and −80°C and 16°C/min ramp rate transition, PC-treated devices retained 95% of initial efficiency after 100 cycles of TS, showing superior stability compared to their counterparts without CeO x . Collectively, this work highlights a new insight into dynamic thermal fatigue in PSCs and introduces a practical route toward thermally resilient, high efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Redox‐Buffering PEAI‐CeOx Passivation Suppresses Thermo‐Mechanical Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells Under Rapid Thermal Cycling (Adv. Energy Mater. 38/2026)
articles.abstract: Perovskite Solar Cells Integrating cerium oxide nanoparticle (CeOx) into phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI) creates a dual‐function passivation strategy that improves both efficiency and thermal shock stability in perovskite solar cells. Enhanced perovskite lattice stability and suppressed thermally induced degradation enable robust device performance, advancing perovskite photovoltaics toward demanding terrestrial and space operation environments. More in article number e71312, Behrang H. Hamadani, Jae Sung Yun, Helen Hejin Park, and co‐workers.

articles.title: Redox‐Mediated Electrified Method for Green and Low‐Cost Spent Lithium‐Ion Battery Materials Recycling
articles.abstract: After 30 years of commercialization and mass production, lithium‐ion batteries have generated massive waste streams, especially with their expanding use in electric vehicles. Recycling spent batteries and valorizing useful components are therefore increasingly urgent for sustainable development. However, conventional pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical methods are limited by high energy consumption or large chemical input, creating demand for greener and more efficient recycling technologies. Here, using LiCoO2 as an example, we report a closed‐loop electrified chemical process based on redox‐targeting reactions to recover valuable species from spent battery materials using only electricity and water. Complementary reductive leaching of LiCoO2 and oxidative leaching of LiFePO4 were performed with anthraquinone‐2,7‐disulfonate as a regenerative redox mediator to sequentially break down LiCoO2 and achieve efficient separation of Co2+ and Li+ in the form of Co(OH)2 and LiOH. This cost‐effective and environmentally friendly method was also extended to the recycling of LiNixMnyCozO2 with a high recovery rate of Li+ and transition metal species. It is anticipated that the electrified chemical recycling method demonstrated here would provide a credible solution to the valorization of battery waste and contribute to the sustainable development of lithium‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Regioisomer‐Induced In Situ Construction of 1D/3D Perovskite Heterojunctions for Efficient and Stable Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are limited by poor operational stability arising from undercoordinated Pb/I defects that induce severe non‐radiative recombination. Here, a regioisomer‐guided molecular engineering strategy is proposed to modulate interfacial coordination and structural reconstruction. Pyridinecarboxamide isomers with distinct substitution positions are introduced, among which para‐configured isonicotinamide (INA) exhibits a larger dipole moment and enhanced charge redistribution, enabling stronger coordination with undercoordinated Pb2+ and more efficient interfacial charge transfer. The cooperative interaction between the amide group and pyridine nitrogen further directs ordered molecular stacking and anisotropic growth, inducing the in situ formation of a 1D (INA)PbI3 layer on the three‐dimensional perovskite surface and constructing a robust 1D/3D heterojunction. This architecture simultaneously suppresses defect‐assisted recombination and enhances environmental tolerance. As a result, INA‐modified devices achieve a high power conversion efficiency of 26.57%, representing one of the highest efficiencies reported for 1D/3D PSCs. Moreover, the unencapsulated devices retain 91% of their initial efficiency after 600 h under harsh damp heat conditions (85°C/85% RH) and exhibit excellent operational stability under cyclic illumination. This work provides a structure–property correlation for isomer engineering and offers an effective route toward highly efficient and stable PSCs.

articles.title: Review on Textile Triboelectric Nanogenerators: From Material Design to Self‐Powered Wearable Energy Systems
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of wearable electronics, smart textiles, and the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased the demand for sustainable, self‐powered energy solutions. Textile‐based triboelectric nanogenerators (T‐TENGs) have emerged as a promising technology by combining efficient mechanical energy harvesting with the flexibility, breathability, stretchability, washability, and wearability of textiles. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in T‐TENGs, covering the complete design hierarchy from fundamental mechanisms to wearable applications. The operating principles of alternating‐current and emerging direct‐current TENGs, including contact electrification, electrostatic induction, electrostatic breakdown, and tribovoltaic effects, are discussed. Recent progress in triboelectric material engineering, fiber and yarn design, and textile architectures—including woven, knitted, braided, embroidered, multilayer, and 3D structures—is systematically reviewed with emphasis on performance enhancement and scalability. Applications in biomechanical sensing, wearable healthcare, human–machine interaction, smart textiles, and self‐powered wearable systems are summarized, highlighting the distinction between self‐powered sensing and fully autonomous wearable platforms. Finally, key challenges, including low current output, environmental stability, washability, durability, scalable manufacturing, performance standardization, and commercialization, are critically analyzed, and future research directions toward intelligent, fully autonomous, and commercially viable self‐powered wearable systems are outlined.

articles.title: Revisiting the Closed‐Pore Formation and Interfacial Micro‐Environment Modulation Mechanisms of Polyacrylonitrile‐Derived Carbon Nanofibers Toward Efficient Sodium Storage
articles.abstract: Polyacrylonitrile‐based carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are widely regarded as promising sodium‐storage anodes owing to their high carbon yield/axial conductivity and superior mechanical flexibility. Nevertheless, the ambiguous understandings into the temperature‐dependent micro‐structure evolution, particularly the closed‐pore formation over pyrolysis, and the electrolyte induced electrode‐electrolyte interface micro‐environments, along with the involved influence mechanism upon sodium‐storage behaviors should be reasonably clarified. With systematical in(ex)‐situ physicochemical/electrochemical characterizations, it is first established that the optimal pyrolysis temperature of 1400°C combined with a “zipper‐like” point‐line‐plane solid‐phase fusion evolution effectively modulates micro‐structures, endowing the optimized pseudo‐graphitized CNFs film (i.e., GCNFs‐1400) with a synergistic balance among ions transport pathways (interlayer spacing), active storage sites (closed pores), and 3D conductive supporting framework (solid‐phase fusion). Concurrently, compared to the ester‐based electrolyte, the ether‐based electrolyte favors the formation of a thinner, more uniform, and chemically stable solid electrolyte interphase layer. It is the dual‐engineering of both material micro‐structures and interfacial micro‐environment that fully guarantees the competitive sodium‐storage properties of GCNFs‐1400 in terms of ultra‐high initial Coulombic efficiency (96.2%), rate capability, and long‐term stability toward presodiation‐free sodium‐ion batteries and sodium‐ion capacitors. More essentially, our in‐depth insights here provide meaningful guidance for future design of advanced hard carbon anodes toward efficient sodium storage.

articles.title: Sodium‐Ion Battery Technology: Advances and Challenges
Strain Engineering in High‐Entropy Electrocatalysts: Mechanisms, Strategies and Water Splitting Applications
articles.abstract: Strain engineering has emerged as an effective strategy for tailoring the electronic structure and catalytic behavior of materials at the atomic scale. For electrochemical water splitting, the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction and oxygen evolution reaction are largely limited by scaling relationships and nonoptimized adsorption energetics of key intermediates. High‐entropy materials, featuring multiprincipal‐element compositions and pronounced lattice distortion, offer a unique platform for strain‐mediated catalytic regulation. Their intrinsic microstrain fields, derived from atomic size mismatch together with sluggish diffusion and cocktail effects, enable tunable electronic structures and abundant metastable active sites. This review summarizes recent advances in strain engineering of high‐entropy materials for water splitting. Fundamental concepts of strain and its influence on d‐band centers, adsorption energetics, and reaction kinetics are first introduced. This is followed by a discussion of strain modulation strategies, including doping, solid solution alloying, and defect engineering. Special emphasis is placed on the distinct behavior of high‐entropy materials compared with conventional alloys, particularly their nonlinear electronic hybridization and multisite synergy. Finally, key challenges involving strain quantification, operando evolution, and strain‐entropy coupling are highlighted, providing guidance for the rational design of next‐generation water‐splitting catalysts.

articles.title: Surface Lattice‐Adaptive Integrity Reconstruction of Perovskite Quantum Dots for Efficient Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead triiodide perovskite quantum dots (FAPbI3 PQDs) receive increasing attention for next‐generation solar cells owing to their remarkable optoelectronic properties and solution processability. However, the dynamic binding of native surface ligands inevitably induces surface lattice vacancies and distortions, significantly deteriorating the optoelectronic properties and stability of PQDs. Herein, a facile surface lattice‐adaptive integrity reconstruction strategy is reported to regulate the surface lattice of PQDs. After molecule screening, the 3‐guanidinopropionic acid (GPA) with a geometry‐adaptive configuration can effectively passivate the intrinsic surface lattice vacancies through the Pb‐O coordination and guanidinium‐mediated hydrogen‐bonding interactions. Meanwhile, the surface lattice‐adaptive configuration of the GPA can also substantially ameliorate the distorted surface lattice, which largely improves the surface lattice integrity and enhances the electronic coupling of PQDs, facilitating charge carrier transport in the PQD solids. Consequently, the power conversion efficiency is increased from 16.15% for the control solar cell to 19.32% for the GPA‐based solar cell. This work provides important insight into the physical design principles for the surface lattice of PQDs through lattice‐adaptive molecules and offers implementable strategies for the development of high‐performance optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Synergistic Gradient Interphase Engineering for Ultra‐Stable and High‐Rate Quasi‐Solid‐State Sodium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Quasi‐solid‐state sodium metal batteries (QSSMBs) have emerged as a pivotal technology for safe, high‐energy‐density, and large‐scale energy storage. However, the practical application of QSSMBs is severely hindered by the formation of an unstable and high‐impedance solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that fails to accommodate the dramatic volume fluctuations of sodium (Na) metal anodes, consequently leading to rapid capacity decay during high‐rate cycling. Herein, we propose a rational design strategy to construct a rigid‐inner/flexible‐outer gradient SEI architecture by modulating the stepwise reduction behavior of functional additives within a poly(1,3‐dioxolane) electrolyte. By introducing 2,2,2‐trifluoroethyl trifluoromethanesulfonate to undergo synergistic decomposition with fluoroethylene carbonate, this formulation enables the in situ construction of the dual‐layer gradient interphase. This unique SEI efficiently facilitates desolvation and accelerates Na+ transport, while achieving even Na plating after cycling. Consequently, the designed electrolyte delivers outstanding electrochemical performance, enabling Na || sodium vanadium phosphate full cells to exhibit long cycle‐life of 5500 cycles at 20 C and 97.5% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 25 C. This work highlights the critical role of gradient SEI engineering and offers an insightful design principle for developing next‐generation QSSMBs.

articles.title: Unraveling Spatial Electrochemical Heterogeneity and Additive‐Mediated Regulation in Scale‐up Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Pouch‐Type Cells
articles.abstract: Scaling aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) to pouch-type configurations amplifies electric-field and Zn2+ flux heterogeneities, causing non-uniform Zn deposition. Here, β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) and Tween 80 (Tw80) are systematically investigated to decouple bulk transport and interfacial kinetic regulation in scale-up pouch-type cells. β-CD increases ionic conductivity (3.44 to 5.95 mS cm− 1) and the Zn2+ transference number (0.16 to 0.47), promoting uniform bulk ion flux and extending symmetric pouch-type cell lifespan beyond 1000 h at 1 mA cm− 2. Conversely, Tw80 operates via interfacial adsorption to regulate local reaction kinetics, achieving stable cycling for >600 h. Spatially resolved analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and in situ thermal imaging reveal that β-CD suppresses macroscopic heterogeneity across near-tab, central, and edge regions by stabilizing bulk solvation, whereas Tw80 mitigates localized interfacial instability. In practical Zn||V2O5 pouch-type full cells, β-CD delivers superior long-term capacity retention, while Tw80 excels under high-rate conditions. This work identifies spatial electrochemical heterogeneity as a primary scaling limit and offers general design principles connecting additive chemistry, transport kinetics, and format-dependent deposition for practical AZIBs.

articles.title: Cation‐Mediated Interface Engineering Directs Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species Pathways
articles.abstract: Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) is more persistent and matrix‐tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation‐induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe2O3‐carbon nanotubes (Cu1/Fe2O3‐CNTs) as a dual‐ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali‐metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation‐size‐dependent trend, whereas 1O2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na+‐containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O2 adsorption. Na+ promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen‐bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1O2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m−3. These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline‐water decontamination.

articles.title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H2O2 Photosynthesis
articles.abstract: Solar‐driven H2O2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O2 to spin‐paired H2O2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O2. Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H2O2, and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H2O2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H2O2 formation. Chiralization enhances H2O2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g−1 h−1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H2O2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

articles.title: Crystallography‐Dependent Plating/Stripping Kinetics and Interfacial Morphologies in Zn Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Crystallographic orientation governs Zn deposition, dissolution, and cycling stability, but its influence on interfacial charge-transfer kinetics remains difficult to quantify. Here, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy coupled with fast scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) is used to resolve Zn plating and stripping on single-crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. Meniscus-confined measurements reveal facet-dependent branch-specific apparent zero-current potentials and apparent exchange current densities, j 0, with the kinetic ordering j 0(100) > j 0(101) > j 0(002) for both plating and stripping. This ordering is reproduced across independently prepared electrodes and retained over different scan rates and aqueous electrolytes. Beyond charge transfer, Zn removal and regrowth are strongly crystallographically encoded: dissolution footprints preserve the symmetry of the parent facets, while potentiostatically deposited Zn adopts substrate-dependent growth geometries. These coupled kinetic and morphological differences translate directly to battery performance. Despite its slower apparent kinetics, the close-packed, low-energy (002) facet exhibits the longest cycling life in Zn/Zn symmetric cells and substantially improved capacity retention in both polyaniline/Zn and Na0.33V2O5/Zn full cells, whereas the faster (100) and (101) interfaces fail earlier. These findings establish a facet-dependent kinetics–stability trade-off and show that durable Zn anodes require coordinated control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and crystallographic reconstruction.

articles.title: Dibenzophenazine‐Fused Heterocyclic Luminophores: Decoding High‐Performance Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes Based on Long‐Wavelength Exciplex
articles.abstract: Developing highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non‐radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen‐rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti‐aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron‐containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange‐red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light‐emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long‐wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.

articles.title: Efficient Bipolar Hydrogen Peroxide Production Through Photoelectrochemistry
articles.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias‐free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H2O2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H2O2 production. Herein, we report a rare‐earth ytterbium oxide (YbOx) modified BiVO4/WO3 photoanode for efficient PEC water oxidation to H2O2. The optimized photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.83 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE, an H2O2 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of over 80% across the potential range of 0.6–1.8 VRHE, and a peak FE of 90.4% at 1.6 VRHE. Yb3+ Lewis acid sites suppress the competitive four‐electron oxygen evolution reaction by forming Yb‐hydroxyl complexes, while YbOx enhances charge transfer and reduces interfacial resistance. Importantly, when coupled with a FeZnWMnYb high‐entropy amorphous oxide cathode for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction, the bias‐free tandem cell achieves ∼160% bipolar H2O2 FE. Scaling the photoelectrode to 20 cm2 under 0.7 suns illumination yields an H2O2 production rate of 3.03 mmol L−1 h−1. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for large‐scale solar‐driven H2O2 synthesis for environmental applications.

articles.title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
articles.abstract: Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point‐of‐care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics‐based dual‐mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein‐containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false‐negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus‐associated toxins and PMA‐treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein‐based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF‐based dual‐mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

articles.title: Intrinsic Near‐Infrared Photothermal Effect Induces Single‐Crystal‐to‐Single‐Crystal Transformation in Organic Molecular Crystals
articles.abstract: Near‐infrared (NIR) light‐driven single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation holds profound significance for supramolecular chemistry and smart materials, yet remains a formidable challenge in purely organic molecular crystals. Herein, we demonstrate SCSC transformation driven by the intrinsic NIR photothermal effect of a rationally designed croconium derivative CR‐DPA‐OMe, which features strong NIR absorption and a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 60%. Solvated CR‐DPA‐OMe single crystals encapsulating CHCl3 molecules exhibit exceptional ambient stability with crystallinity preserved for over two years. Benefiting from the robust dimeric packing of croconium motifs and the conformationally flexible methoxy‐substituted diphenylamine moieties, the resulting crystals successfully reconcile long‐range lattice order with structural flexibility, thus enabling efficient SCSC transformation upon NIR photothermal stimulation. Combined density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction analysis confirm that the transformation is driven by the synergistic interplay of photoinduced molecular conformational reorganization and photothermally‐converted heat, affording markedly faster transformation than conventional oven heating. Furthermore, tailored NIR irradiation enables spatiotemporally programmable guest release, demonstrating a remote manipulation inaccessible via macroscopic conductive heating. These findings highlight the substantial promise of NIR photothermal modulation as an emerging stimuli‐responsive strategy for precise structural engineering in molecular crystals, opening new avenues toward tailored functional material applications.

articles.title: Linear and Branched Alkanes Separation Through Conjugated‐Polymer‐Framework Membranes
articles.abstract: The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane‐based liquid‐phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n‐heptane/iso‐octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated‐polymer‐framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular‐level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n‐heptane/iso‐octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m−2 h−1 bar−1. This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol‐induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.

articles.title: Mechanophotochemistry: Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
articles.abstract: Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis, a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light‐promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent‐minimized and viable alternative to solution‐state photochemical reactions.

articles.title: Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
articles.abstract: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N2Py3OH)]2+ (1‐Fe), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.

articles.title: Precision Matters: Minor Concentration Deviations of DMSO May Cause Major Efficacy Shifts
articles.abstract: Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) represents the most common solvent for dispersing hydrophobic materials in aqueous solutions for biological usage. Generally, a DMSO content of below 1% is believed to exert no effect on cells, and thus little attention is given to its influence on drug efficacy. During our recent research on a lipid droplet‐targeted photosensitizer, PNA‐9, we notice the drastic influence of low‐concentration DMSO (<1%) on its photodynamic therapy (PDT) performance. In‐depth investigations reveal the significant role of low‐concentration DMSO on PNA‐9 particle size, which further affects cellular uptake via passive diffusion and results in a drastic PDT effect. We further extend our investigation of low‐concentration DMSO effect on other common hydrophobic chemotherapy drugs and photosensitizers. The results uncover the differential influences of low‐concentration DMSO: camptothecin (CPT) and TPE‐IQ possess similar DMSO effects, whilst the therapy effects of paclitaxel (PCT), bortezomib (BTZ), and DTTPB are not obviously influenced. This work aims to bring the effect of low‐concentration DMSO to attention and is expected to benefit the development of biomaterials and comprehensive material performance evaluation.

articles.title: Radical‐Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
articles.abstract: Charge‐transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. Here, we report a radical‐mediated surface reconstruction strategy for ligand‐free SnO2 nanocrystals that enables concurrent gains in device efficiency, scalability, and durability. Sonochemical activation generates hydroxyl radicals that selectively passivate oxygen‐deficient Sn sites while inducing electrostatically stabilized dispersions with exceptional shelf stability, allowing the SnO2 colloids to be stored for over 2 years without aggregation or performance degradation. This stabilization enables the formation of uniform electron transport layers with reduced trap density and enhanced electron mobility. These improvements promote buried‐interface perovskite crystallization and accelerate charge extraction, yielding PSCs with an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 26.12%). Importantly, the strategy is inherently scalable, enabling a perovskite module (∼110 cm2) with an efficiency of 21.45%. Devices exhibit enhanced operational stability, retaining 92% efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2), maintaining 88% efficiency under maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and showing negligible degradation over 500 thermal cycles (ISOS‐T‐3). These results establish radical‐mediated engineering of SnO2 nanocrystals as a general pathway in perovskite photovoltaics, bridging high efficiency, large‐area manufacturability, and long‐term operational stability.

articles.title: Redirecting Excited‐State Energy Flow Through Programmed Supramolecular Confinement in Twisted Photosensitizers
articles.abstract: Programmed supramolecular confinement is introduced as a physical strategy to investigate aggregation‐enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)‐active twisted photosensitizers without changing the conjugated photosensitizing unit. In this design, TICT functions as a confinement‐sensitive regulator of excited‐state energy dissipation, while cell membranes (CM) serve as supramolecular platforms that confine photosensitizers within their compact phospholipid bilayer architectures. Through alkyl‐chain engineering, the obtained photosensitizers exhibit similar photophysical properties but tunable interactions with phospholipids, resulting in programmed confinement states within CMs. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that supramolecular confinement suppresses TICT‐mediated non‐radiative relaxation by reducing excitation‐induced donor‐acceptor torsional change and restricting intramolecular rotation, thereby redirecting excited‐state energy flow toward radiative emission and intersystem crossing‐mediated ROS generation. Accordingly, stronger confinement induces higher enhancements in fluorescence and ROS generation, establishing a supramolecular confinement‐dependent correlation among TICT restriction, fluorescence, and ROS generation. Finally, the optimized CM‐photosensitizer assemblies are applied as photodynamic systems and display effective performance in cancer immunotherapy. By coupling TICT restriction with ROS generation, this work establishes supramolecular confinement as a physical strategy for redirecting excited‐state energy flow and provides direct insight into how aggregation enhances ROS generation in twisted photosensitizers.

articles.title: Rotation‐Coupled Guest Anions Stabilize Polymer Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na+ migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. Here we report a rotation‐coupled guest‐anion strategy in a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene)‐based solid‐state electrolyte (PHSE) using Mg(OTf)2. Mg2+ preferentially coordinates DMF and TFSI−, weakening Na+–TFSI− association and limiting solvent‐derived reactions at the sodium metal anode. OTf− enters the Na+ solvation shell as a mobile guest anion. Its C─S rotational axis and equivalent oxygen coordination sites allow conformational rotation to synchronize with Na+ hopping along polymer chains. This anchor–rotator chemistry reorganizes Na+ coordination, lowers the migration barrier, and promotes an inorganic‐rich, Mg─O‐containing interphase. The optimized electrolyte enables Na3V2(PO4)3||Na cells to retain 94.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 2C and supports a 94 mAh pouch cell with stable cycling. It also enables high‐voltage Na3V2(PO4)2O2F||Na cells to retain 93.6% capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5C over 2.5–4.2 V. Comparative evaluation across a total of 20 polymer electrolyte systems with varied polymer matrices and anion structures identifies anion symmetry, rotational periodicity, and finite rotational barriers as molecular criteria for designing stable polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries.

articles.title: Synthesis of gem‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
articles.abstract: The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon‐ and phosphorus‐stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium‐catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp2)─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem‐phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si‐ and P‐stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon‐stereogenic gem‐phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P‐stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

articles.title: Ultra‐Low Thermal Conductivity in Mixed Anionic CuTe2Cl: Strong Antibonding States and Lone Pair‐Induced Te Ring Puckering
articles.abstract: Metal chalcohalides, an emerging class of mixed-anion compounds, have recently garnered increasing interest as they unite the exceptional stability of metal chalcogenides with the versatile electronic tunability of metal halides. Here, we synthesize single- and polycrystalline CuTe2Cl, a two-dimensional layered metal chalcohalide, which exhibits intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κ lat) of ∼0.54–0.24 W m−1K−1 between 300 and 600 K along the layered growth direction. Strong p-d* antibonding states arising from Cu 3d-Te 5p and Cu 3d-Cl 3p interactions in the valence band just below the Fermi level weaken the Cu-Te and Cu-Cl bonds to render the lattice elastically soft. Moreover, heteroleptic polyhedral coordination enforces chemical bonding hierarchy, which, together with the stereochemically active 5s2 lone pair of Te, generates pronounced lattice anharmonicity. These effects give rise to localized low-energy optical phonon modes, which suppress the acoustic phonons, as confirmed by phonon dispersion calculations. 5s2 lone pair driven Te-ring puckering and lattice shearing between layers provide low-frequency optical modes, which are experimentally identified by low-temperature Raman spectroscopy and heat-capacity measurements. Collectively, strong p-d* antibonding interaction induced lattice softening and lone pair driven instability produce strong anharmonicity, which markedly suppresses the heat-carrying acoustic phonons, leading to intrinsically ultralow κ lat in mixed anionic CuTe2Cl.

articles.title: “Direct Injection” Bubble Growth Mediated by Nano‐Interfaced Electrodes for Efficient Chlorine Production
articles.abstract: The chlor-alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. The development of energy-efficient and stable CER system is therefore urgently needed. Nano-interfaced electrodes exhibit superior catalytic performance, yet their mechanism for energy saving and system stability remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine a high-speed camera and confocal laser scanning microscope Platform to visualize and digitalize the bubble evolution and the bubble-induced overpotential (ƞ bub). We provide direct visual evidence that the bubble-induced concentration gradients and fluid flow field disturbances are key regulators of overpotential, and that the nano-interfaced electrode exhibits an ƞ bub of only approximately 49% of that of the flat-interfaced electrode. Specifically, the nano interface not only generates a stronger interfacial electric field and enhanced bubble-induced interfacial turbulence—which promote the Cl− migration to the electrode surface—but also induces a “direct-injection” mode of bubble growth that mitigates the accumulation of reaction products near the electrode. Moreover, the Cl− enrichment capacity of the nano interface endows the near-interface solution with ionic buffering capability, effectively suppressing potential fluctuations. This work demonstrates that regulating bubble dynamics is key to constructing energy-saving and stable gas-evolving electrochemical systems.

articles.title: Cohesin Mutations in Cancer and Development
articles.abstract: Cohesin is a ring-shaped protein complex that wraps around DNA and is crucial for sister chromatid cohesion, chromatin organization, gene regulation, replication, and DNA damage repair. In somatic cells, it consists of the core ring subunits SMC1A, SMC3, and RAD21 and one of two paralogs, STAG1 or STAG2. Germline mutations in the cohesin ring and its loading complex components cause developmental disorders such as Cornelia de Lange and Roberts syndromes, collectively referred to as cohesinopathies. Similar loss-of-function mutations in cohesin are somatically acquired during cancer development and are prevalent across multiple cancer types, particularly myeloid malignancies, bladder cancer, glioblastoma, and Ewing sarcoma. Here, we discuss the context-dependent effects of cohesin mutations in development and cancer and describe their underlying molecular mechanisms. A deeper understanding of cohesin function in normal development and human disease holds promise to identify new therapeutic opportunities for patients with cohesin dysfunction.

articles.title: Engineering the Allogeneic Stem Cell Graft for AML Immunotherapy: From Transplant Protection to Therapeutic Redistribution
articles.abstract: The inability to restrict acute myeloid leukemia immunotherapy to leukemic cells without damaging normal hematopoiesis remains a central challenge. Graft engineering addresses this limitation by modifying donor hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells so that the reconstituting hematopoietic system becomes resistant to a selected immunotherapy while residual leukemia remains susceptible. I examine the molecular principles, target-specific constraints, pharmacological consequences, and translational implications of this strategy across five validated immunotargets: CD33, CD123, FLT3, KIT, and CD45. These targets span a spectrum from dispensable lineage antigens to essential signaling receptors and pan-hematopoietic conditioning targets, requiring either antigen deletion or function-preserving epitope substitution. Beyond preventing hematopoietic toxicity, graft engineering redistributes therapeutic engagement by remodeling normal antigen-expressing hematopoiesis, thereby influencing the efficacy and toxicity of antibody- and chimeric antigen receptor–based therapies. I outline a translational path from single-edited grafts toward multiplex platforms designed to improve disease control while limiting antigen escape.

articles.title: Promoting Toxic Metabolites in Cancer Therapy
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming supports cancer behaviors including proliferation, survival, and therapeutic resistance. Compared to our understanding of these processes, little is known about the detoxification liabilities that are introduced as a byproduct of this reprogramming. Here, we review recent findings that collectively support the notion that the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells is accompanied by increased production of potentially toxic metabolites. As a result, these cells are critically dependent on enzymatic processing or export of these metabolites. When such processes are blocked, endogenously produced metabolites can accumulate in distinct subcellular compartments to exert a variety of cytotoxic mechanisms in cancer cells such as DNA damage and ferroptosis. Toxic metabolite overloading is discussed as an emerging therapeutic strategy that carries potential advantages such as allowing tuning of toxicity via dietary control of metabolite production and exerting microenvironmental toxic effects to enhance overall efficacy in the heterogenous tumor.

articles.title: Normal Science and Middle-Range Theory in Criminology: Assessing the Contested Notion of Offending Specialization
articles.abstract: This review traces the evolution of the specialization concept in criminology and assesses its value for theory, research, and policy. Although empirical research has generally shown that most offenders exhibit versatility rather than long-term specialization, we argue that specialization remains an important dimension of criminal behavior and is productive for middle-range theory and normal science in criminology. We assess common methodological approaches to measuring specialization, highlighting how differences in operationalization shape substantive conclusions. We then synthesize contemporary research that uses specialization to probe theoretical mechanisms, examine social and developmental processes, and evaluate justice system practices and policy. Across these areas, between- and within-individual variation in specialization (versatility) informs questions about opportunity, peer influence, decision-making, and the criminal career. We conclude that specialization should not be treated as a binary property but as a conditional, theoretically generative construct that, if effectively utilized, can advance criminology's objectives.

articles.title: Evolutionary Genetics of Insect Mimicry and Masquerade
articles.abstract: As classic examples of adaptive evolution, insect mimicry and masquerade have been studied extensively for more than a century. Both phenomena protect insects from predators and are widely observed in nature. Previous research on phenotypic, genetic, phylogenetic, and behavioral aspects has laid a solid foundation for in-depth investigations. Recent advances in genomic data resources, analytical methodologies, and gene-editing tools have greatly facilitated the elucidation of the genetic and developmental mechanisms underlying insect mimicry and masquerade. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent progress, encompassing key insect lineages such as Lepidoptera, Hymenoptera, Odonata, and Mantodea; highlights the pivotal roles of evolutionary hot spot genes, noncoding sequences, and structural variations in driving phenotypic diversification and adaptation; and offers novel insights into fundamental evolutionary questions such as sexual dimorphism, convergent evolution, and speciation. Furthermore, this review outlines the ongoing challenges and future prospects in the evolutionary genetics of insect mimicry and masquerade.

articles.title: Machine Translation for Sign Languages
articles.abstract: Sign language machine translation has progressed substantially over the past decade, evolving from isolated sign recognition to end-to-end translation systems. Advances in pose estimation, transformer architectures, and large-scale dataset collection have driven progress, yet challenges remain. Datasets are limited compared to spoken-language resources; evaluation metrics inadequately capture the linguistic quality of output; and models must capture the simultaneous, multilayered, and three-dimensional structure of sign languages. This manuscript provides a comprehensive review that seeks to balance technical challenges with stakeholder considerations. We examine the linguistic properties that make sign languages computationally unique; trace the evolution of recognition, translation, and production systems; and analyze ongoing technical challenges. Crucially, we address ethical considerations around data governance, community involvement, and appropriate use. Drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives spanning computer vision, sign language linguistics, and deaf studies, our analysis emphasizes that continued progress requires sustained collaboration across these fields and with deaf communities.

articles.title: TIME to Target Sarcomas: Lessons from the Tumor Immune Microenvironment
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) has emerged as a crucial regulator of antitumor immune responses with important therapeutic, prognostic, and predictive implications. Despite the success of immunotherapies in select solid tumors, notably melanoma and non–small cell lung cancer, their impact in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs) is limited, often attributed to an immune-cold TIME passively driven by low neoantigen burden. Herein, we review the current understanding of the STS TIME, its variability across STS subtypes, and its implications for STS immunotherapy. We propose that the prevailing view of STSs as passively immune-cold is incomplete and that active tumor-driven immune suppression is likely underappreciated. Distinguishing active from passive immune escape and understanding its mechanistic underpinnings will be important to rationally design effective TIME-targeted therapies in STSs and to serve as a paradigm for therapeutic interventions in other immune-cold tumors.

articles.title: Good Vibrations: A Fortunate Journey in Reaction Dynamics
articles.abstract: My professional life owes a great deal to the popular attitudes about science during my youth. As member of the baby boom generation, I benefited from a national commitment to the progress of science and the creation of institutions to support research. The path that took me into science and a career in fundamental research and, finally, into government service reflects those influences on the research enterprise. I encountered inspiring mentors along the way and eventually began independent research at the University of Wisconsin, exploring vibrations in chemical reactions. Studies of vibrationally excited molecules led from collisional energy transfer to unimolecular reactions, to photodissociation, and to bimolecular reactions. The photodissociation and bimolecular reaction experiments were among the first to demonstrate vibrational-state control of a reaction. Along the way, we did spectroscopy to explore vibrational excitation in polyatomic molecules and worked to recapitulate gas-phase studies in liquids.

articles.title: Trends in Methylidyne Radical Reactions at Temperatures Relevant to the Interstellar Medium
articles.abstract: The methylidyne radical, CH, can react rapidly with an unusually broad range of molecules under temperatures relevant to cold molecular clouds, making CH an important driver of molecular complexity in the interstellar medium. This review focuses on reactions of CH with polyatomic partners where low-temperature kinetic data are available (down to 23 K), drawing together information from theoretical studies, CRESU (Cinétique de Réaction en Ecoulement Supersonique Uniforme), and crossed molecular beam experiments. Trends in reaction rate coefficients as a function of temperature are surprisingly similar despite the differences in molecular reaction partner, with k ( T ) increasing with decreasing temperature before a small turnover in behavior near 50–70 K. This review evaluates k ( T ) and mechanistic trends in the context of a capture-controlled framework, highlighting where it breaks down and how observed trends in fitted rate parameters point toward predictive expressions for CH reactivity, while emphasizing the hydrocarbon and heteroatom-containing systems most in need of further study.

articles.title: An Agenda for Physiology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
The Brain-Gut-Microbiome Axis: Exploring the Link Between Depression and Irritable Bowel Syndrome
articles.abstract: The brain-gut-microbiome system is an integrated communication network linking the central nervous system, enteric nervous system, immune pathways, and intestinal microbiota. Increasing evidence indicates that dysregulation of this bidirectional signaling system contributes to both gastrointestinal and psychiatric disorders. Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), a disorder of gut–brain interaction, and major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently coexist and share multiple biological and environmental risk factors. Advances in microbiome science, neuroimaging, and multi-omics technologies have revealed that microbial metabolites, neuroimmune signaling, and stress-responsive neuroendocrine pathways influence neural circuits regulating mood, visceral perception, and gastrointestinal function. These interconnected mechanisms may explain the high comorbidity between IBS and MDD and suggest that both conditions arise from disturbances across overlapping biological systems. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge of genetic, neurobiological, and potential microbial contributors to IBS and depression, discuss emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the brain-gut-microbiome system, and highlight future directions for developing mechanistically informed treatment strategies.

articles.abstract: Redox-conductive metal-organic frameworks (RC-MOFs) combine molecularly tunable redox chemistry with crystalline, porous architectures. Stacking two RC-MOFs with different redox potentials creates a bilayer in which the direction of electron flow is governed by thermodynamically allowed interfacial redox reactions. This chemical rectification establishes RC-MOF bilayers as electrochemical diodes and provides a molecular strategy for programming directional charge transport.

Two-Dimensional IR Spectroscopy as a Window into the Molecular Structure and Dynamics of Electrolytes and Ionic Liquids: A Review
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.
