articles.abstract: The tunability of electronic structure in intermetallics opens the door to systematic studies in catalysis. Here, we experimentally investigate various descriptors for the electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction using 9 Heusler phases as catalysts (Co2VSn, Co2MnAl, Co2MnGe, Co2MnSn, Co2FeGe, Co2MnSb, Ni2MnSn, Co2FeSi, and Co2FeAl). In contrast to previous studies with Co-based Heusler phases and oxide perovskites for OER, we find that generally, the total valence electron count, rather than eg filling, provides a better prediction of the activity. However, with period 5 Y elements, such as Sn and Sb, at high valence electron counts, Y-site d-band centers must also be considered. Reaction mechanism analysis by DFT also clarifies the role of X/Y sites. Hence, a single descriptor alone is not sufficient to rationalize catalytic activity across the full spectrum of Heusler phase compositions. So far, valence electron control has relied on single metal or binary alloy compositions for nitrate reduction; however, these Heusler phases help decouple the element identity and valence count while also serving as a guide for more catalysts based on ternary intermetallics. This work thus establishes multi-descriptor guidance for a wide group of catalyst compositions that were previously relatively unexplored.

articles.title: Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior and Crystallographic Evolution during Cycling on Zn Metal Anodes
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.

articles.title: Overcoming the Trade-off Between the Activity, Stability, and Cost of OER Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis in a Self-Driving Laboratory
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) offers a sustainable route to hydrogen production, yet its practical deployment is limited by trade-offs among activity, stability, and precursor cost of acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts. Here, we present a self-driving laboratory (SDL) integrating automated batch synthesis, electrochemical half-cell testing, and AI-guided decision-making to simultaneously optimize these properties. A composition-constrained design space, clustering-based batch selection, and relaxed-percentile Pareto filtering enable efficient exploration of ternary Ir–Ru–X (X = Ni, Co, Fe) systems. Using this framework, the platform conducted 24 experiments per ternary system and identified Ir10Ru65Ni25/C as a Pareto-balanced composition exhibiting an overpotential of 211.8 mV at 10 mA cm–2, limited degradation after accelerated durability testing, and reduced Ir content. In PEMWE, Ir10Ru65Ni25 delivered 3.90 A cm–2 at 1.8 V and stable operation for 1000 h at 1.0 A cm–2, demonstrating SDL-driven discovery of multimetallic OER catalysts.

articles.title: Self-Healing Armor Enables Electrode Integrity and Interfacial Stability for Durable Silicon Anodes
articles.abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to stabilize silicon anodes, yet repeated volume changes can fracture the coating and accelerate continuous SEI reconstruction. Here, we construct a self-healing fluorinated acrylate/methacrylate copolymer coating in situ on silicon-based anodes through the UV-induced copolymerization of HFBA and MPS. The resulting copolymer combines strong adhesion with dynamic self-recovery through reversible dipole-dipole interactions, enabling microcrack repair within 1 min. Meanwhile, the HFBA-derived segments act as a fluorine reservoir, promoting the formation of a thin SEI with a polymer-rich outer layer and a LiF-rich inner layer. Consequently, SiOx-P(HFBA+MPS)||Li cells deliver 73.5% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 800 mA g–1. A practical 1.5 Ah NCM811||Si/C/Gr-P(HFBA+MPS) pouch cell achieves 71.9% capacity retention after 300 cycles and shows improved thermal safety. This work provides a scalable strategy for durable and safe silicon-based batteries by integrating autonomous self-healing of the polymer coating with sustained fluorine-assisted interphase stabilization.

articles.title: A Capacitively Coupled Dual-Gate 2D Transistor Unifying Logic-in-Memory and Tunable Synaptic Plasticity
articles.abstract: Integrating logic control with adaptive synaptic learning at the device level is a key step toward high-performance computing-in-memory (CIM) hardware. However, the integration of logic-in-memory (LIM) and synaptic plasticity within a homogeneous device is hindered by the incompatibility between stable logic output and dynamic weight modulation. Here, we demonstrate a logic-synapse function-integrated device based on a two-dimensional (2D) floating-gate field-effect transistor (FGFET) with a coplanar dual-control-gate architecture. With two independent gate-coupling coefficients, the nominally symmetric design allows the gate-induced potential increments to superpose on the floating gate: cooperative inputs induce charge tunneling and write a new memory state, whereas antagonistic inputs approximately cancel the pulse-induced potential increment and latch the stored state. This rule directly implements LIM within a single device, enabling 14 reconfigurable Boolean logic operations with in situ nonvolatile output storage, a logic read margin of 104, and no external cascading for the demonstrated two-input logic functions. The same coupling framework further supports tunable synaptic plasticity, including lateral enhancement/inhibition and spatiotemporal competition/cooperation among multiple synaptic inputs. In particular, asynchronous competitive modulation modifies history-dependent conductance updates, improving the depression nonlinearity to 0.0833 while retaining a dynamic range of 22.82. These results establish an all-electrical device-level route for integrating logic control and neural weight adaptation in compact CIM hardware.

articles.title: Boosting Electron/Mass Transport via Interfacial Coupling in a Dual-Supported Catalyst toward Ampere-Level Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Developing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts with high activity and long-term durability at industrial current densities remains challenging because catalytic kinetics, electron transport, and mass transport must be optimized simultaneously. Here, we report a one-pot method to anchor Pt-single-atom-modified NiCoP onto MXene with a high surface coverage of ∼97%. The Pt-NiCoP@MXene catalyst requires overpotentials of only 13.8 and 175 mV in 1 M KOH to deliver 10 and 1000 mA cm–2, respectively, and exhibits an ultralow decay rate of 7.1 μV h–1 over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm–2 in a three-electrode system. In an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it achieves 1 A cm–2 at 1.74 V in a 4 cm2 cell with 98% voltage retention after 1000 h and maintains 97% retention over 500 h with a scaled 25 cm2 cell. Experiments and DFT calculations demonstrate the interface strong coupling via Ni/Co–O–Ti bonding bridges NiCoP and MXene effectively and accelerates the electron transport of catalytic layer, while the uniform dispersion of NiCoP on MXene improves surface wettability and facilitates bubble release and electrolyte replenishment. Additionally, Pt–P coordination increases the metallicity of Pt atoms and optimizes hydrogen adsorption/desorption. This work provides a facile strategy for synthesizing high-quality dual-supported catalysts and validates their industrial application potential.

articles.title: Electronic Structure Modulation in Isomeric Carborane-Thiolated Cu4 Nanoclusters Boosts CO2 Electroreduction to Methane
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2R) to energy-dense hydrocarbons is central to sustainable carbon recycling, although achieving selective conversion at high current density and lower overpotential remains challenging. Here, we explore three molecularly precise nanomaterials, comprising nearly square planar Cu4 kernel protected by isomeric carborane-thiolate (CBT) cages, viz., Cu4-oCBT (ortho-carborane), Cu4-mCBT (meta-carborane), and Cu4-ICBT (iodinated-ortho-carborane), for eCO2R. Among them, Cu4-mCBT shows the most favorable performance, achieving ∼74% overall eCO2R selectivity and a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of ∼45% at high current densities of 500 mA cm–2 (−0.87 V vs RHE) while maintaining promising production of C2+ products. Furthermore, Cu4-mCBT and Cu4-ICBT catalysts deliver industrially relevant CH4 partial current densities (JCH4 ∼ 323 mA cm–2 at −0.99 V) at low overpotential, representing competitive performance compared to Cu nanoclusters (NCs) stabilized by conventional ligands. First-principles calculations reveal that Cu4-mCBT lowers the free energy barrier for *CHO to *CHOH hydrogenation, the rate-limiting step for methane formation, due to better orbital interactions with the intermediates. In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) confirms the transient intermediate species formed in the predicted eCO2R-to-CH4 pathway. Charge density difference, projected density of states, and in situ X-ray absorption studies demonstrate the primary catalytic role of the Cu-core, while three-dimensional cage-like ligand shells modulate the electronic structure of exposed metal atoms, thereby optimizing the intermediate binding. This study investigates the catalytic performance of carborane-appended tetranuclear copper clusters toward CO2 reduction pathways and elucidates their structure–activity relationships.

articles.title: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
articles.abstract: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

articles.title: Flexible Zwitterionic Hydrogel Ultrasonic Patch Enables Spatiotemporally Controlled Delivery of Mangiferin-Loaded Micelles for Accelerating Diabetic Wound Healing
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, impaired angiogenesis, and delayed tissue remodeling, often resulting in chronic nonhealing ulcers. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) offers a promising noninvasive therapeutic strategy; however, its clinical efficacy remains constrained by unstable acoustic coupling interfaces and the lack of integrated biological activity. Here, we report an ultrasound-responsive zwitterionic hydrogel patch by incorporating mangiferin-loaded micelles into a topologically entangled PCBOH hydrogel (MF@PCBOH). The mechanically robust hydrogel forms a stable and conformal acoustic interface that efficiently transmits ultrasound under dynamic conditions, whereas the incorporated micelles improve the aqueous dispersibility of mangiferin and enable ultrasound-enhanced release. Under LIPUS stimulation, released mangiferin reduces intracellular ROS, shifts macrophages toward a reparative phenotype, promotes endothelial angiogenesis, and enhances cell migration. As a result, MF@PCBOH accelerates diabetic wound healing in rats, accompanied by reduced inflammation, improved collagen remodeling, and enhanced vascular maturation. Similar therapeutic benefits are observed in a full-thickness porcine wound model, supporting the effectiveness of the hydrogel patch in a large-animal setting. This study demonstrates that integrating a durable acoustic interface with ultrasound-responsive drug delivery offers an effective strategy for diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: Generation of Bloch Points with Controlled Spin Texture Using Geometrical Boundary Conditions
articles.abstract: Bloch points are three-dimensional topological singularities in magnetization that play a key role in topological transformations of spin textures such as skyrmion creation or annihilation. While topology often enforces the existence of Bloch points in confined geometries such as cylindrical nanowires, deterministic control over their position and magnetic configuration remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the generation of Bloch points with controlled spin texture by engineering geometrical boundary conditions in three-dimensional nanomagnets. By introducing a chirality interface between two three-dimensional double-helix nanowires of opposite handedness, forming a kinked, noncollinear structure, we impose competing topological constraints that uniquely define the magnetization configuration surrounding the Bloch point. A saturating magnetic field nucleates head-to-head or tail-to-tail domain configurations at the chirality interface, producing a Bloch-point domain wall with deterministic polarity, circulation, and helicity. This geometrical approach enables full three-dimensional control of Bloch point domain walls, allowing deterministic engineering of their spin texture and its selective coupling to current-induced Oersted fields.

articles.title: Nanoscale Spintronic Microwave Devices: From Fundamental Mechanisms to Emerging Applications
articles.abstract: With the rapid deployment of next-generation communication technologies, the demand for highly sensitive and miniaturized microwave detectors has become extremely urgent. Conventional semiconductor diodes suffer from intrinsic drawbacks when detecting submicrowatt signals. Spintronics provides an optimal alternative via the spin rectification effect, which enables widely tunable, low-power microwave rectification at room temperature. This Review examines recent advances in spintronic microwave rectifiers and their future prospects. We discuss diverse physical platforms, including devices with uniform magnetization and special nonuniform topological spin textures. Furthermore, we highlight multiorder-of-magnitude performance improvements in such devices, focusing on strategies to boost sensitivity, reduce noise equivalent power (NEP), and extend broadband as well as multiband detection capacity. Apart from core performance metrics, we discuss emerging applications: ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting, high-resolution vector microwave-field imaging, monolithically integrated spintronic microwave systems, and microwave neural networks that can directly process high-frequency signals for neuromorphic computing. By sorting out the complete technical development route of this field, this Review aims to provide a systematic theoretical framework and technical references to promote the development of spintronic devices for next-generation wireless communication and edge artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Robust and Wide-Range Friction Regulation via Interfacial Bridging-Promoted Hydration Switching in Phase-Separated Gels
articles.abstract: Interfacial friction strongly influences materials performance, but achieving controllable friction with both high robustness and wide-range tunability remains difficult. In conventional friction regulation systems based on phase separations, rigid and incompatible hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces often cause interfacial cracking and poor stability. Here, inspired by the toughening mechanism of cartilage, we introduce amphiphilic bridging segments between hydrophilic and hydrophobic phases to construct an interfacial bridging nanophase-separated gel (IBNSGel) for robust friction control. This design transforms the fragile phase interface into a tough bridging interphase, suppresses aggregation, promotes uniform nanophase separation, and enhances interfacial stability during hydration-induced phase separation. Owing to this bridging effect, IBNSGel exhibits synergistic surface-bulk friction switching upon hydration: the surface forms a stable hydration layer for excellent lubrication, while the bulk hardens with higher modulus and lower damping, reducing conformal contact dissipation. As a result, this gel achieves stable, reversible, and wide-range coefficient of friction (CoF) switching during hydration–dehydration, with switching ratios of 150 at the macroscale and 330 at the microscale. Based on its excellent multimedium stability and biocompatibility, this friction control material demonstrates great application potential in smart medical devices, soft robots, and interface intelligent transportation systems.

articles.title: Targeting the Immune-Neurovascular Interface to Ameliorate Pericyte Dysfunction with a Multifunctional Peptide–Drug Conjugate Nanoprodrug for Multiple Sclerosis Therapy
articles.abstract: Pericyte dysfunction triggers blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption and subsequent aberrant immune infiltration in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet targeted interventions remain lacking. Here, we engineered a dual-functional fusion peptide (VLC) for pericyte targeting and therapeutic intervention and subsequently conjugated it with luteolin to construct a peptide–drug conjugate (PDC)-based ROS-responsive nanoprodrug (VLC@Lut-NPs). This system significantly suppressed MMP-9 overactivation and mitigated neuroinflammation. To optimize the pharmacokinetic profile of the PDC nanotherapeutic, we adopted subcutaneous administration, achieving a prolonged circulation half-life and enhancing brain drug accumulation (AUCbrain) by 2.65-fold compared with intravenous injection. In two MS models, VLC@Lut-NPs restored pericyte homeostasis, reinforced BBB integrity, attenuated aberrant peripheral immune infiltration, and ultimately promoted myelin repair and regeneration. Notably, a once-every-other-day subcutaneous regimen outperformed daily intravenous administration. By bridging peripheral immunity and the neurovascular unit, this work identifies pericytes as a central regulatory node and establishes a pericyte-targeted PDC nanoplatform for durable MS treatment, highlighting its translational potential as a complementary strategy to conventional immunomodulatory approaches.

articles.title: The Future of Nanoscience: Reaching Early-Career Scientists
Turn Shield into Sword: Pathological Hydroxyapatite-Targeting Micelles Drive Metabolic Stress-Induced Autophagy Dysfunction for Bone Metastasis Therapy
articles.abstract: Bone metastasis remains a major clinical challenge in advanced breast cancer because therapeutic efficacy is limited by poor lesion targeting and systemic toxicity. Moreover, the hypoxic bone microenvironment induces protective autophagy in tumor cells, which maintains metabolic homeostasis and limits therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we develop a bone metastasis-targeted micellar system (AD/R) to overcome this protective autophagy “shield”. Based on the low crystallinity of pathological hydroxyapatite (HAP) and the hypoxic bone microenvironment, a pathological HAP-targeting polymer (DSPE-PEG-ALN, DPA) and a hypoxia-responsive polymer (DSPE-AZO-PEG, DAP) are coassembled into micelles encapsulating the oxidative phosphorylation inhibitor resveratrol (RES). Following selective accumulation in bone-metastatic lesions, AD/R undergoes hypoxia-triggered disassembly. The released DPA induces calcium-mediated membrane mineralization to restrict oxygen and nutrient supply, whereas RES suppresses oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production. This “external blockade” and “internal disruption” synergistically aggravate metabolic stress, activate AMPK-dependent autophagy, and impair lysosomal degradation through lysosomal membrane permeabilization, ultimately inducing autophagy dysfunction and autophagy-associated tumor cell death. In murine breast cancer bone metastasis models, AD/R effectively suppresses bone and secondary lung metastases and restores bone homeostasis. This work establishes a “turn shield into sword” paradigm by converting protective autophagy into metabolic stress-induced autophagy dysfunction for the treatment of bone metastasis.

articles.title: Unconventionally Dynamical Regime of Colloidal Nanocrystals on Spherical Surfaces
articles.abstract: Crystallography of colloidal nanocrystals on spherical surfaces underpins the structural organization of a wide range of functional soft and biological materials, from viral capsids and protein nanocages to colloidal microcapsules and curvature-engineered metamaterials. In these systems, the topology dictates that crystalline order on a sphere must incorporate topological defects that can self-organize into scars whose conformations undergo fluctuations. However, how these conformations collectively affect phase transitions on spheres remains unknown. Here, we investigate the phase transitions of colloidal nanocrystal packing on the spherical surface and identify an unconventional regime in the solid phase, which exhibits rapid dynamics with enhanced fluctuations of scars. Further analysis reveals that this regime is governed by the conformational entropy of the scars. Such an entropic effect on dynamics exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on system size and causes disparate scaling laws at intermediate and large system sizes, which are absent in previous experiments and theoretical models. The findings provide insights into the effect of topological defects on curved manifolds and reveal the critical role of the conformational entropy of defect scars in geometrically frustrated systems of colloidal nanocrystals.

articles.title: Strength and thermal conductivity enhancement by solute substitution during laser powder bed fusion of NiWCo/Cu dissimilar alloy joint
Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
articles.abstract: Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na2O/Na2CO3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10−7 S cm−1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na2O (10−12 S cm−1) and Na2CO3 (10−23 S cm−1). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

articles.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
articles.abstract: Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak‐coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)3), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al3+, displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO‐mediated solvation disruption with FEC‐enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel‐to‐layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1. By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

articles.journal: Annual Review of Condensed Matter Physics
articles.abstract: A negative contains all the information for the final photographic print. But held up against the light, the negative often appears glaring and garish—certainly unfamiliar and sometimes difficult to recognize. Immediately after exposure in the quiet acrid environment of the darkroom, the positive enlargement is initially invisible and then starts to appear so faintly that it is scarcely detectable; only with patience as it reacts to the harsh chemical baths into which it was plunged does it emerge into a sharp, detailed, and nuanced image. In the shadows cast by the negative, as the resultant positive emerges from the nearly unrecognizable past, it is surprising and gratifying to discover a memory of the initial moment of exposure. This metaphor serves as an apt though abstract description of the experiences described in this essay.

articles.title: The Biology of the Clonal Raider Ant (Ooceraea biroi) and Its Role as a Social Insect Model System
articles.abstract: The clonal raider ant, Ooceraea biroi , is a blind, subterranean insect that combines several rare life history traits which make it uniquely suited for use as a laboratory model. The species has lost the queen caste; instead, colonies are composed entirely of clonally reproducing workers. Workers lay eggs in synchrony, giving rise to discrete and age-matched cohorts of new workers. Despite this simple biology, the clonal raider ant displays sophisticated social and collective behaviors, including scout-initiated group raids of live arthropod prey as well as regular colony emigrations. The species also relies heavily on pheromones and other olfactory signals to mediate general ant behaviors such as trail following, alarm responses, worker policing, and nonnestmate discrimination. Here, I discuss how the clonal raider ant provides unprecedented access to study these and other social insect behaviors with modern molecular tools.

articles.title: Is the Science of Redistricting Possible in an Adversarial Legal System?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: The incorporation of scientific methods into redistricting litigation has generated considerable optimism. However, for politically charged disputes such as redistricting, embedding scientific rigor within the judicial process faces substantial hurdles. The adversarial process, by design, is inclined to reward rhetorical force over epistemic integrity. While science may provide important insight, to gain such insight we must guard against its distortion and strategic misuse. Ultimately, we must also realize that the task of defining fairness in political representation is a deeply philosophical and normative exercise that belongs to the polity and its democratic institutions, where science can serve in a clarifying but not determinative role.

articles.title: What's a Firm, What's a Corporation, and Why Does It Matter?
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: To understand how corporate activity is changing our economies and societies, we need to distinguish how they organize through bodies of law. In general parlance, the words firm, corporation, and company are used interchangeably. This is a matter of convenience but masks how firms, as organizing units, articulate their activities through corporations as legal entities that offer them affordances. This article reviews the literature in sociolegal studies, sociology, political economy, institutional economics, and accounting studies that considers what is at stake in the firm/corporation distinction. A new way to combine their insights is offered, locating how firms use bodies of law to replicate corporate strategies and structural asymmetries in the world economy.

articles.title: You Don't Have a Selection Problem: We Live in a Selectiony World
articles.journal: Annual Review of Law and Social Science
articles.abstract: Empirical legal researchers often seek to make causal inferences about a class of phenomena that we call selectiony treatments: treatments that are defined by some reasons, rules, or mechanisms that bring them about. Reviewing the literature, we suggest that these types of treatments suffuse the law, because the law is all about limiting the kinds of reasons that can serve as the grounds for a particular legal status. Selectiony treatments pose a distinctive conceptual problem for causal inference: They make it difficult to define counterfactual contrasts that correspond to real-world interventions of interest. We show how this problem surfaces in the study of canonical legal phenomena like bail, incarceration, and police stops, and we clarify how it differs from familiar concerns like confounding and selection bias. We provide a clear way for researchers to think through these issues and diagnose limitations to their causal inferences by emphasizing two prerequisites for coherent causal claims: ( a ) a clear definition of the variables inside a causal model and ( b ) a clear understanding of the causal estimand that is its target.

articles.title: Mechanisms of Regulation of Fetal Hemoglobin Levels: Implications for Treatment of Sickle Cell Disease
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is caused by one of the most common single gene defects in humans and has severe clinical consequences that affect millions of individuals worldwide. It is well established that sufficient levels of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) postnatally can abrogate the pathophysiologic cause of red cell sickling and hence the morbid manifestations of SCD. Major advances in understanding the basis for developmental globin gene regulation and postnatal HbF silencing in recent years have uncovered the detailed molecular mechanisms involved. These discoveries have led to curative gene therapy and identified potential targets for small-molecule therapeutics that could induce similarly high levels of HbF. Successful development of drugs based on knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of HbF silencing would meet a pressing need for treatments that induce sufficient HbF to prevent the morbidity of SCD and that may be accessible in the near future for the majority of affected individuals worldwide.

articles.title: Noncoding RNAs in Cancer: Functions, Mechanisms, and Targeting Approaches
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Ninety-eight percent of the human transcriptome lacks protein-coding potential. A small fraction of this landscape comprises housekeeping noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) with well-defined functions, whereas the heterogeneous group of regulatory ncRNAs, generated from ∼100,000 loci, acts through diverse mechanisms to control gene expression, chromatin states, RNA processing, and signaling networks. Their recent evolutionary expansion reflects the increasing regulatory complexity of cell and tissue specification programs in higher organisms. In cancer, such programs are co-opted, with fine-tuned regulatory control contributing to the rewiring of molecular networks during transformation, metastasis, and adaptation to therapy. Here, we review the molecular functions of ncRNAs and their involvement in cancer, with emphasis on regulatory classes including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs. We also describe emerging technical innovations that advance their investigation, including genetic tools enabling systematic, context-resolved mapping of ncRNA functions. We conclude by discussing the translational potential of ncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Environmental Epigenetic Transgenerational Inheritance and Generational Toxicology
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology
articles.abstract: Environmental chemicals and toxicants can promote phenotypic variation or disease not only in the individual exposed but also in individuals for multiple subsequent generations. This phenomenon is termed epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology. Most environmental factors and toxicants do not promote genetic mutations that alter the DNA sequence, but they can alter epigenetics and the epigenome. Epigenetic changes in the germline allow for epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology as a result of the previous generations’ exposures. The toxicology and pharmacology of environmental chemicals and epigenetic transgenerational inheritance are discussed in the context of generational toxicology.

articles.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
articles.abstract: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

articles.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
articles.abstract: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

articles.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
articles.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

articles.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
articles.abstract: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

articles.title: Structural basis and rational engineering of a thermophilic Cas13a for robust RNA detection
articles.abstract: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.

articles.abstract: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.

articles.title: Single-cell CRISPR screen maps epigenetic regulators of lineage specification and malignancies in human HSPCs
articles.abstract: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.

Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
articles.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

articles.title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
articles.abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

articles.title: Marine Carbonate System Observing and mCDR: New Processes, Needs, and Systems
articles.abstract: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.

articles.title: Activating Interstitial Oxygen Conduction in Sr3V2O8 Palmierite Oxides Through Minimal Mo-Substitution
articles.abstract: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.

articles.title: Alkali Manganese Oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Li, Na): Direct Synthesis, Crystal Chemistry, and Ion-Transport Limitations
articles.abstract: Alkali manganese oxynitridophosphates A1.1Mn2.9P3O8N2 (A = Na, Li) were prepared by one-step solid-state ammonolysis, where the lithium analogue is obtained directly rather than by alkali-ion exchange from the sodium compound. Both compositions crystallize in a previously unreported orthorhombic Pbcn framework, in which ordered O/N environments, unusual manganese coordination in MnO5N and MnO6N2 polyhedra, and alkali–manganese disorder are accommodated within the same structure. The proposed structural model is supported by complementary synchrotron X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, electron microscopy, solid-state NMR and XAS data, as well as density functional theory calculations. Magnetic susceptibility is consistent with predominantly Mn2+ and antiferromagnetic ordering below 35.1 K for the Li phase and 32.6 K for the Na phase. Although the Mn2+/Mn3+ redox couple lies within the accessible potential window of nonaqueous M-ion batteries, reversible alkali extraction is limited by the restricted migration pathways imposed by the framework. Overall, this work expands the compositional and structural landscape of oxynitridophosphates and highlights nitrogen incorporation in phosphate crystal chemistry as a route to unconventional coordination environments, new framework connectivities and functional properties.

articles.title: Magnetic and Electrochemical Properties of the Altermagnetic Layered Antiperovskite Na2Mn2OS2
articles.abstract: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra. Magnetization and neutron diffraction data reveal that the phase undergoes magnetic ordering below 144 K. The low-temperature magnetic structure has zero net magnetization and is invariant under a combination of rotation and time reversal, thereby fulfilling the symmetry criteria to be considered as an altermagnet candidate. Electronic band structure calculations demonstrate that the phase contains spin-polarized bands, providing further evidence that Na2Mn2OS2 can be described as an altermagnet. An electrochemical investigation of this compound was performed, aiming both to tailor the physicochemical properties of the material through desodiation and to yield a possible Na-ion cathode material. While there are indications of Na-deintercalation, the charge compensation mechanism appears to involve irreversible sulfur oxidation rather than manganese oxidation, thus preventing the application of Na2Mn2OS2 as a positive electrode for Na-ion batteries.

articles.title: Metastable Inorganic Materials through Reactive Molten-Salt Ion Exchange
articles.abstract: Material discovery is the foundational process for fundamental investigations and useful applications of functional and structural materials. It is the prerequisite for all downstream processes including property determination, synthetic optimization and scale-up, doping, defect engineering, morphology control, and surface and interfacial tuning. Through extensive experimental and, more recently, computational exploration, the number of yet-to-be-discovered thermodynamically stable compounds in low-order phase spaces has rapidly shrunk. However, new materials are needed to foster advances in established and emerging applications, particularly those related to energy storage, conversion, and efficiency. Thinking beyond equilibrium phase diagrams, a much larger phase space of metastable compounds exists if such phases can be synthetically accessed. This Perspective highlights the role of reactive molten-salt ion exchange (MSIX) as a technique for metastable inorganic material discovery. We discuss the thermodynamics, kinetics, crystal chemistry, and atomic-scale characterization of reactive molten-salt ion exchange. Emergent phenomena in ion exchange such as interdiffusion and the mixed-ion effect and challenges associated with characterizing mixed-ion and heterogeneous systems receive extra attention. In consideration of the breadth of MSIX, fundamental principles and general reaction schemes are used where possible with specific examples extensively referenced. MSIX is contextualized by comparisons to adjacent fields that involve molten salts, ion transport, and metastable materials. Opportunities and missed opportunities associated with computational approaches to molten-salt reactions and metastable materials are discussed. Unique prospects for in situ diffraction and NMR crystallography are highlighted along with future directions, including extensions to solid-state ion exchange (SSIX).

articles.title: Unprecedented Pd(II) Metal–Organic Cages for Simultaneous Adsorption of Iodine Species
articles.abstract: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) with unconventional topologies remain rare owing to the challenges associated with controlling coordination-driven self-assembly. Herein, we report the self-assembly of two unique Pd(II)-based coordination cages–peanut-shaped cage (C1, M18L14) and hemicage (C2, M12M2L22), from semiflexible tetratopic pyridyl ligands incorporating 9,10-dihydroanthracene and benzene backbones, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that cage C1 adopts a rare peanut-shaped structure comprising two interconnected cavities and both inward- and outward-oriented Pd(II) nodes, generating a highly electron-rich confined environment. In contrast, C2 forms an unprecedented boat-shaped architecture assembled through the cooperative incorporation of 90° and 180° Pd(II) acceptors within a single discrete cage. Despite their amorphous and nonporous nature, these assemblies demonstrate exceptional dual-capture performance toward volatile iodine species. Notably, C1 achieves iodine uptake capacities of 2.62 g g–1 under static vapor-phase conditions and 1.21 g g–1 under dynamic flow conditions, together with efficient CH3I adsorption of up to 1.05 g g–1 at 75 °C. Spectroscopic investigations and theoretical calculations reveal that the adsorption process is driven by synergistic charge-transfer interactions, polyiodide formation, electrostatic stabilization, and cavity confinement. Furthermore, both cages display excellent retention capability and recyclability, highlighting their potential as robust materials for radioactive iodine sequestration and environmental remediation.

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique Identifier: NCT05686070.

articles.title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study
articles.abstract: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions. In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions. During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0–42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P <0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm 2 , regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm 2 , regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%–13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07–1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05–1.38]). Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT06836011.

articles.title: Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8
articles.abstract: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)–containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies. We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr −/− mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8. Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr −/− mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition. A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase– and endothelial lipase–mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB–containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

articles.title: Breeding Behaviors and Kinship in the Endangered Hawaiian Stilt (Ae‘o; Himantopus mexicanus knudseni)
articles.abstract: Understanding the genetic underpinnings of cooperative and noncooperative breeding behaviors is critical for species of conservation concern. We investigated the genetic relatedness of Hawaiian Stilts (Aeʻo; Himantopus mexicanus knudseni), a threatened subspecies restricted to the Hawaiian Islands, in relation to nesting behavior, given recent behavioral observations of cooperative breeding, potential conspecific brood parasitism, and potential pairing of closely related individuals for nesting. Using RAD sequencing of blood and feather samples, we generated ~6800 SNPs for parentage and relatedness analysis. Observational data documented behaviors including cooperative incubation, helpers-at-the-nest, and potential conspecific brood parasitism, which are rarely reported in Charadriiformes. Parentage, genomic relatedness, and Bayesian phylogenetic analyses revealed instances of conspecific brood parasitism and potential extra-pair paternity. We also find evidence of inbreeding, with an overall F IS of 0.23 and close genetic similarity between some mates. Ecological constraints and limited dispersal opportunities may promote cooperative breeding, conspecific brood parasitism, and inbreeding in Hawaiian Stilts. These results underscore the importance of maintaining and restoring nesting habitat to reduce pressures that may otherwise intensify inbreeding in this recovering population but also highlight the behavioral flexibility and adaptive capacity in this species.

Individual bumblebee foraging repertoires: Implications for disease persistence
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Generalist species may be comprised of individual specialists. Individual specialization can impact disease transmission at shared resources by shaping contact patterns. Mathematical models of pollinator diseases that spread via flowers have shown that R 0 can be greatly amplified when each forager specializes on one flower species at a time with slow turnover. Yet, such behaviour has not been empirically demonstrated in generalist bumblebees. Here, we used palynology from sequential pollen loads of individual common eastern bumble bees (Bombus impatiens) to assess their foraging preferences over time. We used an automated monitoring system to greatly improve recapture rates, hence allowing a more complete characterization of each bee's foraging behaviours. Individuals in a bumblebee colony exhibited unique foraging repertoires of two to three flower species while the full-colony diet breadth was up to three times larger depending on time of year. Individual repertoires exhibited roughly 50% turnover, on average, over 10 days. Implications for disease transmission when individual repertoire sizes are greater than one may differ from specialization on a single flower species. Hence, we developed mathematical models where each bee has an effective repertoire size of two, and found that ignoring individual specialization still resulted in an underprediction of R 0, although to a smaller extent compared to a single-specialty model. Our results provide novel insights into the foraging behaviours of social bumblebees and improve predictions of how diseases are transmitted and persist in complex plant–pollinator networks. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: A World With Platelets Stored Cold for 21 Days
articles.abstract: A platelet transfusion is a small miracle. To get the platelets, a supplier must find donors who will volunteer to spend 2 hours undergoing apheresis. Every platelet unit donated needs complex bacterial testing or expensive pathogen reduction followed by continuous agitation in a thermally controlled shaker at room temperature. After all this, the platelets have a shelf life of only 5 to 7 days, and because the testing takes up most of the first 2 days, the usable window is only 3 to 5 days long. Platelets are fragile, expensive, and perpetually in short supply.

articles.abstract: This randomized trial assesses the effect of arginine therapy on time to crisis resolution among children and young adults experiencing sickle cell disease (SCD)–related acute pain episodes.

articles.title: Arginine Treatment and Sickle Cell Disease Pain—A Great STArT, but a Hard End Point
articles.abstract: Acute pain episodes, also called pain crises, are a hallmark of sickle cell disease and the leading driver of health care utilization across the lifespan. In the pediatric population, acute pain crises account for more than 70 000 emergency department (ED) visits annually, with many encounters requiring hospitalization. The burden of pain does not end at discharge—nearly 30% of patients discharged from the ED return within days, and similar proportions are readmitted within 30 days of hospitalization. Despite the significant burden of disease, the standard treatment for an acute pain crisis has not significantly changed over decades: intravenous opioids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and intravenous fluids remain the cornerstone of treatment, carrying well-known risks of opioid dependence, respiratory depression, and edema without addressing the underlying vascular pathophysiology. An urgent need exists for a targeted treatment to address the biology of vaso-occlusion itself, rather than relying on symptom management alone.

articles.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
articles.abstract: To the Editor Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) remains one of the most common and treatable causes of dizziness encountered in clinical practice. We enjoyed the recently published JAMA Insights article on the treatment of BPPV and the associated JAMA Patient Page on BPPV. The Epley maneuver has appropriately become the default therapeutic approach for posterior canal BPPV, given its ease of use, robust evidence base, and broad adoption across specialties. However, the near-universal reliance on the Epley maneuver risks narrowing clinician awareness of equally effective and, in some contexts, potentially advantageous alternatives such as the Semont-plus maneuver.

articles.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply Regarding our recent JAMA Insights about the treatment of BPPV, Dr Purks and colleagues question our decision not to advocate for integrating the use of the Semont-plus maneuver into routine practice. We offer 2 points in response.

articles.title: Characteristics of Patients Choosing Intravenous Moderate Sedation for IUD Placement
articles.abstract: This study examined the prevalence of intravenous moderate sedation (IVS) for intrauterine device (IUD) placement when universally offered, as well as the demographic, reproductive, and social factors associated with its use.

articles.title: Clinicopathologic Evaluation of Amyloid Clearance in Alzheimer Disease
articles.abstract: This case report assesses postmortem and in vivo associations between amyloid levels and downstream neuropathology in a patient who had received aducanumab therapy for Alzheimer disease compared with untreated controls.

articles.title: Digitalis Glycosides in Patients With Heart Failure
articles.abstract: To the Editor A recent meta-analysis of 3 large placebo-controlled randomized clinical trials suggested a lower risk of cardiovascular death or first worsening heart failure (HF) event in patients with HF who were treated with digitalis glycosides. However, several important limitations warrant particular consideration.

articles.title: Digitalis Glycosides in Patients With Heart Failure—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We appreciate the letter from Dr Čulić about our meta-analysis, which showed that treatment with digitalis glycosides was associated with a significant 20% relative risk reduction in the primary outcome of cardiovascular death and HF hospitalization, mainly attributable to a lower risk of HF hospitalizations.

articles.title: Digoxin for Symptomatic Rheumatic Heart Disease
articles.abstract: To the Editor The Dig-RHD trial provided valuable evidence that digoxin reduces the composite risk of all-cause death or new-onset or worsening heart failure in patients with symptomatic RHD. However, 2 issues warrant evaluation, as they carry important implications for clinical interpretation.

articles.title: Digoxin for Symptomatic Rheumatic Heart Disease—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr Lu and colleagues and Drs Zhu and Wang for their letters about the Dig-RHD trial. Broadly, it appears that heart failure due to RHD is being conflated with heart failure due to other causes (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction).

articles.title: Poetry, Medicine, and the Body’s Secrets
articles.abstract: Both poetry and medicine are concerned with keeping and, when necessary, sharing confidences. Medicine adopts the sternest stance regarding what is termed protected health information, with numerous regulations (such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA]) explicitly directing how patients’ medical records must be safeguarded. Of all medical conditions, infertility is among those for which treatment unfolds under especially strict conditions of both medical and social concealment. The insistence on patients’ privacy is also expressed in the poem “One Day I Will Tell You,” in which a litany of withheld information—“[a] vial of seed tucked inside my shirt,” hidden injections, undeclared hope, silent miscarriage, and even an unspoken Holocaust survival story—is shared, however piecemeal, accumulating to an important, more nuanced question about when and why such details may be aired. Thus poetry, rather than enforcing some absolute nondisclosure policy, becomes instead a crucial means for navigating the personal vs public. “It was my secret, even when Grandma Helen died,” the speaker declares, thereby joining the possibility of new life with the loss of another and marking a point, perhaps, when such secrets may be told. The title of the poem itself seems to yearn for the moment when hope can transcend fear, whether it be the fear of failure, exposure, or death. The poem’s conclusion, when that day has arrived, is a liberating reminder, combining truths seemingly at odds as only poetry can, of why medicine must always protect patients’ health information: so it remains only in their power to choose whether to disclose it.

articles.title: Tucidinostat Plus R-CHOP for Large B-Cell Lymphoma
articles.abstract: To the Editor Dr Xu and colleagues conducted an important randomized study evaluating the efficacy and safety of tucidinostat added to standard rituximab plus cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) compared with R-CHOP alone as first-line therapy for patients with MYC/BCL2 double-expressor diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. A total of 423 patients were randomized to receive oral tucidinostat or matching placebo in combination with 6 cycles of R-CHOP. The primary end point was event-free survival. The stratified hazard ratio for event-free survival was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.54-0.96; P = .02), favoring the tucidinostat group. However, no statistically significant differences were observed for any secondary end point.

articles.title: Milder winters alleviate seasonal challenges for a migratory goose facing Arctic warming
articles.abstract: By combining extensive body mass records with population‐wide migration counts spanning several decades, this study uncovers long‐term improvements in body condition associated with progressively milder winters, alongside earlier spring departure in an Arctic migrant, highlighting the importance of the full annual cycle in determining species' responses to climate change. Abstract Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non‐breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark‐bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. Earlier departure would require reaching departure body mass earlier, either through a faster accumulation of energy stores during spring staging in the Wadden Sea or via adjustments earlier in the annual cycle. We examined long‐term shifts in spring staging phenology and changes in winter and spring body mass trajectories of brent geese at the population level, with particular emphasis on the effects of winter temperature on body mass and spring body mass on departure timing. We used more than five decades of body mass measurements from individuals caught in the United Kingdom and France and in the Dutch Wadden Sea to reconstruct changes in winter and spring mass trajectories, respectively. These data were combined with over five decades of migration counts in the Netherlands and more than two decades of counts in Denmark to quantify changes in arrival and departure timing, respectively. We found that brent geese were heavier during and after milder winters and that their body mass trajectories flattened over the years: they no longer lose body mass during winter; during spring staging, fuelling rates have declined (in the so‐called ‘fattening phase’), while they also no longer lose body mass in the 1–2 weeks prior to departure (‘plateau phase’). Brent geese have not shifted their spring arrival in the Wadden Sea but have advanced departure timing. Annual variation in body mass was not related to annual departure timing. These results suggest that milder winters have relaxed energetic constraints and improved body condition in brent geese throughout the non‐breeding season. Our findings highlight the importance of considering the full annual cycle when assessing how migratory animals respond to global change, in particular those with limited capacity to adjust migration timing or speed.

articles.title: Legume presence outweighs functional group richness in determining community invasibility under nitrogen enrichment
articles.abstract: These findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR. Abstract Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment often promotes plant invasions by increasing resource availability, yet why resident communities differ in their resistance to the same resource pulse remains poorly understood. Here, we manipulated native plant functional group richness (FGR = 1–3) and community composition while holding species richness constant and assessed the performance of the nitrophilous invader Bidens alba under ambient and N‐enriched conditions to determine whether biotic resistance is driven by diversity per se or specific functional identities. N enrichment consistently increased invader biomass, but its interaction with FGR was not significant across the full richness gradient, indicating that FGR alone was insufficient for predicting biotic resistance. Instead, functional identity strongly governed plant invasion outcomes. Non‐legume communities (grasses and forbs) sustained high biotic resistance under N enrichment through strong above‐ground neighbour suppression. Conversely, legume‐containing communities exhibited weak biotic resistance under N enrichment, permitting a considerable increase in invader biomass. Legumes facilitated plant invasion through a coupled below‐ and above‐ground mechanism: they maintained a high baseline soil nitrate availability while experiencing competitive suppression under N enrichment, resulting in low biomass and minimal physical canopy presence. Combined with N enrichment, this created a favourable resource window that enabled B. alba to reduce its root: shoot ratio—a morphological plasticity response constrained in non‐legume communities by dense native neighbour biomass. Synthesis. Our findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR.
