A Skin-like Hydrogel with Multidimensional Fillers for Stable Human–Machine Interaction
articles.abstract: The deep integration of human–machine interface (HMI) technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) has imposed stringent new requirements for electronic skin (e-skin) in terms of flexibility, comfort, and high sensitivity. Herein we present a multiconductive network hydrogel e-skin (MCNHE-skin) based on a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) dual-network matrix with polydopamine (PDA), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and MXene as conductive fillers. The MCNHE-skin exhibits electrical conductivity (<5 kΩ), high stretchability (∼650%), strong self-adhesion (∼19 kPa), and low modulus (∼3.6 kPa). These characteristics enable its successful application in multimodal sensing systems such as strain sensors, pressure sensors, triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), and physiological signal monitors. Furthermore, by integration with flexible printed circuit boards (FPCBs), MCNHE-skin is developed into smart wearable systems for noncontact HMI. The 0D/1D/2D synergistic conductive network presented in this hydrogel e-skin yields high-fidelity sensing and noncontact control capabilities, marking a significant step forward in the development of multifunctional wearable electronics.

articles.title: Dielectric Interfaces Reshape Dynamic Single-Molecule Optical Fingerprints in Nanometer-Thick Polymer Films
articles.abstract: Fluorescence lifetimes near dielectric interfaces depend on molecular dipole orientation, but this relationship becomes more complex when emitters are confined within finite nanometer-thick polymer films. Here, we combine radially polarized excitation imaging with time-correlated single-photon counting to follow the orientation and fluorescence lifetime of individual PDI molecules undergoing rotational motion in thin poly(n-butyl methacrylate) films. Orientation-sensitive fluorescence patterns were analyzed using vectorial wave-optical simulations, enabling dipole orientation and excited-state lifetime to be correlated over time for the same emitter. The lifetime–orientation relationships vary systematically with film thickness and between molecules within the same film. Electrodynamic calculations for the glass–polymer–air geometry reproduce the principal trends and show that the observed heterogeneity is consistent with different axial emitter positions. These results establish single molecular dipoles as probes of finite nanometer-thick dielectric environments.

articles.title: Erbium Probes of Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Material
articles.abstract: Embedded atomic emitters offer a complementary approach to characterizing magnetism in two-dimensional materials by accessing the magnetic environment from within. Here, we demonstrate that ion-implanted Er3+ centers act as internal optical probes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. Temperature-dependent telecom photoluminescence reveals signatures of the magnetic transition, persistent local magnetic behavior above the bulk Néel temperature, pronounced thermal hysteresis, and redistribution of optical spectral weight near the transition. Upon cooling, the Er resonances sharpen to the instrumental limit, pointing to remarkably homogeneous local environments despite implantation. Measurements spanning a 20-fold range of implantation fluence, structural characterization, and first-principles calculations suggest that the detected emission originates predominantly from an optically active subset of Er centers occupying well-defined environments and minimally perturbing the host magnetism. These results establish rare-earth defects as embedded probes of local magnetism and open opportunities for quantum-optical interrogation at individual lattice sites.

articles.title: Photobattery Architectures to Suppress Charge Recombination
articles.abstract: Integrating solar energy conversion and storage into single-unit photobatteries offers compact energy supplies. However, achieving sufficient photovoltage to charge batteries without external bias remains a critical bottleneck for these devices. Here, we demonstrate that the photovoltage in Zn-ion photobatteries can be modulated and enhanced by selecting and structuring the photoactive materials strategically. Randomly dispersed electrode configurations are easy to manufacture but they can suffer from charge recombination. In our experiments, these yielded a negligible photovoltage of ∼0.01 V. In comparison, our proposed layer-by-layer design, integrating a solid-state dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) with an optimized spinel Zn–Mn oxide cathode, increased the photovoltage output to ∼1 V under 1-sun illumination. This dramatic performance enhancement is achieved by better control over interfaces and charge transport and establishes a strategy for improving the architecture of future photobatteries.

articles.title: Two families of multi-planet systems with distinct architectures and stellar hosts
articles.abstract: The rapidly growing census of exoplanets now includes over a thousand multi-planet systems, revealing architectures that span more than four orders of magnitude in mass and five in orbital scale. Explaining the origin of this striking diversity remains a central challenge for planet formation theory, compounded by observational biases that limit access to Solar System-like regimes. Here we introduce architecture-agnostic metrics to uniformly analyse four independently defined samples of multi-planet systems, uncovering unifying patterns across their diversity. We identify a clear bimodality in system masses, dividing known architectures into two distinct families. The lower-mass family, predominantly hosted by subsolar-to-solar stars, exhibits tightly packed configurations with mass distributions consistent with the ‘peas-in-a-pod’ pattern and modal dynamical excitation comparable with that of the Solar System. By contrast, the high-mass family forms in metal-rich environments around solar-to-supersolar stars, displays gravitationally compact architectures and is an order of magnitude dynamically hotter than both the Solar System and the lower-mass counterparts. Their high level of dynamical excitation points to violent evolutionary pathways driven by global instabilities and planet–planet scattering. Together, these results show that the architectures of planetary systems are born from the combined influence of formation processes and host star properties. Signatures of these roots are preserved across the post-formation dynamical evolution that reshaped most known multi-planet systems.

CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
articles.abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
articles.abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

articles.title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice

Here, the authors identify a macrophage-driven IL-1β inflammatory signaling that regulates the NAD + /NAM metabolic ratio to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction and show that disruption of the NAD + /NAM ratio sensitises tumors to chemoimmunotherapy across multiple preclinical mouse models.

articles.title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
articles.abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

articles.title: Mosquito-based malaria control through genetic, microbial and immunological innovations
articles.abstract: In this Review, Dong and colleagues overview recent developments in mosquito-targeted malaria control, highlighting Anopheles population modification (rendering mosquitoes Plasmodium-resistant) and Anopheles population-suppression strategies based on gene drive technology, engineered microorganisms, vaccines and drugs, and discuss key knowledge gaps and the responsible implementation of these approaches in conjunction with existing malaria interventions.

articles.title: A general synthesis of tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides enabled by a dual-functional directing group
articles.abstract: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.

articles.title: Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis
articles.abstract: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.

articles.title: Metabolic convergence on TOR signaling in the chestnut blight fungus and its regulation by host plant signals
articles.abstract: Proposed model of metabolic convergence on the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway in Cryphonectria parasitica. Twelve core genes involved in diverse metabolic pathways act as upstream regulators or downstream effectors of TOR kinase. Dysregulation of these genes mimics an inhibited TOR state, leading to restricted hyphal growth and enhanced trehalose and autophagy, independent of Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection. Mutants carrying deletions in these genes display severe growth defects in response to CHV1 infection. Changes in CHV1 titer were genotype‐specific, with the genes functioning as antiviral, viral replicative, or defense factors in C. parasitica. Summary Transcriptomic analysis of the chestnut blight fungus Cryphonectria parasitica identified 22 core genes regulated by Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1) infection and sectorization. Twelve genes with common phenocopies were analyzed: all mutants displayed restricted colonial growth, intense pigmentation, hyperbranched terminal hyphae with swollen globose cells, and reduced conidiation. Although gene‐specific mutant phenotypes existed, responses to most stressors were similar to those of the wild‐type. Mutant growth was highly sensitive to nutrient conditions, and growth restriction was notably alleviated by supplementation with 1.0 M sorbitol, nutrient‐deficient media, or skim milk. All mutants showed hallmarks consistent with reduced target of rapamycin (TOR) signaling. Trehalose accumulation, a canonical fungal response to TOR inhibition, was observed in mutants via transcriptional upregulation of core trehalose biosynthetic genes, resulting in altered hyphal osmolarity and common mutant cell phenotypes. Plant signals overrode the mutants' phenotypes, strongly promoting their growth and differentiation. Although a severely retarded growth defect was observed in mutants, mutants' virulence remained intact, which can be ascribed to the host‐plant signals. Cryphonectria hypovirus 1 (CHV1)‐infected mutants exhibited greater growth restriction, accompanied by genotype‐specific CHV1 titers. Despite gene‐specific variation, common phenocopies indicate that diverse metabolic pathways converge on the TOR pathway in the fungal response to host‐plant and CHV1 infection.

articles.title: PnMYB4a, a R2R3 transcription factor, modulates coumarin biosynthesis during melanization in the culms of Phyllostachys nigra
articles.abstract: Conceptual model describing the role of PnMYB4a in regulating coumarin accumulation and promoting melanization in Phyllostachys nigra culms. Summary Culm colour is one of the primary traits determining the ornamental value of bamboos. The black pigment shown to accumulate in Phyllostachys nigra was previously characterized as melanin, but the underlying regulatory mechanism for its deposition remains elusive. Herein, metabolomics data show that coumarins serve as precursor substrates for melanization in P. nigra, and RNA‐seq and weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) revealed that the transcription factor PnMYB4a is integral to coumarin biosynthesis. Overexpression of PnMYB4a promotes coumarin production in both Oryza sativa and Arabidopsis thaliana. Pn4CL4‐2, a biosynthetic gene involved in coumarin biosynthesis, was identified as a direct target gene of PnMYB4a. Additionally, PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2 were found to interact with PnMYB4a both in vivo and in vitro. Both PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2 positively promoted coumarin accumulation in transgenic rice, but they repressed the expression of Pn4CL4‐2 by directly binding to W‐box elements within its promoter. Interestingly, PnMYB4a was found to alleviate the inhibitory effect on Pn4CL4‐2 by forming complexes with both PnWRKY8 and PnWRKY72‐2. Collectively, these findings revealed a PnMYB4a‐PnWRKY8/PnWRKY72‐2 regulatory module involved in the coumarin biosynthetic pathway in P. nigra and provide new insights into the mechanisms of melanization and coloration in bamboo species.

articles.title: Evidence of Galaxy Cluster Rotation and Intrahalo Gas Motions in the Cosmic Microwave Background
articles.abstract: Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background photons off rotating intracluster gas reveals a secondary anisotropy associated with the rotational kinematic Sunyaev–Zel’dovich effect.

articles.title: Far-from-Equilibrium Thermodynamics of Non-Abelian Thermal States
articles.abstract: Noncommutativity of observables is a defining feature of quantum physics. It plays a fundamental role in the formulation of the uncertainty principle for complementary variables and strongly affects the thermodynamic behavior of systems with noncommuting, that is, non-Abelian, conserved quantities. We here derive extensions of the first and second laws of thermodynamics, including nonequilibrium fluctuation relations, for driven quantum systems. We identify an additional non-Abelian contribution to the energy and entropy balances, without which these relations would be violated. This contribution can be harnessed to enhance both work extraction and nonequilibrium currents compared to what is achieved in commuting thermodynamics. These results demonstrate that noncommutativity is a potentially valuable thermodynamic resource.

articles.title: High-Performance Quantum Frequency Conversion from Ultraviolet to Telecom Band
articles.abstract: Quantum frequency conversion (QFC) is essential for bridging the spectral gap between stationary qubits and low-loss optical communication channels. Practicable QFC interfaces connecting ultraviolet and telecommunication bands are of great significance but have remained elusive, constrained by the dual challenges of a high-performance frequency converter and effective noise suppression in short-wavelength pumping configurations. We address this by demonstrating the phase-matching mechanism with domain defects and differential-tuning behavior of the spontaneous parametric down-conversion noises. Based on a quantitative analysis of performance degradation induced by domain defects, we propose specific fabrication guidelines and experimentally achieve an ultrahigh normalized conversion efficiency of $839%/(\mathrm{W}\text{ }{\mathrm{cm}}^{2})$ for the fundamental guided mode in thin-film lithium niobate waveguides. Meanwhile, we reveal a new noise control mechanism for short-wavelength pumping by utilizing the differential-tuning behaviors of difference-frequency generation and spontaneous parametric down-conversion processes. Then a single-stage QFC from 393 nm to the telecom C band with a record-high external efficiency of 28.8% and an ultralow noise level of 35 counts per second is achieved experimentally. The proposed mechanisms would enable other QFCs with higher efficiency and lower noise, advancing the development of scalable quantum networks. Furthermore, it holds significant potential for driving progress in both classical and integrated nonlinear photonics.

articles.title: Mixed-State Phases from Local Reversibility
articles.abstract: Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.

articles.title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
articles.abstract: Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.

articles.title: England’s “Babies Bill” explained: what it promises and what it needs to succeed
articles.abstract: What is the “Babies Bill”?Technically called the Infants, Parents and Carers Bill (but nicknamed the Babies Bill), this is a proposed piece of legislation to protect in law the services provided in England for infants, parents, and carers during a child’s first 1001 days.Extensive research shows that this period is critical to laying the foundations for lifelong emotional and physical wellbeing.The bill proposes that the government should have a legal duty to ensure access to services such as health visiting, midwifery checks, maternity services, infant feeding, and perinatal mental health support. It has been introduced as a private member’s bill by the Conservative MP Desmond Swayne.The bill passed its second reading in the Commons last month and faces its committee stage this week, where MPs will scrutinise the details and propose amendments. It must then face the Lords and other possible amendments before it can become law.What is the bill...

articles.title: From paediatrician to primary teacher: seeing children’s behaviour through a new lens
articles.abstract: I was an NHS paediatrician for over a decade, but it wasn’t until I left medicine and retrained as a primary schoolteacher that I realised how misaligned some of my attitudes were with the reality of children’s lives. I’d spent 15 years viewing children’s behaviour through a medical model of deficit and had completely overlooked the wider picture or what children and their families most needed from me. When children present with “challenging behaviour,” emotional distress, and difficulties attending school, doctors often see their role as making a diagnosis or needing to “fix” the problem. Healthcare professionals need to rethink our response and collaborate with parents and schools to better support the lived reality of families.As a paediatrician, I took histories from children who struggled to cope in mainstream classrooms and whose behaviour was sometimes violent or aggressive. I listened and nodded, perplexed at the mismatch between the parents’ accounts...

articles.title: Health equity in Scotland
articles.abstract: The UK is unhealthy. For healthy life expectancy, it ranks 20th out of 21 high income countries—only the US is lower.1 Within the UK, health in Scotland is worse than in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland.2 In Scotland, a steep social gradient exists: the more deprived the area, the worse people’s health.2 The gap in life expectancy between the most and the least deprived areas is 13.6 years for women and 16.3 for men.2 The gap in healthy life expectancy is even bigger.2It is worth asking what Scotland should do to achieve better health. It has progressive policies, excellent public health scholars and practitioners, collaborative planning, and a focus on community empowerment and high quality data that all have a bearing on the problems of health equity. Child poverty is lower in Scotland than in England.3 Actions such as minimum unit pricing have made a difference to Scotland’s alcohol related...

articles.title: Marmot review for Scotland sets out blueprint to reverse widening health inequalities
articles.abstract: Scotland requires a radical new approach to tackling health inequalities that includes redistributing funding to areas of greatest need, a landmark review has recommended.1The review, led by global expert in health inequalities Michael Marmot, says that Scotland’s efforts to reduce its widening health gap are being undermined by “structural inequalities” in power, money, and resources, which shape the conditions in which people live such as their income, housing, work, and communities.The report, A Fairer, Healthier Scotland, is based on work carried out over the past two years by the University College London Institute of Health Equity, led by Marmot, and Public Health Scotland, under the umbrella of the Collaboration for Health Equity in Scotland.It explored why Scotland’s relatively progressive policies and strong ambition for health equity have not delivered better health for everyone. There is now a life expectancy difference of 13.6 years in females and 16.3 years in males...

articles.title: Plague: Russian authorities must show “full transparency” over lab worker’s death, World Medical Association says
articles.abstract: The World Medical Association (WMA) has called on Russian authorities to share “all available information” about the death of a laboratory technician who worked at a plague research institute, saying the country’s lack of transparency is “of great concern.”1Darya Shipilova, who worked at the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute in the Siberia region of Russia, died on 2 October, two days after being admitted to hospital for severe pneumonia and placed on a ventilator.2Russian officials initially avoided publicly referring to plague. But Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighbouring republic of Buryatia, said that the woman may have died from an unspecified form of plague.3The World Health Organization (WHO) has described the lab worker’s cause of death as “pneumonia of undetermined aetiology” and said that Russia has informed the agency that “no case of plague had been registered recently in Irkutsk Oblast.”4Russia has also said that laboratory testing of contacts has detected...

articles.title: UN adopts political declaration on pandemic preparedness—but without crucial consensus
articles.abstract: A hotly contested political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response has been adopted by the UN.But officials have failed to agree on a fundamental part of the accord that would outline how the benefits from products created using shared pathogen data should be distributed.The text of the declaration was expected to be approved by consensus at a high level meeting on 25 September. But despite months of negotiations members were unable to agree on the terms of the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) annex.Without the PABS annex being adopted the accord as whole cannot be fully formalised and is not legally binding.Talks on the annex have stalled amid a stand-off between developing countries and some high income European nations together with the United States. During negotiations, coalitions representing low and middle income countries in Africa, Latin America, and Asia said that they had shared virus samples and data...

articles.title: [Correspondence] Prioritising the future of youth is an urgent political choice
articles.abstract: Health professionals and policy makers should fully support the students currently protesting in France.1 Apart from the regrettable outbursts of violence happening during protests, this movement reflects the anger of youth at decades of successive policies, both at national and global levels, which have progressively widened educational inequalities. These educational inequalities have led to a cascade of further inequalities: access to employment and type of employment (manual or office-based); level of income—in the past 20 years, the Gini index in France increased from 0·27 to 0·30;2 living conditions and the environment (quality of food, water, noise, air, etc); and, eventually, health inequities.

articles.title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability
Emerging landscape of antibody–drug conjugates in lung cancer: a clinical review
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.

articles.title: A Parameter-Free Reference Hamiltonian for Tight-Binding Vanadium Oxides
articles.abstract: Density-functional tight binding has yet to yield a transferable description of vanadium oxides; for the standard second-order construction and the tested cells, we demonstrate that two of its approximations deviate by electron volts and offset each other in the band-index centroid separation between the V 3d and O 2p bands: the neutral two-centre reference omits electron-volt environmental terms, whereas the Mulliken charge model assigns the compact V 3d shell less than half of the self-consistent potential shift observed in PBE. Instead, we build a tight-binding model where the reference Hamiltonian derives from superposed neutral atoms, the full PBE exchange-correlation potential and frozen-core orthogonality, without adjustable terms, and where the orbital-resolved charge response employs three screening factors obtained from PBE linear response and an unscreened Coulomb range. Relative to the primary PAW reference, the plane-wave Harris-Foulkes energy differences of VO2 are matched by the reference energy at fixed geometry and the stated numerical settings, with signed deviations of +2.6 meV/atom for M1 relative to rutile (an energy difference of 92 meV/atom) and +6.2 and -5.2 meV/atom under 3% volume compression and expansion; the charge response reproduces 14 of 22 fitted and 5 of 8 held-out matched PBE responses within one tolerance, and 28 of the 30 within twice the tolerance, and in rutile the fitted first-radial V 3d shift is -4.39 eV, 0.47 eV more negative than PBE's -3.92 eV, whereas the tested DFTB2 charge model gives -1.53 eV. The convexity of the spinless model at fixed geometry prevents it from spontaneously differentiating symmetry-equivalent sites under the symmetries respected by its implemented operators and sampling, so within this model such differentiation in the Magnéli phases must arise from electron-lattice coupling or an explicit spin or correlation term.

articles.title: A Transferable Machine-Learned Potential Enabling Large-Scale Copper-Carbon Simulations from Equilibrium to Extreme Conditions
articles.abstract: Cu-C materials and interfaces are central to diamond thermal management, metallization, graphene growth and carbon-coating technologies, but atomistic simulations across these applications require a potential that describes metallic Cu, diverse carbon bonding, heterogeneous Cu-C interactions and close atomic encounters. Here we develop NEP-CuC, a transferable neuroevolution potential trained on a dataset of 2,727 uniformly relabelled configurations selected from a heterogeneous Cu-C candidate pool. Disagreement within an ensemble of five independently trained models provides an internal indicator of model sensitivity. A Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark (ZBL) correction describes short-range nuclear repulsion, while a runtime D3(BJ) correction supplements dispersion-sensitive calculations. Tests on source-derived held-out and independent external datasets, together with structural, elastic, defect, interfacial, vibrational and finite-temperature transport benchmarks, establish broad but property-dependent physical fidelity across elemental Cu, diverse carbon environments and heterogeneous Cu-C configurations. Large-scale simulations of amorphous-carbon formation and orientation-dependent shock compression of Cu further test transferability under strongly non-equilibrium conditions. For Cu/diamond interfaces, the same potential describes deposition, annealing and tensile response: preparation history leaves persistent differences in interphase structure, while the mean peak nominal tensile stress at 500 K decreases from $12.35\pm0.71$ to $6.65\pm0.98$ GPa as the incident Cu energy during the initial deposition stage increases from 1 to 50 eV. NEP-CuC provides an atomistic framework for linking processing, interfacial structure and physical response across Cu-C systems, with direct relevance to Cu/diamond thermal-management interfaces, diamond metallization and non-equilibrium Cu-C processing.

articles.title: A basis-set-free reference for the exact exchange-energy density and functional development
articles.abstract: The exact local exchange-energy density, obtained from the Slater potential of the Hartree-Fock exchange hole, is a central ingredient of Becke's B05 and B13 functionals and of many other local hybrids. It is usually evaluated in a Gaussian basis, so the local quantity retains a pointwise basis-set incompleteness error. We describe here a basis-set-free numerical code that solves the Kohn-Sham problem on real-space grids for atoms, diatomics, and polyatomics, and returns the exact local exchange-energy density together with the density, its derivatives, the kinetic-energy density, and the reverse Becke-Roussel hole quantities. Reconstructed from the published record of Becke's non-public NUMOL code, AXEL reproduces numerical atomic references through krypton, scalar-relativistic uranium orbital energies, and Becke's diatomic spectroscopic constants. We then extend the original local-density numerical framework to generalized-gradient and hybrid functionals. Comparisons with the independent adaptive-multiwavelet code MRChem give sub-millihartree agreement for Hartree-Fock and PBE0. The same calculations agree with large Gaussian-basis references to a similar level of accuracy. Atom-centred eXact Electronic Limit (AXEL) is intended as both a basis-set-free numerical reference and a platform for exchange-hole-based density-functional development.

articles.title: A grand potential for molten-salt electrochemical phase diagrams from first principles
articles.abstract: The clean-energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for metals, whose extraction is among the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions. Molten-salt electrolysis offers a path toward carbon-free production of aluminum, iron, titanium, and critical metals. However, corrosive operating conditions and complex, multicomponent feedstocks make experimental development costly and challenging. Here, we introduce a first-principles framework for constructing electrochemical phase diagrams of multicomponent systems to accelerate electrode and electrolyte design and guide the selection of compatible materials and operating conditions for electrochemical cells. We derive a grand potential that generates these diagrams at scale, and supply free energies using first-principles data obtained through a fine-tuned foundation machine-learned interatomic potential. For silicon in molten CaCl$_2$, the construction not only recovers the experimental diagram when using the first-principles framework on a limited set of structures, but also predicts further domains when extended to a larger set of crystal structures. Finally, we demonstrate the predictive power of the approach by screening ten alkali and alkaline-earth halide electrolytes for aluminum electrowinning. Three thermodynamic criteria identify NaF, where cryolite emerges as the stable aluminum-bearing phase, recovering the chemistry that Hall and Héroult established empirically in 1886. The framework provides a first-principles basis for selecting compatible electrodes, electrolytes, and operating conditions toward low-carbon metal production from complex source materials.

articles.title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
articles.abstract: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

articles.title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?
articles.abstract: Although machine learning potentials (MLPs) generalize across configurational and chemical compound spaces, their accuracy is commonly believed to be limited by their training methods, with improvements beyond this limit achieved so far only by refitting to experimental observables. In this Perspective, we argue that MLPs can also be made more accurate than their training methods non-empirically by generalizing across a third space, that of quantum-chemical methods. We propose routes to method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods, with working implementations in both density-functional and wavefunction-based theories showing that they can be more accurate than any of their training methods. Aiming beyond the accuracy of the training methods could also make universal MLPs more accurate than single-method models, even when the method-transferable MLPs remain less accurate than those QM methods. Method-transferable MLPs will shape the construction of training datasets and the evaluation of models, pushing the accuracy limits of chemical simulations.

articles.title: Collision inside an atom: quantum ion-atom dynamics
articles.abstract: Rydberg atoms occupy a central role in quantum science; their loosely bound outer electron gives rise to properties that enable quantum information processing1 or the formation of exotic molecular bonds2. Beyond these roles, they have been proposed as a neutral platform for the observation of quantum effects in collisions and reactions of the ionic core with neutral particles3, 4, a long-standing goal of ion-based chemistry and physics. However, all of the experimental results so far could be explained using a classical description of the internuclear motion5. Here we demonstrate cold collisions inside a Rydberg helium atom, achieved by merging helium Rydberg and ground-state helium beams and imaging individual scattering events. We resolve the fully quantum-coherent motion and observe matter-wave diffraction and tunnelling-driven shape resonances down to collision energies of 90 mK. In the case of identical helium nuclei, we demonstrate a new regime of identical-particle Mott interference6, where quantum statistics begin to govern the total scattering cross section. For distinct isotopes, we show the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and benchmark parameter-free, state-of-the-art theory. We directly measure the helium isotope ionization-energy difference to be 15.0 +/- 0.1 K. Our experiments establish Rydberg atoms as a platform for the direct observation of quantum dynamics with a general class of ions, atoms and molecules.

articles.title: Development of a Minimal Auxiliary Basis for the Particle--Particle Random Phase Approximation (ppRPA): Accelerating Excited-State Calculations in Diradical Nanoparticles and Periodic Systems
articles.abstract: Singlet--triplet gaps set the energy scale of the two-spin manifold in molecular quantum information materials, and such systems frequently carry diradical character: metal nanoclusters, metal--organic frameworks with radical linkers, and the nitrogen--vacancy center in diamond. Time-dependent density functional theory is the standard tool at this size but describes multireference systems poorly. A closed-shell reference is inadequate for a multiconfigurational ground state, and the adiabatic kernel excludes doubly excited configurations. The particle--particle random phase approximation (\pprpa{}) changes the particle number rather than the spin. Singlet and triplet states descend from one closed-shell reference, and double excitations enter on the same footing as single ones. Computational cost has confined \pprpa{} to small systems, and the two-electron integrals that drive it are factorized through an auxiliary basis. We develop \pprpa{}--as, which reduces that basis to a minimal set of atom-centered Gaussian shells whose exponents follow from free-atom radii and one global scaling factor. The approximation enters only the excited-state step, so both calculations proceed from the same self-consistent reference. We test molecules and clusters of up to 286 atoms, including heavy elements, and seven point defects in four periodic hosts, obtaining both multiplicities and their splitting without symmetry breaking or spin projection. We optimize the scaling factor and give guidance on choosing it. An order-of-magnitude smaller auxiliary basis delivers a speed-up of up to eightfold while staying within $0.03$~eV of conventional \pprpa{}, bringing diradical nanoclusters and periodic systems within reach.

articles.title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
articles.abstract: Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly little chemistry beyond what classical molecular features already capture.

articles.title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
articles.abstract: Solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion offers a compelling route to harvest sub-bandgap photons to increase the efficiency of photovoltaics, but low sensitizer doping required to suppress non-radiative aggregation quenching severely restricts light absorption. Here, we present a dual-resonator planar silver microcavity housing a thermally co-evaporated rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer designed to simultaneously enhance triplet-sensitizer absorption and out-couple upconverted emission. By aligning a dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at $32^\circ$, we achieve a 12-fold enhancement in absorptance at 665 nm. This absorption boost, combined with directional outcoupling through a second cavity mode, outweighs cavity-induced reabsorption losses to yield a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission. Overall, this work highlights the potential of microcavity integration to substantially enhance solid-state upconversion performance across low-intensity optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Embossing of Tapered, Isometric Micro-Interdigitated Flow Fields for Enhanced Desalination by Faradaic Deionization
articles.abstract: Engineered transport architectures can improve electrolyte distribution and active-material utilization in porous electrodes, yet their implementation remains limited by fabrication methods that compromise precision, throughput, active-material preservation, or scalability. Here, an integrated embossing-calendering method is introduced to pattern Prussian blue analog (PBA) porous electrodes with embedded, micro-interdigitated flow fields (e$μ$-IDFFs) for electrochemical desalination. This non-subtractive, roll-to-roll compatible method forms channels by controlling plastic deformation while simultaneously calendering the electrode, preserving active material and reducing patterning time by 100-fold relative to mechanical milling. Indentation experiments and a closed-form model further show that embossing requires 15-fold less force than stamping, while electrode microstructures show local densification beneath embossed channels. PBA electrodes are embossed with novel e$μ$-IDFFs that use continuous width-tapering with isometric flow paths that promote uniform electrolyte distribution, increase rate capability, and reduce polarization. Compared with e$μ$-IDFFs patterned using less scalable means and non-isometric flow paths, these e$μ$-IDFFs desalinate seawater-salinity feeds near to potable levels with 1.5-fold of its thermodynamic energy efficiency and water recovery. Brackish desalination benefits similarly. Tapered, isometric e$μ$-IDFFs and the embossing method introduced to pattern them are readily translated other electrochemical energy storage and separations systems.

articles.title: Ensuring Complete Consistency between Hops and Wavefunction Propagation in Fewest-Switches Surface Hopping
articles.abstract: Fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) is a popular and versatile approach for performing dynamical simulations beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, in which nonadiabatic effects are incorporated through stochastic hops of the active potential energy surface. However, the FSSH algorithm does not ensure that hops are completely consistent with the underlying electronic wavefunction dynamics. This can lead to significant errors as well as requiring small propagation time steps, which can significantly compromise the computational efficiency of the method. These problems are known to be particularly severe at so-called trivial crossings, for which the nonadiabatic coupling is entirely localized at the crossing point. Here, we solve the trivial-crossing problem by developing a fully-consistent hopping-probability formula, which generates attempted hops that match the time-evolution of the wavefunction across any size time step by construction. A state-tracking algorithm is also utilized to ensure that attempted hops are always accepted at trivial crossings. Through application to systems that contain extremely challenging trivial crossings, we demonstrate that this hopping scheme is capable of obtaining highly accurate results, even when large propagation time steps are used.

articles.title: Extending the mean first-passage-time formalism to the reconstruction of high free-energy barriers: A top-start approach
articles.abstract: Rare events, such as crystal nucleation in mildly supercooled liquids, are characterized by waiting times that can be much longer than the timescale of the underlying microscopic dynamics. The mean first-passage time (MFPT) formalism [J. Wedekind and D. Reguera, J. Phys. Chem. B 112, 11060 (2008)] provides a route to reconstruct one-dimensional free-energy profiles from the MFPT and steady-state distribution measured along a reaction coordinate, but conventional implementations become inefficient for sufficiently high barriers because spontaneous crossings are rarely observed. We introduce a "top-start" extension that initiates trajectories near the barrier top and reconstructs the free-energy profile from their subsequent evolution away from the barrier toward lower-free-energy regions. We establish the equivalence between the top-start and two-region constructions using a Markov-chain transition-matrix formulation. We validate the method using one-dimensional random-walk simulations across low, medium, and high free-energy barriers, with transition-matrix calculations providing an exact benchmark for the corresponding discretized models. The top-start reconstruction remains accurate in the high-barrier regime where conventional MFPT sampling becomes prohibitively inefficient.

articles.title: Extrapolating Collisional Rate Coefficients for Molecules of Astrophysical Interest Using Neural Networks
articles.abstract: State-to-state rate coefficients for inelastic molecular collisions are essential inputs for non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models, yet their computation using quantum scattering methods is prohibitive for large molecules and highly excited rotational states. We investigate the ability of artificial neural networks to extend existing datasets of collisional excitation rate coefficients without performing additional scattering calculations. A multilayer perceptron model was trained using molecular quantum numbers, level energies, energy gaps, and kinetic temperature as descriptors, and optimized on logarithmic rate coefficients. The model was tested on diverse collision systems ranging from simple diatomic molecules (CO, SiO) to open-shell species (SO), small asymmetric tops (H$_2$O, SO$_2$), and complex organic molecules (benzonitrile and vinyl cyanide) colliding with H$_2$ molecules or He atoms. Extrapolations were performed toward higher rotational levels, higher temperatures, and combinations of both. For most systems, predictions of rate coefficients involving previously unseen rotational states yielded mean error factors between 1.1 and 1.5, with the dominant rate coefficients generally reproduced more accurately than weaker transitions. Temperature extrapolations proved particularly successful, while combined extrapolations in temperature and rotational levels remained accurate to within a factor of two in most cases. The prediction quality depends on the interplay between dataset size, temperature range, molecular complexity, and the presence of clear collisional propensity rules. Overall, the approach demonstrates that machine learning can provide a practical route to extending collisional datasets for astrophysical applications, especially for large molecules for which additional quantum-scattering calculations are computationally demanding.

articles.title: Gas radiation and the gravity limit of flicker in a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame
articles.abstract: Although weak at normal gravity, gas radiation sets the gravity at which a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame stops flickering. Flamelet-based simulations with unity Lewis numbers, which reproduce the flicker frequency measured by femtosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering within 4%, are combined with local stability analysis. At one tenth of normal gravity, the adiabatic flame flickers, the radiating flame does not, and switching the emission off restores flicker. Radiation acts through two mechanisms that do not weaken at reduced gravity. The hot outer layer loses buoyancy in proportion to the gas residence time, and a disturbance that displaces the flame also displaces its emission, which damps the disturbance on the lean flank (displaced-emission damping). Freezing the radiative source, which removes only its response to disturbances, slows the downstream recession of the oscillation more than tenfold. Both mechanisms slow the upstream spreading of disturbances. This spreading, competing with the co-flow, sets the onset location and the critical co-flow. Without radiation, the spreading speed scales with the square root of gravity; its radiative reduction does not. At reduced gravity, the flicker limit therefore becomes a straight line relating the square root of the co-flow Froude number to a radiation number, the ratio of buoyant to radiative time scales. The calibrated line places the critical gravity for the experimental co-flow at 0.13 times normal gravity, 2.6 times the adiabatic value. It correctly predicted whether two further flames keep flickering. Beyond the limit, transient wave packets can mimic flicker throughout a short drop-tower test.

articles.title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
articles.abstract: Living supramolecular materials such as microtubules and actin filaments assemble and function in dynamic, heterogeneous environments, subject to chemical concentration gradients. Their rapid and precise response to such gradients---via aggregation, disassembly, or autonomous motion---underlies the fine spatiotemporal control typical of living systems. Reproducing such responsiveness in synthetic materials is a central challenge in materials science and requires a molecular-level understanding of how gradients couple to supramolecular structure and dynamics, which remains difficult to access experimentally. To this end, we combine implicit-solvent coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) with the constant chemical potential MD (C$μ$MD) technique to investigate, at molecular resolution, the coupling of two prototypical supramolecular polymer models with externally imposed ionic concentration gradients. Despite their contrasting responses to homogeneous ionic conditions, both systems undergo pronounced spatial reorganization under the gradient, generating regions of locally enhanced supramolecular activity that are inaccessible to homogeneous systems with the same overall content of self-assembling species. Crucially, the local supramolecular dynamics is largely determined by the local concentrations, consistent with the formation of local quasi-equilibria: this direct connection between spatial composition and supramolecular activity emerges as a common governing principle across the two models. These findings shed light on the spatially complex supramolecular response that can be triggered by chemical gradients, and show how a single gradient simulation can encode this response across a continuous range of local chemical environments, thus providing a general strategy to investigate and design materials operating under spatially heterogeneous conditions.

articles.title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
articles.abstract: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

articles.title: Organisation and aggregation of calcium carbonate ions in water via molecular simulation
articles.abstract: Crystallisation of calcium carbonate (CaCO$_3$) in aqueous solutions is essential for carbon dioxide sequestration and the sustainable production of calcium carbonate materials, which are widely used in industry and increasingly explored for novel applications. While crystallisation is often analysed within the framework of classical nucleation theory, CaCO$_3$ and other ionic crystals often form through amorphous precursor phases, motivating the need for alternative descriptions. In this work, we investigate the relationship between the formation of the first CaCO$_3$ coordination sphere, a fundamental unit of local ordering, and ionic aggregation using two complementary simulation approaches: on-the-fly probability-enhanced sampling (OPES) and asynchronous and infinite-swap replica exchange transition interface sampling ($\infty$RETIS). OPES was used to explore free-energy landscapes, whereas $\infty$RETIS was used to determine reaction kinetics. We studied systems at two levels of supersaturation, between which the formation of the first coordination sphere exhibited distinct kinetic behaviour. These differences were found to be linked to concentration-dependent ionic aggregation. At lower concentration, aggregation remains limited, whereas higher concentration promotes extensive spinodal-like aggregation. For both concentrations, the first coordination sphere forms within the pre-formed clusters through one of two distinct pathways: either within a cluster close to the minimum size required for its formation, or within larger amorphous aggregates whose size and structure depend on concentration. The coexistence of these pathways at both levels of supersaturation reveals the multifaceted nature of early-stage CaCO$_3$ crystallisation and highlights the importance of differentiating ionic aggregation and organisation.

articles.title: PairIT: Autoregressive Transformers for Low-Data Molecule Optimization
articles.abstract: Generating novel molecules with desired properties is a central challenge in drug discovery. Although foundational work focused on de novo generation, practical use cases require a more complex setting: conditioning on an initial seed molecule, optimizing multiple properties, and operating in data-sparse regimes. We introduce PairIT, a flexible training framework for autoregressive transformers over SMILES sequences that enables seeded generation by learning from pairs of structurally similar molecules. By leveraging matched pairs, the model learns to generate local, chemically meaningful edits that improve a property of the seed molecule. Prompt tokens extend this framework by specifying the target property, desired direction, and approximate magnitude of change. Multiple prompt tokens can be concatenated to enable multi-property optimization at inference time. For properties where pair supervision alone is insufficient, reinforcement learning post-training can further improve optimization, providing a tunable trade-off between proximity to the seed and the optimization objective. PairIT naturally supports pretraining on a large dataset and fine-tuning on a smaller dataset, which is critical for performance in data-sparse regimes. Surprisingly, we observe diminishing returns to the scale of the pretraining dataset. We demonstrate empirically on MoleculeNet and Therapeutics Data Commons datasets that, with appropriate paired-data curation, a standard transformer model of modest size (68M parameters) can achieve robust seeded molecular optimization in low-data regimes.

articles.title: Photoinduced Modulation of Rectification and Charge Transport in Diarylethene-Viologen Molecular Junction
articles.abstract: Large-area molecular junctions combining photochromic and redox-active functionalities provide an attractive platform for controlling charge transport by light. In this work, we study Au/DAEVIO/Ti/Au molecular junctions incorporated with electro-grafted layers of diarylethene-viologen with thicknesses of 12-16 nm. In the initial OFF state, the junctions exhibit low current densities and strong rectification, with a rectification ratio of 300 at 1V. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal a thermally assisted contribution at higher temperatures and a much weaker temperature dependence below 160-180K, consistent with multistep charge transport through molecular and/or interfacial states rather than direct coherent tunneling across the entire molecular layer. Under continuous in situ 385 nm irradiation, the electrical response is strongly and asymmetrically modified. The current density at +1V increases by a factor of 200, while the negative-bias current is only weakly modified, reducing the rectification ratio from 300 to 2. Illumination also produces a nonzero short-circuit current density of + 0.006mA cm-2 and an open-circuit voltage of -0.45V. These results indicate that irradiation simultaneously modifies molecular charge transport and generates a measurable photoelectric response. This behavior is consistent with light-induced changes in electronic coupling associated with DAE photocyclization, combined with photoinduced charge generation and field-dependent charge separation involving the redox-active viologen units and asymmetric electrode interfaces.

articles.title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
articles.abstract: Circuit depth and measurement count are the main limitations for chemical applications of the leading variational quantum algorithms on quantum computers. We show that both resource requirements can be reduced by augmenting adaptive variational quantum algorithms with post-optimization corrective techniques. We focus on two such techniques---Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization and the identity-augmented quantum self-consistent equation of motion (q-sc-EOM)---applied to optimized ADAPT-VQE states without further ansatz growth or nonlinear optimization. Across molecular systems studied with up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduces the optimized iterations (and the corresponding number of adaptive layers) needed to reach the $1.6~\mathrm{m}E_h$ threshold by up to approximately sixfold, with a general trend toward larger reductions at higher determinant Rényi entropy. We also find measurement-cost reductions of up to approximately fortyfold using a suitable resource-cost model. Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM improves molecular potential-energy curves obtained from truncated ADAPT-VQE ansätze with limited expressivity and recovers accuracy from states produced by sampled operator ranking without additional gradient-based operator selection, providing an advantage when small pool gradients make selection measurement intensive. Together, these post-optimization corrections offer routes to improve energy accuracy and reduce adaptive circuit growth in quantum algorithms as quantum hardware advances.

articles.title: QUPEX: A Streamlit-Based Framework for Visualizing Quantum-Mechanical Property Spaces of Organic Molecules
articles.abstract: The growing availability of quantum-mechanical (QM) datasets offers new opportunities to investigate structure-property and property-property relationships in drug-like molecules using data-driven methods. However, interactive tools that integrate molecular visualization, statistical analysis of QM properties, clustering, and machine learning (ML) remain limited, despite their value in facilitating dataset exploration and interpretation. To address this gap, we introduce QUPEX (QUantum Property EXplorer), an open-source Streamlit-based framework for the interactive exploration of QM property spaces in molecular systems. As a demonstration, we apply QUPEX to a subset of the QM7-X dataset comprising 41,537 equilibrium molecular structures containing up to seven non-hydrogen atoms (C, N, O, S, and Cl) and their 24 associated QM properties. In addition to property-space analysis, QUPEX incorporates an XGBoost regression pipeline for predicting PBE0 dipole moments from tight-binding-derived electronic descriptors, together with model evaluation and SHAP-based interpretability functionality. By combining interactive molecular visualization, data analysis, and predictive modeling, QUPEX provides an accessible and extensible environment for investigating molecular datasets and identifying patterns in their structural and electronic properties. These capabilities can support the exploration of chemical space and inform the rational design of drug-like molecules with targeted QM properties.

articles.title: WannierSTM: Efficient superconducting scanning-probe spectroscopy from maximally localized Wannier functions
articles.abstract: We present a Python-based program that combines maximally localized Wannier functions-based first-principles electronic structure with the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism to enable efficient simulations of scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The workflow builds upon standard density functional theory packages to construct compact transport Hamiltonians that preserve the properties of realistic materials. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential within the Nambu-spinor formalism, while coupling to the STM tip and substrate electrodes is treated using the wide-band limit approximation. Within this formulation, transport quantities such as current-voltage characteristics and differential conductance are evaluated in a closed analytical form. This avoids explicit numerical energy integrations and enables rapid spectroscopic calculations over broad parameter spaces. The framework provides a unified and computationally efficient approach for modeling superconducting hybrid nanostructures with spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization. Representative applications in spin chains, two-dimensional and molecular magnets on a superconductor demonstrate its robust capabilities for both simple model systems and realistic ab initio molecular structures relevant to modern STM experiments.

articles.title: A framework for analyzing global Caenorhabditis elegans neural activity
articles.abstract: Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose. We first classified active neurons into six functional clusters: two sensory neuron clusters (ON and OFF responding to addition and removal of stimuli, respectively) and four motor/command neuron clusters (AVA, RME, SMDD, and SMDV). Next, we estimated stimulus selectivity for each cluster and found that while sensory neurons exhibit their maximal responses within 15 s, changes in bacterial stimuli drive maximal responses in command and motor neuron clusters after tens of seconds. Furthermore, we show that bacterial stimuli induce neural dynamics that are best described by a hyperbolic, not Euclidean, space indicating hierarchical organization in C. elegans neural population dynamics. This space was 8-dimensional, with dimensions that aligned in one sensory direction (ON and OFF neurons), two motor directions (forward-backward and dorsal-ventral), and the rest of dimensions corresponding with unclassified neurons. Collectively, we show that C. elegans neural activity can be effectively represented in low-dimensional hyperbolic space and describe how sensory information is processed by the neural network.

articles.title: Allosteric disulfide control of ligand binding and endocytosis of KIR2DL4, the natural killer cell receptor for HLA-G
articles.abstract: Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA)-G is selectively expressed by fetal trophoblast cells that encounter maternal natural killer (NK) cells early in pregnancy. In response to HLA-G, the endosomal NK cell receptor KIR2DL4 induces a transcriptional program to support placental development. Structural features of KIR2DL4 that control HLA-G binding and endocytosis are unclear. Random mutagenesis revealed that three cysteines in the first immunoglobulin domain of KIR2DL4 regulate endocytosis and uptake of HLA-G. The atypical Cys10–Cys28 disulfide bond in the KIR2DL4 structure is an allosteric disulfide with potential to switch to a conventional Cys28–Cys74 bond. KIR2DL4 in human cells exists in both disulfide-bonded states, as shown by mass spectrometry analysis. The Cys10–Cys28 bond in a Cys74Ser KIR2DL4 mutant was reduced by protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) in vitro. Inhibition of PDI prevented HLA-G uptake by KIR2DL4 in NK cells. Mutants in the Cys10–Cys28 configuration endocytosed spontaneously but did not bind HLA-G. Conversely, KIR2DL4 with a Cys28–Cys74 bond was detectable at the plasma membrane and internalized soluble HLA-G. A purified Cys10Leu KIR2DL4 mutant bound HLA-G with micromolar affinity in a peptide-dependent manner. Thus, allosteric disulfide-mediated conversion from an inactive to an HLA-G binding form regulates KIR2DL4 trafficking and a functional response that promotes fetal development.

articles.title: Anatomy and mechanics of tsetse fly blood feeding
articles.abstract: Human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) is a neglected tropical disease transmitted by infected tsetse flies (Glossina spp.) in sub-Saharan Africa. Infected tsetse flies can transmit trypanosomes, including Trypanosoma brucei subspecies that cause HAT in humans, as well as other trypanosome species that cause animal African trypanosomiasis in domestic animals and infect wildlife. Tsetse flies feed on a broad spectrum of hosts, including humans, elephants, buffaloes, rhinos, hippos, turtles, and monitor lizards. To understand how the insects can penetrate such diverse skin types, we detailed the anatomical structures involved in tsetse blood feeding, their mechanical properties, and the forces exerted by the fly during probing. We found that the tsetse fly’s feeding apparatus does not rely on exceptionally unique structures or extraordinary forces. Instead, the tsetse fly has evolved subtle yet highly efficient adaptations, which include a labellum equipped with arrays of small teeth. When combined with a robust retraction movement of the proboscis, these structures create lesions on various types of skin, thus facilitating blood pool feeding on a broad host spectrum.

articles.title: Designing optimal perturbation inputs for system identification in neuroscience
articles.abstract: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms, such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.

articles.title: Endosome-associated Rab GTPases control distinct aspects of neural circuit assembly
articles.abstract: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.

articles.title: Gluconeogenic compensation renders glycogen phosphorylase non-essential as an insecticidal target in Plutella xylostella
articles.abstract: Glycogen phosphorylase (GP) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of glycogenolysis and supplies precursors for chitin biosynthesis in insects. Acyl urea compounds structurally related to benzoylphenylurea (BPU) insecticides are potent inhibitors of mammalian GP, raising the question of whether insect GP could serve as an independent insecticidal target. Here, we show that a mammalian GP inhibitor (GPI) potently inhibits recombinant Plutella xylostella GP (PxGP; IC50=2.96 nM), while the BPU insecticide diflubenzuron does not. Molecular docking and MM/GBSA analysis predict that this selectivity reflects differential side-chain engagement. Despite potent in vitro inhibition, GPI exhibits no insecticidal activity, and RNAi-mediated knockdown of PxGP does not impair development or survival. We provide evidence that insects compensate through upregulation of gluconeogenic enzymes (PEPCK, G-6-Pase) and protein catabolism, with enzyme activity measurements confirming ~29% reduction in GP-a activity following RNAi. Fitness assessment reveals transient larval weight loss with complete recovery of pupal weight, adult morphology, and fecundity. These findings demonstrate that GP is functionally non-essential under the tested conditions, likely through gluconeogenic compensation and alternative carbon sources, and highlight the importance of metabolic network redundancy in target-based insecticide design.

articles.title: JAK-STAT pathway heterogeneity governs immunotherapy response in breast cancer
articles.abstract: The JAK-STAT pathway (JSP) is a well-known oncogenic cascade; however, recent clinical trials have detected JSP upregulation in breast cancer following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. This paradoxical observation warrants further investigation into JSP’s intercellular heterogeneity, tumor dynamics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications for immunotherapy. JSP expression showed dynamic shifts during breast cancer progression, with higher levels in T cells and paracancerous epithelial cells. In human breast cancer tumor cells, elevated JSP is highly correlated with malignant phenotypes. JSP-high tumor cells overexpressed oncogenic pathways, while exhibiting increased immunosuppressive signaling via the MIF-CD74 signaling axis. In T cells, higher JSP levels were associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved differentiation, and reduced exhaustion, reflecting robust anti-tumor immunity. Analysis of immunotherapy datasets revealed that higher JSP levels were associated with improved responses toward PD-1 inhibitors, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients, with JSP serving as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy sensitivity. As a key JSP component, STAT4 exerts dual roles in breast cancer: it drives tumorigenesis in malignant cells, sustains breast epithelial cell proliferation, and bolsters T-cell anti-tumor functionality, while also acting as a highly accurate biomarker for predicting immunotherapy response. This indicates that JSP targeting demands a nuanced approach: broad inhibition may impair anti-tumor immunity, and optimized therapeutic strategies paired with precise biomarkers are critical to maximize JSP’s utility in breast cancer immunotherapy. Our findings highlight JSP’s functional heterogeneity in epithelial, tumor, and T cells, with high JSP activity correlating with enhanced immunotherapy efficacy in breast cancer.

articles.title: Reduced dorsal CA1 activity limits retention of the temporal component of declarative memory in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism
articles.abstract: Growing evidence implicates the hippocampus in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder, particularly in the domains of social interactions and cognition. Yet, the mechanisms driving the hippocampal-dependent cognitive atypicalities in autism remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized how dysfunction of the CA1 subfield of the dorsal hippocampus drives abnormalities in critical components of declarative memory. Using trace fear conditioning in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism, we found that capabilities to retain the association of temporally distant stimuli (i.e. temporal binding) were reduced relative to wildtype mice. Fiber photometry and optogenetic experiments demonstrated that reduced CA1 activity during temporal gaps underlies this impairment, linking CA1 dysfunction to a deficit in long-term memory retention in autism. Using a relational/declarative memory task, we also revealed a deficit in flexible spatial memory, and a preferential use of egocentric learning strategy. This inflexible learning strategy resulted from an imbalance between memory system activity, promoting frontostriatal-dependent procedural learning instead of dorsal CA1/hippocampus-dependent relational/declarative memory. Overall, this study establishes dorsal CA1 dysfunction as a circuit-level mechanism underlying cognitive inflexibility in autism, providing a neurobiological framework for hippocampal-dependent memory deficits in the condition.

articles.title: Cation-Gated Interfacial Electrocatalysis: Mechanisms and Effects of Alkali and Alkaline Earth Metal Cations
articles.abstract: Electrolyte cations, long considered inert charge-balancing species, are now recognized as active regulators of electrocatalytic interfaces.
