Time to hang up the stethoscope?
Ground‐penetrating radar amplitudes to roots: A numerical modelling framework for mapping coarse root system architecture
articles.abstract: Observations of three‐dimensional (3D) coarse root system architecture remain limited because most measurement approaches require excavation. Here, we combined dense single‐ and multi‐channel 500 MHz ground‐penetrating radar (GPR) surveys with a flow‐guided connectivity framework to non‐destructively characterise the coarse root architecture of two trees. Migrated and depth‐normalised GPR amplitudes were treated as spatially variable hydraulic conductivities in a steady‐state numerical model. The resulting connectivity fields transformed spatially discontinuous, collapsed diffraction hyperbolae into continuous 3D representations of root architecture extending 10–15 m from the trunk. We applied this approach to a swamp oak (Quercus palustris) and a river red gum (Eucalyptus camaldulensis). The two trees were surveyed under different environmental conditions and acquisition parameters. The reconstructed architectures revealed shallow, laterally extensive coarse root systems and captured substantial variation in root structure between the two trees. The oak roots exhibited an asymmetrical architecture with preferential development towards the upslope, wind‐exposed side of the tree, whereas the river red gum displayed a more radially distributed root architecture with deeper roots near the trunk. Approximately 80% of reconstructed roots for both trees occurred within 6.2 m of the trunk and above 60 cm depth. Together, these results demonstrate that dense GPR surveys, coupled with connectivity‐based modelling, provide a non‐destructive and repeatable approach for characterising coarse root architecture.

articles.title: UNIQAT: An open‐source toolkit for reproducible image quality assessment in marine surveys
articles.abstract: Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. Manual quality screening is labour-intensive, subjective and inconsistent across observers and teams, hindering reproducible science, creating large backlogs of unprocessed imagery, and limiting real-time algorithmic and robotic applications. We present UNIQAT (UNderwater Image Quality Assessment Toolkit), an open-source Python toolkit for automated underwater image quality assessment. The toolkit computes reference-free quality metrics across nine categories of image characteristics relevant to underwater images, such as colour cast, turbidity and contrast loss. Metrics can be combined with user-defined weights into task-specific quality scores tailored to different ecological applications. High-performance computing (HPC)-aware multiprocessing and optional deep learning architectures for metric approximation support processing at scales matching modern survey data collection. We evaluated UNIQAT on 130,845 images from nine coral reef surveys conducted by the Australian Institute of Marine Science; every result reported in the main text was produced by the traditional metrics pipeline, with no deep learning model involved, and a separate training demonstration is reported in the Supporting Information. The traditional metrics pipeline, run as 48 CPU workers on a 64-core cluster node, processed 7.9 4K-images/s, with processing time scaling linearly with image count (r 2 = 0.98). The resulting quality scores captured expected patterns of image modulation based on the environmental context of the imaged scenes: All nine surveys showed negative depth–quality correlations (r = −0.16 to −0.89), consistent with the depth-dependent deterioration of image quality in underwater environments. Cross-survey metric profiles were highly consistent (mean Spearman ρ = 0.99 across all 36 pairwise comparisons, minimum 0.96), confirming measurement stability across different dates, locations, camera systems and environmental conditions. Synthesis. UNIQAT can help deliver objective and tunable image quality metrics in a versatile toolkit that enables transparent reporting and supports unsupervised quality assessment for applications in marine monitoring and robotics.

articles.title: A CK2-β-TrCP kinase-E3 ubiquitin ligase cascade is a metabolic sensor regulating tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase stability
articles.abstract: How metabolic enzyme levels are regulated is poorly understood. Studying the tryptophan (Trp)-metabolizing enzyme TDO2, Thielen et al. discover a CK2 kinase-β-TrCP E3 ligase pathway that regulates stability in response to substrate availability. Trp occupation of an exosite restricts degron accessibility, whereas low Trp releases the degron for phosphorylation-ubiquitylation-mediated degradation.

articles.title: PHYHD1-mediated translational control regulates renal cell carcinoma progression
articles.abstract: Liang et al. identify phytanoyl-CoA dioxygenase domain containing 1 (PHYHD1) as a tumor suppressor that regulates protein production in kidney cancer. Loss of PHYHD1 promotes disease progression by increasing ceramide transporter 1 (CERT1) production, uncovering a regulatory pathway that may help predict patient outcomes and provide a therapeutic opportunity for PHYHD1-deficient tumors.

articles.title: Advancing Marine Mammal Conservation Through Omics Tools and Integration of Indigenous Ecological Knowledge
articles.abstract: Conservation of biodiversity is a global priority as human‐driven pressures continue to intensify and alter ecosystems worldwide. Marine mammals are vulnerable species, facing numerous escalating anthropogenic threats. Here, we evaluate how, as omics technologies become more accessible and affordable, established and emerging tools are advancing effective marine mammal research and conservation management. Assessments of genetic diversity, adaptive capacity, demographic history and local adaptation provide vital insights into how marine mammal populations respond to environmental change across contemporary and evolutionary timescales. Whole‐genome sequencing, functional genomics, epigenetics and multi‐omic integration enable deeper insights into the molecular basis of complex fitness‐related traits. Approaches like epigenetics, ancient DNA and environmental DNA offer new opportunities to study cryptic, rare, or historical populations and evolutionary processes. Yet, effective marine mammal conservation management cannot rely exclusively on increased availability of omics tools and data. We emphasize the need and obligation for genuine collaboration and integration of Indigenous perspectives with marine mammal genomics approaches to foster ethical, inclusive and effective conservation, and suggest best practices for this. Additionally, we highlight that translating omics data into practical conservation outcomes remains challenging, requiring clear communication, collaboration and integration into management. Using marine mammal genomics to address conservation challenges in a changing world requires innovation, partnership and the integration of diverse knowledge systems, such as Indigenous Ecological Knowledge.

articles.title: Chilling Injury to Algal Symbionts Induces Host Starvation and Metabolic Reorganization in a Temperate Cnidarian
articles.abstract: Global temperature anomalies increasingly disrupt the cnidarian‐algal symbiosis resulting in a phenomenon termed bleaching. In contrast to heat stress, the mechanisms underlying symbiotic breakdown under cold stress remain largely unknown. Combining physiological and metabolomic measurements, we investigated the response of the photosymbiotic sea anemone holobiont Aiptasia couchii to an experiment mimicking a cold spell in the Mediterranean Sea. Within 4 weeks, we observed the onset of symbiotic breakdown reflected in reduced algal endosymbiont density and chlorophyll a content. While photosynthetic efficiency remained largely unaffected, no gross photosynthesis was detectable in cold‐stressed anemones and decreases in glycosyldiacylglycerols and fatty acyl glycosides indicated chloroplast lipid remobilization. This breakdown of symbiotic carbon cycling was reflected in increased dipeptide and ceramide levels suggesting anemones catabolized protein reserves and induced pre‐apoptotic pathways. Taken together, these responses suggest a decoupling of light and dark reactions of photosynthesis in cold‐stressed endosymbionts, resembling chilling injury in higher plants and free‐living microalgae. This chilling‐induced collapse of symbiotic nutrient cycling eventually leads to host starvation in cold‐stressed Cnidaria. Hence, while cold and heat stress may invoke contrasting physiological effects on endosymbionts, our results suggest that both stressors destabilize the symbiosis through similar mechanisms culminating in host starvation.

articles.title: Host‐Associated Differentiation in a Parasitoid Wasp Connected to Venom‐Related but Not Chemosensory Genes
articles.abstract: The mechanisms driving the megadiversity of parasitic wasps remain a central question in evolutionary ecology. To investigate the genomic architecture underlying host‐associated differentiation in parasitic wasps, we generated a de novo genome assembly and performed whole‐genome re‐sequencing of 17 populations of the parasitoid wasp Asecodes parviclava (Eulophidae) across a latitudinal gradient and multiple Galerucella host species. Despite panmixia in host populations, we identified three genetically differentiated wasp lineages, with the most profound divergence separating Galerucella tenella‐associated wasps from other populations. Locus‐specific scans revealed that selection acts highly asymmetrically. We detected significant differentiation and copy‐number expansion clustered within venom‐related gene families, contrasting sharply with a near‐complete lack of divergence in chemosensory genes. This decoupled evolution suggests that host finding may rely on behavioural plasticity, whereas physiological compatibility is genetically hard‐wired via multi‐layered immune‐suppression mechanisms. Finally, asymmetrical gene flow in northern populations demonstrates that fine‐scale habitat overlap creates ecological connectivity without eroding specialized lineages, as intense host‐mediated selection purges maladapted hybrids. Ultimately, our study demonstrates that physiological barriers, rather than behavioural recognition, may maintain specialized parasitoid lineages, providing new insights into the genomic basis of speciation with gene flow in specialized natural enemies.

Dimensional Engineering of Co/W Superlattices Enables Out-of-Plane Spin Polarization with 90% Field-Free Switching in Perpendicular CoFeB
articles.abstract: Deterministic spin–orbit torque (SOT) switching of perpendicular magnets without external magnetic fields remains a central challenge for scalable SOT-MRAM. Here, we demonstrate that dimensional engineering of a Co/W superlattice spin–orbit layer enables >90% field-free switching of perpendicular CoFeB. Harmonic Hall measurements reveal an unconventional out-of-plane torque, while first-principles calculations reveal reconstruction of the spin-resolved electronic structure and increased W-projected out-of-plane spin character, together supporting the modification of torque symmetry through Co/W superlattice engineering. The optimized superlattice achieves a critical current density of 23.3 MA cm–2 and a thermal stability factor Δ ≈ 45. Nanoscale devices (100 nm) preserve deterministic field-free reversal with comparable efficiency, confirming scalability toward magnetic tunnel junction integration. Micromagnetic analysis shows that out-of-plane spin-polarized torque together with canted anisotropy enables intrinsic symmetry breaking, highlighting superlattice engineering as a route to tailor torque symmetry for effective field-free SOT devices.

articles.title: Directional Manufacturing of Defect Mitigation and Large-Scale Single-Crystalline Metal Foils via Gas Flow Optimization toward Commercialization
articles.abstract: Single-crystalline metals, with their distinctive symmetries, are the ideal medium for high-order molecular arrangement and the diminishing of grain boundaries and defect sites coupled with high anisotropy. However, conventional synthesis via bulk growth or epitaxial deposition remains complex, costly, and difficult to scale. Here, we report a simple and inexpensive strategy as an alternative to conventional strategies for manufacturing single-crystalline metal foils. Miraculously, by miniaturization of grain boundaries and promoting surface energy minimization during the rotation of the crystal lattice followed by the consumption of neighboring grains, high-quality and large-scale single-crystalline metal foils (Cu(111), Ni(111)) were obtained via vertically suspended chemical vapor deposition (CVD) annealing of polycrystalline metal foils. This discovery offers a potential strategy for manipulating and producing large-scale metal foils that may be used for industrial-scale applications.

articles.title: Dynamics of Charge-Density-Wave Puddles in 2 H -NbSe2
articles.abstract: Electronic phases in quantum materials are often governed by nanoscale inhomogeneity, where local order develops within spatially confined regions, or puddles. A prominent example is an incommensurate charge-density-wave (I-CDW) comprising locally commensurate domains. In 2H-NbSe2, such an I-CDW state persists alongside lattice anharmonicity and superconductivity, raising fundamental questions about the dynamical stabilization of CDW order in puddles. Here, using Raman scattering, we reveal a strong Fano-coupling between interlayer shear phonons and the CDW amplitude mode. Our time-resolved reflectivity measurement shows a low-frequency ∼0.2 THz coherent overdamped oscillation onsetting within the CDW regime at ∼17K, indicating a previously unexplored transition. This we identify as a Fano-coupled phonon-CDW hybrid emerging from the collective dynamics of CDW puddles. We establish an overdamped-oscillator framework for capturing such intertwined glassy dynamics. These results highlight how lattice pinning and electronic correlations shape CDW order in layered materials, insight crucial for designing novel van der Waals devices.

articles.title: Enhanced Electron Charging Induces Positive Aging of QD-LEDs: An Electrically Excited Transient Absorption Study
articles.abstract: Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs) require encapsulation to extend their storage and operational lifetime. However, acidic encapsulants commonly used usually induce an anomalous positive aging phenomenon─the device performance improves rather than decreases in the initial days. These uncontrollable gains hinder the commercialization of QD-LEDs, yet no study to date has directly probed the in situ evolution of charge carriers during this process. Here, we employ electrically excited transient absorption (EETA) spectroscopy to investigate how encapsulants influence charge carrier dynamics in QD-LEDs. Taking red QD-LEDs as a model system, we demonstrate that positive aging is accompanied by enhanced electron charging in the quantum dot (QD) layer and accelerated electron injection into the emissive layer. Furthermore, we show that acid-induced progressive passivation of surface defects on ZnMgO nanoparticles improves electron injection efficiency. This work reveals that enhanced electron charging induces positive aging in QD-LEDs.

articles.title: Excitation-Wavelength-Dependent Dual Emission in Au42 Quantum Rods
articles.abstract: Dual emissive materials are of particular importance in chemical and biological assays. Herein, we focus on a rod-shaped Au42(SCH2CH2Ph)32 nanocluster that exhibits dual emission at 875 and 1040 nm owing to fluorescence (FL) and phosphorescence (PH), respectively. Transient absorption analysis shows a slow intersystem crossing (ISC, ∼500 ps) from lowest singlet S1 to triplet T1 upon direct S1 excitation, leading to dual emission from both S1 and T1. However, upon excitation of the higher Sn state, we observe a metastable singlet state (S′). We rationalize two competing decay pathways from S′: (i) internal conversion to S1 and (ii) ISC to high triplet Tn≥2. These processes alter the populations of the S1 and T1 states, which explains the excitation-wavelength-dependent dual emission and FL/PH ratios. The revealed excited-state mechanism and the dual emissive Au42 material will serve as a paradigm for future research on atomically precise nanoclusters.

articles.title: Excitonic Physics in Emerging 2D Semiconductors: A First-Principles Many-Body Perspective from Photodetection to Solar Energy Conversion
articles.abstract: Chemically and structurally diverse two-dimensional semiconductors exhibit a broad range of excitonic and optical phenomena that have direct implications for optoelectronic functionality. We examine these materials from a first-principles many-body perspective, emphasizing the connection between microscopic excitonic structure and optoelectronic functionality. Reduced symmetry and orbital character produce polarization-selective absorption, while dimensionality, dielectric screening, and exciton fine structure govern binding energies and radiative behavior. In layered systems, interlayer electrostatics and type-II band alignment promote charge separation, whereas exciton–phonon coupling activates indirect optical transitions and shapes temperature-dependent spectra. These mechanisms establish common design principles for excitonic engineering, whereby the dielectric environment, crystal geometry, lattice dynamics, and stacking are used to control exciton properties and tailor optical functionality. This perspective moves beyond description toward the ab initio prediction and design of emerging 2D materials for targeted optoelectronic applications, including polarization-sensitive photodetection and ultrathin solar-energy conversion.

articles.title: From Micro to Nano: Boosting γ-MnO2 Cathode Performance through Particle Size Engineering
articles.abstract: Fast-charging lithium-ion batteries require cathodes that sustain rapid Li+ transport while maintaining structural and interfacial stability. Here, we investigate particle-size effects in γ-MnO2 by comparing micron-sized (4.4 ± 0.8 μm) and nanosized (62 ± 21 nm) particles under identical conditions. Nanosized γ-MnO2 delivers 160.1 mAh g–1 at C/10 and retains ∼66% capacity at 5C while exhibiting lower charge-transfer and diffusion-related impedance. Cyclic voltammetry and Dunn’s analysis reveal a 68.9% capacitive contribution at 2 mV s–1, indicating a shift toward faster surface-controlled charge storage enabled by increased surface area and shorter Li+ diffusion pathways. GITT measurements show deeper lithiation (x ≈ 0.65 vs 0.48 in LixMnO2) and a more homogeneous solid-solution-like intercalation regime in nanosized particles, avoiding bulk phase-transition kinetic bottlenecks. The nanosized cathode retains 70% capacity with ∼99.5% Coulombic efficiency after 400 cycles at 3C, demonstrating particle-size engineering as an effective strategy for high-rate, long-life advanced battery energy storage.

articles.title: Interface-Induced Crystallographic Orientation of Zinc Deposition Enabled by a Zwitterionic Dynamic Buffering Interface for Ultralong-Life Aqueous Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: The development of aqueous zinc batteries is critically constrained by the electrode–electrolyte interfacial instability at the Zn anode. Herein, a zwitterionic dynamic buffering interface (ZDBI) is constructed by using trace glufosinate ammonium (GA). The dissociated GA– anchors onto the Zn(101) surface via its phosphinate and carboxylate groups with its protonated amino group (−NH3+) extending into the electrolyte to dynamically respond to interfacial electric fields. Meanwhile, free NH4+ cations can form an electrostatic shielding layer under an electric field. This synergistic chemisorbed-mobile-ion buffering network thickens the electric double layer, inhibits water-splitting parasitic reactions, and induces (101)-oriented deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn symmetric cells sustain stable cycling for over 7800 h with a cumulative capacity of 3.9 Ah cm–2, while Zn||Cu half-cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.3%, and Zn||V2O5 full cells retain 88% capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g–1. This work offers an efficient strategy for addressing electrode–electrolyte interfacial issues.

articles.title: Low-Dimensional Chiral Perovskites for Polarization-Sensitive Photodetection
articles.abstract: Emerging low-dimensional chiral perovskites have recently demonstrated significant application potential in circularly polarized light detection, spintronics, and quantum information technology due to their unique chiroptical activity and spin-selective properties. This review systematically summarizes their material systems, synthesis methods, chirality transfer mechanisms, and applications in photodetectors. The critical role of chiral organic cations in crystal regulation and chiroptical properties along with corresponding fabrication strategies is analyzed. Then, the inherent mechanisms of chirality transfer from organic to inorganic components are thoroughly discussed, encompassing structural distortion induction and electronic orbital coupling. Subsequently, recent advances in circularly polarized photodetectors based on low-dimensional chiral perovskites are highlighted from device performance, spin selection efficiency, to bio-inspired polarization vision systems. Finally, the challenges and future directions in this field are prospected. This review provides a comprehensive summarization for the development of low-dimensional chiral perovskites and their applications in next-generation polarized photodetectors.

articles.title: Natural Hyperbolic Dispersion in Anisotropic Bulk and Nanoscaled Copper Chalcogenides
articles.abstract: Hyperbolic media support high-k electromagnetic modes, enabling subdiffractional confinement, anomalous refraction, and enhanced light–matter interactions. While most hyperbolic metamaterials rely on artificial structuring, natural hyperbolicity arises from crystal anisotropy and direction-dependent plasma frequencies. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for natural hyperbolicity in copper chalcogenides by spectroscopic ellipsometry in the visible–near-infrared range. We demonstrate hyperbolic dispersion in bulk covellite CuS by identifying a spectral window where the real parts of the in-plane and out-of-plane permittivity components have opposite signs. The study is then expanded to size-controlled CuS nanosheets as oriented films. Using the Bruggeman effective medium approximation to account for the nanostructure/void composite, we show that hyperbolicity persists upon nanoscaling and that the epsilon-near-zero condition and hyperbolic bandwidth shift with size. Finally, we demonstrate analogous behavior in klockmannite CuSe nanosheets, establishing copper chalcogenides as a tunable platform for natural hyperbolicity at the boundary of the NIR and visible ranges.

articles.title: Optically Active Single Hole Spin in ZnSe
articles.abstract: Semiconductor hole spins offer a pathway to extended coherence times by decoupling from nuclear magnetic noise, while their spin–orbit coupling enables fast all-electrical control. In ZnSe, however, realizing this potential has been limited by p-doping challenges. Here, we circumvent this limit by optically activating acceptors and demonstrate optical spin initialization. We isolate a single-hole spin bound to a shallow acceptor, confirmed by antibunching and accessed via the fast (244 ps) radiative recombination of a bound exciton. Magnetic and Raman spectroscopy reveal a spin-selective Λ system with an effective hole g-factor of 0.7 and an optical line width of 26.7 GHz. Time-resolved measurements reveal optical pumping of the hole spin with an estimated initialization fidelity of 90.7%. First-principles simulations combined with the experiment identify nitrogen as the most likely acceptor impurity. These results introduce a promising new platform for optically active spin qubits and single-photon sources in ZnSe.

articles.title: Polyaniline-Modified MXene/Carbon Nanotube Scaffold Enabling High-Rate and Long-Cycle Zinc–Iodine Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are attractive for large-scale energy storage because of their low cost and inherent safety. However, the practical use of an I2 cathode is severely restricted by poor electronic conductivity and the shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides. Herein, a synergistic scaffold composed of MXene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) modified with protonated polyaniline (PANI) via electrostatic interactions was designed. The MXene/CNT scaffold ensures overall conductivity and structural integrity. The protonated PANI immobilizes iodine species through nitrogen-containing groups and accelerates their interconversion, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. The MXene/CNTs/PANI-I2 cathode with an iodine loading of 43.96 wt % achieves a superior specific capacity of 150 mAh g–1 at a high rate of 20 C as well as excellent cycling stability over 10 000 cycles. This work offers a viable strategy for developing stable I2 cathodes for high-performance Zn–I2 batteries.

articles.title: Polymorphic Hf(Zr)O2-Based Films for High-k Dielectrics
articles.abstract: HfO2/ZrO2-based (HZO) materials are promising high-k dielectrics for integrated capacitors and advanced electronic devices. However, their performance is fundamentally constrained by polymorph competition and the trade-off between the dielectric constant and leakage current. Here, we report a stacking-engineered strategy that integrates HZO layers with optimized ferroelectric and dielectric properties separated by an Al2O3 interlayer (HAZO). A nonswitching pulse measurement is employed to exclude polarization-switching contributions and directly probe the intrinsic dielectric response. The optimized HAZO dielectric exhibits an enhanced dielectric constant while simultaneously suppressing leakage and improving the dielectric breakdown characteristics. Structural characterizations reveal that the engineered stacking stabilizes the coexistence of nonpolar tetragonal and polar orthorhombic phases and increases the phase-boundary density. This polymorphic configuration suppresses irreversible domain switching and enables a stable enhanced dielectric response. These results establish a robust pathway toward high-performance HZO-based dielectrics and provide key insights into tailoring dielectric properties through polymorphic-phase engineering.

articles.title: Farewell NASA ADS
articles.abstract: After more than 33 years, NASA’s Astrophysics Data System will close its virtual doors in November 2026 and be replaced by its much-expanded successor, Science Explorer. While the core functionality and astrophysics database will remain the same, SciX will extend its relevance to a broader range of scientists.

articles.title: Transitioning from ADS to SciX to serve twenty-first century astronomy
articles.abstract: For decades, the NASA Astrophysics Data System (ADS) has been the foundational digital library for astronomy. As ADS now becomes the Science Explorer (SciX), the team prioritizes preserving this trusted experience while increasing their support for space and Earth sciences more broadly, without diluting its commitment to astrophysics.

articles.title: A health-system-scale, episode-resolved multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia
articles.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010–2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia. Using longitudinal data from 52,236 patients with cancer, this study created a multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia, demonstrating that weight loss episodes are linked to systemic serologic signatures and specific tumor genotypes and can be predicted using integrated clinical and molecular data, enabling earlier identification.

articles.title: Population-scale reconstruction of menopause dynamics reveals a physiological cliff at the final menstrual period
articles.abstract: By using a novel computational framework, a cross-sectional analysis on laboratory data from two independent cohorts reveals that the final menstrual period marks an abrupt, multisystem physiological shift, with sex hormone changes beginning more than 10 years before menopause onset.

articles.abstract: The genetic changes associated with development of the human cortex are difficult to test functionally, especially in the context of gene regulation. In this issue, Matoba et al. show that variants that shape human cortical structure are hiding inside Alu transposable elements, co-opting their inbuilt machinery to rewire regulatory networks in the developing brain.

articles.title: Genome-wide analysis of common structural variants in Alzheimer’s disease identifies a risk-associated regulatory CCG repeat in FAM193B

articles.title: Chip-mediated manipulation of photonic quantum skyrmions
articles.abstract: Although photonic quantum skyrmions can be generated as entangled or single-photon states, a means to switch between the two is required for quantum information processing. Now, entangled skyrmions and their manipulation on chip is realized.

articles.title: Morphogenesis of a stratified cell mound at a vortex defect
articles.abstract: In cell monolayers with a vortex-like orientation defect, cells converge towards the core of the defect and form a highly organized three-dimensional mound. This mechanism may be relevant for morphogenesis and tumorigenesis.

articles.abstract: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.

articles.title: Photocatalytic tetrapeptides for enantioselective visible light-induced transformations
articles.abstract: Upon irradiation with visible light (λ = 425 nm), a tetrapeptide with a C-terminal photocatalytic site and an N-terminal site for substrate recognition promotes photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. The required spatial proximity of catalyst and substrate is corroborated by NMR spectroscopy studies and molecular dynamics simulations.

articles.title: Scrambling-free synthesis of heteroleptic silylium ions by halide abstraction from halosilanes
articles.abstract: Access to silylium ions with three different substituents has remained elusive owing to substituent scrambling under established synthetic methods. Now, harnessing the Lewis superacidity of halogen-substituted silylium ions, a broadly applicable protocol for synthesizing such heteroleptic silylium ions without substituent redistribution by halide abstraction from readily available halosilanes is reported.

articles.title: Avirulence genes of Magnaporthe oryzae are a pathogen defense arsenal shaped by cognate rice resistance genes in the field
articles.abstract: Population structure and AVR gene presence/absence of 383 single‐spore isolates from the US Mo population. Summary We examined the frequency of and variation in eight avirulence (AVR) genes from 840 Magnaporthe oryzae field isolates collected from the Southern United States relative to rice resistance (R) genes deployed from 1959 to 2017. Little coding or noncoding variation was detected in AVR‐Pi9, AVR‐Pib, ACE1 and AVR‐Pizt, which correspond to R genes not used in the United States. In the United States, AVR‐Pik, corresponding to rice R gene Pi‐k alleles deployed at varying levels since the late 1960s, was present in 37% of the isolates over six decades. AVR‐Pita1, corresponding to Pi‐ta deployed in the late 1990s, reached a low point in the 5‐yr period following Pi‐ta deployment and then recovered to 99% in recent years. Our results suggest a fitness penalty for M. oryzae isolates carrying nonfunctional AVR variants and provide concrete data on how changes in plant R gene composition can impact pathogen populations. These findings will inform localized strategies for R gene usage and durable control of blast disease. AVR frequencies differ over time between United States and global samples for AVR‐Pik, AVR‐Pi9, AVR‐Pii and AVR‐Pita1. Further whole genome analysis including additional US samples is necessary to confirm whether the United States is a geographically isolated population.

articles.title: Excess endopolyploidy associated with cellular defects in neo‐autotetraploid Arabidopsis arenosa is in part corrected by a naturally evolved allele of CYCD3;2
articles.abstract: Ploidy level distributions and endoreduplication profiles in diploid and tetraploid Arabidopsis arenosa. Summary Endopolyploidy (within‐organism polyploidy) is an often‐beneficial aspect of development. But polyploids, which have a higher baseline genome content, have been reported to have less endoreduplication than diploid relatives. Why has remained unclear; we explored this in Arabidopsis arenosa. We measured endopolyploidy levels and phenotyped cellular traits, comparing diploids, neo‐autotetraploids, and established autotetraploids of A. arenosa. We used a genetic approach to ask whether CYCD3;2, a polyploidy regulator with evidence of selection in tetraploids, might be responsible for endopolyploidy‐related phenotypic differences between neo‐ and established polyploids, and whether there are associated costs. Neo‐tetraploids had the most 16C and 32C cells, whereas established tetraploids have proportions of 16C and 32C cells comparable to diploids. Tetraploid plants homozygous for a novel allele of CYCD3;2 have reduced endopolyploidy compared to homozygotes for the diploid allele and, surprisingly, also show cellular defects seen in neo‐tetraploids. Suggesting this link is specific, we find that A. thaliana cycd3;2 mutants have not only increased endopolyploidy but also root hair defects like neo‐tetraploids. Our results suggest reverting endopolyploidy in polyploids to diploid‐like levels could be advantageous, and that one driver might be cellular defects that arise with excess high‐ploidy cells.

articles.title: Ten rules for robust taxonomy in ecological datasets
articles.abstract: A workflow for better use and integration of taxonomic‐related information into ecological datasets. Summary Accurate taxonomy, including species identification and naming, underpins ecological inference, yet taxonomic information in ecological datasets is often inconsistently recorded or weakly standardized. With the increasing integration of ecological datasets across taxa and regions, datasets with poor taxonomic practices can hinder data exchange and propagate errors. We propose 10 rules to improve the storage and management of taxonomic information in ecological datasets. These rules draw on our experiences in plant ecology and taxonomy, but the conclusions may be generalized to other organisms and disciplines. They emphasize aspects from species identification to the permanent storage of verifiable records (e.g. voucher specimens) and include taxonomic standardization, nomenclature, validation, and updating. We also address the treatment of morphotypes and incomplete identifications, the use of automated name‐matching tools, and (meta)data standards. Closer collaboration between ecologists and taxonomists is key to ensuring more robust datasets. The application of these rules consumes more time and resources, but they enhance data quality and interoperability, saving time during data integration and improving the reliability and scalability of ecological research. Resumo Uma taxonomia precisa, incluindo a identificação e nomenclatura das espécies, é fundamental para a inferência em ecologia. Entretanto, as informações taxonômicas em conjuntos de dados ecológicos frequentemente são pouco padronizadas. Com a integração contínua de dados ecológicos entre diferentes grupos taxonômicos e regiões, a adoção de práticas inadequadas pode dificultar o intercâmbio de dados e propagar erros. Neste trabalho, nós propomos dez regras para aprimorar o armazenamento e curadoria de informações taxonômicas em conjuntos de dados ecológicos. Essas regras foram baseadas em nossa expertise em ecologia e taxonomia vegetal, mas suas conclusões podem ser generalizadas para outros organismos e disciplinas. As regras enfatizam aspectos que vão desde a identificação de espécies até o armazenamento permanente de registros verificáveis (por exemplo, espécimes‐voucher) e incluem assuntos referentes a nomenclatura, padronização, validação e atualização taxonômica. Também abordamos o tratamento de morfotipos e identificações incompletas, o uso de ferramentas automatizadas de correspondência de nomes e padrões de (meta)dados. Uma colaboração mais estreita entre ecólogos e taxonomistas é essencial para garantir conjuntos de dados mais robustos. A aplicação dessas regras demanda mais tempo e recursos, mas melhora a qualidade dos dados e a interoperabilidade, economizando tempo durante a integração de dados e aprimorando a confiabilidade e escalabilidade em ecologia. Resumen Una taxonomía precisa, que incluya la identificación y asignación de nombres científicos, es fundamental para la inferencia ecológica; sin embargo, la información taxonómica suele estar poco estandarizada en las bases de datos ecológicos. Con el aumento en la integración de bases de datos ecológicos de distintas taxones y regiones, los conjuntos de datos con prácticas taxonómicas precarias pueden propagar errores y dificultar el intercambio de datos. En este manuscrito, proponemos diez reglas para mejorar el almacenamiento y el manejo de información taxonómica en bases de datos ecológicos. Estas reglas se basan en nuestra experiencia en ecología y taxonomía de plantas, pero pueden extrapolarse a otros organismos y disciplinas. Estas reglas enfatizan aspectos desde la identificación de especies hasta el almacenamiento permanente de registros verificables (e.g. especímenes de colecciones), también incluyen estandarización taxonómica, nomenclatura, validación y actualizaciones.…

articles.title: Attacks on healthcare: World Medical Association issues new declaration on “medical neutrality”

articles.abstract: Bangladesh’s measles death toll could now be as high as 1144,1 with most of the deceased being children.These figures come amid an investigation into the country’s national immunisation programme and the current deadly outbreak.The latest update from the government (8 October) showed that, since mid-March, there were 201 625 suspected measles cases and 22 116 confirmed cases.2There have also been 1040 suspected and 104 confirmed deaths.But Bangladeshi officials warned that these were likely an underestimate.In April, a senior official at the Directorate General of Health Services told The BMJ that the case and death toll was probably higher owing to a lack of laboratory capacity to confirm cases, as well as delayed treatment, and deaths being recorded as the result of other causes.3The current outbreak started in January, with the first case detected in the Cox’s Bazar camp for Rohingya refugees, but cases began spiking in March.Writing in The BMJ,...

articles.title: The BMJ Medics’ Revue 2026: sincere silliness
articles.abstract: I watched the surgeons make practised movements, bright lights illuminating each mesmerising flick of their wrists. A curtain formed a vital barrier between us. I was there only to assist, holding an instrument ready for the critical moment.Sweat poured down their faces. It was almost time.In perfect sync, they completed the final steps. For a single, breathless moment, they were still.The audience exploded with applause. Darkness swept the stage as the dancers ran off and I scurried on, rushing to set up the keyboard for the next act.I was nowhere near a hospital: I was a stagehand for The BMJ’s Medics’ Revue 2026.After being on hiatus since 2000, the revue was revived this year, taking place at the Shaw Theatre in London. As a BMJ Clegg Scholar, I joined the organising team for the final month of preparations and discovered the value of the event from behind the scenes.Around two...

articles.title: [Comment] Hepatitis C—is discrimination preventing elimination?
articles.abstract: The UK (chiefly driven by England and Scotland) is expected to be the first country to meet WHO's goal for the elimination of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection by 2030. In April, 2026, the UK Health Security Agency's analysis of progress by the National Health Service (NHS) towards elimination showed that 84·6% of people living with HCV had been diagnosed and prevalence in people who inject drugs had fallen to 5·2% in 2024, with an estimated incidence of 4·4 infections per 100 person-years, predicted to fall below WHO's target of two infections per 100 patient-years by 2030.

articles.title: [Comment] Tailoring levels of evidence in trials comparing common treatments
articles.abstract: In many disease settings, physicians and patients can choose between several treatment options that are in common use, but how should they make the choice? The problem is often not the absence of evidence but the absence of robust randomised controlled evidence directly comparing treatments that are already widely used in practice. Treatment options might have been directly compared with a common comparator, but not to each other; for example, in respiratory syncytial virus prevention in infants, both maternal vaccination and infant monoclonal antibodies have shown efficacy versus placebo but have not been directly compared.

articles.title: Thiol reactivity: lost in the crowd?
articles.abstract: Predictions of cysteine reactivity rely heavily on acidity (pKa) data from dilute solutions. However, the intracellular milieu is crowded and dynamic, with substrates, cofactors, and metabolites that modulate reactivity, thereby affecting cell signaling and metabolic adaptation. This forum argues that Cys pKa values are necessary but insufficient, proposing an integrated, microenvironment-dependent framework.

articles.title: From species richness to interaction architecture
articles.abstract: Biodiversity research has long focused on the number and identity of species, but recent advances suggest that ecosystem functioning depends on how species are connected. Predicting the consequences of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene will therefore require moving beyond inventories of species toward a predictive ecology of interaction networks.

articles.title: Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
articles.abstract: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxides. Whether universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs), which lack explicit electronic degrees of freedom, can describe them remains unclear. Here, we investigate H-induced electron localization across a range of TM oxides using a geometric descriptor based on TM-O bond-length expansion (Z-score) to identify polaronic distortions. We find that uMLIPs exhibit varying degrees of electron localization, from delocalized states to metastable small polarons, with their behavior strongly dependent on the training data and treatment of electronic correlations. In particular, the absence of Hubbard U corrections for specific TM cations in the training data leads to electron delocalization, in contrast to DFT+U predictions. Although some uMLIPs reproduce polaron hopping barriers during coupled proton-polaron transfer, all of them fail to stabilize spatially separated polaron-donor configurations, instead favoring localization near the H dopant.

articles.title: Chromatographic Peak Shape beyond the High-Péclet Approximation: Analytic Time-Domain Expression and Derivatives
articles.abstract: Analytic time-domain expressions for the elution-time density and its parameter derivatives were recently derived from a stochastic model of linear isocratic chromatography incorporating advective-diffusive transport, injection dispersion, and fast and slow retention mechanisms. A Gaussian approximation, justified asymptotically at high column-scale Péclet numbers, was adopted for the distribution of the combined mobile-phase and fast-retention time, while slow retention was incorporated through a series of Gaussian-Gamma convolutions. Here, the underlying normal-inverse-Gaussian density is approximated by a finite Gaussian mixture using an existing quadrature rule. The elution-time PDF is a weighted sum of series of the previously derived Gaussian-Gamma form. Its parameter derivatives are also obtained. Newly derived recurrences reduce the cost of evaluating the coefficients of that series and their derivatives from quadratic to linear in truncation order for a fixed number of mechanisms. Through a probabilistic analysis of the series coefficients, the required number of terms is found to be small enough for rapid evaluation under usual chromatographic conditions. A relative roundoff-error estimator is derived to quantify finite-precision loss in the inherited forward recurrence for Gaussian-Gamma convolutions. For the cancellation-prone regime, a backward reconstruction is developed, initialized from an exact ratio of consecutive Gaussian-Gamma terms expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. A highly accurate approximation is derived for rapid evaluation of this ratio. Independent high-precision calculations confirm the high accuracy of the resulting double-precision evaluation in the tested numerical case.

articles.title: Exact Gaussian--Hermite closure of the mapping quantum--classical Liouville equation
articles.abstract: Liouville equation contains an excess coupling term in addition to the Poisson bracket. Neglecting this term yields the Poisson bracket mapping equation (PBME). We expand the mapping dependence of the density in Hermite functions about the Gaussian factor common to all physical mapping densities. In this basis, the excess coupling term acts purely as a raising operator and exactly cancels the raising contribution generated by the back--reaction force. Consequently, the exact dynamics does not generate higher Hermite orders and closes on a finite, sparse system of equations for the coefficient fields. Within the physical sector, these equations reduce to the subsystem quantum--classical Liouville equation. In contrast, the PBME retains the raising contribution of the force, modifying the back reaction within the physical sector while continuously generating higher Hermite orders. For Tully's dual avoided crossing model, direct propagation of the coefficient equations confirms this finite closure and agrees with independent solutions of the subsystem equation. Comparison with converged full quantum dynamics further shows that, across all regimes examined, the PBME is less accurate than the quantum--classical description for populations, coherences, and momentum distributions.

articles.title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
articles.abstract: The nearly collinear configuration of highly stretched polymer chains before fracture motivates one-dimensional models. At fixed extension, stretching one bond redistributes length among the others, coupling rupture to the whole chain. In this work, I develop a framework for fracture-healing rates in periodic Morse chains, combining deterministic theories, equilibrium simulations and a quasi-deterministic approach using equilibrium fluxes and barrier-top trajectories. Constrained-partition calculations closely reproduce simulated populations and intact-state tensions. An intact-reservoir potential of mean force (PMF) supplies the first-fracture surface probability, while recrossing corrects the attempt flux without a rate-fitted prefactor. Independent rate tests identify an operational chain-length boundary for accurate two-state kinetics; failed-return durations decrease relative to population relaxation as chains grow. Kramers-Grote-Hynes (KGH), nonlinear reactive-flux and equilibrium rates show excellent agreement in this regime. KGH predicts rates away from coexistence and a chain-dependent local activation length dominated by the barrier response. Rates decrease approximately exponentially before declining more gently for longer chains: barrier growth dominates, additional fracture sites partly compensate, and transmission varies more weakly. Beyond coexistence, long chains can fracture practically irreversibly because healing becomes too rare to observe. Projected committor crossings, where the configuration-averaged probability of reaching the fractured core first is one half, lie near site-PMF maxima, although configurations at equal bond length retain different fracture probabilities. Multiple fractures remain negligible near coexistence through at least $N=50$. The framework could supply state-dependent rates to mesoscopic fracture models of polymer networks.

articles.title: MIRRA: Fast, High-Fidelity Molecular Generation with Chemistry-Informed Discrete Flow Matching
articles.abstract: Fast, high-fidelity molecular generation requires accurate chemical choices and efficient sampling. Chemical building blocks reduce graph size, but make each node a choice among tens of thousands of related identities. We introduce MIRRA (Molecular Identity Representation, Refresh and Assembly), a discrete flow-matching generator that learns from chemical knowledge and evaluates identity probabilities only when needed, while keeping every identity in its vocabulary available. Chemical features share information across related blocks, and learned identity corrections distinguish them in molecular context. By deciding which positions will refresh before computing their probabilities, the sampler avoids unused predictions while preserving each sampling transition. Against the strongest baselines in each task, MIRRA reduces chemical and graph distribution errors on ZINC250k by 29-31% and 53-60%, respectively, with generation up to 8.6 times faster. Property targeting yields an estimated 7.8-20.8 times more distinct novel hits per second. On a held-out polymer test set, MIRRA achieves 100% periodic validity with known chain topology, versus 57.0% for a polymer variational autoencoder. These results demonstrate fast, high-fidelity generation with the full chemical vocabulary available throughout sampling.

articles.title: Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry
articles.abstract: Most machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on gas-phase data, which limits their use for chemistry in solution. Here, we introduce AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation potential that provides solvent-dependent energy and force corrections to existing gas-phase potentials without retraining them. It is trained on 1.4 million solvation energies and forces computed with density functional theory (DFT) and SMD in 36 solvents, spanning charged, open-shell, and transition-state structures. Because solvents are represented by continuous physical descriptors, AnySolv supports 179 solvents, including those absent from training. On external benchmarks, AnySolv reproduces DFT-SMD solvation energies to 2-4 meV mean absolute error at more than three orders of magnitude lower cost, and it matches the accuracy of DFT-SMD against experimental solvation free energies. This enables screening of the mechanisms of 120 nucleophilic aromatic substitution reactions in six phases as well as molecular dynamics simulations that reproduce the experimentally observed solvent-dependent conformational preferences of alanine dipeptide. By providing transferable solvation corrections to existing MLIPs, AnySolv enables scalable simulations of solvent-dependent chemical reactivity and molecular dynamics.

articles.title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
articles.abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

articles.title: Genome-wide mapping of Cas9-induced sister chromatid exchange across single and over 200 genomic sites in human cells
articles.abstract: CRISPR/Cas9-induced DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are widely used for genome engineering, yet their capacity to provoke sister chromatid exchange (SCE) remains incompletely understood because exchanges between identical sisters leave no sequence change and are invisible to conventional sequencing. Using sci-L3-Strand-seq, a scalable single-cell template-strand sequencing platform, we mapped SCE following targeted Cas9 cleavage. Cas9 targeting of a unique genomic locus strongly enriched SCE at the break site, reaching 41% in the same cell cycle and 17% in the subsequent division, indicating frequent non-local inter-sister repair. Targeting 237 repetitive Alu sites produced mild enrichment of on-target SCE, whereas cells with elevated SCE burden showed significant enrichment at programmed cut sites, suggesting context-dependent recombination at repetitive loci. Reciprocal daughter-cell pair analysis revealed large-scale structural alterations on chromosomes with induced SCEs and at SCE junctions, indicating that Cas9-induced SCE does not universally reflect error-free homologous recombination. Disruption of LIG3, LIG4, XRCC1, and XRCC4 at Cas9 cut sites did not measurably alter SCE frequency, consistent with delayed functional loss following editing. Together, these findings identify Cas9-induced DSBs as potent local triggers of SCE and reveal structural outcomes invisible to conventional sequencing.

articles.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1–ligand complexes and three virtual screens
articles.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Boltz-2, and Chai-1 each reproduced >50% of the Mac1 ligand poses to better than 2 Å root-mean-square deviation of experiment. Despite the potential for co-folding to describe protein conformational changes that stabilize ligand binding, we did not find that common conformational rearrangements, including peptide flip and a large loop opening, were recapitulated by the co-folding prediction. For AF3 and Chai-1, ligand pose prediction confidence weakly, but significantly, tracked experimental potency, while DOCK3.7 energies were only weakly correlated. Boltz-2 affinity predictions showed the strongest correlation with measured potency and, after calibration, achieved lower mean absolute error than a baseline predictor. We next assessed whether co-folding scores could rescore docking hit lists to distinguish true ligands from non-binders among hundreds of molecules prospectively experimentally tested against AmpC β-lactamase, the dopamine D4, and the σ2 receptors. AF3 ligand pose confidence values did not separate true ligands from high-scoring false positives as effectively as docking scores or Boltz-2 affinity predictions did. Taken together, the modest, but independent correlations of docking score and co-folding confidence or affinity suggest that integrating physics-based and deep-learning approaches may help with hit prioritization and subsequent optimization in structure-based ligand discovery.

articles.title: Product-stabilized filamentation by human glutamine synthetase allosterically tunes metabolic activity
articles.abstract: To maintain metabolic homeostasis, enzymes must adapt to fluctuating nutrient levels through mechanisms beyond gene expression. Here, we demonstrate that human glutamine synthetase (GS) can reversibly polymerize into filaments aided by a composite binding site formed at the filament interface by the product, glutamine. Time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) confirms that glutamine binding stabilizes these filaments, which in turn exhibit reduced catalytic specificity for ammonia at physiological concentrations. This inhibition appears induced by a conformational change that remodulates the active site loop ensemble gating substrate entry. Metadynamics ensemble refinement revealed >10 Å conformational range for the active site loop and that the loop is stabilized by transient contacts. This disorder is significant, as we show that the transient contacts which stabilize this loop in a closed conformation are essential for catalysis both in vitro and in cells. We propose that GS filament formation constitutes a negative-feedback mechanism, directly linking product concentration to the structural and functional remodeling of the enzyme.

articles.title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG
articles.abstract: Non-invasive recordings of brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. This makes it challenging to establish a clear consensus on the frequency, location, and direction of any single reported effect within the larger body of research. We estimate a full-frequency whole-head profile of the ageing effect on eyes-closed resting-state MEG using the GLM-Spectrum. This data representation is easily sharable, facilitates meta-analyses, and provides a framework for estimating statistical power of age effects for future study planning. We use this to show that the effect of age replicates across open-access MEG datasets and is robust to modelling of common covariates. Distinct components within the full-frequency profile have different effect sizes, indicating that sample-size planning for ageing effects must consider the specific features of interest. The frequency profile of ageing is strongly robust to a range of common covariates and partially robust to modelling of grey matter volume. We establish that what seems a well-powered study may become underpowered when analyses target an age effect that is linearly separable from an age-relevant covariate such as grey matter volume. These results provide a pathway towards formal comparison and assessment of candidate markers for brain health in ageing.

articles.title: Svep1 orchestrates distal airway patterning and alveolar differentiation in murine lung development
articles.abstract: Disruptions in airway branching or alveolar differentiation during lung development can lead to severe respiratory deficiencies and neonatal death. The molecular mechanisms governing branching patterning and early alveolar formation remain elusive. Loss of Svep1 function in mice results in various developmental defects, including lung hypoplasia and perinatal lethality. Our examination of the lungs of Svep1 knockout (Svep1-/-) mouse embryos, both in vivo and in vitro, revealed that Svep1 mutants exhibit an increase in the number of disorganized distal airway tips, progressively greater disruption of lung lobe morphology over time, and disrupted saccular development. Svep1 interacts with FGF signaling to regulate smooth muscle differentiation and, together with Fgf9, guides airway branching patterning. Transcriptomic data from the lungs of Svep1-/- embryos revealed dysregulated gene expression affecting saccular maturation. Our findings demonstrate that Svep1 is a key extracellular matrix player shaping airway morphology and influencing alveolar fate. These insights offer potential avenues for therapeutic interventions in congenital lung disorders.

articles.title: Synaptic connectome of a neurosecretory network in the Drosophila brain
articles.abstract: Hormones mediate inter-organ signaling, which is crucial in orchestrating diverse behaviors and physiological processes, including sleep and activity, feeding, growth, metabolism, and reproduction. The pars intercerebralis and pars lateralis in insects represent major hubs that contain neurosecretory cells (NSCs) that produce various peptide hormones. To obtain insight into how hormonal signaling is regulated, we have characterized the synaptic connectome of NSCs in the adult Drosophila brain. Identification of neurons providing inputs to multiple NSC classes implicates diuretic hormone 44-expressing NSCs as a major coordinator of physiology and behavior. Surprisingly, despite most NSCs having dendrites in the subesophageal zone (primary taste processing center), inputs from peripheral gustatory neurons to NSCs are largely indirect. We also deciphered pathways via which diverse olfactory inputs are relayed to NSCs. Using an influence metric, based on a linear dynamical systems approach, we identify enteric neurons as the strongest influencers of NSC activity compared to other sensory modalities. Further, our analyses revealed substantial inputs from brain descending neurons to NSCs, suggesting that descending neurons regulate both endocrine and motor output to synchronize physiological changes with appropriate behaviors. In contrast to NSC inputs, synaptic output from NSCs is sparse and mostly mediated by corazonin NSCs. We show that both corazonin-expressing NSCs and their downstream synaptic partner DNg27 influence egg-laying. We additionally explore putative paracrine interconnectivity between NSC classes and peptide hormone pathways from NSCs to peripheral tissues by analyzing single-cell transcriptomic datasets. Our comprehensive characterization of the Drosophila neurosecretory network connectome provides a platform to understand complex hormonal networks and how they orchestrate animal behaviors and physiology.

articles.title: Synaptic vesicle undocking induces low-frequency depression
articles.abstract: Synaptic depression is often interpreted as reflecting depletion of the readily releasable pool (RRP) following exocytosis. Such a mechanism predicts little or no depression at low stimulation frequency, as RRP replenishment should then offset the loss of vesicles by exocytosis. Nevertheless, in several types of mammalian central synapses, repetitive presynaptic stimulation at low frequency (<5 Hz) elicits synaptic depression (low-frequency depression or LFD). In the present work, we count the number of synaptic vesicles released at individual active zones to study the RRP and its replenishment during LFD. Contrary to depletion models of synaptic depression, we find that LFD does not depend on previous SV consumption. We find that LFD displays a long recovery time course (tens of seconds) when challenged by isolated stimulations but is immediately reversed by a high-frequency train. We suggest that LFD results from undocking, a shift between two classes of synaptic vesicles organized sequentially inside the RRP (replacement vs. docked vesicles) in favor of the upstream (replacement) state. To explain the dependence of LFD recovery on stimulation frequency, we propose that, while undocking is apparent hundreds of milliseconds after a stimulation, calcium-dependent docking takes only a couple of milliseconds. Consistent with the undocking model, we find that double presynaptic stimulations alleviate LFD as they favor vesicular docking and RRP replenishment. Finally, we expand our model to explain how stimulation frequency shapes short-term synaptic depression, changing from depression at low frequency to a facilitation-depression sequence at medium- or high-frequency trains.

articles.title: Decoupled Channel and Contact Modulation in α-In2Se3/ZrO2/Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 Dual-Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistor
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) utilizing either a ferroelectric dielectric (FeD) or a ferroelectric semiconductor (FeS) are highly promising for neuromorphic computing. While integrating FeD with emerging FeS could provide new degrees of freedom for synaptic plasticity, direct integration inevitably suffers from unintended electrostatic coupling and a lack of independent polarization control. Here, we demonstrate a structurally decoupled dual-ferroelectric field-effect transistor (Dual-FeFET) based on an α-In2Se3/ZrO2/HZO heterostructure, in which a ferroelectric dielectric and a ferroelectric semiconductor are integrated into a single transistor while retaining independent functional roles. The inserted ZrO2 interfacial layer mitigates unintended polarization coupling between HZO and α-In2Se3, enabling two orthogonal memory operations: gate-bias-induced HZO polarization switching globally modulates the carrier density of the α-In2Se3 channel, whereas drain-bias-induced α-In2Se3 polarization switching predominantly modulates the drain-side Schottky barrier near the contact region. Dual-mode PFM, Hall-bar analysis, temperature-dependent transport measurements, and ZrO2-thickness-dependent control experiments support the largely decoupled modulation of channel transport and contact injection. By sequentially exploiting these two modulation modes, the Dual-FeFET extends the conductance dynamic range and improves the linearity of synaptic potentiation compared with conventional single-mode FeFET operation. The device exhibits robust nonvolatile memory characteristics with stable endurance over 105 cycles and retention up to 105 s. When implemented in convolutional neural network simulations for CIFAR-10 image recognition, the Dual-FeFET-based synapses achieve an accuracy of 89.2%, approaching the ideal software accuracy of 96.5% and outperforming conventional single-FeFET-based synapses (74.1%). These results demonstrate that structural ferroelectric decoupling enables independently programmable channel and contact modulation in multifunctional 2D ferroelectric transistors.

articles.title: Marine-Inspired Synergistic Adhesion Enables Highly Efficient and Atraumatic Macromolecular Transdermal Delivery on Dynamic Skin
articles.abstract: Effective transdermal drug delivery (TDD) demands both the ability to bypass the stratum corneum (ST) and the robustness to sustain delivery efficiency under real-life conditions. Despite advances in nanocarriers, microneedles, and electrostimulation, many TDDS strategies face limitations due to cytotoxicity, invasiveness, device dependence, and poor performance for large molecules in real-world conditions. In this study, we present a marine-inspired TDDS patch (PDA@SC) that integrates adhesion strategies from marine organisms to achieve stable skin attachment and atraumatic macromolecular delivery, even on dynamic skin surfaces. The suction-cup (SC) structure, inspired by octopus’ suckers, generates negative pressure upon preload-induced deformation, promoting temporary mechanical modulation for nanolevel control of the ST barrier and enhancing drug delivery without external power. Simultaneously, the mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) coating modifies hydrophobic surfaces into high surface energy interfaces capable of chemical bonding, thereby ensuring intimate adhesion and minimizing drug leakage. Experimental findings confirmed that the delivery of the high molecular weight compound was enhanced on deformed skin, showing a 600% improvement compared to conventional topical application. In addition, preliminary human evaluation demonstrated that PDA@SC effectively improved key dermatological parameters. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of PDA@SC as a platform that can drive technological progress in wearable therapeutics and cosmetics.

articles.title: Triple-Encoding Platform for Multiplexed In Situ Profiling of Extracellular Vesicle miRNAs Enables Precision Diagnosis of Ovarian Cancer
articles.abstract: Ovarian cancer, the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, urgently demands early and accurate diagnostic methods. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tEVs) hold great promise as noninvasive biomarkers, yet their clinical translation is severely hampered by inherent heterogeneity and the inability of conventional assays to detect multiple types of biomarkers. To break this bottleneck, we developed a novel one-pot, triple-encoding platform that integrates size–fluorescence-encoded beads with a membrane fusion strategy. This enables simultaneous in situ profiling of 11 miRNAs across three distinct EV subpopulations defined by EpCAM/PD-L1 expression. Leveraging machine learning, an 11-miRNA logistic panel achieved tumor versus health discrimination (AUC = 0.995), and a combinatorial signature based on EV subpopulations and miRNA profiles enabled the classification of ovarian cancer subtypes, achieving 78.6% accuracy in the validation cohort. Our work provides a versatile and scalable approach for multiparameter EV analysis, enabling comprehensive EV miRNA profiling and ovarian cancer classification.

articles.title: The Evolution of Vinyl Acetate Monomer Catalysis: From Feedstock Transitions to Active Site Engineering
articles.journal: Applied Catalysis B: Environment and Energy

articles.title: Orbital Coupling Engineering through P-Block Metal Doping in NiFe Layered Double Hydroxides for Enhanced Anion-Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck in anodic water splitting because of sluggish adsorption and desorption kinetics of O-containing intermediates. Optimizing the adsorption strength of various O-containing intermediates in accordance with the Sabatier principle involves the precise tuning of the active-site electronic structure. Herein, we explore a p-block metal-assisted synergism regulation strategy in NiFe layered double hydroxides (LDHs) by introducing group-13 elements (Al, Ga, In) as dopants. Among various doped LDHs, In-doped NiFe-LDH shows the highest OER activity by demanding an overpotential value of 298 mV at 10 mA/cm2 along with enhanced intrinsic turnover frequency and long-term stability. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals that In3+ preferentially occupies the Fe coordination sites, while valence-band X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VB-XPS) confirms enhanced electronic coupling in the Ni–O–In framework. Density functional theory (DFT) additionally suggests that the In 5p orbitals strongly hybridize with the O 2p and Ni 3d states, establishing a Ni3d-O2p-In5p electronic interaction that regulates the Ni electronic structure and optimizes the adsorption energies of O-containing intermediates. The resulting d-p-p orbital hybridization offers an efficient pathway for charge delocalization and strengthens the M–O covalency, thereby accelerating the OER kinetics. This study elucidates the structure–activity relationship and identifies p-block metal-induced orbital hybridization as an effective strategy for developing high-performance oxygen evolution electrocatalysts, offering an alternative to conventional transition-metal modification approaches.

articles.title: Synergy of Solid-State NMR and Dielectric Spectroscopy Reveals Synchronized Multi-Rotor Dynamics in Crystalline Supramolecular Gyroscopes
articles.abstract: Understanding the correlated dynamics of multiple molecular rotators in crystalline supramolecular assemblies is essential for designing functional molecular machines, yet deconvoluting the motions of distinct components remains inherently challenging due to the limitations of individual techniques. Here, we report a synergistic approach that combines solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SSNMR) and dielectric spectroscopy to quantitatively resolve multirotor dynamics in a family of isostructural supramolecular gyroscopic complex architectures composed of alkyl ammonium, crown ether, and metal halide hydrate. SSNMR unambiguously reveals both the tert-butylammonium cation and the 18-crown-6 macrocycle as independent rotators─a distinction often ambiguous in such systems. Crucially, by correlating SSNMR-derived dynamics of the crown ether with dielectric relaxation of the coordinated water molecule, we uncover their synchronized rotation across a wide temperature range, mediated by charge-assisted hydrogen bonding. These findings reveal a cooperative multirotor gyroscopic model featuring synchronous rotation of an integrated coaxial crown ether–water–ammonium trio-rotator, accompanied by correlated alkyl reorientation. This synergy validates the dielectric relaxation principle in a complex, multirotor crystalline environment where unambiguous peak assignment has been a longstanding challenge. This work establishes a generalizable methodology for dissecting complex, multicomponent dynamics in crystalline materials, directly bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopic dielectric response.

articles.title: Clarifying the Clinical Relevance of V Waves
Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease
articles.abstract: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave–corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m 2 , P <0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P <0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P <0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P <0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P <0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P =0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid–A wave PAWP (R 2 =0.96 versus R 2 =0.86, P <0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P <0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53–2.86]; P <0.001).
