More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

articles.title: Asymmetrical Parental Investment Across Breeding Stages in the Globally Endangered Egyptian Vulture (Neophron percnopterus) in Nepal
articles.abstract: Understanding sex‐specific parental roles is critical for interpreting reproductive strategies in long‐lived, monogamous birds with low fecundity. Birds of prey often exhibit asymmetric biparental care; however, empirical evidence from South Asia, mainly on Neophron percnopterus ginginianus sub‐species remains limited. We investigated breeding phenology and sex‐specific parental investment between 2021 and 2024, across breeding stages of the globally endangered Egyptian Vulture, Neophron percnopterus ginginianus, in the Kaski district, which supports a high density of the species' breeding population. We monitored 46 breeding attempts to document breeding phenology and conducted behavioral observations at 38 unique breeding attempts from 17 nests, comprising 20 nest‐building, 18 incubation, and 18 chick‐rearing attempts. Using generalized linear mixed‐effects models and an information‐theoretic model‐selection approach, we evaluated sex‐specific parental investment and the influence of offspring development and environmental conditions on breeding behavior. Breeding onset varied among nests and years, with nest‐building occurring predominantly in March, and the overall breeding cycle lasted approximately 18.4 weeks. Egyptian Vultures exhibited bi‐parental care throughout the breeding cycle, but parental roles were asymmetric and varied among stages. Males delivered nesting materials more frequently than females, whereas females contributed more to nesting material maintenance. During incubation, both sexes contributed similarly to incubation effort, while incubation bout duration decreased with increasing sunlight exposure. During chick‐rearing, females were most likely to attend and spent longer duration at nests and feeding chicks when present, whereas males delivered more food more frequently. Food provisioning rate increased with chick age, whereas feeding duration decreased with increasing precipitation. Chick became increasingly independent as they developed, with the probability of self‐feeding increasing with chick age. Aggression by chicks toward parents also increased with chick age and was directed predominantly toward females. Overall, our findings reveal complementary and stage‐dependent parental roles in Egyptian Vultures, with males contributing more strongly to resource acquisition and females investing more in direct offspring care. These findings provide detailed evidence of how parental roles shift across the breeding cycle and offer region‐specific insights into the reproductive ecology of this globally endangered scavenger.

articles.title: Borrowing Data From Other Populations to Forecast Epidemic Size
articles.abstract: Forecasting infectious disease dynamics is important for ecological management and emerging disease preparedness, yet many systems lack the long‐term datasets required to develop reliable predictions. Spatial replication may provide an alternative by allowing information to be shared among populations, but the extent to which this improves forecasting remains unclear. Here, I used epidemic and temperature data from 20 replicated semi‐natural Daphnia–parasite pond populations monitored across four seasons (80 epidemics) to test whether information from multiple populations improves forecasts and whether environmental similarity identifies informative populations. I forecasted disease prevalence, infected host density, and healthy host density using a benchmark model, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and time‐series regression models. Models were trained using focal‐population data alone, mean dynamics across other populations, or temperature‐weighted mean dynamics from environmentally similar populations. Epidemics showed strong seasonal structure, with prevalence and infected host density generally peaking during the warmest period of the season. However, no forecasting approach consistently outperformed others across all variables. Temperature improved forecasts of prevalence and infected host density but not healthy host density. Multi‐population training improved forecasts in some cases, particularly for ARIMA models, whereas temperature‐weighted averaging provided no additional benefit over simple averaging. Regression models consistently produced the most accurate forecasts of healthy host density. These results show that borrowing information among populations can improve forecasts under specific conditions but is not universally beneficial, highlighting the importance of matching forecasting approaches and data sources to the ecological processes being predicted.

articles.title: Compromised Refugia: Latitudinal Gradients Mimic Depth and Constrain Subtropical Reef Habitats in the Nilotic Basin
articles.abstract: Upper‐mesophotic rocky reefs (25–30 m depth) have been proposed as climate refugia in the ultra‐oligotrophic Eastern Mediterranean for fish communities in warming shallow waters. A pronounced environmental gradient runs from north to south along the southeastern Levant, driven by sediment and nutrient discharge downstream of the receding Nile Delta. We hypothesized that higher surface productivity near the Nile Delta would support an algae‐dominated epibenthic food web and richer fish assemblages at the southern sites. We surveyed epibenthic cover, habitat structure, and fish assemblages at five sites spanning ~160 km of coastline within a shared 25–30 m depth band between 2017 and 2022. Contrary to this hypothesis, our findings reveal a distinct coastal ecocline, a benthic shift from algae‐ to bryozoan‐dominated epibenthos that closely mirrored the depth‐related shift observed at the northern sites (between 10 m and 45 m). This benthic shift was coupled with reduced abundance of herbivorous and micro‐invertivorous fish and with significantly lower fish species richness and diversity at the southern sites, despite their higher structural complexity. Redundancy analysis showed that depth, latitude, visibility, and season together explained 55.5% of the variance in epibenthic community composition, while an analogous spatial model explained 20% of the variance in fish abundance. This benthic shift, associated with gradients in depth, latitude, sedimentation, and light attenuation, appears to be a major architect of fish community structure in this region, rather than structural complexity. This implies that the southern Levant may act not as a corridor but as a restrictive filter, trapping species between warming surface waters and a deep‐sea‐like habitat that lacks the conditions required to support higher trophic levels; the capacity of upper‐mesophotic reefs to serve as thermal refugia is not uniform across space.

articles.title: Desert Milkweed (Asclepias erosa) as a Midsummer Resource for Arthropod Communities in the Great Basin Desert
articles.abstract: In arid ecosystems, consumer communities are often structured by strong temporal fluctuations in resource availability. During midsummer in the Great Basin Desert, high temperatures and declining soil moisture cause many early‐season plants to senesce, potentially concentrating arthropod activity on the few species that remain physiologically active. We characterized arthropod assemblages associated with the desert milkweed (Asclepias erosa) to evaluate its potential role as a focal plant during this seasonal period of reduced floral and vegetative productivity. Arthropods were surveyed on randomly selected plants across four sites in northern Nevada during June 2025 using standardized observations, during which arthropod identity, behavior, and location on the plant were recorded. Across 41 plants, we recorded 1779 arthropod individuals representing 67 morphospecies across six orders. Arthropods occupied nearly all plants surveyed and used all aboveground plant structures, including flowers, leaves, and stems. Community composition was highly skewed toward a few dominant taxa, with two dipteran morphospecies accounting for over 40% of all recorded individuals. Furthermore, the majority of morphospecies were rare in their distribution, occurring on fewer than three plants. Flowering plants supported significantly greater arthropod abundance and morphospecies richness than vegetative plants; however, most vegetative individuals also harbored arthropods. While nectar‐feeding individuals accounted for many observations, numerous arthropods were resting, moving among plant structures, or occupying stems and leaves without actively feeding, indicating that A. erosa may also provide structural habitat, refuge from thermal stress, and opportunities for predation or other trophic interactions. These results provide baseline natural history data on plant–arthropod interactions in Great Basin Desert system and suggest that A. erosa may function as a localized resource patch supporting diverse arthropod assemblages during the midsummer period of resource limitation.

articles.title: Dual‐Locus Metabarcoding Reveals Dry‐Season Dietary Differentiation Between Elephants and Impalas in a South African Savanna
articles.abstract: Large herbivores in African savannas experience intense nutritional constraints during the dry season when declining forage quality intensifies competition for limited resources. Sympatric mixed feeders are therefore expected to differ in their use of forage resources, yet specific plant taxa underlying these dietary differences remain poorly resolved. Here, we used dual‐locus DNA metabarcoding (rbcL and trnL) to characterise and compare dry‐season diets of African elephants (Loxodonta africana) and impalas (Aepyceros melampus) in a semi‐arid savanna ecosystem in South Africa. Despite substantial differences in body size and digestive physiology, dietary alpha diversity did not differ significantly between herbivores for either marker. In contrast, FOO‐based Jaccard beta‐diversity analyses revealed significant differences in dietary composition between species for both markers, with the strongest differentiation detected using trnL. Pianka's niche overlap index and relative read abundance analyses supported these patterns, showing lower overlap between species than within‐species. Both herbivores relied heavily on woody taxa during the dry season. Elephants consumed a narrower assemblage dominated by browse genera such as Grewia, Dichrostachys and Vachellia, whereas impalas incorporated a more compositionally diverse mixture of woody, graminoid and forb taxa. Our findings demonstrate that dry‐season dietary differentiation between these mixed feeders is associated less with differences in overall dietary breadth than with fine‐scale taxonomic differences and contrasting use of woody, graminoid and forb resources. These results highlight the potential importance of maintaining taxonomic and growth‐form heterogeneity in forage resources to support savanna herbivore assemblages under increasingly variable environmental conditions.

articles.title: Mitogenomic Insights Into the Ancient Split and Cryptic Diversity of the Poecilochirus carabi Complex (Acari: Mesostigmata)
articles.abstract: Phoretic associations with insects are widespread in the Mesostigmata. These temporary symbiotic associations have been important in driving the evolutionary development of this taxon. The phoretic mite genus Poecilochirus, which is considered obligately associated with burying beetles, is of great value in forensic entomology. However, due to the morphological conservatism and the difficulty of obtaining adult specimens, the taxonomy of this genus has long been based on deutonymphal characters, and the true species diversity is far from resolved. Here we used next‐generation sequencing to determine, for the first time, the complete mitochondrial genomes of P. austroasiaticus, P. subterraneus, and two distinct lineages of P. carabi (BJ1 and BJ2). All the sequenced mitogenomes contain 37 genes with a gene order identical to that of the ancestral arthropod arrangement and they all show pronounced AT bias and negative GC skew. All 13 protein‐coding genes are under strong purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1). Sliding window analysis identifies nad2 and nad5 as nucleotide diversity hotspots, which could serve as high‐resolution markers for future species delimitation. Phylogenetic reconstruction tentatively recovered Poecilochirus as paraphyletic with Parasitus nested within it (ML = 44%, BI = 0.982), while Parasitinae and Pergamasinae are not reciprocally monophyletic. The cox1 genetic distance between P. carabi BJ1 and BJ2 reached 0.409, with both mPTP and ASAP analyses of the mitogenomic dataset partitioning them into separate candidate molecular operational taxonomic units. Bayesian divergence time estimation revealed that the two lineages diverged in the Eocene about 52.4 million years ago (Ma), before the split between the morphologically recognized species P. subterraneus and P. davydovae (39.0 Ma). Our results give strong molecular evidence for cryptic speciation within the P. carabi complex and provide a solid genomic foundation for the future systematic and taxonomic research in the Parasitidae.

articles.title: Soil Moisture and Prey Life Cycles Promote Seasonal Dietary Shift in a Grassland‐Breeding Migratory Shorebird
articles.abstract: Understanding the dietary flexibility of migratory birds is essential for predicting their resilience to rapid environmental changes. For the continental black‐tailed godwit (Limosa limosa limosa), precise knowledge of seasonal diets and the underlying causes of prey selection on their breeding grounds has remained limited. This is largely due to challenges of observing foraging in tall vegetation and the rapid digestion of soft‐bodied prey. We utilized DNA metabarcoding of 207 fecal samples to describe the diet of flock‐foraging godwits in southwest Friesland, the Netherlands, during pre‐nesting (March) and post‐nesting (May–June) periods. To assess whether dietary changes were resource or selectivity based, we simultaneously quantified soil macrofauna biomass and measured biophysical variables, including soil moisture content, soil penetration resistance, and vegetation height. Earthworms (Lumbricidae) and leatherjackets (Tipulidae) were the primary prey taxa detected. A significant dietary taxa shift occurred between periods: earthworm relative read abundance (RRA) dropped from 73% pre‐nesting to 21% post‐nesting, while that of leatherjackets increased from 3% to 47%. While earthworms were consumed in proportion to their soil biomass in March, their selectivity declined significantly in May and June as soils became drier and harder. Conversely, leatherjacket consumption was higher in the post‐nesting period as their individual biomass increased. Our results demonstrate that the seasonal shift in godwit diet is caused by an interaction between prey life cycles and habitat conditions that impact prey harvestability. Soil desiccation post‐nesting reduces the detectability and accessibility of earthworms, even when they remain present in the soil, potentially forcing birds to switch to leatherjackets as they become more profitable. As climate change and intensive land use exacerbate soil drying in agricultural grasslands, the window for godwits to access earthworms is narrowing. This study highlights that maintaining high soil moisture is critical not just for prey abundance, but to ensure food remains accessible to meadow birds during the vital fueling period before southbound migration.

articles.title: Stand and Landscape Drivers of Trap Captures of the Pine Wilt Disease Vector Monochamus alternatus (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) in the Qinling Mountains
articles.abstract: Monochamus alternatus (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) is the principal vector of pine wilt disease, one of the most destructive forest diseases affecting conifer ecosystems in East Asia. However, the relative roles of stand structure and surrounding landscape context in shaping spatial variation in trap captures of this vector in mountainous forests remain poorly understood. The associations of stand‐ and landscape‐level factors with trap captures of M. alternatus were assessed in the Qinling Mountains of central China, a topographically complex region experiencing rapid expansion of pine wilt disease. Twenty pine forest plots were monitored with pheromone traps from April to October 2023, and stand characteristics and landscape variables were quantified at multiple spatial scales. Generalized linear models and multimodel inference showed that the proportion of Pinus massoniana within stands was significantly positively associated with beetle trap captures, whereas the proportion of construction land within a 250 m radius was strongly negatively associated with beetle trap captures (p = 0.006, ∑wi = 1). Stand and landscape predictors contributed comparably to explaining spatial variation in trap captures. These results indicate that local host composition and fine‐scale anthropogenic disturbance are associated with spatial variation in M. alternatus adult activity in mountainous forest landscapes. The identification of 250 m as the spatial scale of strongest landscape association provides a spatially explicit reference for improving surveillance and management strategies for pine wilt disease in topographically complex forest systems.

articles.title: Sustainable Landscaping and Sustainability Education on a College Campus: A Case Study in Place‐Based, Collaborative Ecosystem Science
articles.abstract: Sustainability education on college campuses can leverage interdisciplinary collaborations between facilities services, sustainability offices, environmental studies researchers, and students to provide hands‐on opportunities for place‐based learning. In an effort led by student researchers that could be replicated in academic practice at other academic institutions, we collaborated across campus groups to improve campus landscaping and turfgrass management. Turfgrass is an ideal cover for high‐traffic areas and recreation, but is energy intensive to maintain, inefficient at carbon sequestration, and requires fertilizing which contributes to nutrient pollution. Here, we outline a student‐led research effort that combined experiential learning, using a college campus as a “living laboratory,” and an ecosystem services case study to advance not only campus sustainability goals but also provide a rigorous research opportunity for undergraduates. Supported by a collaborative, multi‐office team at Macalester College, students provided recommendations on campus land management practices that would increase a multi‐faceted suite of sustainability goals. Student researchers used geospatial data to measure campus land cover types then adapted an easily accessible ecosystem model, i‐Tree, to quantify changes to ecosystem services due to converting strategic parcels of lawn to native plant beds or trees. Based on model results, students proposed increasing Macalester's tree cover to 30% campus area and converting 6381 m2 of lawn to low‐input native gardens. These landscape changes were modeled to sequester 26.3 tons of carbon year−1 for a value of USD $521 year−1 and remove air pollutants, a health benefit valued at USD $1034 year−1. This proposal balanced campus climate and environmental sustainability goals, Facilities' labor and economic constraints, and landscaping use goals. This use case of a college campus as a “living laboratory” offers a novel case study that empowered undergraduates and can be adapted to similar campuses that integrate the work and expertise of multiple students, faculty, and staff.

articles.title: The Complete Chloroplast Genome of Dioscorea hypoglauca: Comparative Genomics and Phylogenetic Insights
articles.abstract: The complete chloroplast genome of Dioscorea hypoglauca—a medicinal plant native to southern China—was assembled and characterized. The genome is circular, 153,219 bp in length, and follows the typical quadripartite organization: a large single‐copy (LSC) region of 83,692 bp, a small single‐copy (SSC) region of 18,813 bp, and two inverted repeat (IR) regions, each 25,357 bp. In total, 129 genes were annotated, including 84 protein‐coding genes, 37 tRNA genes, and eight rRNA genes. Thirty‐five simple sequence repeats (SSRs) were detected; most were mononucleotide A/T repeats. A comparison with 22 other Dioscorea species showed that IR boundaries vary considerably across the genus. One notable finding is the boundary shift of the ycf1 gene in D. hypoglauca, which has not been observed in other examined species. Nucleotide diversity (Pi) analysis revealed that intergenic spacers‐especially rpl22‐rps19 (Pi = 0.11204)‐are highly variable, whereas tRNA genes are extremely conserved. Codon usage analysis indicated a strong bias toward A/T‐ending codons. Phylogenetic reconstruction based on complete plastomes (using maximum likelihood and Bayesian inference) placed D. hypoglauca as a close relative of D. aspersa and D. pyrifolia. Overall, these results clarify the systematic position of D. hypoglauca, illustrate the dynamic evolution of IR regions within Dioscorea, and provide a genomic resource for future evolutionary and population genetic studies.

articles.title: The Complete Chromosome‐Level Genome and Mitogenome Assembly of Seriola lalandi lalandi (Yellowtail Kingfish) for Aquaculture and Fisheries Management
articles.abstract: Seriola lalandi comprises three genetically distinct clades, with S. lalandi lalandi inhabiting the Southern Hemisphere. While a chromosome‐level genome exists for the Northwestern Pacific S. lalandi aureovittata, no such resource is available for S. lalandi lalandi, limiting genetic research and aquaculture advancements. This study presents a high‐quality chromosome‐level genome assembly of S. lalandi lalandi using Illumina short‐read, long‐read (ONT) and Hi‐C. A total of 289.12 Gb of raw genomic data were generated, and a final assembly of 644 Mb was produced with 99.64% of the assembled bases anchored into 24 pseudo‐chromosomes. Genome annotation identified 24,600 protein‐coding genes, with 96.1% completeness based on 3640 Benchmarking Universal Single‐Copy Orthologues (BUSCO). Additionally, the complete mitogenome was assembled and annotated for S. lalandi lalandi. This genomic resource will help to inform comparative genomic studies, improve aquaculture breeding programmes, and support appropriate fishery strategies, particularly in Aotearoa New Zealand, where S. lalandi lalandi is a culturally significant species for Māori.

articles.title: Drought and soil macrofauna functional diversity effects on Mediterranean tree growth in an Ecotron ecosystem experiment
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract The intensity, frequency and severity of drought events are projected to increase in the Mediterranean region under ongoing climate change. This may impact plant growth and survival in Mediterranean forests leading to altered ecosystem dynamics. The functional diversity of soil macrofauna may have a critical role in mitigating negative climate change effects as it determines soil structure and regulates biogeochemical cycling as well as water retention. However, very little is known on how changes in climate and soil biodiversity conjointly influence plant growth. In a 5‐year experiment, we tested two levels of soil macrofauna functional diversity (Low and High), using combinations of endogeic and anecic earthworms, diplopods and isopods, and measured growth and biomass allocation in three tree species (Acer monspessulanum, Arbutus unedo and Quercus pubescens) as well as total tree biomass production. Our results showed that tree growth was overall only moderately affected by stronger drought and functional diversity of soil macrofauna. The effects of functional diversity of soil macrofauna differed among tree species. High functional diversity was associated with greater stem diameter in Q. pubescens. In contrast, low functional diversity was associated with greater stem diameter in A. unedo and proportionally greater biomass allocation to roots in A. monspessulanum. Individual macrofauna groups had stronger effects than overall functional diversity. Endogeic earthworm presence was associated with greater ecosystem‐level fine root and total plant biomass, but with lower fine root and total biomass in A. unedo. Diplopod presence was associated with greater stem diameter and higher total tree biomass in Q. pubescens. Overall, four consecutive summers of intensified drought had few significant effects on tree growth and biomass production, possibly because of high variability among individual trees. Most macrofauna effects were independent of drought, although drought modified the effect of diplopods on ecosystem‐level shoot biomass. These results show that macrofauna effects on tree growth depend on both macrofauna group and tree species identity. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: HGTScanner: Detecting horizontal gene transfer at the fine scale using whole organelle genomes
articles.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) has profoundly shaped eukaryotic organellar genomes like plant mitochondria. Yet no generalized tools are currently available to efficiently characterize HGT across these genomes due to both high structural complexity and low sequence divergence compared to prokaryotic HGTs. Accurate identification of HGT, including the genomic location and donor lineage, is critical for understanding its impact on genetic novelty and genome evolution as well as species interactions that generate HGTs. Here, we introduce HGTScanner, a Python tool to characterize HGT across whole organellar genomes. HGTScanner automatically establishes homology, produces alignments and phylogenies, and tests hypotheses of HGT based on BLAST, phylogeny and synteny. It contains a built‐in database of green plant (Viridiplantae) organellar sequences to facilitate the characterization of promiscuous mitochondrial HGTs and mitochondrial plastid DNAs (MTPTs) in plants but may also be adapted to other organisms like fungi which share many similar genomic features. Using benchmark data from the early diverging angiosperm Amborella and parasitic plant Orobanchaceae, we demonstrate that HGTScanner can effectively locate and identify the donor lineages of MTPT and HGT. In Amborella, we recovered the well‐documented fusion of moss and green algae mitochondria, and discovered prevalent HGTs from the New Caledonian parasitic plant Hachettea (Mystropetalaceae). In the parasitic Orobanchaceae, non‐native MTPTs are strongly linked with their sympatrically distributed host plants. HGTScanner is an efficient and flexible tool that can drive discoveries of HGT without a priori knowledge regarding the donor identity. The sympatric distribution of donor‐recipient pairs in HGT events suggests that HGTs can serve as valuable genetic markers for organismal interactions across time and terrain.

articles.title: Limited Lifetime Costs of Inbreeding in a Large Wild Population of Superb Fairy‐Wrens
articles.abstract: Inbreeding depression can have major negative effects on both individual fitness and population performance. The impact of inbreeding depression in wild populations remains poorly understood, and our knowledge is primarily based on estimations in insular populations with limited dispersal, which has been predicted to enhance the capacity for outcrossing. Limited migration and small population sizes, which make insular and endangered populations tractable models for fieldwork, often experience low genetic variation and may be subject to stronger inbreeding effects. Estimating inbreeding effects is difficult in many populations because pedigrees of migrants are unknown. Genomic data offer methods to estimate realised inbreeding even in migrants. Here, we apply genomic methods to a superb fairy‐wren (Malurus cyaneus) population that has been subject to detailed study of fitness variation over three decades. The population has sex‐biased dispersal, resulting in many immigrant females. We use genomic inbreeding estimates to explicitly test for inbreeding depression across several key components of individual fitness, including nestling condition, juvenile survival and adult traits. Genomic methods were able to recover previous pedigree‐based findings of inbreeding depression in early nestling condition and additionally identified some evidence for inbreeding depression in fledgling but not juvenile mortality. The only adult fitness trait affected, male extra‐pair paternity, is highly variable and under strong sexual selection. Our findings suggest that natural populations experiencing high effective population sizes and regular dispersal might be less affected by inbreeding depression than previously assumed based on studies of often insular and smaller populations.

articles.title: High-output elastomeric SBS/PAN piezoelectric nanofibrous membranes via thermal engineering
[Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
articles.abstract: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

articles.title: [Health Policy] Strengthening health systems to prioritise, provide care, and prevent osteoarthritis: a roadmap for global health policy
articles.abstract: By 2050, almost 1 billion people are expected to live with osteoarthritis—a disabling musculoskeletal condition with currently no cure. Despite its burden and costs, osteoarthritis remains largely invisible in national and global health agendas, is poorly integrated within service models for other chronic health conditions, and is frequently perceived as inevitable with ageing and associated with limited therapeutic options. This context drives an osteoarthritis identity problem that fuels frustration among those living with the disease and health-care professionals, perpetuates stigma and inequities, undermines access to effective interventions, and crucially, deprioritises osteoarthritis in health policy.

articles.title: Emerging trends in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis
articles.abstract: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.

articles.title: CNT-Mediated Integration of Pd and In2O3 Circumvents Activity–Stability Trade-Off in CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
articles.abstract: Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability (>230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.

articles.title: Curvature-Induced Electric-Field Effects Govern Controllable N2 Electrocatalysis on Single-Atom Catalysts
articles.abstract: Electric field-enhanced electrocatalysis represents an innovative strategy for improving the efficiency of electrochemical transformations. However, quantitative evaluation of microscopic electric-field effects under operando conditions remains challenging, limiting a rigorous, predictive understanding of field-mediated reaction regulation. Here, by integrating rigorous numerical methods, constant-potential microkinetic simulations, and machine learning models, we establish electric-field intensity as a quantitative descriptor that directly correlates local fields with catalytic performance. Using curvature-engineered M–N–C single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we demonstrate that curvature-induced electric fields modulate electron occupation at active sites and shift the potential of zero charge in a controllable manner. This field-driven electronic perturbation selectively tunes adsorbate binding energetics, thereby dictating limiting potentials, steering reaction pathways, and governing the thermodynamics and kinetics of interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer in nitrogen electroreduction. Notably, we uncover an inverted volcano–type dependence of catalytic activity on curvature, wherein optimal activity is achieved within a moderate field-strength window. This nonmonotonic trend underscores the necessity of balanced curvature regulation, rather than simply maximizing field intensity, in optimizing electrocatalytic performance. These findings provide a quantitative framework for monitoring and regulating catalytic trends under realistic operating conditions via curvature-induced electric fields, offering generalizable design principles for diverse SAC systems and electrochemical reactions.

articles.title: Diffusion-Selective Modulation Strategy for Enhanced Propane Dehydrogenation via Mixing Inert CHA Zeolite
articles.abstract: Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.

articles.title: Hydration Changes are Essential for Efficient Breakdown of Faropenem by the L1 Metallo-β-lactamase
articles.abstract: Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. The calculated free energy barriers for the formation of both products are consistent with the experimentally determined catalytic constant, and the calculated greater stability of the imine with its crystallographic observation. These simulations provide dynamic insight into L1 catalysis, highlighting features that can be exploited for inhibitor design.

articles.title: Mild Heterogeneous Thiophene Hydrogenation Enabled by a Modified Palladium Catalyst
articles.abstract: Thiophenes are readily available sulfur heteroarenes and prominent motifs in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, but their direct heterogeneous hydrogenation to thiolanes remains challenging due to sulfur-induced catalyst deactivation and competing hydrodesulfurization. Here, we report a chloroform-induced surface modification strategy that enables the heterogeneous Pd(OH)2/C-catalyzed hydrogenation of thiophenes to saturated sulfur heterocycles. The method proceeds under mild hydrogenation conditions and provides access to a range of alkyl-, silyl-, aryl-, and benzofused thiolane derivatives. A hydrogenation-focused robustness assessment revealed compatibility with several functional groups that are commonly sensitive under Pd/H2 conditions, while preparative scope studies showed that functional-group-containing thiophenes can be converted when potentially interfering motifs are separated from the thiophene core by suitable alkyl or aryl spacers. Mechanistic experiments indicate that CHCl3 is not merely a beneficial solvent: CHCl3/H2 pretreatment of Pd(OH)2/C generates a catalytically competent material whose activity is retained after replacing CHCl3 with 2-MeTHF. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) analyses support the formation of persistent chloroform-derived organochlorine/C–Cl-type surface environments and chlorocarbon fragments. These findings establish solvent-induced catalyst modification as a useful design principle for challenging heterogeneous hydrogenations of sulfur-containing heteroarenes.

articles.title: Formamidinium-Solvent Intermediates Mediate Self-Seeding Crystallization for Efficient Inverted α-FAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.

articles.title: Improving the Calendar Life of Silicon Anodes with Inorganic Solid–Electrolyte Interphases
articles.abstract: Silicon anodes unlock higher energy density in Li-ion batteries but suffer from poor calendar life due to inadequately passivating solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Here, we contrast the calendar aging behaviors of single- and mixed-salt locally superconcentrated electrolytes (LSCEs) against carbonate electrolytes. Mixed-salt LSCE cells retained 96% and 44% of precalendar capacity after one month and then after five months, while carbonate electrolyte cells retained 77% and 1%, respectively. The mixed-salt LSCE advantage is tied to the formation of a predominantly inorganic SEI, evidenced by nanoscale Fourier transform infrared spectromicroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and 3D time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry. After 5 months, however, perturbations to SEIs were evident in all cells, accelerating voltage decay and capacity loss by lithium inventory loss associated with SEI growth. These findings suggest that future electrolytes may benefit from strategies that continuously reinforce the SEI through controlled anion and solvent redox in LSCEs.

articles.title: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers
articles.abstract: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell–tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

articles.title: Oncolytic Virus-like Nanoparticle Targets the Golgi Apparatus via Sphingomyelin
articles.abstract: The Golgi apparatus (GA) has emerged as a promising target for cancer therapy. Commonly, therapeutics are guided to the GA by recognizing specific receptors on the GA membrane. However, the low and heterogeneous expression of these receptors often results in suboptimal targeting efficiency. Here, we present an oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle for GA targeting by exploiting sphingomyelin, an abundant component of the GA membrane. This nanoparticle consisted of a polymeric nanocarrier complexed with a plasmid encoding the secreting peptide-deleted α-hemolysin (αHL), a pore-forming protein with high affinity for sphingomyelin. The nanoparticle could transfect cancer cells to induce intracellular expression of αHL, enabling GA targeting through binding to GA-associated sphingomyelin while bypassing the cell membrane. Consequently, the transfected cells exhibited GA structural disassembly and underwent a pyroptosis-like programmed cell death with immunogenic characteristics. Notably, αHL-rich microvesicles were subsequently secreted, effectively killing neighboring tumor cells. Intratumoral administration of this formulation significantly suppressed subcutaneous tumor growth and elicited robust antitumor immunity, preventing tumor rechallenge. Furthermore, by incorporating iRGD-modified polymers, we constructed a tumor-targeting oncolytic virus-like nanoparticle with neutral surface charge. Following intravenous administration, this iRGD-modified nanoparticle could efficiently suppress tumor growth without causing obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work presents a robust strategy for GA-targeting via sphingomyelin recognition, providing a potential approach for GA-targeted anticancer therapeutics.

articles.title: pH-Programmed Poly(amino acid) Nanoparticles for Mucus-Penetrating and Bacteria-Targeted Eradication of Helicobacter pylori
articles.abstract: The global prevalence of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection stands in stark contrast to the limited clinical efficacy of antibiotics, primarily attributed to their rapid inactivation under gastric acidity and poor penetration through the gastric mucus barrier. Here, we report a pH-programmed poly(amino acid)-based nanoplatform for the precise eradication of H. pylori. This platform is constructed from poly(amino acid) block copolymers (FAR) incorporating d-aminoalanine side chains and rhamnolipid (RHL) moieties, which self-assemble into amoxicillin-loaded nanoparticles (Am@FAR NPs). Under strongly acidic gastric conditions (pH < 3), Am@FAR NPs undergo extensive protonation, adopting a compact, stabilized configuration that suppresses premature drug release and preserves antibiotic activity. Upon entering the gastric mucus layer (pH ∼ 4–6), partial deprotonation induces surface charge reversal, reducing nonspecific mucin adhesion and facilitating efficient mucus penetration. Cooperative recognition, mediated by RHL and d-aminoalanine residues, enables selective targeting of H. pylori within the mucus niche; here, further local pH elevation (∼6–7) triggers particle swelling and on-site drug release. Consequently, Am@FAR NPs achieve 99.99% eradication efficiency against H. pyloriin vivo, offering a highly effective and biocompatible strategy for the treatment of gastric H. pylori infections.

Practical Considerations for Operando 7Li Nuclear Magnetic Resonance in Coin and Pouch Cells
articles.abstract: Operando nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy provides unique insight into chemical changes in batteries during use but has largely been limited to custom plastic cells. Unfortunately, the metal casings that house commercial batteries distort and shield radiofrequency (RF) fields required for excitation and detection in NMR. Here, we use operando7Li NMR spectroscopy to study metal-encased batteries in both coin and pouch cell formats without modifying the cell or casing. We benchmark NMR spectra obtained from stainless-steel coin cells and aluminum-laminate pouch cells to plastic coin cells and show that casing composition, auxiliary hardware, and sample placement strongly influence observed shift, signal intensity, and line shape due to bulk magnetic susceptibility effects and RF attenuation upon interacting with cell parts. These effects are most severe in stainless-steel coin cells (and in particular 304-grade stainless steel) but can be mitigated through the use of Al spacers while retaining the stainless-steel caps and springs. In light of these considerations, we leverage operando7Li NMR to track lithium plating/stripping and monitor the accumulation of electrochemically inactive “dead” lithium (Li0) during galvanostatic cycling in coin and pouch cells. In pouch cells, the lean electrolyte volume allows us to resolve changes in the 7Li electrolyte signal during formation that are consistent with electrolyte redistribution and wetting. Taken together, these results demonstrate how to alter cell susceptibility to improve NMR signals during operando measurements in commercially relevant form factors while also establishing the cell design constraints that limit quantitative interpretation.

articles.title: Unraveling the Mystery of Near-Infrared Emission in an Antimony Halide Dimer Driven by the Jahn–Teller Effect
articles.abstract: Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Here, we report the observation of an NIR-II emission signal (band gap = 1.13 eV) from a (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 single crystal at room temperature. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A strategy that spatially confines 5s2 ions within edge-shared [Sb2Cl8]2– units with controlled lattice distortion is proposed to cause a Jahn–Teller effect (JTE) during the interconfiguration transition (3P1 → 1S0). A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (λex = 330 nm; λem = 1100 nm). Leveraging the (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 sample, electroluminescence pumped by a UV-LED chip yields a highly efficient NIR-II emission, and the phosphor displays diverse functions in night vision and anticounterfeiting.

articles.title: Snail Inventories for Short‐Term Impacts: Methodological Differences and Their Underlying Causes
articles.abstract: In research on terrestrial gastropod communities, a fundamental methodological question is whether to include empty shells in the investigations alongside living individuals. In this study, we examined potential biases introduced in the analyses by the inclusion of fresh empty shells (with intact periostracum). We started by reanalysing a dataset about the short‐term effects of mowing and mulching on a grassland snail community. For the original analysis, only live specimen data were used, whereas here we used a so‐called combined dataset including live individuals and fresh empty shells. While the live data revealed significant negative impacts of mowing on the snail community, these effects were undetectable with the combined data. Concurrently, we observed substantial interspecific variation in the overrepresentation value among species (the ratio of a species' combined abundance to its live abundance), which represents a distortion in the distribution of the total number of individuals across species. To explore the underlying causes of this phenomenon, we investigated the physical and chemical resistance of the shells of eleven species under laboratory conditions and simulated the effects of life history traits and shell‐degradation rate on overrepresentation using a multistage population model. Contrary to expectations, our results indicated that this variation in overrepresentation was not explained by shell resistance but rather by shell size: significantly higher overrepresentation was observed in smaller species, even though their shells are weaker, so may decompose faster. This relationship may be driven by the faster life cycles and higher turnover rates of smaller species, a finding corroborated by our population model. We concluded that the inclusion of empty shells can significantly distort the perception of the instantaneous state of the community and mask short‐term temporal changes. We recommend prioritising live data for detecting short‐term impacts and explicitly stating and justifying the chosen data type in scientific publications.

Shrubs benefit from being functionally more conservative and distinct from neighbour trees
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Multi‐strata forests can enhance ecosystem functioning, with interactions between overstorey trees and understorey shrubs playing a pivotal role. However, how the structure and composition of neighbouring trees, together with shrub traits, influence shrub growth remains poorly understood. In a large‐scale subtropical biodiversity experiment manipulating tree and shrub species richness, we inventoried 4411 shrubs and their surrounding trees after 11 years of interactions. We found that individual shrub biomass declined with increasing neighbour tree species richness, basal area and functional diversity, but exhibited a U‐shaped trend with the proportion of ectomycorrhizal‐associated neighbour tree individuals. Shrubs with more conservative resource‐use strategies attained higher biomass, particularly when surrounded by trees with low functional diversity and a high proportion of ectomycorrhizal associations. Biomass was also greater when shrubs were more resource‐conservative and functionally distinct from the neighbouring trees. Our findings highlight how shrub functional traits, combined with tree diversity, competition and functional traits, shape tree–shrub interactions, with shrubs benefiting more from resource‐conservative and functionally distinct traits relative to their neighbouring trees. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Why don't all birds lay early? Causes and consequences of breeding timing for a long‐lived migratory seabird
articles.abstract: Why don't all birds lay early? Our 16‐year study of Manx shearwater behaviour shows that selection on breeding timing fluctuates among years. We also find that lay dates are influenced by persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration, and pair synchrony, potentially constraining breeding phenological advancement under ongoing climate change. Abstract The relationship between earlier laying and higher breeding success is well‐established in avian species. However, a wide distribution of breeding timings is often maintained within a population, and the causes and consequences of this variation require further exploration, particularly as many avian species advance breeding phenology in response to climate change. Using a 16‐year dataset combining colony observations and biologging of Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus), we show that earlier laying does not always result in higher breeding success, with later laying becoming less costly in recent years. We additionally report a slight advancement in breeding timing within breeding pairs, despite finding no temporal trends in spring bloom onset. Nonetheless, birds adjusted lay date in response to interannual variation in phytoplankton bloom timing, and years with stronger Celtic Sea blooms exhibited stronger selection for early breeding. Breeding timing was also influenced by repeatable individual differences in migratory behaviour, with birds undertaking generally earlier, shorter migrations to less southerly destinations laying earlier across years. However, lay date was not determined solely by individual behaviour. In this long‐lived species with stable pair bonds, the arrival date of the second‐returning bird constrained advancement in laying. This study suggests that variation in breeding timing is maintained through the combined effects of fluctuating selection, persistent individual differences, variation in non‐breeding duration and pair‐level processes. Competing Magnetic Configurations Enable Low-Field Magnetoresistance Switching in Cr3Te4
articles.abstract: Large magnetoresistance typically emerges from transitions between distinct electronic phases or magnetic configurations, yet controllable switching between competing magnetic configurations within a single metallic material remains challenging. Here we investigate magnetotransport in Cr3Te4 and demonstrate a magnetic-field-switchable resistance modulation of up to −37.6%, enabled by the near degeneracy between antiparallel and parallel magnetic configurations. Remarkably, a magnetic field of ∼0.25 T suffices to induce switching between these competing magnetic configurations, accompanied by a reconstruction in electronic transport supported by Boltzmann transport calculations. Substituting 5% of Cr with Co suppresses the switching behavior, consistent with a suppression of the competition between the nearly degenerate magnetic configurations, while the magnetoresistance evolves into a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, suggesting a possible Weyl-band-related contribution associated with a Co-induced upward shift of the Fermi level. Our results establish competing magnetic configurations as an effective route toward large magnetoresistance in structurally simple metallic systems.

articles.title: Continuously Tunable Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance of Anisotropic Gold Nanopolyhedrons for Multiplexed Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Imaging
articles.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is attractive for multiplex bioimaging owing to its excellent photostability and ultranarrow spectral bandwidth. However, achieving synergistic enhancement of excitation and Raman scattering fields remains challenging. Herein, the relationship between geometry and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) was investigated by continuously tuning the aspect ratio (AR) of anisotropic Au nanopolyhedrons (Au NPHs). Central-body modulation while preserving sharp terminal tips enables continuous LSPR tuning while retaining tip-associated electromagnetic enhancement. The SERS behavior was further analyzed by considering the spectral matching between the LSPR and the excitation/scattering wavelengths. For different excitation wavelengths, the optimal SERS response can be achieved by selecting Au NPHs whose LSPR band best matches with the excitation and Raman scattering wavelengths. These results demonstrate that Raman enhancement is governed by spectral matching rather than a fixed optimal geometry. The optimized Au NPHs enabled the use of dual SERS probes for proof-of-concept multiplex biomarker imaging.

articles.title: Experimental Signature of Transient Symmetry Breaking in a Cavity Dirty-Limit Superconductor
articles.abstract: Transient states of matter far from equilibrium may exhibit physical properties beyond those allowed by the equilibrium-state crystalline symmetries. We explore ultrafast and direct electronic excitations of transient states in a dirty-limit superconductor with time-resolved terahertz-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy. By embedding the superconductor into a designed microcavity structure of metallic split-ring resonators, we can sensitively probe the pump field-induced transient variations of the superconducting states around the cavity’s resonant frequency. Our results show that the strong terahertz field can transiently modify the symmetries of the electronic subsystems via the injection of a picosecond supercurrent, leading to high-order nonlinear dynamical responses that are not compatible with the equilibrium-state symmetries, which is evidence for transient symmetry breaking on the picosecond time scale.

articles.title: Probing Valence Electron Distributions at Subatomic Resolution in a Charge Density Wave Material
articles.abstract: Probing the internal electronic structure of complex materials with atomic spatial resolution has remained an outstanding challenge in condensed-matter science. A promising approach is convergent-beam electron diffraction (CBED) in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Here, we apply 4D-STEM CBED to the charge-density-wave (CDW) material 1T-TaS2. We demonstrate a qualitative breakdown of the conventional independent atom model (IAM) in reproducing the experimental CBED patterns. A robust low-angle intensity maximum is systematically absent in IAM-based simulations but is consistently reproduced in simulations that use electrostatic potentials derived from density functional theory. A comparison of CBED patterns with projected charge densities reveals a remarkable correspondence between the local real-space valence charge distribution and diffracted intensities, reflecting site-dependent charge density variations within the CDW structure. These results establish atomic-resolution CBED as an experimental probe of valence electron contributions to the scattering potential and open a route to resolving complex electronic ordering phenomena.

articles.title: [Perspectives] John Wong: making an impact on population health at scale
articles.abstract: “I’m concerned that the narrative now around ageing populations is one of doom and gloom. But long-lived populations are not the problem. The problem is that we haven’t allowed people to get to an older age healthy”, says John Wong, Executive Director of the Centre for Population Health at the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Executive Director of The Yong Pung How and Yong Wei-Woo Centre at the National University Health System (NUHS), Singapore. “Two-thirds of the world is now below the fertility replacement rate, and unless we keep our populations healthy throughout their whole lifespan, we’ll have this major challenge of more and more unwell older people”, continued Wong, who is also Isabel Chan Professor in Medical Sciences in the Division of Haematology-Oncology at the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, NUS, and Emeritus Consultant in the Department of Haematology-Oncology, National University Cancer Institute, NUHS, Singapore.

articles.title: [Review] Addressing threats to future global health—what is the right timeframe?
articles.abstract: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own.

articles.title: [The Lancet Commissions] The Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health
articles.abstract: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.

articles.title: Crystal Phase-Dependent Electronic Metal-Support Interactions Enable Chemoselective Hydrogenation of α, β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
articles.abstract: Electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) provide an effective means of tuning the electronic structure of supported metal catalysts and thereby modulating their catalytic properties. However, how the crystal phase of supports governs EMSI and in turn influences the selective hydrogenation remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a crystal-phase engineering strategy to precisely regulate EMSI in ultrafine Ir nanoclusters (NCs) supported on polymorphic Nb2O5. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization reveals that the orthorhombic Nb2O5-T phase forms a distinctive socketed metal-support interface that strongly anchors Ir NCs and induces substantial electron transfer from the support to the metal. Distinct from classical strong metal-support interactions that often compromise active-site accessibility, this socketed interfacial configuration simultaneously enhances EMSI, stabilizes the Ir NCs, and preserves abundant exposed active sites. The resulting electron-rich Ir species facilitates H2 activation and interfacial hydrogen spillover while favoring preferential adsorption of the carbonyl group over the C=C bond in α, β-unsaturated aldehydes. Consequently, Ir@Nb2O5-T exhibits high activity, selectivity, and durability for the selective hydrogenation to unsaturated alcohols under mild conditions, overcoming the typical activity–selectivity trade-off. This work establishes a direct crystal phase–EMSI–reactivity relationship and highlights crystal-phase engineering as a powerful strategy for manipulating metal–support interfaces toward highly selective heterogeneous catalysis.

articles.title: Engineering the Interfacial Microenvironment to Boost Ethane Dehydrogenation on Ga2O3-Pt Catalysts via Metal Doping Modulation
articles.abstract: Inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts have exhibited better catalytic performance in propane dehydrogenation due to their tunable interfacial electronic properties. This study explores the potential of inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts and their single-atom-doped variant (Ga2O3-M/Pt) systems for ethane dehydrogenation using DFT calculations and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. The results show that Ga2O3-Pt exhibits low ethylene formation activity (0.83 × 102 s–1) and selectivity (84.28%) due to its interfacial sites that weakly and uniformly adsorb hydrogen, impeding the differential regulation of key CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption behavior. Single-atom doping (M = Ti, Co, etc.) creates a Pt–M–O interfacial microenvironment, modulating the electronic structure of interfacial oxygen sites, which enables the effective differential regulation of CH2CH3* intermediate adsorption, thereby enhancing catalytic performance. Among the 14 screened dopants, the Ga2O3-Ti/Pt catalyst emerged as optimal, showing high activity (2.86 × 103 s–1) and selectivity (97.13%) for ethylene formation at the optimal 873.15 K and CH3CH3(g) partial pressure of 0.20 bar. This advantage stems from its moderate p-band center and Ti–O charge transfer, which yield an ideal hydrogen adsorption energy for CH2CH3* regulation. The H* adsorption energy can serve as a descriptor for qualitatively evaluating the activity of CH2CH2(g) formation for a series of Ga2O3-M/Pt catalysts. This work proposes the strategy of “interfacial microenvironment reconstruction to regulate the electronic structure” as a design method for developing high-efficiency alkane dehydrogenation catalysts.

articles.title: Enhanced Aqueous-Phase Hydrodeoxygenation of Fatty Acids over CoP Anchored on P–N Co-Doped Carbon
articles.abstract: The aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of biomass-derived fatty acids offers an alternative route for the production of diesel-range hydrocarbons, but remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a hydrophobic CoP catalyst anchored on P–N co-doped carbon spheres (CoP@PNC-900), which exhibits high performance for the aqueous-phase hydrodeoxygenation of palmitic acid at 270 °C and 2 MPa H2, delivering nearly complete conversion together with over 99% yield of C15+C16 alkanes. The enhanced performance arises from the synergy between CoP active sites and the hydrophobic interface, which promotes C–O bond cleavage while enhancing the contact between hydrophobic substrates and catalytic sites. Isotopic-labeling experiments demonstrate that water acts exclusively as the reaction medium rather than a hydrogen source. In situ FT-IR–MS analysis combined with DFT calculations confirms the hydrodeoxygenation- and decarbonylation-related pathways, with C–O bond cleavage of the alcohol intermediate identified as the rate-determining step in the hydrodeoxygenation pathway. Moreover, the catalyst exhibits a broad substrate scope for various fatty acids and esters as well as stable recyclability under hydrothermal conditions. Finally, a preliminary life cycle assessment (LCA) highlights the potential environmental benefits of the aqueous-phase catalytic process. This work establishes an effective strategy that integrates active-site engineering with interfacial hydrophobic microenvironment regulation for the aqueous-phase valorization of biomass-derived fatty acids.

articles.title: LiH/FePcG-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis via Interfacial Hydride-Mediated Dinitrogen Activation
articles.abstract: Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions remains challenging because of the inertness of the N≡N bond and the limited ability of conventional catalysts to couple efficient dinitrogen activation with rapid hydrogenation. Here, we report a LiH/FePcG catalyst in which strong interfacial coupling between LiH and Fe–N–C sites enable efficient ammonia synthesis. Comprehensive characterization, including structural analysis, kinetic study, isotopic-labelling, gas-phase mass spectrometry, and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveal that the catalytic activity originates from interfacial active sites. Under reaction conditions, structural nitrogen atoms within the Fe–Nx moieties undergo reversible consumption and reconstruction, demonstrating the dynamic participation of the Fe–N–C framework in ammonia synthesis. Concurrently, hydridic hydrogen supplied by LiH directly participates in the initial hydrogenation steps, while the LiH/Fe–N–C interface generates Fe-centered multicomponent hydride species essential for N2 binding and activation. An inverse H/D kinetic isotope effect, an H2-promoted 28N2/30N2 exchange rate, in situ spectroscopic evidence, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations collectively support a non-classical, hydrogen-assisted pathway for dinitrogen activation rather than the conventional direct N≡ bond cleavage. These findings establish interfacial hydride chemistry as a cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis and provide a strategy for designing advanced catalysts under mild conditions.

articles.title: Mechanistic Investigation and Optimization of a Mixed-Oxide@Alkali Carbonate Redox Catalyst Platform for Enhanced Ethane Oxidative Dehydrogenation
articles.abstract: Chemical looping oxidative dehydrogenation (CL-ODH) of ethane has emerged as a promising alternative for ethylene production, with the potential to mitigate the environmental and sustainability concerns associated with conventional steam cracking. The main challenge of CL-ODH is the design of active and selective redox catalysts to enhance ethane activation while minimizing the generation of by-products such as COx (CO and CO2). This study employs ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations to investigate the formation and reactivity of oxygen species in mixed metal-oxides@Li2CO3 and Na2CO3 redox catalysts. Estimated reaction free energies are used as thermodynamic descriptors, while the computational insights are supplemented with experimental validations. Our analysis indicates that peroxide (O22–) and •OH radicals provide more favorable thermodynamic driving forces for ethane C–H activation at the outer carbonate surface than monatomic oxygen radical anion (O–) and superoxide (O2–). In addition, mechanistic investigations into COx formation reveal that the product water can interact with peroxide-derived species at the gas–carbonate interface to generate •OH radicals, consistent with prior experimental observations. In Li2CO3, •OH-mediated pathways retain favorable ethane C─H activation thermodynamics while reducing the driving force for selected COx-forming transformations relative to peroxide. These findings provide important mechanistic insights into the design and optimization of mixed-oxide@alkali carbonate core-shell redox catalysts for CL-ODH.

articles.title: Proton-Donor Identity Shapes Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction on Silver
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is a key reaction in nitrogen cycling and water remediation, yet the mechanistic interpretation of its voltammetric response remains poorly understood. On silver electrodes, cyclic voltammograms often display multiple cathodic features assigned to different reaction steps, although a consistent mechanistic interpretation remains elusive. Here, we combine cyclic voltammetry analysis with in situ product detection using scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM), and hydrodynamic analysis using rotating disk electrode (RDE), to investigate nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction on silver. We show that the cathodic response changes from a single peak to two distinct features with increasing nitrate concentration when using phosphate buffer as a supporting electrolyte. Analysis of concentration, scan rate, and pH dependencies, together with systematic variation of phosphate electrolyte composition, indicates that these features arise from distinct interfacial proton-transfer regimes associated with the availability of H2PO4– as a proton donor. In addition, SECM enables the assignment of each feature to local nitrite formation, ruling out changes in product identity as the origin of each feature. These findings show that phosphate electrolyte modulates proton-donor availability, and, consequently, the voltammetric response of nitrate reduction on silver, providing a framework for interpreting the complex electrocatalytic behavior observed in this system.

articles.title: Synthesis of Chiral α-Aminophosphonate Derivatives through Copper(I)-Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation
articles.abstract: Efficient methodologies for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of α-aminophosphonic acid derivatives remain limited, particularly those involving carbon-carbon (C-C) bond formation. Herein, we report a copper(I)-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonates with alkyl halides, which provides a versatile strategy for accessing diverse chiral α-aminophosphonate derivatives. A wide range of alkyl halides, including allyl bromides, propargyl bromide, benzyl bromides, and alkyl iodides, act as efficient alkylating agents. Control experiments demonstrate that the employment of the 9H-fluoren-9-ylidene group and the incorporation of a sulfur atom into the phosphonate moiety are crucial for facilitating efficient deprotonation. NMR studies indicate that N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonate undergoes effective chelation with the copper(I) catalyst, a process that plays a pivotal role in promoting the reaction. Finally, both cleavage of the imine moiety and oxidation of the thiophosphonate group can be readily achieved under mild reaction conditions.

articles.title: Pioneering MOF-303 in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries: Coordination Defect Engineering Enables Accelerated Sulfur Redox and Dendrite-Free Plating
articles.abstract: Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are severely hindered by the shuttle effect of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) and uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth. Herein, a defect-engineered MOF-303 (D-MOF-303) modified separator is developed via a ball-milling strategy to simultaneously mitigate both issues, marking the first application of MOF-303 in the Li–S battery field. The intentional introduction of ligand defects and oxygen vacancies reduces particle size, establishes a hierarchical porous structure, and amplifies local Lewis acidity. Consequently, the D-MOF-303 coating layer provides exceptional chemisorption and accelerated electrocatalytic conversion kinetics for LiPSs, while concurrently homogenizing lithium-ion flux to achieve long-term dendrite-free lithium plating. Benefiting from these synergistic merits, the resulting Li–S full cells exhibit high capacity retention over 500 cycles at 0.5 C, enhanced rate capability up to 3 C, and notable environmental resilience under high-humidity aging conditions. This work demonstrates the potential of coordination defect engineering in metal–organic frameworks for advancing high-energy-density and commercially viable energy storage technologies.
